reading: The friend tells the lord of the great hill embraced by cool rain clouds, where peacocks dance and big bees hum, that the girl is dearer to them than he is, for by holding in desire the strictly guarded wedding in the good house he has given them back their own well-being, and she is now theirs for good.
nuance: The friend's praise of the bride is also a claim on her: the girl the man has married is more precious to her own circle than the man, and their own welfare (எம்நலம்) rose with the wedding, so the secret love's anxiety is over for the friend as much as for the girl.

thinai_evidence.note: peacocks and bees of the rain-clouded hill

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: speaker inferred: the colophon gives no thurai; someone who says 'us' (எமக்கே, எம்நலம்) of the bride and addresses the groom after the wedding, most likely the friend

reading: The man asks the girl who covered his eyes with her lovely hand, like a fragrant cluster of kanthal that scents the hillside, the maiden of bamboo shoulders with the grace of a peacock who has become his sweet companion of the bed, whether anyone but her dwells in his heart.
nuance: The game of covering his eyes from behind asks 'guess who'; his answer turns the game into a vow, since there is no one else it could be. The flower of the hand is the kanthal, the hill's own flower, so she is praised with things of her land.

thinai_evidence.note: the kanthal that scents the hillside

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: speaker inferred: the colophon gives no thurai; the man answers the woman who covered his eyes; பாயல் இன்துணை, companion of the bed, suggests wedded life

comparisons.tenor: her hand and fingers
the maiden's grace
her shoulders

reading: The friend tells the lord of the land where the peacock perched on the fire-bright vengai looks like a jewelled maiden that he has done a sweet thing, and blesses his father, for holding the wedding in the good house and setting flowers in the girl's thick braided hair.
nuance: The simile already shows the wedding before the friend names it: a peacock dressed in the vengai's red-gold blossoms is a bride dressed in jewels, and the last line has the man himself dress her hair with flowers. The blessing on his father (நுந்தை வாழியர்) praises the man through his lineage, as one praises a good family's son. That the peacock and the bride make a hidden comparison is ruled out by the marker -இன், which states it.

thinai_evidence.note: the peacock on the flowering vengai

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: speaker inferred: the colophon gives no thurai; someone who speaks of the bride as இவள் and thanks the groom for the wedding, most likely the friend

comparisons.tenor: the vengai in red-gold bloom
the peacock perched on the vengai

reading: The girl asks whether her heart, which went off with the man of the hill country, where the peacock, driven by the field-clearers' firebrands, rushes out like girls at ball play and harries the sparrows on the millet stubble, will come back, or will settle there because it wants to live with him.
nuance: The question is put to no one: she cannot recall the heart and does not know its mind. The picture of the startled peacock scattering the sparrows like girls chasing a ball is lively play beside her stillness; reading it as a hidden image of her own unsettled heart would need more than one match, so it is left as scene. Line 3 (புனவர் கொள்ளியின் புகல்வரும்) may mean the peacock flees the firebrands or comes eagerly toward them.

thinai_evidence.note: the hill country's peacock, millet stubble and field-clearers

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: speaker inferred: the colophon gives no thurai; the girl speaks of 'my heart' that went with the hill man; the friend as hearer is a guess, the poem may be spoken to no one

comparisons.tenor: the peacock's rush among the sparrows

reading: The friend tells the lord of the land where the slope's peacock steals the heavy-eared millet the hill girl guards that he comes even in the dark of midnight, and that if a fierce beast should strike him she would not know what to do.
nuance: The refusal is made as fear for him, not as blame. The opening scene does double work: the guarded millet stolen by the peacock is the guarded girl he takes in secret, and the millet field is also where the girls are by day, a hint of where he might meet her instead of at midnight.

thinai_evidence.note: the hill girl guarding millet and the night visit

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: speaker inferred: the colophon gives no thurai; the speaker tells the man he comes at midnight and fears for him, the friend's refusal of the night tryst

comparisons.tenor: the man who takes the guarded girl in secret

ullurai.tenor: the guarded girl and the man who comes for her by night

pairs.situation: the girl is kept under guard by her household
the man takes her love in secret, slipping past that guard

ullurai.speaker_fit: the friend uses the millet field and peacock of the kurinji hill in a kurinji poem (porul 7.27)

reading: The friend tells the lord of the land where the peacock on the great bough of the spreading vengai looks like women plucking flowers that even if he goes away, the love of the girl who has joined with him will not go away.
nuance: The play on பிரி (part) carries the poem: his parting is one thing and her bond's parting another, and the second will not follow the first. It is an assurance, but also a reminder that the bond holds her whether or not he returns.

thinai_evidence.note: the peacock on the flowering vengai of the hill; the parting is the short one of secret love, not a journey

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: speaker inferred: the colophon gives no thurai; the speaker tells the man about 'the maiden joined with you', so not the girl herself; the friend, as he is about to leave

comparisons.tenor: the peacock among the vengai blossoms

reading: The man says that though the slow-gaited hill girl of the good town on the slope, where peacocks dance without knowing whether rain will come, shows him no grace, he has never once forgotten her, thinking of her always.
nuance: உள்ளுபு மறந்தறியேம், 'thinking of her, we have never known forgetting', is the same turn the Kural gives the man in 1125. The peacock that dances before any sign of rain is the man who keeps loving before any sign of her favour.

thinai_evidence.note: the dancing peacock of the hill slope and the hill girl

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: speaker inferred: the colophon gives no thurai; the man speaks of a girl who does not favour him (அருளாள்); speaking to her friend to win her help is a guess

iraicchi.act: the peacock dances in hope though it does not know that the rain will come
iraicchi.sense: the man keeps the girl in his thoughts and loves on, though no sign of her grace has come

reading: The man says that the split-mouthed blue lilies blooming in the green spring on the hill-man's slope can hardly open like the eyes of the slow-gaited hill girl with her fine thin locks, and that even the peacock can hardly have her soft grace.
nuance: The comparison is turned round: the lily and the peacock, the hill's usual likenesses for eyes and grace, are measured against her and fall short. Both come from her own hill (குன்ற நாடன் குன்றத்து), so it is her land's best that she outdoes.

thinai_evidence.note: the lily of the hill spring and the peacock

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: speaker inferred: the colophon gives no thurai; the man praises the girl as இவள், one present or near; he names the hill as குன்ற நாடன் குன்றத்து in the third person, read here as her father the hill chief; the friend as addressee is a guess, and the friend as speaker is possible

comparisons.tenor: the blue lilies, which cannot open as her eyes do
the peacock, which cannot have her grace

reading: The friend tells the girl of sweet words that the lord of the great-rocked hill, where the peacock spreads its lovely plumes like a hill girl's hair, has come, and her kin have agreed to give her to him: may her good fortune flourish.
nuance: The decade closes with the marriage settled. Here the peacock is likened to the girl, not she to it: by the end of the decade she is the standard the hill's birds are measured by.

comparisons.tenor: the peacock's spread plumes

title: பாலை செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து decade 31
theme: Ainkurunuru 301 to 310, Othalanthaiyar's paalai decade செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து, in which the friend tries to stop the man from crossing the waste for wealth: the road's flowers, its seized water, its starving elephant pair and its fires are set against the woman's grief, her slipping bangles and the smile of an unborn son.
source_issues: 301-310: the colophon gives thinai only, no thurai; every speaker and addressee in thurai_akam (the friend to the departing man) is inferred from the decade title செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து and the poems, so occasion words are null.
302: line 4 மல்லம் புலம்ப is obscure (perhaps மல்லல் அம், the rich place, grieving); the reading of the closing line turns on it.
306: பல்கழ் in line 2 (perhaps பல்காழ், many strands of beads) and விழவொலி கூந்தல் in line 4 are hard to fix; the reading of the woman's ornaments and hair is uncertain.
308: the sense of பிரிந்தெனப் பிரிமே (who parts, and from what) is not settled by the text.

reading: The friend tells the man of the dark-hilled country that if he crosses that range, where travellers on the hard waste crown their heads with the white clusters of the great pale lodhra, the woman he leaves will suffer greatly.
nuance: The only image of the road is a festive one: those who cross it wear its flowers on their heads. The friend grants the journey its attraction and sets against it a single plain clause about the one who stays; அவ்வரை, that range, is set against his own மைவரை, the dark hills he would leave.

thinai_evidence.note: a warning against a crossing of the waste that is still only intended

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives thinai only, no thurai; the friend speaking to the departing man is inferred from the decade title செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து and the poem's address

reading: The friend tells the man that his hard-won work for rare wealth has a right not to be failed, and the broad-shouldered woman has an equal right to hold him back; it would be good if he did not go, leaving her weeping and the rich place forlorn.
nuance: The two claims are set in matching lines (உரித்தே, உரியள்): she does not call the wealth-work wrong, only equal, and தகைத்தல், holding back, is the very act the decade is named for. She asks for a choice, not a verdict.

thinai_evidence.note: a departure for wealth that the friend tries to stop

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives thinai only, no thurai; the friend speaking to the departing man is inferred from the decade title செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து and the poem's address

reading: The friend asks the young man, since in summer's hard waste the banyan with fruit like new-fired pots holds back the போகில் bird, to take them with him so that the road may be cool and sweet.
nuance: Near miss for iraicchi: the banyan detaining the passing bird does what the decade wants done to the man, but lines 1 and 2 also carry the waste that line 3's wish (தண்ணிய இனிய வாக) refers to, so the deletion test does not plainly pass; it stays scene. The plea changes ground: not 'do not go' but 'go with us'.

thinai_evidence.note: summer on the hard waste

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives thinai only, no thurai; the friend speaking to the departing man is inferred from the decade title செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து and the poem's address; எம்மொடும் makes the friend speak with the woman as 'us'

comparisons.tenor: the banyan's ripe fruit

reading: The friend warns the young lord of strong horses that if he goes by the stony forking path, where the elephant seizes the cattle's water from the trough the unlettered herdsmen dug with their sticks, the soft woman with long cloud-dark hair will grieve; let him not be capable of it.
nuance: வல்லாதீமே asks him to be incapable: the strength his epithet praises (வயமான் தோன்றல்) is the strength the friend asks him to lack. The road's one water is dug by hand and still taken by force, so the waste is shown as a place where even what is made is lost.

thinai_evidence.note: the hero's intended crossing and the woman's grief

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives thinai only, no thurai; the friend speaking to the departing man is inferred from the decade title செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து and the poem's address

comparisons.tenor: her long hair

reading: The friend asks the young man what gain his going will bring, if it makes the girl of bright bangles grieve, on the parched hills where the tusker, holding his mate close, does not wander to other lands but suffers with her as hunger eats them.
nuance: பிறபுலம் படராது is the exact negative of the hero's plan: the beast will not go to other lands even for food, the man will go to other lands for wealth. பயம், gain, is the hero's own measure turned against him.

thinai_evidence.note: hills whose green has dried, the waste of the hot season

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives thinai only, no thurai; the friend speaking to the departing man is inferred from the decade title செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து and the poem's address

iraicchi.act: the tusker embraces his mate and, though starving, does not leave for other lands but suffers the hunger with her
iraicchi.sense: even the beast in drought will not leave his mate for a richer land, so the man who would leave her for wealth falls below it

reading: The friend tells the warrior lord that if he crosses the wide waste, the dark woman with hair like a festival's abundance will grieve more than the flute laments, as the fine lines on her jewelled waist wither.
nuance: Her grief is measured against the flute (குழலினும்), the instrument of the evening's mourning music, so her lament is pictured as heard, not only felt. The address வெல்போர்க் குருசில் praises his victories in war just as it asks him not to set out.

thinai_evidence.note: an intended crossing and the grief it would cause

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives thinai only, no thurai; the friend speaking to the departing man is inferred from the decade title செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து and the poem's address

comparisons.tenor: her grieving

reading: The friend tells the lord of the shore that he has set his heart on the hill-bound hard waste where even the strong beast shies from the roaring flame of the fire-drill bamboo, and that his wealth is not good, since it comes by parting from his doll-like companion.
nuance: The beast fears the fire and the man does not fear the road, which the friend does not praise. The wealth is the grammatical subject that comes (வருமே) by the parting, so the parting is its price, paid by her. கொண்க, the shore-lord's address, is unusual in a paalai poem.

thinai_evidence.note: the hard waste of hills where fires blaze

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives thinai only, no thurai; the friend speaking to the departing man is inferred from the decade title செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து and the poem's address; நின் துணை names the woman as his wife

comparisons.tenor: his companion

reading: The friend tells the man that it would be good not to part from the soft woman of thick dark hair; if he parts, they will part as one parts from the great hill where Murugan dwells and the bright blossoms of the eru tree lie strewn.
nuance: பிரிமே is first person plural: the friend speaks of the women's own parting, and the comparison is to leaving the sacred home hill, so his going would uproot them too. Whether this means leaving home with him, or leaving life, the poem does not settle.

thinai_evidence.note: the parting the friend tries to prevent

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives thinai only, no thurai; the friend speaking to the departing man is inferred from the decade title செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து and the poem's address

reading: The friend tells the man of the steep-hilled country that he is set on crossing the hot waste in the summer month, and asks whether the wealth he would make by going is sweeter than seeing the smile of the little son his loving wife carries in her heavy pregnancy.
nuance: The son is not yet born (கடுஞ்சூல்), so the smile weighed against the wealth is one he has never seen; the friend sets made wealth (செய் பொருள்) against a good that needs only his presence. நன்று in line 2 is ironic.

thinai_evidence.note: summer on the hot waste

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives thinai only, no thurai; the friend speaking to the departing man is inferred from the decade title செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து and the poem's address; கடுஞ்சூல் places the poem in married life

reading: The friend tells the young man that if he is capable of parting, so that the bright bangles of her soft shoulders and her ornaments slip loose, the beauty of her fine brow will be hard to keep.
nuance: Her body is described first by its ornaments (the gold girdle of coins, the bangles) and the harm is told as their loosening, the visible sign of wasting. வல்லுவை, 'if you are able', makes the departure a test of his hardness, not of his means.

thinai_evidence.note: the parting and the wasting it would cause

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives thinai only, no thurai; the friend speaking to the departing man is inferred from the decade title செலவு அழுங்குவித்த பத்து and the poem's address

title: பாலை செலவுப் பத்து decade 32
theme: Ainkurunuru 311 to 320, Othalanthaiyar's paalai decade on the going (செலவுப் பத்து): the man, and in 313 the girl, crosses the wasteland of killing elephants, scorched trees and flaming silk-cotton, and those left behind measure the road by their own wasting, ask whether he will delay or forget, bless the hill that hid him, and find that the heart too has gone and not come back.
source_issues: 311-320: the colophon gives no thurai for the decade (செலவுப் பத்து), so every speaker in thurai_akam is inferred from the poem.
312: என்னை may be 'my man' or 'my father'; the speaker (the woman left behind, or the girl in flight) turns on it.

314: line 2 reads கர்ங்கண் காக்கையொடு, a misprint for கருங்கண் (dark-eyed); the karu form is taken from காக்கையொடு. Line 1 (அவிர்தொடி கொட்பக் கழுதுபுகவு அயர) is obscure: whose bangles whirl is not clear.
315: line 3 (விழைநெகிழ் செல்லல் உறீஇ) is hard to construe; the reading 'a sorrow that undoes what she cherished' is tentative.
319: line 2 மண்புரை is taken as cracked or heaped earth; the sense is not certain.

reading: The woman says her lover has crossed a forest whose road so frightens travellers that even the panchuram call of the girls plucking vengai flowers alarms them, and her heart keeps asking whether he will stay away long.
nuance: The fear is put first in the travellers, not in her: a harmless sound from the hill, the flower-pluckers' cry, is enough to startle anyone on that road, so the danger he faces is measured by other people's nerves before she turns to her own worry about delay (நீடுவர் கொல்).

thinai_evidence.note: the man has gone across the hard tract and she is left behind

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (செலவுப் பத்து); speaker and addressee inferred from the poem: நினையும்என் நெஞ்சே gives the woman's own voice; the friend is the likely hearer

reading: The woman blesses, again and again, the hill with falls bright as a sword that has hidden her man, strong in the hunt, from her sight, praying it stay full of virtue even if drought comes upon it.
nuance: She blesses rather than curses the hill that robbed her of the sight of him: the wish that it keep its virtue (and its water) even in drought is a wish for his safe passage over it. If என்னை is read as 'my father', the speaker would instead be the girl in flight looking back at the hill that hides her home, and the blessing would be for the cover it gives.

thinai_evidence.note: the hill has taken the departing man out of sight, in a land that may dry

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (செலவுப் பத்து); speaker and addressee inferred from the poem: the vocative குன்றே makes the hill the addressee; என்னை is taken as 'my man', the one it hid

comparisons.tenor: the gleam of the hill's waterfall

reading: The speaker tells the mother that her daughter's desire is a scorching thing: leaving them wasted with grief, life ebbing and hearts ruined, their beloved girl has crossed the forest of a tract that lies between lands.
nuance: தெறுவது, 'that which burns', is said of the girl's love itself, not of the man or the road: the household's grief is laid at the door of her desire, the force that made the forest crossable for her.

thinai_evidence.note: the girl has gone through the forest with her lover

thurai_akam.speaker: sevili
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (செலவுப் பத்து); speaker and addressee inferred from the poem: நும்மகள் (your daughter) is said to the mother by someone of the household, and நம் காதலோள் claims the girl as the speaker's own as well; the foster mother fits best, the friend is possible

reading: The woman says they report that the road taken by the man who tired of lying on her shoulders is a long hard waste where ghouls feast with whirling bright bangles, dark-eyed crows and vultures fill the sky, and the small-eyed elephant roams after killing men.
nuance: The scene is a battlefield's: ghouls, crows and vultures over men the elephant has killed. தோளிடை முனிநர், 'those who grew weary between our shoulders', turns his going into a rejection of her embrace, so the road of corpses is what he preferred to it.

thinai_evidence.note: the long hard wasteland with its killing elephant is the tract of separation

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (செலவுப் பத்து); speaker and addressee inferred from the poem: நம் தோளிடை முனிநர் is the woman's complaint about the man; the friend may also be the speaker on her behalf

reading: The woman says they report that he is far away and does not hear the outcry of her long eyes, cool as dewy flowers, that have taken to the bed, he who crossed the forest of groves where bamboo grows old, leaving her in a sorrow that undoes what she cherished.
nuance: பூசல், an outcry or public clamour, is given to the eyes, so the weeping is imagined as a shout he is too far to hear: her grief is loud and the distance makes it silent.

thinai_evidence.note: he is far beyond the forest and she is left to grieve

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (செலவுப் பத்து); speaker and addressee inferred from the poem: the outcry of the eyes is hers; the friend is the likely hearer

comparisons.tenor: the woman's long eyes

reading: The woman says that, letting her golden ornaments and gold-wrought discs fall away and the fine lines of her chariot-broad waist fade, he has surely gone into the forest on the shining mountains where the thin-barked omai stands tall and tigers walk the paths.
nuance: The two halves are set as cause and place: the loss of her gold and the fading of her waist-lines happen here, the tiger paths and omai trees are there, and மன்ற ('surely') makes her body the proof that he has gone.

thinai_evidence.note: he has gone into the forest and her body wastes

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (செலவுப் பத்து); speaker and addressee inferred from the poem: the ornaments and waist are hers; the friend may be speaking of her

comparisons.tenor: the woman's broad waist

reading: The woman asks her friend to come and think with her why her heart, which went to the country of the man who crossed the hard track of the hot paalai forest, burnt bare of all green, has stayed there so long.
nuance: The man's delay is restated as the heart's: it is her heart that has gone to his land and lingers (சென்ற நெஞ்சம் நீடிய), so she asks the friend to deliberate about her own absent heart, the one part of her that did make the crossing.

thinai_evidence.note: the poem names the hot paalai forest and its hard track

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (செலவுப் பத்து); speaker and addressee inferred from the poem: she opens with சூழ்கம் வம்மோ தோழி

reading: The woman says that the men who crossed the high-peaked mountains of a tract where roaring fire ran have surely killed her longing outright, leaving her chosen beauty pale, hard distress tormenting her, and the bangles slipping from her broad shoulders like bamboo.
nuance: நசைநனி கொன்றோர், 'those who utterly killed my longing', names the man as a killer: what dies is not her love but her hope, and the forest fire of line 4 runs through the land he chose over her.

thinai_evidence.note: the men have crossed the mountains and her body pales and wastes

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (செலவுப் பத்து); speaker and addressee inferred from the poem: the pallor and shoulders are hers; the friend is the likely hearer

comparisons.tenor: the woman's broad shoulders

reading: The woman asks whether their lover has crossed the forest of withered trees and cracked earth in a tract scorched by rays that hurt the eyes, and whether he has forgotten them, who do not forget.
nuance: The two questions run in parallel (இறந்தனரோ, மறந்தனரோ): crossing the forest and forgetting her are offered as the same act, and மறவா நம்மே sets her constancy against his.

thinai_evidence.note: the sun-scorched tract of dead trees is paalai

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (செலவுப் பத்து); speaker and addressee inferred from the poem: நம் காதலர் and நம்மே are the woman speaking with the friend

reading: The woman says the man who brought her an unending hard sickness has gone by the forked hard track where the wind, stirred by roaring heat, lifts the bright clustered flowers of the thorny-trunked silk-cotton and scatters them on the earth like embers struck from the sky by thunder.
nuance: The flowers do not simply glow; they fall like thunder-struck embers, so the beauty of the path is turned into a rain of fire, matching the sickness without end (தவலில் அருநோய்) he has left her.

thinai_evidence.note: the flowering silk-cotton of the scorched track belongs to paalai

comparisons.tenor: the falling silk-cotton flowers

title: பாலை இடைச்சுரப் பத்து decade 33
theme: Ainkurunuru 321 to 330, Othalanthaiyar's paalai decade on the middle of the waste (இடைச்சுரப் பத்து): in every poem the man, on the burning road away from the girl, sets the cruelty of the land against her nature (பண்பு, குணன்), which cools the heat, travels with him, takes his heart and at last turns him back.

reading: Crossing a burning forest where the chisel-beaked hen of the dry-headed kite climbs the fork of the omai tree and calls out in loneliness, the man says that though he passes many hills where the language changes, the good nature of the girl with bright bangles does not leave him.
nuance: The distance is measured in languages, not miles (மொழிபெயர்): he has left the land where her speech is spoken, and still what stays with him is her nature (குணனே), not her face.

thinai_evidence.note: the kite on the omai in a land the heat burns is the dry waste

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade; inferred from the poem: the man on the road speaks to himself of the girl he left, naming her by her bangles

iraicchi.act: the hen kite, alone on the bare fork, calls out for its mate
iraicchi.sense: the lonely call on his road is the call of the woman he has left behind, which is why her nature does not leave him however far he goes

reading: The man tells the road through the waste that before, when summer lingered, the tall bamboo withered and the fierce sun scorched the rock, it was hot; now, each time he thinks of the girl with the bright forehead, the path has become cool.
nuance: The weather has not changed: முன்னே and இனியே divide the same road by his thought, not by the season, so memory of her is made the one thing stronger than the paalai sun.

thinai_evidence.note: the lingering summer that splits the rock and the waste road fix paalai

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade; inferred from the poem: the man addresses the waste road itself (வெய்ய வாயினை), contrasting its heat before with its coolness now

reading: The man tells his heart that what came with him across the forking roads of the hot waste, where a strong-toothed red dog watches for a boar among the cactus for his craving pregnant mate, is the nature of the girl it desired.

thinai_evidence.note: the red dog and the cactus of the hot waste are paalai things

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade; inferred from the poem: the closing words address the heart (நெஞ்சம் நீ நயந்தோள்)

iraicchi.act: the male red dog hunts for his pregnant mate who craves food
iraicchi.sense: the male providing for his mate is what the man has gone out to do, and seeing it he finds her nature, not the errand, has travelled with him

reading: On the long road where the summer heat has eaten everything like fire, the man says that if he closes his eyes even a little he will surely see, in the great house in the dead of night, the dark girl with spreading hair whose beauty spots outdo the vengai blossom.
nuance: The dream is placed exactly: not her in general but her in the house at midnight (நள்ளென் கங்குல் நளிமனை), so the man's longing is for the home life the road has interrupted. The certainty (காண்குவென் மன்ற) is his; whether the dream holds is not asked.

thinai_evidence.note: the summer heat on the long road fixes paalai; the night and the house are where his dream goes

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade; inferred from the poem: the man speaks to himself of the sleep he can snatch on the road

comparisons.tenor: the beauty spots on her skin

reading: The man says the hard waste of scorching heat, where a bird, frightened by the rattle of leaves on the summer peepal, does not go in to feed and flies off to another land, does not harm him, for he has the nature of his beloved as his companion.
nuance: The bird gives up and goes elsewhere because the place frightens it; the man, who has also gone elsewhere, says he is not harmed because he does not travel alone. A reader may hear the bird as the man who left; it does nothing a lover should do here, so it stays scene. Line 2's புகாவுண்ணாது is read here as not going in to eat.

thinai_evidence.note: summer and the hard waste fix paalai

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade; inferred from the poem: the man speaks of himself (எம்வெம் காதலி) on the road

reading: In the broad land where the blaze shimmers, where a young doe with her fawn withers for want of any shade and the path never fills because its water has been cut off, the man says the waste is truly cruel, yet sweet is the nature of the girl he left behind.
nuance: The poem is built on இன்னா against இனிய: the waste is harsh, her nature is sweet. The doe withering with her fawn could be read as the woman at home, but she only suffers and does nothing a person of the situation does, so it stays scene. மறையான் in line 5 is hard: perhaps that she stayed behind in secret or out of sight.

thinai_evidence.note: the blazing land and the waterless road are paalai

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade; inferred from the poem: the man sets the cruel road against the girl he left

reading: On the high-bamboo waste where the groves are withered by the sun and a small-eyed elephant, afraid its spotted trunk will burn, will not touch the ground, the man says that even in such a hard place the nature of this fine girl has made things cool.
nuance: The elephant, the largest creature, holds its trunk off the ground for fear of burning; the coolness the man claims is measured against that.

thinai_evidence.note: the sun-withered groves of the waste are paalai

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade; inferred from the poem: the man speaks of this girl (இத் தகையோள்) as present to his mind on the road

reading: The man says that though the forest of ripe-musth groves he has crossed is cool, with light rain falling and fragrant flowers strewn, it is truly hot for him, since he has left behind his gentle sweet companion.
nuance: The decade's other poems have her memory cool the hot road; this one reverses it, and a road the rain has cooled burns because she is not with him. Paalai here is a state of the man, not of the land.

thinai_evidence.note: the man has left her and crossed the forest; the separation, not the weather, makes it paalai

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade; inferred from the poem: the man speaks of himself (இறந்தேற்கே) who has crossed the forest

reading: Having crossed the vast ruined land where no one goes and the hard waste of hostile frontiers, the man wonders whether his strong heart will come back with him, the heart taken by the girl who stayed behind with her close-fitting bangles slipping off.
nuance: The heart is called strong (உரங்கெழு), the strength that let him leave, yet she has kept it; the slipping bangles are the sign at home of what the road costs.

thinai_evidence.note: the ruined, peopleless waste is paalai

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade; inferred from the poem: the man speaks of his own heart (என் உரங்கெழு நெஞ்சே), which she has taken; whether he addresses it or his companions (நம்மொடு) the poem leaves open

reading: Though they have come through the sun-scorched forest gone to hot dust, the man says the journey should stop now, for the girl with bright bangles, her eyes wet with weeping and her beauty ruined, keeps thinking in her heart of the scorching waste he is crossing.
nuance: The decade's last poem turns him back. What stops him is not the road but her picture of the road: she suffers his journey in her mind (உள்ளத்துப் படரே), so his going is her pain.

thinai_evidence.note: the sun-scorched waste fixes paalai

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade; inferred from the poem: the man, partway through the journey (வந்தனம் ஆயினும்), resolves to give it up; this is the situation of செலவழுங்குதல்

title: பாலை தலைவி இரங்கு பத்து decade 34
theme: Ainkurunuru 331 to 340, Othalanthaiyar's paalai decade of the wife's lament (தலைவி இரங்கு பத்து): every poem opens on அம்ம வாழி தோழி and the wife, her man gone across the waste for wealth, measures his leaving against the beasts and birds that should have stopped him, against stone, against the embrace, and against the season and the evening that should have brought him home.
source_issues: 333 line 3: பெர்ந்தோடு is a misprint for பெருந்தோடு (great flock).
334 line 5: அழப்பிர்ந் தோரே is a misprint for அழப்பிரிந் தோரே (who parted, making her weep).
340 line 4: தட்டைத் சென்றனர் நம்மே is a spurious line conflating line 3 (விட்டுச் சென்றனர் நம்மே) with the start of line 5; the poem reads as four lines without it.

reading: The wife tells her friend that on the hill where the white blossoms on the low boughs of the black-trunked maraam, its clusters opening, smell so sweet that those crossing the hard waste think of the ones they left, people still call the road her man took a painful one.
nuance: The poem sets sweet against painful in adjacent lines (இனிய கமழும், இன்னாது): the scent on the road exists to turn travellers' thoughts homeward, so if even that road is called painful, the pain is his choice to keep going, not the land's.

thinai_evidence.note: a man gone across the hard waste and a wife left behind is the separation of paalai

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (தலைவி இரங்கு பத்து); inferred from the poem: the vocative தோழி and the lament over the man gone across the waste point to the wife speaking to her friend while he is away

reading: The wife tells her friend that the herds of beasts of the forest round the high hills are surely without any virtue, since they did not say to him, 'parting from a beloved is cruel; do not go, sir.'
nuance: She calls the beasts lawless (அறன் இல) for failing to state a rule of right, that leaving a beloved is cruel: the reproach that belongs to the man is shifted onto the animals he passed. The beasts are the subject of the poem, not a side image, so the deletion test for iraicchi fails.

thinai_evidence.note: the man's parting through the hill forest is the situation

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (தலைவி இரங்கு பத்து); inferred from the poem: the vocative தோழி and the lament over the man gone across the waste point to the wife speaking to her friend while he is away

reading: The wife asks her friend whether the great flocks of birds in that good stony land are good for nothing at all, since they did not say to him, 'we live joined with our mates; how will you live apart?'
nuance: The birds' imagined speech is the argument she could not make: their own paired life is the proof, so she wishes the creatures had used their example where her words failed. As in 332 they are the poem's subject, so this is not iraicchi.

thinai_evidence.note: the parting across stony country is paalai's situation

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (தலைவி இரங்கு பத்து); inferred from the poem: the vocative தோழி and the lament over the man gone across the waste point to the wife speaking to her friend while he is away

reading: The wife tells her friend that the man who went through the stony waste where small-leaved nelli grows tall, with her foolish heart following behind him, and who left while her many-petalled kohl-lined eyes wept, is surely harder than stone.
nuance: The stone comes back twice: he crosses a land of stones (கல்வாய்) and is harder than stone (கல்லினும் வலியர்), so the country he chose has become his character. Her heart went with him (பின்செல), so what is left behind is only the weeping eyes.

thinai_evidence.note: the man leaving through the waste with her heart behind him

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (தலைவி இரங்கு பத்து); inferred from the poem: the vocative தோழி and the lament over the man gone across the waste point to the wife speaking to her friend while he is away

comparisons.tenor: the man who left
her eyes, like a many-petalled flower

reading: The wife tells her friend that the roads taken by those who will be long in coming back to them here are said to be very cruel, where the vulture with ears red as blood watches for stinking carrion on the stony slopes.
nuance: நீடி இவண் வருநர், 'those who will come here after delay', admits he will return while fixing on the delay; the vulture waiting for flesh is her fear of what the road does to travellers, a mood, not an act of the love situation, so it stays scene and simile.

thinai_evidence.note: fear for the man on the road of the waste

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (தலைவி இரங்கு பத்து); inferred from the poem: the vocative தோழி and the lament over the man gone across the waste point to the wife speaking to her friend while he is away

comparisons.tenor: the vulture's red ears

reading: The wife tells her friend that those who crossed the waste where summer heat lingers, seized by the sickness for wealth that never stays, surely embraced them as if they would never part.
nuance: The wealth he chases is called நின்றது இல், 'what does not stay', the very fault she finds in him: the embrace that seemed to promise permanence and the wealth that cannot keep it are set side by side, and he traded the first for the second.

thinai_evidence.note: the long summer and the waste fix paalai

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (தலைவி இரங்கு பத்து); inferred from the poem: the vocative தோழி and the lament over the man gone across the waste point to the wife speaking to her friend while he is away

comparisons.tenor: the way he embraced her

reading: The wife tells her friend that for the man who went to the cold dark hills, wealth is surely sweeter even than the embrace of clasping hands, desired body against body, with her.
nuance: She does not say he loves her less; she says he has weighed two sweetnesses and found wealth the sweeter, so the grief is about a measured choice. The last word of the poem is பொருளே, held back to the end like a verdict.

thinai_evidence.note: the man gone for wealth is paalai's parting

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (தலைவி இரங்கு பத்து); inferred from the poem: the vocative தோழி and the lament over the man gone across the waste point to the wife speaking to her friend while he is away

comparisons.tenor: the wealth he went for

reading: The wife tells her friend that on the slope the tall silk-cotton, blooming leafless, shows at the edge of the waste as a fire on the mountain, and even in this season when parting is hard, their lover is skilled at the hard thing of parting.
nuance: The play on அரு is the point: in a season when parting is hard (பிரிவருங் காலை) he is able at what is hard (அரிது வல்லுநர்), so his strength is named in the very word for her pain. The blossom like a hill fire marks the spring that should keep lovers together.

thinai_evidence.note: the leafless silk-cotton in flower at the edge of the waste

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (தலைவி இரங்கு பத்து); inferred from the poem: the vocative தோழி and the lament over the man gone across the waste point to the wife speaking to her friend while he is away

comparisons.tenor: the red blossoms of the leafless silk-cotton

reading: The wife asks her friend whether, in the land her lover went to, there is no evening, the hour when bats fly up to eat the fragrant fruit of the short-boughed, small-leaved neem.
nuance: The question assumes that evening, if it reached him, would bring him home, since it is the hour of longing; she can only explain his staying by supposing his land has no dusk. The bats going to the fruit at evening could be read as creatures returning to what they crave, but they do nothing the lovers do, so they stay scene.

thinai_evidence.note: the evening of a wife whose man has gone away

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (தலைவி இரங்கு பத்து); inferred from the poem: the vocative தோழி and the lament over the man gone across the waste point to the wife speaking to her friend while he is away

reading: The wife asks her friend whether her lover does not think of them, or whether she has fallen into delusion, for he went away and left them while the town's gossip rose like fire in dry bamboo.
nuance: Gossip in paalai is unusual: here it does not expose a secret love but mocks a wife who was left, and it spreads with the crackle and speed of a bamboo fire. Her two questions (does he not think of us, or am I deluded) leave open whether the fault is his or hers.

thinai_evidence.note: he has gone and left her

comparisons.tenor: the town's gossip

title: பாலை இளவேனிற் பத்து decade 35
theme: Ainkurunuru 341 to 350, Othalanthaiyar's paalai decade of early spring (இளவேனிற் பத்து): every poem opens on the same line, he does not come but the time has come, and closes on one sign of spring (the koel, drunk bees on the nunavam, the kongu bud, punku leaves on young breasts, the kadamba grove, the paathiri, the mango's flame-red shoots, the neem), until the last names it as the time his sweet words had promised.
source_issues: 341-350: the colophon has no thurai for this decade; speaker (the wife) and addressee (her friend) are inferred from the refrain, so occasion words are null.
344 line 2: இஅள்முலை is a corrupt form; 347 line 2 has இளமுலை in an otherwise identical line, which is the reading taken.

344 and 347 are word for word the same poem (apart from the corrupt letter), and so are 345 and 348; a ten-poem decade on ten spring signs would not repeat two of them, so the source has probably filled two lost or misread poems with copies of their neighbours. Both pairs are marked as printed.

350 line 3 is a repaired line (tamilvu reading); தேம்படு கிளவியவர்த் தெளிக்கும் is taken as 'the time of which he assured (us) with honeyed words', a reading not fully certain, and line 2's உறப்பத் (crowding, pressing thick) is read with it.

reading: She says that he has not come, but the time has come, the time when the female koel calls in her sweet voice and the fine sand-ripples, the colour of grit, sway in the thinning stream.
nuance: The refrain sets two subjects against each other: அவர் (he) does not come, தான் (it, the time) has come of itself. The poet chose the female koel, the calling mate, but the poem gives her no answering male, so she is left as a sound of the season rather than an act (scene, not iraicchi); the shrunken stream over fine sand is the first sign of the hot months of paalai.

thinai_evidence.note: he has gone and not come back, though the season has, which is the grief of parting

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade; inferred from the refrain: a woman whose man has gone (அவரோ வாரார்) speaks of him in the third person, most likely the wife to her friend in the household stage of parting

reading: She says that he has not come, but the time has come when the black-stemmed nunavam, its big branches loud with drunken bees, gives out its scent.
nuance: The bees are drunk with the season (களித்து ஆலும) while she is sober with waiting; the revel is only a mood, with no act of a lover in it, so it stays scene.

reading: She says that he has not come, but the time has come when women smear the tender leaves of the punku, its flowers like puffed rice, on their young breasts to make their beauty shine.
nuance: The season's custom is an adornment for a lover's eyes: the young leaves are worn so that the breasts may be seen, and the one who should see them is away, so the beauty the season makes is wasted on her.

nuance: நம் makes the grove theirs: the place that blooms is the one they shared, so the spring is not only a date he has missed but a meeting place that keeps its appointment without him.

reading: She says that he has not come, but the time has come when the mango with its cracked bark puts out young shoots like flame, so many that its branches are buried in them.
nuance: பொரிகால் and எரிகால் rhyme across the two lines: the old trunk looks scorched and the new shoots look like fire, so the tree that seemed burnt out renews itself, which is what the parted woman cannot do.

reading: She says that he has not come, but the time has come, the time of the neem's bright flowers crowding the branches, the very time of which he assured us with honey-sweet words.
nuance: The last poem names what the refrain has meant all along: the time that has come is the time his own sweet words fixed (தெளிக்கும், to make one sure), so the decade ends on a broken assurance, not on a season. The neem is the bitter tree, and its bright flower stands beside the honeyed words.

title: பாலை வரவுரைத்த பத்து decade 36
theme: Ainkurunuru 351 to 360, Othalanthaiyar's paalai decade on the return (வரவுரைத்த பத்து): the friend tells the wife that the men who crossed the waste have come back, and the man himself tells her that thinking of her he gave up the wealth-quest, and that the long burnt road grew short and easy on the way home.

source_issues.issue: The word உடிஅத்தெழு is not a regular form; the sense (a flood that breaks out) suggests உடைத்தெழு. Marked uncertain; the word is not used as evidence.
The colophon has no thurai for any poem of this decade; speakers in thurai_akam are inferred from the poems.

reading: The friend tells the woman that the men have come back, leaving behind them the wasteland where travellers on the hard road eat the small sun-scorched fruit of the desert jackfruit and pass on, so the withered state of her lovely waist may now be cured.
nuance: The road is measured by its food: the only meal it offers is a fruit the sun has already eaten (வெயில்தின்), so the men's return is set against a land that half-consumes whatever is in it, as separation had wasted her body.

thinai_evidence.note: the hard road under a sun that eats the fruit fixes the waste

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (வரவுரைத்த பத்து, poems telling of the return); the friend tells the woman, whom she addresses (மடந்தை நின்), that the men have come

comparisons.tenor: her kohl-lined eyes

reading: Our lover has come back, says the speaker to her friend, without calling hard the burning waste where the great-trunked elephant, its hide ridged like the lettered hero-stone of men who fell to the arrows of strong-bowed warriors, vents its dark rage.
nuance: The hero-stone, the waste's sign of men killed on the road, enters only as the likeness of a living elephant's hide, so the danger is doubled while the poem's point stays that the man did not count it (அரிய என்னார). Lines 1 and 2 repeat a formula of Akananuru 53.

thinai_evidence.note: the hot waste road is the land of the poem

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (வரவுரைத்த பத்து, poems telling of the return); the vocative தோழி with நம் காதலோர் would also fit the woman speaking to her friend; the decade's title favours the friend announcing the return

comparisons.tenor: the elephant's ridged, roughened hide (விழுப்பிணர்)

reading: The men who crossed the hills of great dark groves have come back, so that she may sweetly embrace that beautiful raised chest on which bright ornaments shine like a red hill encircled by a creeper of flame.
nuance: The image gives the returning man's chest the look of a hill, the very thing he crossed: the land he left her for comes back to her as the body she embraces. எரிக்கொடி may be a red-flowered creeper or a line of fire; either way the basis is colour.

thinai_evidence.note: the men who crossed the hills return to end the separation

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (வரவுரைத்த பத்து, poems telling of the return); the friend tells the woman (நீ இனிது முயங்க) that the men have come

comparisons.tenor: his broad chest with its shining ornaments

reading: The friend tells the woman that he has crossed back over the hard road where the red wild-dog, having mated with its tender female, passes by the doe with her fawn without seizing her, hurrying because her nature drew him.
nuance: The predator of the waste, which in other paalai poems kills on the road, here holds back: the beasts the man passed on the way home already show the restraint and tenderness he is bringing back.

thinai_evidence.note: the hard waste road of the wild dog

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (வரவுரைத்த பத்து, poems telling of the return); the friend addresses the woman (தெரியிழை அரிவை நின்)

iraicchi.act: the male wild dog, keeping to its mate, lets the doe with her fawn go unharmed
iraicchi.sense: a beast at one with its mate spares another's mother and young, as the man, drawn by his wife, left off his own seizing of wealth and hurried home

reading: The man tells his wife that, thinking of her beauty, he turned back without so much as saying 'may the hard work of the wealth-quest win great fortune', from the forest whose tracks cross the path and where small-eyed elephants with spotted faces roam.
nuance: He abandons the wealth-quest without even the courtesy of a blessing on it: the omitted farewell (சொல்லாது) is the measure of how completely her beauty outweighed the project.

thinai_evidence.note: the man gives up the journey for wealth and comes back

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (வரவுரைத்த பத்து, poems telling of the return); the man speaks of himself to the woman (திருந்திழை அரிவை, நின்னலம்)

reading: The man tells his wife that her virtues are truly sweet to think of, for in the waste that bright fire has grazed over they drew his heart back like the gold-worked rope with which rich men tie their elephant.
nuance: The comparison is made by the case ending of கயிற்றின், not by அன்ன or போல. The rope is costly as well as strong: what pulls him home is fine and precious, and he is the great beast that it holds.

thinai_evidence.note: the fire-burnt waste road

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (வரவுரைத்த பத்து, poems telling of the return); the man addresses the woman (நின் குணனே)

comparisons.tenor: her virtues pulling his heart

reading: Our lover has come back, the friend tells the woman: seeing the forest dressed for the season, kuravam opening and maravam in flower, he said 'let the journey for wealth be given up' and came, longing for her, so that her lovely dark glowing skin may regain its beauty.
nuance: The flowering that usually marks a promised season of return here works on the man himself: the forest he was crossing put on its adornment (அணி) and reminded him of his own wife's beauty, so he turned back mid-journey.

thinai_evidence.note: the man gives up the journey on seeing the season

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (வரவுரைத்த பத்து, poems telling of the return); as in 352 the vocative தோழி could also make the woman the speaker

reading: Though he has crossed many high-peaked hills, will her eyes let him stay away long, eyes that, thinking long of him, cloud over each time they are wiped and have become a flood that bursts out?
nuance: The subject of நீடவிடுமோ is the eyes: the tears are imagined as a force that will not allow his delay, so grief itself becomes the pledge of his return.

thinai_evidence.note: the man has gone beyond the hills and is waited for

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (வரவுரைத்த பத்து, poems telling of the return); the speaker is not named; the third-person இறந்தனர் and the assurance that he cannot stay long fit the friend comforting the woman, but the woman speaking of her own eyes is also possible

comparisons.tenor: her tears

reading: The man tells his wife that when he left her, wanting rare wealth, and parted on the rocky tracks, the ways through the waste were very long, but now, as he comes thinking of her, they have become near.
nuance: The same road has two lengths: going out for wealth it stretched, coming back for her it shrank, so distance is made a property of desire, not of the land.

thinai_evidence.note: going for wealth and coming back

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (வரவுரைத்த பத்து, poems telling of the return); the man addresses the woman (அணியிழை)

reading: The man tells his doe-eyed wife that the long way through the summer heat, whose growth fire has seized and eaten, though hard, was easy when he drove his swift-horsed sturdy chariot, his aching heart longing for her embrace, thinking of her as he came.
nuance: மான் occurs twice in two lines with two senses, the swift horse he drives and the deer whose look is hers: the creature that carries him and the creature she resembles meet in the last two lines.

thinai_evidence.note: the long summer road scorched by fire

comparisons.tenor: her look

title: பாலை முன்னிலைப் பத்து decade 37
theme: Ainkurunuru 361 to 370, Othalanthaiyar's paalai decade of direct address (முன்னிலைப் பத்து): each poem speaks to someone face to face, the man to the girl whose beauty strikes him and to a mango shoot like her, the friend to the man who comes by night, who would hurry away, who has been gossiped about, and to the mother asking why the girl is pale, all set among the kongu, paathiri and silk-cotton of the dry season and the hunters of the waste.

source_issues.issue: The colophon has no thurai for any poem of this decade; speakers in thurai_akam are inferred from the poems.
Line 5 was repaired from the sangamtamil.com reading (முறியிணர்க் கோங்கம்); the sense of பயந்த மாறே (because the kongu bore flowers) carries the poem, so it is marked uncertain.

reading: The man tells the simple girl who wears a garland strung from summer paathiri flowers heaped on the wide shining sand of a high-banked forest stream that her breasts strike harder than her eyes, and her broad soft shoulders harder than her breasts.
nuance: The climb runs against the usual order of the love poems, where the eyes are the weapon: here each part of her is fiercer (கதவ) than the last, so the praise turns into a mock complaint of being attacked, while the paathiri garland shows her at ease in the waste.

thinai_evidence.note: a forest stream in summer with paathiri in flower is the waste in its season

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (முன்னிலைப் பத்து, poems of direct address); the man addresses the girl directly (மடவரல் மகளே); the summer stream and the garland she has made on the way point to the couple on the road of elopement, as in Akananuru 99, though the poem does not say so

reading: The speaker asks the man with the flower-garlanded chest how he came in the night, when the dark pressed in, by the forked paths hard to walk and strewn with stone cairns, giving no thought to the deadly hatred of the small-eyed elephant, driven by a heart bent on kindness.
nuance: The cairns (பதுக்கை) are the waste's graves of travellers, so the kurinji visit by night is set on a paalai road; the line அருள்புரி நெஞ்சம் turns the reproach into praise, since what drove him across it was kindness, not mere desire.

thinai_evidence.note: the lover's night journey to the tryst and the fear it raises is the kurinji situation, though the road is the waste's

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (முன்னிலைப் பத்து, poems of direct address); the friend (or the girl herself) questions the man who has come by night; the decade's direct address makes the complaint of the dangerous road a question put to his face

reading: The man tells the sister of the killing Eyinar, who carry bows with arrows and wear red-dyed cloth, that she takes the pale spots on her breasts for mere freckling, while his stricken heart takes them for a goddess that strikes.
nuance: The poem turns on a rhyme, சுணங்கு against அணங்கு: the same mark is a blemish of the skin to her and a dread power to him, and the killing trade of her brothers (கொலைவல் எயினர்) stands behind the girl, so the danger he feels is doubled.

thinai_evidence.note: the girl is of the bow-carrying hunters of the waste

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (முன்னிலைப் பத்து, poems of direct address); the man speaks to the girl (நின், நீயே) about his own heart

reading: The speaker asks the young man of the white spear not to hurry until she has told the young Eyitri, sister of the Eyinar who live on porcupine, how things stand and has pleaded with her.
nuance: The -உம் of எயிற்றிக்கும் (to the Eyitri too) suggests the youth has already been told and the girl has not, so the friend stands between his haste and the girl's consent; இளமா may be a young doe or a young mango, either a likeness of the girl.

thinai_evidence.note: the hunters of the waste and the youth of the paalai road

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (முன்னிலைப் பத்து, poems of direct address); the friend asks the youth (விடலை) to wait while she speaks to the girl; the occasion is most likely the plan to leave together, which she must first put to the girl

reading: The man asks a tender mango shoot what penance it did to have such desirable beauty, like the lovely-toothed Eyitri who drives off the birds that come at the fat meat her brothers brought home after killing deer from the herd.
nuance: The comparison is reversed: the shoot is praised for being like the girl, not the girl for being like the shoot, so the question 'what penance did you do?' measures her beauty as a thing a plant must earn.

thinai_evidence.note: a girl of the hunters of the waste, among their kill

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (முன்னிலைப் பத்து, poems of direct address); the man addresses a mango shoot (மாஇன் தளிரே), comparing it with the girl

comparisons.tenor: the mango shoot's colour and beauty

reading: The friend tells the mother that if she, with reddened eyes, keeps pressing for no purpose, saying the girl has grown very pale, nothing will come of it: the pallor is because the kongu with its tender-leaved clusters has come into flower.
nuance: The answer hides and reveals at once: the flowering kongu is the season the man would have named for his coming, so the friend's seasonal excuse is also a hint to the mother that the pallor has a man behind it.

thinai_evidence.note: the kongu's flowering in the dry season

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (முன்னிலைப் பத்து, poems of direct address); the friend answers the mother's questioning with the formula of Akananuru 48 (அன்னாய் வாழி வேண்டு அன்னை); whether the hearer is the mother or the foster mother is not fixed

reading: The friend tells the mother that the girl's life is now joined to the name of the man who came near with his chariot by the summer forest stream strewn with spread blossoms, wearing the gold-like fresh flowers of the rough-barked kongu set apart with the open clusters of vengai.
nuance: பேரொடு புணர்ந்தன்று is stronger than a story of meeting: her life is united not with the man but with his name, as if already married to it, and that is the friend's whole case to the mother.

thinai_evidence.note: the summer forest stream fixes the waste in its season

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (முன்னிலைப் பத்து, poems of direct address); the friend tells the mother (அன்னை) that the girl belongs to the man

comparisons.tenor: the fresh kongu flowers

reading: The speaker asks the lord to share with them the pleasure of the cool spell of summer, when the many spent blossoms of the fire-flowered silk-cotton stripe the dappled shade of the puffed-flowered pungu, if he wishes her of the soft dark hair not to be ruined.
nuance: The dissuasion makes no argument against the journey; it offers a season too sweet to leave, and only the last line, அழிவிலள் எனினே, shows the threat inside the invitation.

thinai_evidence.note: the summer season of the waste, with its silk-cotton in flower

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (முன்னிலைப் பத்து, poems of direct address); the friend tries to hold back the man from a journey by inviting him to the season's pleasure, with the girl's ruin as the price of his going

comparisons.tenor: the red silk-cotton flowers
the white pungu flowers

reading: The speaker tells the man that the gossip, louder than the cry of the great koel of the season that lives on the long kuravam branch, says that yesterday he made a tryst with a woman whose smile is a row of sprouts, in the fragrant grove thick with rich flowers where bees swarm.
nuance: கௌவை means both a loud cry and public talk, so the koel's seasonal call and the town's gossip are measured on one scale, and the gossip wins; a tryst only one day old (நெருநல்) is already louder than the season.

thinai_evidence.note: the kuravam and the koel of early summer

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (முன்னிலைப் பத்து, poems of direct address); the friend tells the man that his tryst is known; the woman of the tryst may be the girl herself, which makes this a warning that urges marriage, or another woman, which makes it a reproach

comparisons.tenor: the town's gossip about the tryst

reading: The speaker asks the man to tell her, and not hide it, who the woman is that he longs for and lives for, while the great swarm of dark-winged bees crowds the cool fragrant garland of rich-branched kongu.
nuance: The bee-swarmed garland can be the man's gift or the woman's ornament; either way the bees give away where it has been, and the friend's 'do not hide it from us' presses him to own the love openly.

thinai_evidence.note: the kongu garland of the dry season

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai for this decade (முன்னிலைப் பத்து, poems of direct address); the friend asks the man, who comes with a kongu garland swarmed by bees, who the woman is, as if she did not know; the question could also be a wife's suspicion

title: பாலை மக்ட் போக்கிய வழித் தாயிரங்கு பத்து decade 38
theme: Ainkurunuru 371 to 380, Othalanthaiyar's paalai decade of the mother's lament after her daughter's elopement (மகட்போக்கிய வழித் தாய் இரங்கு பத்து): the mother blesses the road, asks if she is remembered, curses the youth's mother and the fate that joined them, weeps over the doll and parrot and the toys left behind, grieves for the friend left alone, and ends saying she was mother only in name.
source_issues: Decade title as printed reads மக்ட் போக்கிய வழித் தாயிரங்கு பத்து; மக்ட் is a misprint for மகட் (மகட்போக்கிய).
374 line 1: நல்லென் றூழ is hard to divide (நல் என்று ஊழ, or a form of நல்லேன்); the reading is marked uncertain.

reading: The mother prays that rain may fall on the high hills where peacocks dance to the warriors' drumming, so that the wasteland her crescent-browed girl has gone through may be pleasant, the girl who made up her mind that this was the path of right.
nuance: The mother does not blame the girl: she grants that the daughter judged the going to be அறநெறி, the right way, and turns her grief into a wish for rain on the road. The peacocks dancing to a drum are the hill country's festivity imported into a paalai wish.

thinai_evidence.note: the girl has gone through the wasteland with her lover

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (மகட்போக்கிய வழித் தாய் இரங்கு பத்து) names the mother lamenting after her daughter's elopement; she speaks a wish for the road, to no one named

reading: The mother asks whether her daughter, who crossed many rich hills with the youth of oaths who won her heart, while gossip rose in the noisy old town, thinks even of her.
nuance: என்னும் asks only for the least: not that the girl grieve, but that she remember her mother at all. The youth is named by his வஞ்சினம், the sworn word that persuaded the girl, so the mother places the cause of the going in speech.

thinai_evidence.note: the daughter has crossed the hills with the youth

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (மகட்போக்கிய வழித் தாய் இரங்கு பத்து) names the mother lamenting after her daughter's elopement; the question is spoken aloud to no one named

reading: The mother wishes on the mother of the strong-bowed youth who led her daughter into the hot wasteland, where an old forked-horned stag that escaped a tiger's grip calls in its male voice for its doe to come to it, a grief that makes her weep each time she thinks of it.
nuance: The curse asks the other mother to suffer exactly what the speaker suffers (நினைத்தொறும் கலிழும்), so it is grief demanding a mirror rather than plain hatred. The stag that has just escaped death and at once calls its doe is the danger and the pull of the road in one image.

thinai_evidence.note: the youth has led the daughter into the hot waste

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (மகட்போக்கிய வழித் தாய் இரங்கு பத்து) names the mother lamenting after her daughter's elopement; the curse names the youth's mother in the third person

iraicchi.act: the stag, just escaped from the tiger, calls its doe with its male voice to come and join it
iraicchi.sense: the youth's call drew the daughter into the same danger, so the mother sees on the road the very call that took her girl

reading: The mother, turning it over many times, says that her girl, whose hair is not yet long enough to be gathered into a knot, has crossed, guarded by the youth of fierce strength, a forest that even the male monkey does not know.
nuance: Hair too short for the knot (முடியகம் புகாக் கூந்தல்) is the mother's proof that the girl is still a child. Line 1's நல்லென் றூழ is hard to divide: it may be நல் என்று ஊழ (fate called good) or a self-description, so whether the mother consoles herself or despairs is open.

title: பாலை மறுதரவுப் பத்து decade 40
theme: Ainkurunuru 391 to 400, Othalanthaiyar's paalai decade of the return (மறுதரவுப் பத்து): the household bribes the crow to caw the eloped girl home, asks the mother whether her daughter has come, says that the loveless right has shown grace; the man brings the girl through the burnt wasteland to his hill country, decks her hair and enters his town with her as an evening guest; she sends word to her companions; the mother blesses the road, proposes to divide the rites with the youth's house, and the message comes that the couple arrive today.
source_issues: 393 line 2: அண்கணாட்டி is a rare word whose sense is not fixed; read here as a name for the mother (the one addressed), and the verse is marked uncertain.
397 line 4: விரந்தநீர் is read as விரைந்த நீர் (you who hasten); the form may be a scribal variant.
Every colophon thurai in this decade is null; speakers in thurai_akam are inferred from the poems and the decade's title.

reading: The speaker promises the small black crow of flawless feathers a meal of raw flesh and fresh fat, served in a gold-worked bowl for it to share with its loving kin, if it will caw so that the girl of the few lovely tresses comes home with the youth of the fierce, victorious spear.
nuance: The crow's cawing was the household's sign that a guest was on the way; here the reward is offered before the sign, so the meal is a bribe to the omen rather than thanks for it. Promising a gold bowl to a crow measures the household's longing.

nuance: The tree and creeper repeat the couple in the season's own figures, the warrior-like tree held by the woman-like creeper, but the similes are stated with அன்ன, so the scene is open comparison, not ullurai. அரும்பதம் கொண்ட பெரும்பத வேனில் is hard to fix: a summer that holds rare food in plenty, or a summer of great heat.

title: முல்லை செவிலி கூற்றுப் பத்து decade 41
theme: Ainkurunuru 401 to 410, Peyanar's mullai decade of the foster mother's words (செவிலி கூற்றுப் பத்து): visiting the married daughter's house, the foster mother reports the couple lying with their son between them like a deer family, the father's embrace of mother and nursing child, the toddler named for his grandfather, the wife become the lamp of the house, and the evening on the courtyard cot that outdid the bard's lute.
source_issues: 408 line 2: வணுதல் is presumably வாணுதல் (வாள் நுதல், bright brow); line 4: துனிதீர கொள்கைத்தன் presumably துனிதீர் கொள்கைத் தன். Read so.
The colophons of the decade give no thurai; the speaker is taken from the decade title (செவிலி கூற்றுப் பத்து) and the addressee (the mother) from tradition.

reading: The foster mother says that the way the couple lie, their son in the middle like a fawn lying between a stag and his doe, is truly sweet, a thing that neither this earth ringed by the blue sky nor the heaven above could easily come by.
nuance: The sevili sets the bed of the household above both worlds: ஈனும் உம்பரும் (this world and the upper world) together cannot obtain it. The deer family is mullai's own beast, so the simile also places the house in the forest pasture.

thinai_evidence.note: the deer pair of the forest pasture is the vehicle of the poem's one image

reading: She says that the way he lies, full of desire, embracing from behind the mother who holds their son, is sweet like the music bards draw by plucking their strings, and it is seemly as well.
nuance: பண்புமாருடைத்தே adds a judgment of propriety to the pleasure: the foster mother approves the embrace as fitting the married house, not only as sweet. The embraces are nested, son in the mother's arms, mother in the father's.

reading: She says that his heart, already settled on the beloved he joined, has grown great toward their son as well, as he watches the boy who bears the name of his illustrious grandfather practise sweet smiles and pull a little toy chariot with tottering steps.
nuance: தந்தை பெயரன் makes the toddler the carrier of the line: named for the father's father, he continues a house of wide fame, so the sevili's joy is also the household's continuity. Whose heart grows (the husband's, or her own) turns on how தலையும் and அமர்ந்த உள்ளம் are joined.

title: முல்லை கிழவன் பருவம் பாராட்டுப் பத்து decade 42
theme: Ainkurunuru 411 to 420, Peyanar's mullai decade of the hero praising the season (கிழவன் பருவம் பாராட்டுப் பத்து): home again as the rains begin, the hero invites his wife to bathe and play in the flowering scrub, likens the peacocks and the beasts to the two of them, calls youth sweet when spent together, wonders whether she is a woman of the sky, and promises the scrub itself that they will come to see it.
source_issues: The decade's colophon gives no thurai for any poem; the speaker and situation are taken from the decade title கிழவன் பருவம் பாராட்டுப் பத்து.
415 line 4: அவர்ப் புணர்வே puts the beloved in the third person in a poem addressed to மடந்தை; the reading is marked uncertain.
418 line 1: வானம் பாடி is printed as two words and may be the rain-bird வானம்பாடி or the sky singing; marked uncertain.
413 line 4: நாநயத்தகவே is printed run together, apparently நாம் நயத்தகவே.
420 line 1: பொன்னெனமலர்ந்த is printed without word breaks (பொன் என மலர்ந்த).

reading: The hero tells his wife that the full-voiced cloud has scattered its heavy drops and the rains have begun in the lovely scrub, and bids her, the woman of long dark hair, come quickly so they may bathe together in the new water that is falling.
nuance: The first rain that once marked the deadline of his absence is now an invitation to play: the season the waiting wife dreaded is turned, by his return, into a holiday for both.

thinai_evidence.note: the rains beginning in the scrub

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (கிழவன் பருவம் பாராட்டுப் பத்து) names the hero, home again, praising the rainy season

reading: The hero tells his wife that with kaayaa, konrai, water lily and mullai, the thalavam opening its buds and the pidavam in bloom, the scrub has grown lovely and put on an ornament of flowers, and asks her, the woman of large wide eyes, to come quickly and play there.
nuance: The catalogue is of mullai's own rain flowers; the scrub is pictured as a woman who has dressed herself (பூவணி கொண்டன்று), the adornment he once could not give his wife while away. The நெய்தல் here is the lily of the scrub's pools, not a token of the seashore.

comparisons.tenor: the scrub in flower, as a woman adorned

reading: The hero tells his wife that in the cool scrub, fragrant as her own brow, the peacocks dance just as she does and the season of rain has begun, a time for the two of them to delight in.
nuance: The comparison runs backwards: the woman is the standard and the peacock is likened to her (நின்னே போல), and the scrub smells of her brow rather than she of it; the land is read through her.

reading: The hero tells the young woman that this is the season they longed for and that the scrub they kept in mind; youth is sweet if spent together, and sweet indeed now is the union.
nuance: The near and far demonstratives (இதுவே, உதுவே) point at the time and the place as if both had been promised; the season they 'longed for' is the one that ended his absence. nuance: ஏர் in line 2 can be beauty or the plough; with the fields spread level it may be the ploughing of the first rains, which would set the couple's embrace beside the farmers' sowing.

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (கிழவன் பருவம் பாராட்டுப் பத்து) names the hero, home again, praising the rainy season; he speaks of her in the third person (முயங்கினள்), to no one named

reading: In the scrub made lovely to see, where the rain-bird's drought has been ended and the heavy drops have poured without stopping, the hero asks his wife whether she is a woman of the sky, she who held him close against her fine breasts.
nuance: வானம் பாடி can be the rain-calling bird whose thirst is ended, or the sky that 'sang' (thundered) and drove off the drought; the line division decides it. The hero's question makes the embrace of his own wife a wonder, as if no earthly woman could give it.

nuance: Again the humans are the standard (நம்போல்): the couple's bond is what the beasts are measured against. பிரிந்துறல் அறியா, 'not knowing parting', is said of the beasts but speaks for a couple who have just come through a parting.
