207: the colophon thurai reads 4தாய், a stray footnote numeral before தாய்.
212: the colophon thurai has a stray numeral (1நெருங்கிச்) and breaks off without its verb (…நெஞ்சினை நெருங்கிச் with no சொல்லியது).

tamil: ஆண்டு அமைந்து உறைகுநர் அல்லர்- முனா அது
reading: The friend asks the grieving woman why she despairs that gossip has filled the common ground like the sea swelling at full moon off the Pandya's Korkai and that her mother lies sleepless and sighing: the man who crossed the long summer desert, where a male bear sports with his she-bear and their cub on the hill slope, would not settle there even if he were given the rich rice country of the Cholas.
nuance: The friend first repeats the woman's own complaint (lines 1 to 11) and only then answers it, so the gossip and the mother's sighing are given in the woman's voice. The comfort rests on a hyperbole of refusal (not even the Chola land) rather than on a promise of his return date.

thinai_evidence.note: the friend comforts a woman whose man has crossed the summer desert

comparisons.tenor: the gossip that has filled the common ground
the thick fur of the bear cub

iraicchi.act: the male bear stays and sports with his she-bear, whose cub is with them, on the hill slope of the desert road
iraicchi.sense: the man who saw even the bear keep to its mate and young on that road will not stay away from his own woman

reading: The friend tells the lover who leaves after a night meeting that in his hill, where a wounded tusker that beat off a tiger lifts its trunk and sighs among its young she-elephants and the vengai blossoms fly up like a smith's sparks onto the dark bushes, she wonders whether anyone but themselves suffers as they do while he comes at midnight, spear for company, down the dark stony path where thunder splits the hooded snake.
nuance: The question 'are there others besides us?' turns the women's fear for him into pressure to marry: the colophon says she is urging marriage, and the poem does it only by counting the dangers. A traditional reading takes the wounded tusker among its she-elephants as the lover who braves the night to reach the girl; it is left as scene here because only one correspondence (danger overcome) is clear.

colophon.thurai: இரவுக் குறிக்கண் வந்து நீங்கும் தலைமகற்குத் தோழி சொல்லி வரைவு கடாயது.

thinai_evidence.note: a lover comes to the night meeting through the hill path

comparisons.tenor: the vengai blossoms flying up
the vengai blossoms settling on the dark bushes

tamil: யாய் அறிந்து உணர்க' என்னார், தீ வாய்
எனக்கு எளிது ஆகல் இல்' எனக், கழற்கால்
reading: The mother whose daughter has eloped says that she kept silent when the gossiping women told her day after day what the girl was doing, sparing her shame, but the girl feared her mother would know and left with her spear-bearing young man across the hills; may it prove that she was not such a mother, and may she herself be the housewife of the lonely hill hamlet with its nochi hedge who takes the girl in as a passing guest when she arrives safe.
nuance: Her wish is not that the girl come back but that she be the stranger on the road who shelters her: a mother's care transferred to the place the daughter has chosen. Her silence, meant as kindness, is what the daughter read as danger, so the poem turns on a misunderstanding between them.

thinai_evidence.note: the daughter has left with her lover across the desert hills

reading: The man, his work done in the Pandya's great camp, tells his charioteer that the evening of the rains has come over the grassland, with bee swarms humming at the fragrant mullai, so he must drive fast to reach the shoulders of his bright-bangled wife, whose hair smells like the groves of Vaanan's Sirukudi where the reapers' drums scare birds from the flowered pools.
nuance: The season he promised to return in has arrived on its own (உதுக்காண் வந்தன்று பொழுதே), so his haste is the keeping of a word. The camp opens with the king's world-shading umbrella and sea-like army; the close sets that public scene against a farming village's fragrance in his wife's hair.

thinai_evidence.note: the rains, the grassland and the jasmine evening of return

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the addressee is the charioteer (பாகன்)

comparisons.tenor: the Pandya's army
the fragrance of the wife's hair

reading: The woman tells the friend who urges her to bear up that her lover, who swore with a lying heart that he would never leave her, like those joined in an old flawless friendship of mingled lives, has gone and left her weeping; even so, may he easily gain wealth enough to feed guests in a house as rich as Killi's Kaveri port, as he crosses the hill path of strange speech in the cool season where an elephant's musth runs and the male monkey calls and leaps on the high branch.
nuance: The reproach and the blessing come in one breath: she names his oath a lie and still wishes his errand success, and what she wishes him is wealth for hospitality, the householder's duty, not riches for himself.

thinai_evidence.note: he has left her to cross the desert for wealth

comparisons.vehicle: உயிர்கலந்து ஒன்றிய தொன்றுபடு நட்பின் செயிர்தீர் நெஞ்சமொடு செறிந்தோர்
comparisons.tenor: the lover as he spoke his promise
the rich house she wishes him
the vengai blossoms falling

reading: The woman, refusing the go-between, asks her friend what this will be called: the lord of a town where small boys climb the dark back of a buffalo whose twisted horns spread as ludicrously as a dancer's gestures, looking from afar like monkeys on a boulder, delights in marrying women with mango-sprout skin in his festive city, and sulking at it her broad soft shoulders have melted like the salt heaps of Veerai in heavy rain.
nuance: The mockery is in the image: the great buffalo carries boys about like a toy and looks absurd, and so does he, ridden by every woman. Her own body, not her words, gives the refusal its force: the shoulders that waste like rained-on salt.

colophon.thurai: வாயில் வேண்டிச் சென்றவிறலிக்குத் தலைமகள் வாயில் மறுத்து.

reading: The mother whose daughter eloped wonders whether the girl, who refused with a sick heart the sweet milk mixed with honey that her mother held out while combing her hair and coaxing her, has drunk, sighing and with sweat on her crescent brow, the brackish pot of water her heartless lover drew from a well dug where a sun-scorched tusker had rolled, on the dread forked desert path cut by the hooves of the salt traders' grey donkeys.
nuance: The road is built from the salt trade, carried from the sea to the western uplands, so the desert here is a merchant road, not wild land. The poem's last image is of the girl at home refusing milk, so the mother's question about the well water is also about the comfort she failed to give.

thinai_evidence.note: the scorched desert road the girl has taken

comparisons.tenor: salt

reading: The lover, leaving after their meeting, blesses the girl of fine dark hair, fragrant as the flowers of Ori's Kolli, who came and gave herself with a desire that shame could not hold back, like a flood the salt-pan bank cannot stop and like Akuthai who brought back the kin after the outcry of the Vel women when Aay Eyinan fell to Minjili at Paazhi and Nannan would not look on the field.
nuance: Most of the poem is a puram story told inside a single simile: Eyinan the generous, killed at noon, the birds that should have shaded him, Nannan's refusal to see. What it measures is the girl's boldness, a thing usually blamed in akam, here blessed. Line 18 (அகுதை கிளைதந்தாங்கு) is obscure, and the turn of the Nannan episode is uncertain.

thinai_evidence.note: the hero rejoices after a secret union

comparisons.vehicle: வசைவிடக் கடக்கும் வயங்குபெருந் தானை அகுதை கிளைதந் தாங்கு
comparisons.tenor: her coming to him
her desire that shame could not hold
the fragrance of her hair

reading: The friend tells the woman not to weep that her shoulders have lost their beauty, her mother grieves and the gossip is louder than the roar at Alankanam when Chezhiyan beat the seven: though her man has gone beyond Pulli's Vengadam, he cannot forget her beauty, which is like the statue set up by the god on Kolli, the hill Kaari of Mullur gave to the Cheras after killing Ori.
nuance: The friend first speaks the woman's complaint in her own words and then answers it, as in 201. Both measures in the poem come from puram: a Pandya victory for the gossip, a Kolli statue that outlived the change of its lords for her beauty, which is the friend's point: his love will last as the statue did.

thinai_evidence.note: he has crossed the rocky land beyond Vengadam

comparisons.tenor: the gossip about her
Chezhiyan's shoulders

comparisons.vehicle: கொல்லி நிலைபெறு கடவுள் ஆக்கிய பலர்புகழ் பாவை
comparisons.tenor: her beauty

reading: The friend, knowing the lover stands by unseen, tells the woman that the lord of the shore, where a great fish struck by the fishermen's harpoon stains the sea with its blood, arcs through the waves like a rainbow and follows the boats with its strength gone, once came at midnight thinking of her shoulders and praised their seaside grove endlessly, and now, they hear, says the screw-pine thickets block his chariot and the way is hard.
nuance: The friend sets his first praise of their shore against his present excuse about the same shore, and lets him overhear the comparison. The wounded fish that still follows the boats is sometimes read as a hidden image of a lover hurt yet clinging; it is left as scene because its matching to the people is not fixed by the poem.

thinai_evidence.note: fishermen, the seaside grove and screw-pine

comparisons.tenor: the wounded fish arcing through the waves

reading: The friend, seeing the woman changed, tells her that though her man is in the land of strange speech beyond Vengadam, where a tusker rubbing against the maraam scatters its lime-white blossoms like hail onto the rock where farmers dry their rice seed, he will be kind and return, he who left her weeping with gossip roaring like the water at Mathi's stony ford, where Ezhini's teeth were set into the gate of Venmani.
nuance: The gossip is again measured by a war story, here a grim trophy: a fallen raider's teeth driven into a fortress door. Lines 9 to 15 compress the Ezhini episode so tightly that its sequence (the cattle, the outcry, the king's command) cannot be fixed.

thinai_evidence.note: he has gone to a far land leaving her in tears

the falling blossoms
the great gossip

reading: The lover, after a meeting that failed, curses his heart: desiring a girl whose beauty is like a golden statue holding the young sunlight, whose teeth are like the shoots of reed tubers in sand and whose speech is like the music of a lute played in sevvazhi, it never thought she was hard to win and crossed the bitter waste every day, bringing him endless pain; may its keen pride be broken as the sea was when Kuttuvan's tempered spear drove it back.
nuance: The curse runs through a puram image, the Chera who besieged the ocean itself; the heart's pride is set against the sea's, and both are pierced. Line 9 (the water troubled by the elephant herd) is unclear in its connection.

thinai_evidence.note: the lover's longing for a girl who is hard to meet

comparisons.vehicle: தாஇல் நன்பொன் தைஇய பாவை விண்தவழ் இளவெயிற் கொண்டுநின் றன்ன
comparisons.tenor: her beauty

comparisons.vehicle: நாணற் கிழங்கு மணற்கு ஈன்ற முளைஓ ரன்ன
comparisons.tenor: her teeth
her sweet speech
Kuttuvan's rage
Kuttuvan's army

reading: The friend tells the woman that though her man chose to cross the shadeless waterless waste beyond the Tondaiyar's Vengadam, into the land of the Vadugar who wear wilted athiral in their curly hair and offer toddy to the cattle they raid, he will not linger there even if he were given the world of the worthy together with its nectar, forgetting to join her shoulders like the bamboo of Kolli and her hair rippled like Kaveri sand.
nuance: The friend's hyperbole goes past any kingdom to heaven itself: not even the gods' world and its nectar outweighs the woman's embrace. The road is drawn from its people, a raiding folk with their own rites, which makes the distance cultural as well as physical.

thinai_evidence.note: the waterless, shadeless desert he crossed

comparisons.tenor: the gems shining in the field
her shoulders
her rippled hair

reading: In the war camp, where the rain pours ceaselessly from a sky that has hidden the day, chilling the elephant herds, and the king, eager for glory, does not sleep, the man tells his heart that the war is their duty, and asks how she of thick hair, who knew him as her own, will fare as she hears alone in the rainy evening the sad sevvazhi lute and the flute of cowherds driving home cattle with bells.
nuance: The colophon gives the speech to the woman, but the speaker is in the camp and says the war is ours (அமரும் நம்வயினதுவே), so it can only be the man; he imagines her evening, not his own. The music that wounds her is his invention, placed in her hearing.

thinai_evidence.note: the rains, the evening and the cowherds of the waiting season

reading: The friend tells the man, who stands ready with spear in hand to cross the hills for work in a land of other tongues, that wishing him a swift and successful going would be well enough for those who could bear to stay behind grieving for the absent, on a road where bowmen who bite the finger that missed its mark raise dread stone heaps over men they kill and a red-beaked male vulture picks the eyes from the heads of corpses and drops them for his mate.
nuance: The blessing is withheld by a conditional: it would be fine to say 'go well', but only to someone able to stay behind, which the woman is not. The vulture feeding its mate is the poem's sharpest stroke: on a road of killing, even the carrion bird provides for its partner without leaving her.

colophon.thurai: செலவுணர்த்திய தோழி தலைமகள் குறிப்பறிந்து தலைமகனைச் செலவழுங்குவித்தது.

thinai_evidence.note: the robbers' road of stone heaps and vultures

iraicchi.act: the male vulture gathers what it finds on the killing ground and brings it to its mate
iraicchi.sense: even the vulture of that road provides for its mate without leaving her, so the man need not part from his wife to provide

reading: The courtesan, speaking so that the wife's women will hear, says the wives of the lord of the cool-ford town, where a bard's daughter fishes with a fine rod and roasts the varaal on vanji wood for her toddy-drinking father, are said to talk of her as they please; if she is caught in that gossip, so be it, but if she goes to their street they will suffer like the great tusker when the Chelli lord's white spear struck Aathan Ezhini's chest.
nuance: Her threat is to visit, not to fight; she makes her mere presence in their street a wound. The simile's referents are uncertain: whether the suffering tusker is Ezhini's own elephant or Ezhini himself called a tusker cannot be settled from the line.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகட்குப் பாங்காயினார் கேட்பத் தனக்குப் பாங்காயினார்க்குப் பரத்தை சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: the courtesan's quarrel with the wives of the town's lord

comparisons.tenor: the wives' suffering

reading: Told of the coming parting, the woman says that now the cold season has come, with white rain-clouds like carded cotton, cane flowers swaying, pakandrai blooming white, avarai and thondri opening, herons crying in every field and women at the ford shivering without their ornaments, she will proclaim to every couple 'whatever wealth you gain, do not part', for her body is ruined by the lover who took her beauty and left, and she shivers in the hard cold with chattering teeth.
nuance: Her answer to news of his going is a public maxim addressed to all lovers, made from her own case. The long catalogue of the cold season is not decoration: every flower and bird marks the time he should be home, and the women shivering at the ford are a picture of her own state.

thinai_evidence.note: the threatened parting is what she answers

comparisons.tenor: the white rain-clouds
the white pakandrai blossoms
her breaking heart

tamil: படாஅ வாகும், எம் கண் என, நீயும்
reading: The friend tells the lover, who said his eyes would not close except on her shoulders on nights when the storm cloud flashes and thunders over the peaks, after the tusker has fed sprouts and fodder to his herd, and who thinks it easy to come at midnight through the mountain clefts where the tiger waits for travellers, that if they cannot embrace his chest even one day they too will waste; let mother know and the old town gossip: let him come by day to the cool slope where vengai and thondri smell sweet.
nuance: Moving the meeting to daytime is a dare: the friend accepts the risk of discovery (let mother know, let the town hear) rather than his risk on the night path, which forces the matter toward marriage. She quotes his own lover's oath back to him before setting her terms.

colophon.thurai: தோழி தலைமகளை இடத்துய்த்து வந்து பகற்குறிநேர்ந்த வாய் பாட்டால் தலைமகனை வரைவுகடாயது.

thinai_evidence.note: the friend arranges a day meeting for the lovers

comparisons.tenor: the lightning
the red thondri blossoms

iraicchi.act: the tusker who cherishes his herd feeds them sprouts and the fodder they want
iraicchi.sense: as the tusker openly provides for his own, the lover should take up the care of the girl in marriage rather than steal visits by night

reading: The mother whose daughter has gone grieves that the girl who ran ringing her anklets through their great house and played ball with her friends, whom she fed from a bowl of milk like a white pakandrai flower brimming with dew ('drink your father's share too'), and adorned from birth, has gone with a heartless man; she cannot forget and wonders whether the girl walks, wasting, the long waterless road where a stag flees the red dog and the hot wind in the dry vila pods sounds to cowherds like a flute.
nuance: The feeding scene is told in the mother's own coaxing words, which makes the loss concrete: the voice that coaxed is still speaking, with no child to hear it. The flute that the cowherds imagine in the wind is the road's one sound of home, and it is false.

thinai_evidence.note: the waterless road and the hot wind

comparisons.tenor: the bowl of milk
the red dog's teeth
the wind in the dry vila pods

reading: The friend, meeting the lover as he leaves the night tryst, tells him that while gossip rises in town and street he goes about in his chariot and speaks humbly, shivering whenever he thinks of her body, unapproachable as the guarded pillar of the sacrifice the axe-bearing tall one completed at Chellur; he stands outside and suffers, and should instead, like the great bird at Oonur by the sea, settle in a steady union and speak the words that protect her beauty, so that they may be at ease.
nuance: The sacrificial pillar roped at its waist, which none may approach, makes the girl's guarded state a sacred enclosure that only a public rite can open: the friend is asking for marriage. Several phrases (நோலா இரும்புள், the whole of lines 10 to 21) are obscure and the reading is tentative.

colophon.thurai: இரவுக்குறிவந்து நீங்குச் தலைமகனை யெதிர்ப்பட்டுத் தோழி சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: the sea tide, backwaters and shore grove

comparisons.tenor: her unapproachable body
the steady union the lover should enter

title: மணிமிடைபவளம் 221-240
theme: Akananuru 221 to 240, from the மணிமிடைபவளம் section: half the poems are paalai partings and comforts in which the friend argues from memory, glory or the lover's body that the man will return, set among kurinji night-tryst poems pressing for marriage, two mullai homecomings, two marutham reproaches and two neythal meetings, with puram fame (Kazhar, Uranthai, Unur, Uthiyan Cheral's feast, Nalli) used repeatedly as a scale of comparison.
source_issues: akananuru:224: line 13 reads குரலிசைப் கடுப்ப; the doubled ப் before க is not regular sandhi and is probably a misprint for குரலிசை கடுப்ப.
akananuru:225: the flag reports 17 lines in our base text against 18 in the commentary edition (pmuni0523_02); the poem reads complete as it stands, but the lineation differs.
akananuru:230: lineation flag: a printed line number 5 stands on line 10 of the base text.
akananuru:234: the colophon thurai has தலைமமகன், a doubled ம, for தலைமகன்; copied as is in `colophon`.
akananuru:236: line 5 இடைனில is probably இடைநில, and line 10 உய்ர்த்தனென் is probably உயிர்த்தனென்.
akananuru:238: line 10 பெருகல் நாட is probably பெருங்கல் நாட, the usual epithet of the hill lord.

reading: The friend tells the girl that, since their people have begun the wedding rites with toddy and heaped sand, she has arranged for her to leave with the dark-bearded young man of the new spear, who will crown her hair with kadamba blossoms, along the hard forest track where a tiger that missed its elephant roars and the she-elephant bolts.
nuance: The poem never says whom the kin mean to marry her to; that the wedding is not to her lover is the colophon's reading (போக்குடன்பட), and it is what makes the friend's arrangement urgent. The kadamba spray the young man will pick for her hair is a small wedding of their own set against the kin's wedding at home.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகற்குப் போக்குடன்பட்ட தோழி, தலைமகட்குப் போக்குடன்படச் சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: the girl is to leave home with her lover over the dry track, the parting of udanpokku

reading: With the hill lord listening, the friend says that since the sickness he caused is wasting her beauty she will speak out: let us go, along the river cold with many nights of thunder and rain, to win a fame like Maruthi's, who showed Aathi Manthi her lover taken by the Kaveri at the Kazhar festival and then went into the sea.
nuance: The friend borrows a known story of love and drowning to hint at a desperate act; aimed at the overhearing hero, the hint presses him to marry rather than keep coming by the flooded night path. The Maruthi part of the legend is told only here in this chapter; poem 236 uses the same story from Manthi's side.

thinai_evidence.note: the great hill of the hero's country and the night rain on his path

comparisons.tenor: the fame the friend hopes the two of them will win

reading: The friend tells the grieving girl not to fear that the man who could leave her will forget her: though he has crossed the long shadeless waterless track where wind-tossed flame-of-the-forest pods curved like a boar's tusk blaze like a fire-spouting elephant, how could he sleep forgetting the sleep he found in her garlanded hair?
nuance: The comfort rests on his memory of her hair, which he once gathered over her shoulders and decked with athiral and kuvalai; the friend argues from the body's habit, not from his promise.

thinai_evidence.note: the shadeless, waterless long track he has crossed

comparisons.tenor: the long curved pods of the flame-of-the-forest
the wind-lifted mass of red murukku blossom
her curling dark hair

reading: The hero, his task done, tells his charioteer to drive on as the day ends, horses breathing hot as a smith's bellows and flecked with milk-white froth, the wheel cutting the sand with the sound of a housewife's quern, while he pictures his wife pushing back her bangles and looking again and again toward the gate, asking whether he is coming.
nuance: The two domestic similes, the smith's bellows and the quern turned by a housewife, bring the home into the journey before he reaches it; the wife he imagines speaks only one line, and it is a question.

thinai_evidence.note: a wife waits at home for the returning husband, in the woodland after the heat has gone

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the addressee is the charioteer (பாகன்)

comparisons.tenor: the horses' hot breath
the horses' speed
the white froth on the horses
the fine flecks of froth
the sound of the wheel in the sand

reading: The hero asks his heart whether, after being one with her today in love, innocence and gentle speech, they will lodge tomorrow in a rainless hamlet on the hard track, where wind through bee-bored bamboo sounds like a herdsman's flute and iruppai flowers drop like loosened pearls, thinking of her anguished look and her sulking.
nuance: Today and tomorrow (இன்றே, நாளை) frame the poem: the whole journey is imagined from inside the embrace. The music of the bamboo is the one soft thing on the track, and it belongs to the herders' land, not the desert.

thinai_evidence.note: the hard track and the hamlet the rain has forgotten

comparisons.tenor: the wind sounding through the bored bamboo
the clustered iruppai blossoms
the iruppai flowers falling on the red ground
her dark hair

reading: The friend refuses the lord of the rich town his tricks: his bathing yesterday in the Kaveri's dawn flood at Matthi's Kazhar ford with the woman he desires has raised more uproar than the shout when Katti fled without a fight on hearing the kinai drum at Thithan Veliyan's court in Uranthai.
nuance: The scale is the joke: a private bathe is measured against a famous rout, and the hero is mocked by being set beside a king who ran. The women scaring herons with sedge in the karanthai fields are the town's ordinary life, which has now seen him.

thinai_evidence.note: the husband's bathing with another woman, the sulking of the marutham house

comparisons.tenor: the gossip about his bathing

reading: The friend tells the girl to stop brooding over her pale forehead and slack shoulders: though he has crossed many tracks where a lone tusker in musth tears at a vengai and roars like warriors taking a field, may our lover stay well, he who left with a clamour like the bright market of Marungur beyond Thazhumban's Unur.
nuance: The friend's blessing, நோய்இலராக, turns comfort into a wish for the absent man. Thazhumban is praised for a drum that brought Tamil under it (தமிழ் அகப்படுத்த), an early use of தமிழ் for a land or people; line 17's பிடிமிதி வழுதுணை is obscure to us.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகன் பிரிவின்கண் வேறுபட்ட தலைமகட்குத் தோழி சொல்லியது. பிரிவின்கண் வேறுபட்ட தோழிக்குத் தலைமகள் சொல்லியதூஉமாம்.

thinai_evidence.note: the red-dust tracks the tusker roams

occasion.words: தலைமகன் பிரிவின்கண் வேறுபட்ட தலைமகட்குத் தோழி சொல்லியது

comparisons.tenor: the roaring tusker
the vengai's blossom
the clamour of his departure

reading: With the hero listening, the friend says it would be well enough if he spent the days with them bathing in the kuvalai pool under the cold slope, and went home at night; but on the moonlit path to his hamlet the vengai blossoms look like a tiger's spots and the she-elephant bolts.
nuance: The danger is an illusion of moonlight, yet the friend uses it to turn him from night meetings to day ones, and in the end toward marriage. The she-elephant fleeing a flowering tree it takes for a tiger is a traditional candidate for a hidden sense (the girl's fears for him); it does not pass the act condition here, so it stays scene.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகன் சிறைப்புறத்தானாகத் தலைமகட்குச் சொல்லுவாளாய்த் தோழி சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: the cold hill slope and the moonlit night

occasion.words: தலைமகன் சிறைப்புறத்தானாகத் தலைமகட்குச் சொல்லுவாளாய்த் தோழி சொல்லியது

comparisons.tenor: the opened kuvalai
the moonlight
the bright vengai blossoms

reading: The girl answers her friend's comfort: you tell me not to grieve as tears blur my eyes and gold-like pallor spreads, yet he who crossed the far hills of a waterless track where starving she-elephants stand like huts of a deserted village, and promised to come at once, has not come even in the sweet young spring when the cuckoo calls from the mango.
nuance: The spring is the proof: the cuckoo's call marks the season by which he promised to be back, so the beauty of the season is itself the evidence against him. The poem gives his own words, இன்னே வருதும், only to set them against the calendar.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகன் பிரிவின்கண் வேறுபட்ட தலைமகளை வற்புறுத்துந் தோழிக்குத் தலைமகள் வன்புறை யெதிரழிந்து சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: the waterless long track he crossed

occasion.words: தலைமகன் பிரிவின்கண் வேறுபட்ட தலைமகளை வற்புறுத்துந் தோழிக்குத் தலைமகள் வன்புறை யெதிரழிந்து சொல்லியது

comparisons.tenor: the gaunt she-elephants standing together
the pallor on her body

reading: The hero tells his heart how he asked the shore girl in her leaf skirt, gathering punnai pollen like gold with her playmates, whether any harm would come if the right of this house were joined to him, and how, as his chariot drew near, she held back her tears and bowed her head a little, leaving him in great pain.
nuance: Her answer is a gesture, not a word: the bowed head and checked tears can be read as consent or as refusal, and the hero's pain comes from not knowing which. His proposal is couched in the language of household right (மனைக் கிழமை), unusual in a first meeting.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகளைக் கண்ணுற்று நீங்கும் தலைமகன் தன் நெஞ்சிற்குச் சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: the backwater, its neythal flowers and the punnai pollen on the sand

occasion.words: தலைமகளைக் கண்ணுற்று நீங்கும் தலைமகன் தன் நெஞ்சிற்குச் சொல்லியது

comparisons.tenor: the large flowers of her leaf skirt
the punnai pollen she gathers

reading: The friend tells the girl that men who prize fame, holding that crushing foes and helping kin in need are not for those who stay home, have crossed the dreaded track of hunters' victims under stone heaps, yet they will come back with melting hearts, those who lay in her bee-loud hair, which is like the Pandyan's famed Koodal.
nuance: The friend argues with a puram value: glory is earned away from home, so the parting is honourable, and the same honour guarantees the return. The stone heaps over men killed by forest bowmen are the road's reminder of what that glory costs.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகன் பிரிவின்கண் வேறுபட்ட தலைமகட்குத் தோழி சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: the hot track lined with the graves of travellers

occasion.words: தலைமகன் பிரிவின்கண் வேறுபட்ட தலைமகட்குத் தோழி சொல்லியது

comparisons.tenor: her hair, or her as its wearer

reading: With the hero listening, the friend tells the girl that her bond with the lord of the rock country, where an elephant takes midnight thunder for a tiger and flees, has now brought on the season when mother, guarding the house, has the velan come, saying it is Murugu, with mixed flower offerings, in a courtyard strewn with vengai gold like a festival ground where the kuravar women dance.
nuance: The velan's rite shows the secret is close to discovery: the mother reads the girl's lovesickness as Murugu's seizure. The elephant mistaking thunder for a tiger matches the mother mistaking love for possession; we leave it as scene because only one correspondence holds firmly.

colophon.thurai: தோழி, தலைமகன் சிறைப்புறத்தானாகத் தலைமகட்குச் சொல்லுவாளாய்ச் சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: the vengai, the hill people and their kuravai dance

comparisons.tenor: the vengai's buds
the flower-strewn courtyard

reading: The friend tells the weeping girl that though he has crossed a summer track of fire-blackened land where lean elephants languish and short and tall hills crowd together like the host of ghouls gathered at Uthiyan Cheral's great feast, he will not linger over wealth, forgetting the sweet sleep of her dark hair.
nuance: The Cheral's great feast, a puram fame, is turned into a picture of the landscape: the hills crowd like the ghoulish guests. The friend's assurance turns on the same memory of sleep in her hair that poem 223 uses.

thinai_evidence.note: summer, and the track where the rain has gone

comparisons.tenor: the short and tall hills crowded together

reading: The hero tells his charioteer to drive the swan-swift horses fast over the rain-washed sand, so that by dusk, when the doe frolics with the stag and bees hum at the mullai, he may reach the pleasant woodland town where his pale, tear-eyed wife can at last undo her braid.
nuance: The braid is a sign: she bound her hair at his leaving and will loosen it at his return, so his speed is measured by her hair. The doe at play with the stag is what the arrival will be.

thinai_evidence.note: the rains, the evening and the mullai flower

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the addressee is the charioteer (பாகன்)

comparisons.tenor: the swift horses
the speeding chariot
her hair

iraicchi.act: the young doe, tired of browsing, frolics unharmed in the joy of joining the stag
iraicchi.sense: the wife's release at his return will be as glad and as safe as the doe's play with her mate

reading: The girl asks her friend whether, set on wealth, he has not thought of them, or thinking has forgotten for his greater work, while the cold north wind and the drizzling east cloud open the thonri like a lamp and the musundai like stars on the grass, the crab hides in its hole, and the graceless wind torments her at evening, he who never asked what would become of her, pale and wasted.
nuance: The season is the rains and the cold wind, and the torment is the evening: by the Tholkappiyam's times this is mullai waiting, though the colophon files the poem as paalai because he went for wealth.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகன் பிரிவின்கண் வேறுபட்ட தலைமகள் ஆற்றாமைமீதூரத் தோழிக்குச் சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: a woman waits through the rains and suffers the evening; she is not on the road

comparisons.tenor: the opening thonri bud
the white musundai flowers on the grass
the wet bending sugarcane flowers

reading: The girl tells her friend that, not knowing how great the town lord's love was, she suffered: last night, not knowing he lay among bejewelled women, she went about with a broken heart telling her trouble, like Aathi Manthi who lost her lover and asked land after land whether anyone had seen Attan Atthi, crying that the sea had taken him, the flood had hidden him.
nuance: The phrase about the greatness of his love is bitter: the love she did not know was his love for others. She casts herself as the tragic Manthi while he was safe among other women, and the gap between the legend and his conduct is the reproach.

title: மணிமிடைபவளம் 241-260
theme: Akananuru 241 to 260, in the மணிமிடைபவளம் section: paalai poems of women left for wealth and of friends who answer them with the man's memory of their bodies, two elopement poems, kurinji night trysts threatened by the mother's watch and the velan's rite, mullai homecomings by chariot, and marutham refusals in which the friend measures the husband's scandal by public shouts at Venni, Kudal and Kallur. Puram history runs through the roads: Karikal, the Pandyan, the Kosar, the Moriyar, Nanda's treasure, Nannan's Paazhi.

akananuru:242: line 19 has சிறுயிலைச் for the regular சிறியிலைச் / சிற்றிலைச், probably a misprint.

reading: The woman tells her friend that, whatever kind words the friend says of the man's untiring, quarrel-free love, he who once never left her side was hers only once: he has crossed the hills where bamboo shoots shrivel, the rains have forgotten the land and the falls have run dry, where a lone old stag that ran after the white mirage taking it for rain lies spent in the hot forest, and where a red-faced she-monkey plays with fallen nelli fruit scattered like round play-pebbles.
nuance: The single particle மன் in நமர்மன் carries the poem: he was ours, once. The stag fooled by the mirage (பேஎய் வெண்தேர்ப் பெயல்செத்து) is left as scene, since it does nothing a person of the situation does; a reader may still hear in it the woman's own hope, chasing comfort that the friend's words hold out.

nuance: The deadline is exact: மறி உயிர் வழங்கா அளவை, before the kid is slain. The diviner is called அறியா வேலன், the one who does not know, so the rite is mocked even as it threatens to expose the secret. Spoken for the man's ears, the poem presses him to marry.

reading: The woman tells her friend that the merciless north wind has come and settled, now that the avarai flowers fall, eengai blooms like red coral, pagandrai opens around the town, the new rains have stopped and the paddy hangs in ripe ears; if they could make him know their lonely state, which is past their bearing, it would be well, but now, with streaming eyes, the pain is theirs alone, and such is the fruit of their old deeds.
nuance: She ends not with blame but with தொல்வினைப் பயன், the fruit of former deeds, a word the later ethics books make doctrine; here it explains nothing away and comforts no one. The wind is கண்இல், eyeless or pitiless, the only one who has come.

reading: The man rebukes his heart, which has driven him toward wealth: if it knows well that she has the strength to hold the house, telling herself he went with good intent to bring wealth dearer than life, then let it go alone through the rainless bamboo tracks where bandit chiefs who live by robbing caravans pledge a wild elephant's tusk for toddy and stroke a child's head in the frontier hamlet, past flame-red ilavam flowers humming with bees and white bones that feed the camel's hunger; as for him, he will not come.

reading: The woman tells her friend that the man who left her pearl-strung breast lonely has no grace: set on wealth, he did not think how hard the forest is, where the fiery-mouthed male bear with its clan, tired of white iruppai blossom, digs at the top of a red anthill, where a killer elephant watches the waste frontier for men, and where flocks of long-necked vultures, hungry for carrion, roost on the high peaks he crossed.

reading: With the man listening outside, the friend tells the woman a joke: last night, after a hunter spared a boar that had killed his hound and stood guarding its young in a narrow pass because it looked like his own chief holding the path while his army fell back, the hill lord came to the house, his garland torn by the thicket and swinging on his shoulders like the rope on a bull's hump, and their mother saw him, looked straight at my face, said 'you are a fine one!' and went off laughing.
nuance: The joke is a warning. The mother has seen the man at the door and chosen, for now, to laugh, as the hunter saw the boar and chose not to shoot; the next sight may not end so lightly, so the man should stop coming by night and ask for her.

colophon.thurai: இரவுக்குறிச் சிறைப்புறமாகத் தலைமகட்குச் சொல்லுவாளாய்த் தலைமகன் கேட்பத் தோழி சொல்லியது.

reading: The woman asks her friend what the town's long gossip is for, when her young beauty, fine as Vembi, town of Musundai of many spears who daily gives bards gold-horned bulls, garlands, heaps of food, chariots and elephants, is wasting and he shows no grace, having crossed the bamboo hills where Mazhavar in peacock-feather garlands kill a young cow and eat its roast flesh, and the dusty summer wind over that place sounds so like a hungry tiger's roar that the deer herds scatter on every path.
nuance: The gossip is idle because there is nothing left to gossip about: the beauty it talks of is already going. Her beauty is measured by a patron's giving, so her worth is set on the scale of puram generosity.

reading: The friend asks the woman what has happened: while they played with their companions on the fragrant dune under the wave-beaten punnai, a man with garland and chaplet left his chariot with his young men, came close praising their sand-house, got no word in reply and went away; since then he has wasted with longing, the fishing hamlet's women talk, and even the shore stays awake at night with us whose bangles slip.

reading: The friend tells the woman that the messages have gone, her shoulders will fill out and her pallor fade, for if he hears of their grief he will not stay there even for Nanda's treasure, he who loosened her bangles and went the long way past the rock-cut road the Moriyar's wheels rolled through when they came against Mokur that would not submit, after the Kosar of wind-swift chariots had broken the enemy at the hall of the old banyan, into the teak groves where a tiger that escaped the elephant's tusk lies unguarded.
nuance: Mamulanar's long relative clause runs history into the road: the Kosar's victory, Mokur's refusal, the northern Moriyar cutting a road for their chariots. The man's path is laid down by empires, and the friend still bets that the woman's grief outweighs Nanda's gold.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகன் பிரிவின்கண் வேறுபட்ட தலைமகளது வேறுபாடு கண்டு தோழி சொல்லியது.

reading: With the man listening outside, the woman tells her friend that he is not afraid to come alone with one spear down the hill slope where the yali, making the tiger tremble, strikes an elephant's spotted brow and tears out its tusk, but she cannot bear to stay alone with streaming eyes; shall they make some plan, for their strict mother has forgotten sleep like the watchman of a great tank at midnight when the rain has poured and scattered the eengai blossom.
nuance: Two kinds of courage face each other: his on the beast-haunted path, hers that fails at home. The mother as a sleepless tank-keeper is a sharp image: she guards the girl as one guards water that may break its banks.

reading: As they elope, the man tells the woman that, on these summer days when the paathiri blossom wilts, he gathers her full hair, decks it with maraa flowers, and she cannot keep the bees off her honeyed hair, yet she walks well, swinging her bamboo-smooth arms with bangles ringing, on the way through the hills where robbers climb the forked yaa tree to watch the roads, where the fibre an elephant chewed for water serves the salt-merchants as kindling, and where a young bear pulls a white snake out of an anthill.

thinai_evidence.note: the lovers leave together through the waste

reading: The man, whose night tryst failed, tells his heart that though it knew she was as hard to reach as the gold the ancient Velir kept in Nannan Uthiyan's guarded Paazhi, it would not accept it; let it perish like a stone falling into a dark cave on the windy hill, for longing for her it came every night by the narrow, snake-haunted path and did not get her, and now, its face dull, it has made itself a laughing-stock to all the world and brought on unending pain.
nuance: The colophon's அல்லகுறி is the night signal that turned out false, and the poem is the man's anger at himself, not at her. Paazhi's buried gold is the measure of her guardedness, a puram treasure-story turned into a picture of a girl beyond reach.

thinai_evidence.note: the night journey to a tryst on the hill

comparisons.tenor: the girl, as hard to reach as the gold of Paazhi
the heart, told to perish like a stone falling into a dark cave

reading: The friend tells the woman, whose elopement is agreed, that the spears gleam, the young men are ready, garlands and leaf-skirts are made, rain has ended the earth's heat and the trees put out new leaves, the groves look roofed with flowers, the forest is at its best, and the message has come on this evening of milk-white moonlight; so with a steady mind let her take her word: even if the terrace dries and the vayalai and nochchi she tended wither, bearing the grief of the mother who, more innocent than she, loved her so, and facing her brothers' tiger-like pride, let her be strong and hold him to her breast still.
nuance: The friend turns the paalai land green for the journey: the season itself has been arranged in the lovers' favour. The withering vayalai and nochchi are the girl's own garden plants, the home she leaves untended. Who bears the mother's grief (அன்னை அல்லல் தாங்கி) is not stated; we read it as the girl, and the closing wish (வலியாய் இன்னும் தோய்க, நின் முலையே) is terse, so the sense is uncertain.

thinai_evidence.note: the friend urges the girl to leave with the man

comparisons.tenor: the groves, as if roofed with flowers
the moonlight, spreading like milk
the brothers' pride, like a tiger's

reading: With the man listening outside, prompted by her friend, the woman says that as the sun dims, the hills glow, the bees dive into flowers, herons cry on the kandal shore, the crab slips into its hole, the waves fall quiet, the boats stop work, the sky reddens, the paired anril settles in the palmyra's inner frond, the backwater flowers close and the punnai blossom loses its gold, and the day drains away, she wonders what will become of her, she who still longs for the loveless man's mind, at midnight when the old owl hoots and ghosts walk.
nuance: Ten clauses of closing (each thing withdraws to its place) end in the one who has no place to go. Spoken for the man's ears, the paired anril in its nest is the reproach the woman will not make aloud.

colophon.thurai: இரவுக் குறிக்கண் தலைமகன் சிறைப்புறமாகத் தோழியாற் சொல்லெடுக்கப்பட்டுத் தலைமகள் சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: the shore at sunset

iraicchi.act: the paired anril birds settle together in the palmyra's inner frond at nightfall
iraicchi.sense: even the birds are with their mates at dark, while the man leaves her waiting alone through the night

title: மணிமிடைபவளம் 261-280
theme: Akananuru 261 to 280, in the anthology's fixed order of lands: paalai roads seen from both ends of an elopement (the man recalling her shyness, two mothers at the empty house), wives counting seasons and refusing to blame the absent man, hill courtships threatened by a mother's Murugu worship and a midnight storm, neythal suitors who would marry by servitude, and marutham quarrels in which the wife or the courtesan speaks. Puram matter (Minili's vow, Evvi's victory feast, the Nandas' hoard, hero-stones, Kuttuvan's Kazhumalam) supplies the measures for private feeling.
source_issues: 266: the colophon thurai says தலைமகன் சொல்லியது, but the speaker addresses the husband (மகிழ்ந, line 9) and complains of his oath; it should read தலைமகள் சொல்லியது. thurai_akam gives thalaivi.
271: the colophon thurai begins with a stray alternative number (1செலவுணர்த்திய) and gives no second alternative.
275: the colophon thurai has a stray numeral (1தாய்) and gives no second alternative.
276: the colophon thurai reads தலைமகட்ருப், a misprint for தலைமகட்குப்.
272: line 18 spells மஞ்ஜை with ஜ for the usual மஞ்ஞை.
275: lines 4 and 5 (இளமைத் தகைமையை வளமனைக் கிழத்தி; பிதிர்வை நீரை வெண்நீறு ஆக) are obscure, perhaps corrupt; who is addressed is unclear.

reading: Back home, the man tells the friend how on the elopement road the girl, flowers of the forest pressed into her hair and bangles chiming, was too shy to walk ahead when he asked to see her back, and stood with bowed head, so he slowed and they camped in the wild, hearing a tiger roar over a killed elephant and the drums of drunk bowmen in their fort.
nuance: The danger of the road (tiger, bowmen's drums) comes only after the moment of shyness and is told as background to it: the memory he brings back to the friend is her நாண் on the road, not the peril. His small joke, asking to see her back, turns flight into courtship.

colophon.thurai: புணர்ந்துடன் போயினகாலை இடைச்சுரத்துப் பட்டதனை மீண்டு வந்த காலத்துத் தோழிக்குத் தலைமகன் சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: the lovers going together through the waste land

occasion.words: மீண்டு வந்த காலத்துத் தோழிக்குத் தலைமகன் சொல்லியது

comparisons.tenor: her glance, which outdoes a deer's

reading: Leaving the night meeting, the man tells his heart he is full of joy because her sweet voice came to him smelling of Pekan's rain-wrapped hill, joy like that of Anni Minili, who after the Kosar blinded her father over a cow that strayed into the gram field fasted and wore no clean cloth until Thithiyan killed them, and then let her anger go.
nuance: The simile is a whole revenge story: his joy is measured not by a happy thing but by the release of a vow kept through long self-denial, which hints at how long he has waited and suffered. Pekan, the patron known for giving, lends his hill's rain-smell to her speech.

colophon.thurai: இரவுக்குறிக்கண் தலைமகளைப் புணர்ந்து நீங்குந் தலைமகன் தன் னெஞ்சிற்குச் சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: the joy of a secret meeting on the hill

comparisons.tenor: his joy, like Minili's when her vow of anger was fulfilled

reading: A mother whose daughter has gone off with a bold young man across the sun-scorched waste, where bowmen watch from raised ground for travellers, says that had she known the girl's resolve she would gladly have married her to him in her rich house, splendid as Kothai's spear-guarded Vanji.
nuance: The lament is not against the elopement but against having been left out of it: the mother would have given the wedding herself. The closing lines, about the untroubled sleep on the young breast, are hard to construe; they may picture the girl asleep in his arms as she would have been at home.

thinai_evidence.note: a girl taken across the waste by her lover

comparisons.tenor: her own rich house, like Kothai's capital Vanji

reading: As the cold season sets in, with musundai flowers white as stars, cowherds coming home in the rain with their wet garlands and the water running down every street, the woman asks whether the men in the fierce king's camp, ringed by elephants at night, even if they do not know her plight, at least know their own.
nuance: The cowherds going home at the rain's appointed time are the silent contrast: everyone returns with the season except the men in the camp. Her barb (they may not know our state, but do they know theirs?) turns pity into reproach.

colophon.thurai: பருவங் கண்டு வன்புறை யெதிரழிந்து தலைமகள் தோழிக்குச் சொல்லியது; தோழி தலைமகட்குச் சொல்லியதுமாம்.

thinai_evidence.note: the rains and the cowherds' evening return mark the waiting

occasion.words: பருவங் கண்டு வன்புறை யெதிரழிந்து தலைமகள் தோழிக்குச் சொல்லியது

comparisons.tenor: the white musundai blossoms, like stars in a cloudless sky

reading: Her bangles slipping and her eyes wet, the woman asks her friend what the wealth can be that her man rated above her, crossing the Venkatam wastes where bowmen roast flesh and drink beer: is it as great as the red Himalayan peak, or the treasure the Nandas hid under the Ganges at Pataliputra?
nuance: The two guesses are the largest measures of value a Tamil poet could name, one natural and one royal and northern; set against them, her own worth is the unspoken third term. The bowmen eating 'like demons' make the road the price of that wealth.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவிடை வேறுபட்ட தலைமகள் ஆற்றாமை மீதூரத் தோழிக்குச் சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: the man has crossed the waste for wealth, leaving her

occasion.words: பிரிவிடை வேறுபட்ட தலைமகள் ஆற்றாமை மீதூரத் தோழிக்குச் சொல்லியது

comparisons.tenor: the red Himalayan peak, like a creeping flame
the wealth he went for, matched against the Himalaya

comparisons.vehicle: நந்தர் சீர்மிகு பாடலிக் குழீஇக் கங்கை நீர்முதற் கரந்த நிதியம்
comparisons.tenor: the wealth he went for, guessed to be the Nandas' hidden hoard
her hair, rippled like fine sand in shaded water
the bowmen eating fresh meat

reading: The wife tells her husband that his bathing yesterday in the evening flood with young women, clinging to a float and losing all shame as he gazed at one woman's eyes, is now gossip as loud as the feast at Uraththur after Evvi's men won; that does not grieve her now, but the oath he swore to her by Murugan of Alaivay does.
nuance: The point is in the last turn: public scandal she can bear, a broken oath sworn before the god she cannot. The image of peacocks scared by ploughmen's shouts flying in to the temple precinct carries the oath's setting from field to shrine. Lines 10 to 13, Evvi's victory at Uraththur, are syntactically hard; the sense of the simile, a famous loud feast, is clear.

colophon.thurai: பரத்தையிற் பிரிந்துவந்து கூடிய தலைமகற்குத் தலைமகன் சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: the wife confronts a husband back from other women

comparisons.tenor: the gossip about him, as loud as the victory feast at Uraththur

reading: When her friend grieves that the man who swore unbreakable oaths has changed for the sake of work, the wife answers that the men who crossed the summer hills, where bears raid iruppai blossoms and monkeys leaping on bamboo scatter its rice to pop on hot rock, are not to blame; her own shoulders are, for letting the bangles slip and not knowing how to hold him.
nuance: She shifts blame from the absent man to her own body, a loyal defence that is also an accusation of the friend who called him faithless. The hill scene is crowded with creatures taking and scattering food, abundance in a dry season.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவிடை வேறுபட்ட தலைமகளது ஆற்றாமை கண்டு ஆற்றாளாகிய தோழிக்குத் தலைமகள் சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: the man gone across the waste for his work

comparisons.tenor: the closed iruppai buds, like a wild cat's paw
the white iruppai flowers, like turned ivory
the monkeys' dark faces, as if smeared with ink
the bamboo rice popping on the hot rock, like the crack of a nail

tamil: யான் அலது இல்லை, இவ் உலகத் தானே-
reading: The friend, having taken up the man's suit, tells the girl that if she truly loves the lord of the hill where vengai and wild jasmine sweeten a field bloodied by an elephant and tiger, she should say so; for she herself, without consulting the girl dear as life, has already slipped past their father's strict guard and taken on a great blame that is not deserved.
nuance: The friend's confession puts the girl in her debt: she has risked the shame already, so the girl can only say yes. The hill whose flower-scent drives off the blood-smell may hint that love will cover the scandal; that reading is traditional and not forced by the poem.

colophon.thurai: குறைவேண்டிப் பின்னின்ற தலைமகனுக்குக் குறைநேர்ந்த தோழி தலைமகட்குக் குறைநயப்பக் கூறியது.

thinai_evidence.note: the hill country and its flowers frame the courtship

comparisons.tenor: the girl, dear to the friend as her own life
their father among his kin, like bamboo with its shoots

reading: The friend tells the wife to let her bangles climb back and her hair be dressed, for the man who crossed the road of hero-stones, set where warriors who held off the Mazhavar's spears fell and now washed, smeared with turmeric and crowned with red karanthai, has hurried home at the end of Thai's cool rains to wipe her tears, eyes like the red water-lilies of Vaanan's Sirukudi.
nuance: The hero-stones carry no hidden sense of the lovers (the brief's model of a failed iraicchi); they mark the road's danger and its honour. The return is timed by a seaside festival, women bringing sand dolls to the ghat and dancing the kuravai to horn and drum, so comfort arrives with a feast.

thinai_evidence.note: the man who crossed the waste is reported on his way back

comparisons.tenor: the low hillock, like a she-elephant lying down
the unplanted tall stone that looks as if set up
her eyes, red from weeping, like the red water-lily

reading: The friend tells the lord of the shore, where fishermen wear backwater lilies and njazhal, that the girl's shoulders have thinned and her beauty, once like Kuttuvan's Kazhumalam, is wasting as she gazes sleepless at the bay, while he, even on nights when the little black hen-bird in the thorny nest of the sacred tree suffers apart from her mate, thinks only of his own town.
nuance: The demand for marriage is made without the word: the friend sets the girl's nights beside his, and lets the unpaired hen-bird make the case. நோகோ யானே, 'shall I grieve, then?', closes on the friend's own helplessness.

thinai_evidence.note: fishermen, punnai and the shore

comparisons.tenor: the girl's former beauty, like Kuttuvan's rich town Kazhumalam

iraicchi.act: the little hen-bird, not joined with her mate in the nest, suffers through the night
iraicchi.sense: the girl spends the same nights apart from him, so he should marry and not leave her mateless

reading: Knowing the girl's mind, the friend tells the man who has announced his journey that if he means to cross the waste where doves peck grit with their mates and the nelli's tart fruit holds back the departing lives of thirsty travellers, may his work prosper; but if the bangles slip from her shoulders, smooth as the bamboo of Aviyan's cloud-capped hill, is there a medicine for her in the land where he will stay?
nuance: The road has a remedy for travellers (the nelli that restores them) and the dove that travels with its mate; she will have neither. The blessing on his work is ironic, the real sentence is the closing question.

colophon.thurai: 1செலவுணர்த்திய தோழி தலைமகளது குறிப்பறிந்து தலைமகனைச் செலவழுங்கச் சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: the man is set on crossing the waste for wealth

comparisons.tenor: her long soft shoulders, like the joints of bamboo

iraicchi.act: the dove cock goes to the far land together with his small hen and feeds there with her
iraicchi.sense: even the dove takes its mate along on a far journey, while he means to go alone and leave her

reading: With the man listening outside, the friend tells the girl how he comes alone through the dark cleft of the hill, his spear lighting the path, wearing a garland of koothalam and wild jasmine whose scent the wind carries into their hut, and how the mother, seeing him so, took him for Murugu, greeted him and scattered red millet in worship of Nedu Vel; what will become of their bond with the lord of the hill?
nuance: The friend's comedy has a point: the mother's piety is the measure of how near discovery is, and the man who hears it is told that night visits cannot go on. Who is மெய்ம்மலி உவகையன் and what the mother actually sees are not certain; the reading here takes the comer as the man, mistaken for the god he resembles by spear and garland.

colophon.thurai: இரவுக்குறி வந்த தலைமகன் சிறைப்புறத்தானாகத் தலைமகட்குச் சொல்லுவாளாய்த் தோழி சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: the hill's cleft, kino, peacock and Murugu

comparisons.tenor: the vengai in flower, gold-like

reading: As the new cold season comes, with white herons wheeling like a garland flung across the sky, the woman, wasting with pallor, asks whether he does not know her pain or, knowing it, lacks a heart soft as hers; and she pictures her love-sickness as a great shameless tree, sprouting between her breasts, swelling with the north wind, branching with the town's gossip and budding with scandal over the whole earth, while he does not come.
nuance: The tree is built part by part: sprout, trunk, branches of அம்பல், shoots of love, buds of அலர். 'Praised by poets' and 'shameless' make it a public thing, the opposite of a secret love. The poem is about waiting through a season, which is why the inferred thinai is mullai against the colophon's paalai.

thinai_evidence.note: she waits through the season he should have returned by

comparisons.tenor: the white herons wheeling in the sky, like a flung koothalam garland
her love-sickness, grown into a great tree fed by gossip

reading: Returning, the man tells his charioteer that her town lies in the cool fragrant scrub where, on a midnight of the rainy season, a lone herdsman stands on one leg propped on his staff with his pot, sling and hide, a small fire lit with a drill, the drizzle wetting one side, and his whistle sends the jackal watching his leaping lambs scurrying into the thorn bushes.
nuance: The poem is almost all scene; the woman appears only in the last two lines, as one whose chastity is worthy of the mullai flower. The herdsman keeping lone watch over his flock through the rainy night can be felt as a picture of her guarded steadfastness, but he does nothing of the lovers' situation, so it stays scene.

thinai_evidence.note: herdsman, scrubland and mullai at the rainy midnight

reading: The mother whose daughter left yesterday with a stranger, trusting his love, across the hot hills where bear cubs and their clan raid the iruppai's white flowers, remembers the girl watering the vayalai on the pandal and playing ball, answering scolding with lisping sweet words, and asks those who have eyes to look at the sand house her small red fingers traced under the nochi.
nuance: The last image is the whole grief: a child's sand house still standing after the child has gone into the waste. Lines 4 and 5 (the address வளமனைக் கிழத்தி and the scolding பிதிர்வை நீரை வெண்நீறு ஆக) are obscure, so who is addressed and what she was scolded for cannot be fixed. The bear cubs feeding with their kin are scene, though a reader may feel the contrast with the girl who left hers.

thinai_evidence.note: the girl gone through the waste with her lover

reading: The courtesan, so that the wife's women will hear, says that the lord of the ford, who slips aside like a thief creeping into a guarded house, as the stork stalks the white vaalai fish softly so its steps are not known, may come to her street; before his wives' eyes she will seize his garland and cloth and bind him with her hair like the bull elephant the Aryans lure with a she-elephant, or else let her mother-guarded beauty go to waste like the wealth of a man who hoarded and gave nothing to those who asked.
nuance: Her oath ends on the image of the miser's wealth: beauty not spent is wasted as wealth not given is wasted. She speaks as a challenger, and the furtive stork makes the husband a thief before the wives.

thinai_evidence.note: pond, fish and stork of the town by the fields

comparisons.tenor: the stork stalking the fish, and through it the man slipping off to her
the man she will bind with her hair
her beauty left to waste unless she wins him

ullurai.tenor: the husband stealing away to the courtesan while hiding it from his wives

pairs.situation: he goes softly, afraid his wives will learn where he went
he goes to take his pleasure with the courtesan
he slips aside from the household's ford to her street

ullurai.speaker_fit: the courtesan speaks freely as one outside the household (porul 7.29), with the stork and fish of the marutham pond

reading: Her forehead's glow fading like the moon by day, the woman tells her friend that before the man returns from the dry road, where a tiger that cannot bear its hungry mate's hunger watches for a bristly boar and travellers rest in the spotted shade of hollow trees, the spring has come, the murukku in flame-red bloom like the fighting cock's neck, its blossoms shaken down by bees; he has not come.
nuance: The season is announced with violent colour, a domestic cock's fighting hackles for the red flowers. The tiger hunting for its mate makes the road itself an argument for why he went and why he should return.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகன் பிரிவின்கண் தலைமகள் தோழிக்குப் பருவங்கண் டழிந்து சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: the dry road and the coming of spring

comparisons.vehicle: தண்கதிர் மண்டிலம் அவிர்அறச் சாஅய்ப் பகலழி தோற்றம் போலப்
comparisons.tenor: her forehead losing its glow, like the moon by day
the boar's coarse bristles, like palmyra fibres
the cock's dense hackles, like leaping flame
the murukku blossoms, like the fighting cock's fiery neck

iraicchi.act: the tiger, unable to bear his mate's hunger, lies in wait to hunt for her
iraicchi.sense: a male who goes out for his mate's need, as he did, should bring what he hunts home to her, yet the season has come and he has not

reading: With the man listening outside, the friend tells the girl that the clouds drawn from the eastern sea have massed over the mountain at midnight like the shields of kings' armies, with lightning and thunder; tomorrow the falls will come down bending the bamboo to the ford of their town, and they will bathe in that water, which played on the mountain of the man who wasted her beauty, to ease the pain of their sleepless nights.
nuance: The storm warns the listening man that the night path is dangerous and the waiting long; the bath in water from his own mountain is the only contact with him left to them, which presses him toward marriage without naming it.

colophon.thurai: இரவுக்குறிக்கண் தலைமகன் சிறைப்புறமாகத் தலைமகட்குத் தோழி சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: the mountain at midnight

occasion.words: இரவுக்குறிக்கண் தலைமகன் சிறைப்புறமாகத் தலைமகட்குத் தோழி சொல்லியது

comparisons.tenor: the massed dark clouds, like rows of shields in kings' armies
the lightning, like a banner raised on its pole
her body, dark as a sapphire

reading: Setting out for wealth, the man tells his heart that the fire of the old saying, that only men who never leave their wives' breasts can bear to live in one town watching friends in want and kin in distress, burned in him night and day and was not quenched by the rain of effort; but while he toils in the waste, how will she fare in the mornings when the koel wakes sleeping pairs, walking softly like a swan, helpless of heart?
nuance: Duty to friends and kin is the reason given for leaving, not desire for wealth itself, and it is put as a proverb he cannot answer. The swan's gait and the paired sleepers waked by the koel make her mornings the cost. Lines 11 to 13, joining a lute and the koel, are hard to construe.

colophon.thurai: பொருள்வயிற் பிரிந்து போகாநின்ற தலைமகன் தன்னெஞ்சிற்குச் சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: the man leaves home to labour across the waste

occasion.words: பொருள்வயிற் பிரிந்து போகாநின்ற தலைமகன் தன்னெஞ்சிற்குச் சொல்லியது

comparisons.tenor: her soft walk, like a fine female swan's
the burning resolve in his heart, which the rain of effort did not put out

reading: Having seen the girl with her garland of gold-bright serunthi playing at chasing crabs on the shore, the man tells his heart that since even a shipload of wealth would not win her, he will leave his country, plough salt and go into the deep sea on a float with her father, and serve him humbly, in the hope that the fisherman who shares out pearls on the wide shore will give her to him.
nuance: A suitor proposes to earn a bride by servitude, not by bride-price, because the father's pride makes wealth useless; அறம் தெரிந்து makes the humbling a matter of right conduct, not of desperation.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகளைக் கண்ணுற்று நீங்குந் தலைமகன் தன்னெஞ்சிற்குச் சொல்லியது. அல்லகுறிப்பட்டுப் போகாநின்றவன் சொல்லியதுமாம்.

thinai_evidence.note: crabs, salt pans and the fisherman of the shore

occasion.words: தலைமகளைக் கண்ணுற்று நீங்குந் தலைமகன் தன்னெஞ்சிற்குச் சொல்லியது

comparisons.tenor: the serunthi blossoms of her garland, like beaten gold

title: மணிமிடைபவளம் 281-300
theme: Akananuru 281 to 300, in the anthology's fixed order of lands: ten paalai poems weigh the wealth-road against the woman left behind, mostly from the man's side as he speaks to his own heart on the way (her rites of waiting, her farewell, her offer to come), with two elopements urged and blessed by the friend; hill poems press for marriage through the father's consent, the shut-in girl and the dreaded veri rite; neythal and marutham poems use Thondi, Korkai and Koodal as measures of pallor and gossip, and the friend turns maxims and hospitality into ways of binding the lover.
source_issues: 285: the colophon thurai begins with a stray footnote numeral, '1உடன்போக்குடன்'; copied as it stands.
288: the base text numbers the last line 27 and line 10 as 20 though the poem has 17 lines (misprinted numbers); line 16 reads கொங்தொடு, apparently a misprint for கொங்கொடு (with pollen).
291: line 1 reads வானம் யெல்வளம், which is not a Tamil word form (no word begins with யெ); probably a misprint, perhaps for பெயல்வளம் (the wealth of rain). Marked as the sky withholding its rain.
294: the base text has 16 lines, the commentary edition (pmuni0523_02) 17; marked as the base text stands.
295: the base text has 22 lines, the commentary edition (pmuni0523_02) 20; marked as the base text stands.
296: the poet is given as மதுரைப் ரோலவாயார், which cannot be right (no Tamil word begins with ர); a misprint for some other name, left as it is in the core record.

reading: The woman asks her friend what she should do: the man who spoke boldly of his manhood went off without fear that his word would prove false, a peacock's shed feather wound on his bow, across the rock the Moriyar's wheels cut on their march south with the Vadugar in the van, leaving her only gossip loud as a beaten drum.
nuance: The bow wound with peacock feather and the Moriyar's rock-cut pass are the very images Akananuru 69 uses to promise a quick return; here they describe a man already gone, and the only thing he has left behind is talk. The Moriyar road is history used as distance: he has gone as far as an emperor's army once came.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகன் பிரிவின்கண் வேறுபட்ட தலைமகளது வேறுபாடு கண்டு ஆற்றாளாகிய தோழிக்குத் தலைமகள் சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: she speaks of a man who has crossed the rock-cut pass and left her

occasion.words: தலைமகன் பிரிவின்கண் வேறுபட்ட தலைமகளது வேறுபாடு கண்டு ஆற்றாளாகிய தோழிக்குத் தலைமகள் சொல்லியது

comparisons.tenor: the gossip he left behind, spread aloud through the town

reading: Within the hero's hearing, the friend tells the woman that their father has agreed to give her to the hill-lord whose hunters bring down ivory, gold, gems and pearls together; the gossiping town now speaks on his side, the mother praises his shoulders and says he is the one, and they themselves fold their fingers to the house god praying that the fixed day come quickly.
nuance: The three kinds of mountain wealth carried down together on a sandal-wood pole read like the bride-gifts the man should bring, and the poem is meant to be overheard: everyone has consented, so the only delay left is his. Even the alar that threatened secret love has turned to approval.

colophon.thurai: இரவுக்குறிக்கண் தலைமகன் சிறைப்புறமாகத் தோழி தலைமகட்குச் சொல்லுவாளாய்ச் சொல்லியது. தலைமகன் பிரிவின்கண் தோழிக்குத் தலைமகள் சொல்லியதுமாம்.

thinai_evidence.note: hunters, vengai garland and mountain slopes of the hill country

occasion.words: இரவுக்குறிக்கண் தலைமகன் சிறைப்புறமாகத் தோழி தலைமகட்குச் சொல்லுவாளாய்ச் சொல்லியது

comparisons.tenor: pearls spilled from the broken elephant tusk

reading: The friend tells the man who has resolved to take the woman away with him that she is eager to go, and asks him not to think the road too hard; she wishes the rains to fall on the long forest so that its heat is quenched, grass springs up and the red velvet mites streak the cool ground like tufts of dyed cotton, making the way sweet for her to leave hardship and go with him.
nuance: The friend's blessing is a wish that the paalai road turn into mullai: rain, new grass and the red mites of the wet season. The village women who give scant food and the owl's thin cry belong to the hard road she hopes will soften.

thinai_evidence.note: she will leave home to go with him

comparisons.tenor: the red mites scattered on the cool ground

reading: The man, his work done, says that the town of the fair woman whose love is more distracted than his own lies in the lovely forest where the small-eyed hare eats swollen varagu ears, sleeps curled, and wakes to go with its mate and drink at a little pool in a doorway, where millet-fed bowmen hunt deer in the jasmine gardens.
nuance: The whole first half is the home country seen with longing as he nears it; the hare that rises and goes off with its partner is the image of what he is about to do. The last lines turn the usual complaint around: he grants that her longing is greater than his.

colophon.thurai: வினைமுற்றிய தலைமகன் தேர்ப்பாகற்குச் சொல்லியது. தன் நெஞ்சிற்குச் சொல்லியதுமாம்.

thinai_evidence.note: jasmine gardens, scrub forest and varagu millet of the pasture land

comparisons.tenor: the hare's small round eyes

iraicchi.act: the hare wakes from sleep and goes off with its mate to drink
iraicchi.sense: the man, his work done, will now go back to live beside his wife

reading: The friend, having won the woman's consent to elope, says that where they once grieved that the men would go and leave them, now the lover has said that she too will come with them through the desert where the red dog cuts down a stag to feed its hungry mate, travellers in stone-torn rags climb trees and the vulture watches; so come, friend, let us embrace many times.
nuance: The road is described at its cruellest just as the friend announces joy: the grief of being left is undone by the decision to go together. The red dog hunting for its mate shows the provision the man will make for her on that road.

thinai_evidence.note: the scorched desert road

comparisons.tenor: the travellers' rags torn by thrown stones
the woman's kohl-lined eyes

iraicchi.act: the male wild dog kills a stag to end the hunger of its mate
iraicchi.sense: the man who takes her through that land will provide for her as the beast does for its mate

reading: When the man takes her hand as if swearing, the friend, addressing him as lord of the cool-ford town where girls pound sand in the kaanchi shade and a kingfisher full of fish sleeps on a marutham branch, says the great hold back even what the heart desires, weigh virtue and wealth and their own worth, and only then carry out what they intended; if falsehood appears even in men like him, where is truth to be found in the world?
nuance: She raises him to the rank of the great precisely so that a broken promise would be a failure of truth for the whole world; the maxim is a trap built to hold him to his oath of marriage. Her reading of his gesture as an oath is the colophon's point.

colophon.thurai: வரைந் தெய்துவலென்று நீங்குந் தலைமகன் தலைமகளை ஆற்று வித்துக் கொண்டிருத்தல் வேண்டுமென்று தோழியைக் கைப் பற்றியது. தன்னைத் தொட்டுச் சூளுறுவானாகக் கருதித் தோழி சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: marutham tree, kaanchi shade and cool ford of the river town

occasion.words: தன்னைத் தொட்டுச் சூளுறுவானாகக் கருதித் தோழி சொல்லியது

comparisons.tenor: the white sand heaped by the girls
the girls' slender waists
what one has heard from the wise, restraining desire as a goad turns an elephant

reading: On the road, the man asks his heart whether the poor woman suffers at home, praying with bunched fingers and a vow-bound heart for company by day, while he toils on the endless way through deserted hamlets where the shrine has forgotten its daily offering, the west wind scatters a pair of doves from a banyan, a doe licks a stag's back and the herd gazes at thin shade as evening comes on.
nuance: The abandoned shrine that has forgotten its daily offering sits beside the woman who keeps her daily vow: the desert is full of things given up, while she is not. The pair of doves driven apart by the wind and the doe comforting the stag frame the two kinds of pairing he has in mind.

colophon.thurai: பிரிந்து போகாநின்ற தலைமகன் இடைச்சுரத்து நின்ற தன்னெஞ்சிற்குச் சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: the endless dry way and the abandoned hamlets

iraicchi.act: the doe licks the back of her stag in the heat of the road
iraicchi.sense: even beasts on that road soothe their partners, while he has left her to bear her pain alone

reading: On a day meeting the friend tells the hill man, who comes daily in sandal paste and a vengai garland and has made light of them on finding them alone, that he may go; their father now guards the sweet-voiced girl as closely as the sacred mango grove of the hill goddesses on the cold slope, where even a monkey father who touches a fruit to feed his hungry mate is struck with sickness.
nuance: She tells him the girl is now shut in (செறிப்பு) without saying so: her guarded state is a forbidden grove where touching brings affliction. The monkey that cannot even take a fruit for its mate is the hero who can no longer reach her unless he marries.

colophon.thurai: பகற்குறிக்கண் தோழி செறிப்பறிவு றீ இ வரைவு கடாயது.

thinai_evidence.note: vengai of the slope, millet field and monkeys of the hill

comparisons.tenor: the father's guard over the girl, which none may touch without harm

reading: On a desert way of arrow-killed travellers' cairns and tall hero-stones given daily offerings, the man who has set his mind on his work asks his heart whether the girl who fretted if his embrace loosened even a little now sits dazed on her feathered bed, watching the wall where she marks the days, tears falling on her breast like pearls off a slack string, praying 'speak good' each time the lizard chirps, and fighting the dull evening.
nuance: Everything he imagines her doing (scoring the days on the wall, praying at the lizard's call) is the ritual of waiting, matched against the stones on his road that receive their own daily offering: both she and the dead are kept by daily rites.

colophon.thurai: பிரிந்து போகா நின்ற தலைமகன் தன் நெஞ்சிற்குச்சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: a desert way marked with cairns and hero-stones

occasion.words: பிரிந்து போகா நின்ற தலைமகன் தன் நெஞ்சிற்குச்சொல்லியது

comparisons.tenor: her tears falling on her breast

reading: With the man listening outside at night, the woman asks her friend why, though he came alone with an unwavering heart to the backwater grove even before marrying her, her eyes, once lovely as the cool neythal of Kuttuvan's Thondi harbour, have lost their sapphire beauty and taken on the hue of gold, in his shore where a heron hen whose mate was caught in the fisher boys' net refuses food at evening and cries clutching her chick.
nuance: 'Even before marrying' turns the question into a warning: if he wastes her like this now, what after? The neythal of Thondi, the emblem of Kuttuvan's port, is what her eyes have stopped resembling.

colophon.thurai: இரவுக் குறிக்கண் தலைமகன் சிறைப்புறத்தானாகத் தோழிக்குச் சொல்லுவாளாய்த் தலைமகள் சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: the shore lord, backwater grove, neythal flower and heron

occasion.words: இரவுக் குறிக்கண் தலைமகன் சிறைப்புறத்தானாகத் தோழிக்குச் சொல்லுவாளாய்த் தலைமகள் சொல்லியது

comparisons.tenor: the former dark beauty of her eyes
the pallor her eyes have taken
her eyes before the pallor

iraicchi.act: the heron hen whose mate is caught refuses food and cries at nightfall holding her chick
iraicchi.sense: in his own shore a bird fasts and cries for a lost mate, so he should see what his delay does to the woman

reading: The man going for wealth tells his heart, live long, that crossing the sun-scorched desert where the sky has withheld its rain, pebbles glitter like fireflies on slopes where an elephant fought a tiger, leaf-crowned robbers with arrows humming like bees seize the caravans' goods, and a stag with new horns in velvet calls out meaning to feed its spotted doe, it has remembered the fine beauty of their beloved's hair, eyes and shoulders.
nuance: The heart's remembering is blessed (வாழிய) rather than rebuked: the desert has not driven her out of his mind. The stag that has lost its old horns and calls for its doe is the one tender thing on the road.

colophon.thurai: பொருள்வயிற் போகாநின்ற தலைமகன் இடைச்சுரத்துத் தன்னெஞ்சிற்குச் சொல்லியது.

thinai_evidence.note: ponds dried and the hard desert

comparisons.tenor: the pebbles glittering everywhere on the slope
the robbers' whistling arrows

iraicchi.act: the stag with broken horns calls out, thinking to feed his spotted doe
iraicchi.sense: the man too, far on the road, thinks of the one he means to provide for

reading: The woman, afraid of the veri rite, asks her friend what to do: mother has misread her loosened bangles and spends wealth in worry, and if the stranger velan, to kill a kid not yet weaned, sways in his garland she will be ashamed, all because the lord of the hill, where a hunter's sling-stone flung at a night-grazing elephant flies off scattering vengai blooms and honey and lodges in a jackfruit, has not married her.
nuance: The sling-stone that misses the elephant and ends in the jackfruit, wrecking flowers and honey on its way, may be read as the mother's rite aimed at the wrong cause; but the poem gives no second correspondence firm enough to make it a hidden comparison, so it is left as scene.

thinai_evidence.note: hunter, vengai and the hill country

comparisons.tenor: the flight of the sling-stone
