reading: The woman tells her friend that they cannot be consoled in the cold time when the spray scatters, in the sorrowful evening when women with carp-like kohl-lined eyes and heavy earrings, cupping their hands as a raft, lift the lamp-flame lit with ghee; those women, when their hard-won lovers come, prepare a feast and, with joy filling their bodies, wipe away the tears that rise.
nuance: The lamp-lighting of the evening is seen from outside: other wives shelter the flame and later weep for joy at their men's return. Who the last lines describe is uncertain; they may instead be the friend's promise of a joy the woman refuses to believe in (தேற்றாம்).

reading: The woman says her pallor is like the moss at the drinking ghat of the village well: wherever her lover touches, it parts, and wherever he lets go, it spreads again.
nuance: The moss parts when a pot or a hand breaks it and closes as soon as the hand is lifted: the pallor is not a slow wasting but a surface that re-forms the moment his touch stops. The doubled தொடுவுழித் தொடுவுழி and விடுவுழி விடுவுழி make the motion repeat in the line.

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the poem names no addressee and the colophon gives only the speaker

comparisons.tenor: her pallor

reading: The man tells his charioteer that, resolving with a mind set on good to go the far road and remove without hindrance the love-sickness of the broad-shouldered one, he who is wise and skilled broke across the gravel and led the chariot on a new way through the waste: today he has brought the chariot, and so given grace to her who lived in pain.
nuance: The praise goes to the driver, not to the man himself: the charioteer took the shorter, harder way across the gravel because he too thought of the wife. The pain is hers (நோயுழந் துறைவியை), and the gift is the chariot's arrival.

reading: The woman says that even laughing play, one day, with the lord of the shore, where the girls of the orai game, their wet hair crowned with long strands of neythal mixed with choice adumbu flowers, fear the wet crab that scuttles into the sea, has been forbidden: how slight is the friendship of touching bodies!
nuance: The play on the beach with flower-crowned girls who shriek at crabs is the most innocent of meetings, and even that is now forbidden: the girl is kept at home. Line 6 (றைதே கம்ம) divides uncertainly; read as ஐதே, 'slight, fragile'.

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the poem names no addressee and the colophon gives only the speaker

title: கடவுள் வாழ்த்து 0-20
theme: Natrinai 0 to 20: an invocation that builds the discus-bearer's body from the cosmos, then poems across the five lands: hill girls guarding millet and hiding a first love, elopements seen by the lover as spring groves and by onlookers as a tiger's road, men who weigh wealth against a wife's gaze and stay, shore friends who press for marriage with gossip and threats of death, and a marutham wife who answers a husband's denial with an ironic portrait of the other woman; Ori's forest, Poraiyan's Thondi and Pazhaiyan's spear lend puram fame to private love.
source_issues: 7: the colophon's நெட்டி இடைக் கழிந்து looks like a bad word division of நெட்டிடை கழிந்து (the colophon quotes the Tholkappiyam's phrase on a man who leaves for wealth without marrying); copied as it stands.
11: line 3 reads தௌளிதின், which looks like the TSCII fault flagged elsewhere (ௌ for ெள்), that is தெள்ளிதின்; not repaired in the core text.
5, 10, 20: repaired lines (5 line 8, 10 line 3, 20 line 5) as flagged by show; the readings follow the repaired text.
13: the construction of lines 1 and 8 (எழாஅ ஆகலின், மயில் அறிபு அறியா மன்னோ) is unsure, so the friend's excuse is uncertain in detail.

tamil: விசும்பு மெய் ஆக திசை கை ஆக
பசுங் கதிர் மதியமொடு சுடர் கண் ஆக
reading: The invocation: they say that the god of the discus, who shines free of all harm, is the first lord of the Veda, whose feet are the great earth, whose garment is the sea where conches sound, whose body is the sky, whose hands are the quarters, whose eyes are the moon of cool rays with the sun, and who holds within himself all that has come to be.
nuance: The god is never named; he is known only by the discus (திகிரியோன்) and drawn as a body made of the cosmos, and the claim is put at one remove (என்ப, 'they say'), as if the poet reports the teaching of the Veda rather than a vision of his own.

thinai_evidence.note: praise of the god, the கடவுள் வாழ்த்து placed under paadaan

comparisons.tenor: his feet
his garment
his body
his hands
his eyes

reading: The heroine answers the friend who told her he will leave: a man of steady word, sweeter the longer one knows him, he has never known how to part from her shoulders; the bond of the noble is high and pure like the sweet honey bees make from cool lotus pollen and store on a lofty sandal tree, and he, who graciously loves her because she cannot live without him as the world cannot live without water, fearing that her fragrant brow would pale, does not know how to do a mean thing.
nuance: Her proof is his character, not his promise: she reasons from what kind of man he is (நின்ற சொல்லர், புரையோர் கேண்மை) to what he cannot do. The honey simile carries the reasoning: a sweetness gathered from the low lotus and stored at the top of the hill tree, a bond made in one land and kept high in another. The world-and-water clause is the formula of Kural 20, bent here to her dependence on him.

thinai_evidence.note: honey stored high on the hill sandal; no parting has happened, the bond is the matter

comparisons.vehicle: தாமரைத் தண் தாது ஊதி மீமிசைச் சாந்தில் தொடுத்த தீம் தேன்
comparisons.tenor: the bond of the noble

tamil: மான் நோக்கு இண்டு இவர் ஈங்கைய சுரனே
reading: Onlookers on the wasteland road, where in the bare forest of rustling date palms below a great cool hill the big-headed tiger cub, its head stained red and its mouth bloody from the travellers it struck down, eyes the deer at evening among the climbing iṇṭu and īṅkai, say that the youth who goes ahead of his sharp-toothed lovely girl through that country has a heart crueler than the thunder that, with wind-driven rain, shakes the great mountains.
nuance: The blame falls on the man alone, and its measure is a storm: beside the tiger cub's bloody evening the onlookers set a heart harder than mountain-shaking thunder, so the danger of the road and the youth's will are made the same kind of force. Line 1's அழுந்துபட and line 8's எல்லிடை (by night, or in the open light) leave the scene's time unsure.

comparisons.tenor: the youth's heart

tamil: ஈன் பருந்து உயவும் வான் பொரு நெடுஞ் சினைப்
வில் ஏர் உழவர் வெம் முனைச் சீறூர்ச்
மனை மாண் சுடரொடு படர் பொழுது எனவே
reading: The man, whose heart again urges a journey for wealth, recalls an earlier one: at the strength-draining evening that met him at the edge of the wasteland, by a hot frontier hamlet of men whose plough is the bow, where under the dappled shade of a cracked-barked neem with sky-touching boughs, where the brooding kite cried, untaught children scratched a board like a gauge and played dice with gooseberries, did he not think of her, sweet as a finished task, at the hour she moves about the house with its fine lamp?
nuance: He likens her to the very thing the journey seeks, a task completed (வினை முடித்தன்ன), so the wife at home already is the success he would go out to win. The children's gooseberry game on the hot frontier pictures a home life he lacked at the hour it most mattered: evening, when the lamp is lit.

comparisons.tenor: the board the children scratched
his sweet wife

tamil: கானல் அம் சிறுகுடிக் கடல் மேம் பரதவர்
நீல் நிற புன்னைக் கொழு நிழல் அசைஇ
தண் பெரும் பரப்பின் ஒண் பதம் நோக்கி
அம் கண் அரில் வலை உணக்கும் துறைவனொடு
அலரே அன்னை அறியின் இவண் உறை வாழ்க்கை
கண நிரை கிளர்க்கும் நெடு நெறிச் சகடம்
இருங் கழிச் சேர்ப்பின் தம் உறைவின் ஊர்க்கே
reading: With the man standing unseen nearby, the friend asks the heroine: if we tell the lord of the shore, where the fishermen of the grove hamlet rest in the rich shade of the dark punnai and dry their nets watching for the bright hour on the cool wide sea, that if mother learns of the gossip our life here will become hard, will he take us away to his own town on the dark backwater coast, where the roar of the salt-sellers' long-road carts, sunk in sand as they cry the sale of white crystal salt and rouse their herds, frightens the black-legged white heron in the fields?
nuance: The question is put so that he hears it, and its last image answers it: in his own town the clamour of the salt carts frightens even the heron of the fields, as the clamour of gossip frightens her here. The fishermen idling in the punnai shade while their nets dry is the leisure the lovers have had, now ending. Fear of the mother is entered as accham from இறை, the authority one lives under.

ullurai.speaker_fit: the friend uses the salt carts and the heron of the backwater, things of the poem's own neythal shore (porul 7.27)

tamil: அகல் வாய்ப் பைஞ் சுனைப் பயிர் கால்யாப்ப
குறவர் கொன்ற குறைக் கொடி நறைப் பவர்
மயங்கு இதழ் மழைக் கண் பயந்த தூதே
reading: To the heroine, changed since she sensed the man's plan to leave, the friend says that even in this dewy season, when the clouds that have poured great rain thunder as they rise in the south, the land is soaked, the hills sprout, crops take root by the wide green pools and the fragrant creeper the hill-men cut sprouts again and twines round the sandal, it is hard for a lover to part; and the message her rain-heavy eyes have sent, with the north wind that brings back the young men setting out today, will hold him.
nuance: The poem never says he will stay; it lets the season argue (rain, sprouting, the cut creeper twining the sandal again) and calls her tears a தூது, an envoy, as if weeping were already a message he cannot ignore. The cut creeper that sprouts and winds round the sandal can be read as parted lovers rejoined, but it does no act of a person here, so it stays scene. The sense of lines 7 to 9 is unsure, and line 8 is a repaired line.

colophon.thurai: தலைவன் செலவுக் குறிப்பு அறிந்து வேறுபட்ட தலைவிக்குத் தோழி சொல்லியது

occasion.words: தலைவன் செலவுக் குறிப்பு அறிந்து வேறுபட்ட தலைவிக்குத் தோழி சொல்லியது

comparisons.tenor: her tear-filled eyes

tamil: குவளை அன்ன ஏந்து எழில் மழைக் கண்
அத்தக் குமிழின் கொடு மூக்கு விளை கனி
reading: The man, kept from the night meeting, tells his own heart within the friend's hearing that if he could find someone to go to the young girl, with skin like the tender stalk of the water lily stripped of its fibre, eyes like kuvalai and full shoulders, and tell her, she would not ask 'who is he?' but, she whose dark thick hair smells of the forest of Ori of the strong bow, where the bent ripe fruit of the kumizh by the path falls as food for the young deer, would be wholly overcome at hearing 'he has come'.
nuance: He does not doubt her love, only the means of reaching her: the speech is a wish for a messenger (செப்புநர்ப் பெறினே), and since it is said where the friend can hear, the wish is a request to her. Paranar gives the same pairing of Ori's forest and a girl's hair in Kuruntokai 199.

tamil: சூருடை நனந் தலைச் சுனை நீர் மல்க
கல் அலைத்து இழிதரும் கடு வரற் கான் யாற்றுக்
கழை மாய் நீத்தம் காடு அலை ஆர்ப்ப
reading: The friend tells the heroine, whose man has gone after wealth without marrying her, that the sky, roaring with its thunderbolts, is flashing to pour at once on the great forest of small-leaved sandal on the cool fragrant slope where the stripe-browed elephant that ate white paddy sleeps, while the spring in the wide god-haunted upland brims, waterfalls roar on the great slopes and the forest torrent, tumbling stones and drowning the bamboo, makes the woods resound.
nuance: The friend says nothing about him; she only announces the rains, and whether they comfort (the season he named for return has come) or alarm (the land he crosses is in flood) the poem leaves to the hearer. The fed elephant asleep on the cool slope is the one creature at rest in the storm; its ease, which she lacks, is a mood, not an act of the lovers, so it is scene.

colophon.thurai: பட்ட பின்றை வரையாது கிழவோன் நெட்டி இடைக் கழிந்து பொருள்வயிற் பிரிய ஆற்றாளாய தலைவிக்குத் தோழி சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the friend points to the coming rains in a separation: the time of waiting

occasion.words: பட்ட பின்றை வரையாது கிழவோன் நெட்டி இடைக் கழிந்து பொருள்வயிற் பிரிய

tamil: அல்கு படர் உழந்த அரி மதர் மழைக்கண்
பல் பூம் பகைத் தழை நுடங்கும் அல்குல்
தண் சேறு தாஅய் மதனுடை நோன் தாள்
தன் திறம் பெறுக இவள் ஈன்ற தாயே
reading: At the end of their first meeting, seeing her again among her companions, the man asks whose daughter she is, this simple girl with proud, red-lined rain-eyes that have known lingering longing, a leaf skirt of many flowers swaying at her waist and a body like a fine gem, who has brought him such pain; long live her father, and may the mother who bore her have the fortune of Thondi of Poraiyan of the strong chariots, where in the wide fields, even as reapers cut and binders carry, the eye-like neythal, spreading its strong stems through the cool mud, blooms in the stacked sheaves.
nuance: His first question is about her kin (யார் மகள்கொல்), and his first wish is a blessing on her father and mother, so desire already turns toward the family he will have to ask for her. The Thondi image is of fields so rich that flowers bloom in the cut stacks, a plenty that does not stop at harvest, and that is what he wishes on her mother.

colophon.thurai: இயற்கைப் புணர்ச்சி இறுதிக்கண் தலைமகளை ஆயத்தொடும் கண்ட தலைமகன் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: a man struck by the girl at the end of their first meeting

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no addressee; he speaks to himself

comparisons.tenor: her body
the neythal flower

tamil: நல மென் பணைத் தோள் எய்தினம் ஆகலின்
பொரிப் பூம் புன்கின் அழற் தகை ஒண் முறி
சுணங்கு அணி வன முலை அணங்கு கொளத் திமிரி
மா நனை கொழுதி மகிழ் குயில் ஆலும்
குறும் பல் ஊர யாம் செல்லும் ஆறே
reading: Eloping with her, the man tells his white-toothed girl that, having won her soft bamboo-like shoulders so that his whirling distress is gone, as eager devotees who strive without fail see with their own eyes the god they worship, she may go without strain, rubbing the fire-bright young leaves of the flowering pungu on her lovely spotted breasts so that they hold a charm, lingering long at every shade and making sand dolls at every stretch of sand, for the road they take runs through forest of fragrant cool groves where the happy koel, pecking mango buds, calls, past many small villages.
nuance: The wasteland of the colophon is drawn as a spring garden and the journey as play (shade, sand dolls, leaves to rub on her breasts), so the man answers in advance the fear every elopement poem raises. Likening himself to devotees who at last see their god puts the girl in the god's place.

thinai_evidence.note: the lover leads the girl away on the road; elopement is paalai's matter even through a pleasant land

comparisons.vehicle: அழிவிலர் முயலும் ஆர்வ மாக்கள் வழிபடு தெய்வம் கண் கண்டாஅங்கு
comparisons.tenor: his winning her
the young pungu leaves
her shoulders

tamil: இன் கடுங் கள்ளின் இழை அணி நெடுந் தேர்க்
reading: Handing over the girl as she elopes, the friend tells the man of the flowering town: even when her lifted lovely breasts sag and her fine long hair, hanging below the gems on her gold-like body, is bound up with grey, take care never to leave her, who has trusted your unfailing good word as one trusts the spear of Pazhaiyan, lord of Por of the white-tusked elephants, which struck true so that the victorious Cholas, of tall ornamented chariots and sweet strong toddy, could humble the Kongar.
nuance: The friend looks past the elopement to old age, naming the very changes (sagging breasts, grey hair) that might later be his excuse to leave, and binds him in advance. She holds him to his word with a war image: his promise must strike as surely as a famous spear, so his speech becomes a weapon he must answer for.

thinai_evidence.note: the poem shows only the entrusting; the elopement comes from the colophon

comparisons.tenor: the man's unfailing word
her body

tamil: மெய் சாயினை அவர் செய் குறி பிழைப்ப
reading: With the man standing unseen nearby, the friend tells the heroine, wilted in body like a garland left unworn since the signal he set failed her, to give up the resentful thought that he surely will not come: on the shore of flowered sand beaten by the waves the charioteer, sparing the crab beside the wheel's track, checks the reins as he drives, and the moonlight has spread over the seaside grove.
nuance: The answer to her doubt is a sound and a sight, not a promise: the chariot is already on the shore, driven slowly so as not to crush the crabs, and the moon is up. The care that spares a crab is the care he brings to her, though the poem leaves that unsaid; the crab is acted on, not acting, so it is not iraicchi. Lines 3 and 4 are compressed and their exact construction is unsure.

colophon.thurai: காப்பு மிகுதிக்கண் இடையீடுபட்டு ஆற்றாளாய தலைமகட்கு தலைமகன் சிறைப்புறத்தானாகத் தோழி சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: crab, waves and the seaside grove

comparisons.tenor: her wilted body

tamil: வைகு புலர் விடியல் மெய் கரந்து தன் கால்
அரி அமை சிலம்பு கழீஇ பல் மாண்
reading: The friend tells the man that at first dawn, when the worn churning stick, its rope frayed, roars at the post as it stirs out the ghee in the full-bellied pot that smells of wood-apple, the girl, hiding herself, slipped the pebble-filled anklets from her feet and set aside her finely striped ball as she went, saying 'whenever they see these my companions will grieve; pitiable, pitiable they are', and even as she eagerly made ready to come with you, her eyes wept beyond her control.
nuance: The report is meant to make him fear for her (the colophon's அஞ்சுவித்தது): her will is set but her eyes are not, and the things she leaves behind (anklets, the striped ball) are the things of girlhood her friends will find. Taking off the anklets, a rite of marriage, she does alone and in hiding while the house churns at dawn.

thinai_evidence.note: a girl making ready to elope

tamil: எறி பொன் பிதிரின் சிறு பல தாஅய்
வேங்கை வீ உகும் ஓங்கு மலைக் கட்சி
பயில் குரல் கவரும் பைம் புறக் கிளியே
reading: The friend, seeing the heroine changed the day after her first meeting and wanting her to hide it, says: you of the good great shoulders and red-lined rain-eyes like the arrows the millet-watchers pulled out after felling a beast, do not weep and spoil your beauty before strangers because the birds will not rise; the green-backed parrots that carry off the thick ears in the high hill glade, where vengai blossoms fall small and many like the sparks from gold a smith beats, know the peacock, it seems, and do not fear it.
nuance: The friend hands the girl an excuse to give out (the parrots will not leave the millet, so she weeps) to hide the real cause, her new love. The arrow simile is pointed: eyes red-streaked like arrows drawn bloody from a beast, a hunter's image for a girl who has just been struck herself. Lines 1 and 8 can be construed more than one way, so the excuse is uncertain in its detail.

colophon.thurai: இயற்கைப் புணர்ச்சியின் பிற்றை ஞான்று தலைவியின் வேறுபாடு கண்ட தோழி தலைவி மறைத்தற்குச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: millet-guarding, vengai and parrots of the hill

comparisons.vehicle: ஏனல் காவலர் மா வீழ்த்துப் பறித்த பகழி
comparisons.tenor: her red-lined eyes
the falling vengai blossoms

tamil: தொல் கவின் தொலைய தோள் நலம் சாஅய
பகல் தீ வேட்ட ஞாட்பினும் மிகப் பெரிது
அலர் எழச் சென்றனர் ஆயினும் மலர் கவிழ்ந்து
இனம் சால் வயக் களிறு பாந்தட் பட்டென
reading: To the friend who blamed the man, the heroine speaks for him: though he left without grace, her old beauty gone and her shoulders wasted, he will be gracious, for he loved her; though he went with gossip rising louder than the battle in which Sembiyan shattered Kuttuvan's Akappa and lit a fire by day, he has crossed the forest where fierce beasts roam, where on the kanthal slope, its great petals open and flowers bowed, the cry of a she-elephant, sleepless and afraid because the strong bull of her herd was seized by a python, echoes through the long mountain clefts.
nuance: She grants everything the friend says (the lost beauty, gossip loud as a war) and still affirms him; the comfort is her trust, not his return. The she-elephant crying for her mate on the road he crossed is a sound he too has heard.

thinai_evidence.note: she speaks of a man gone across the wasteland

comparisons.tenor: the gossip

iraicchi.act: the she-elephant, sleepless with fear, cries through the clefts for her bull seized by a python
iraicchi.sense: the man who crossed that land has heard a mate grieving for its lost partner, and will remember the one he left

tamil: நுணங்கு துகில் நுடக்கம் போல கணம் கொள
reading: Pressing the man to marry, the friend tells the lord of the shore of strong waters, where the north wind blows the huge dune the roaring waves heaped up into drifts like the ripple of fine cloth, that since we are not women you joined only to taste a flower-like beauty while it was new, we have held up our pledged heart as best we could, and, like a chaste young mother who lets her child go when a demon seizes it, have let go even the modesty that came with us from far back: let this town gossip.
nuance: The simile is the poem's force: modesty is given up as a faultless mother gives up her child to a demon, not by choice but to a power she cannot resist, so 'let the town talk' is defeat turned into a threat. The waves heap the dune and the wind scatters it; a reader may see his love and the talk that disperses it, but the poem anchors no such pairing, so the dune is scene.

colophon.thurai: வரைவு நீட்டித்தவழி தோழி தலைமகற்குச் சொல்லி வரைவு கடாயது

thinai_evidence.note: waves, dune and shore

occasion.words: வரைவு நீட்டித்தவழி தோழி தலைமகற்குச் சொல்லி வரைவு கடாயது

comparisons.tenor: the drifting sand
her beauty

comparisons.vehicle: மாசு இல் கற்பின் மடவோள் குழவி பேஎய் வாங்கக் கைவிட்டாங்கு
comparisons.tenor: their letting go of modesty

tamil: எழு மாண் அளக்கும் விழு நெதி பெறினும்
reading: The man, his heart set on a journey for wealth, gives it up: stay with her and wealth will not come, go after wealth and union will not stay; between these, my heart, whether you go or not you have a claim to the good; but wealth perishes like the trail of a fish darting through a pond of unwithering flowers, and even if I won a treasure measured seven times over with the wide wet world as the grain measure, I would have killed the sweet gentle look of her red-lined rain-eyes that suit her heavy earrings; let wealth be whatever it may.
nuance: The poem is a dilemma argued out, and the choice turns on what each side loses: wealth leaves no trace, like a fish's path in water, while going would destroy a look no measure of treasure could buy back. The world used as a grain measure makes the refusal absolute.

colophon.thurai: பொருள் கடைக்கூட்டிய நெஞ்சினை நெருங்கித் தலைவன் செலவு அழுங்கியது

thinai_evidence.note: a journey for wealth weighed and given up

occasion.words: பொருள் கடைக்கூட்டிய நெஞ்சினை நெருங்கித் தலைவன் செலவு அழுங்கியது

comparisons.tenor: wealth
the measure of the treasure

tamil: அகல் இருங் கானத்து அல்கு அணி நோக்கி
ஏந்து எழில் மழைக் கண் கலுழ்தலின் அன்னை
எவன் செய்தனையோ நின் இலங்கு எயிறு உண்கு என
வான் தோய் வெற்பன் மார்பு அணங்கு எனவே
reading: The heroine tells her friend, in words meant for others too, that when, gazing at the beauty lingering in the wide dark forest of the tall hill where the day's rain fell and the falls come down like the waves of the great sea, her lifted lovely rain-eyes wept, the water swirling and not stopping though she tried to hold it, her mother asked 'what have you done? let me kiss your shining teeth', and at such soft sweet words she nearly forgot the modesty dearer than life and almost said that what afflicted her was the chest of the man of the sky-touching hill, where the sapphire-coloured bee that sucked the kanthal on the slope hums like a sweet strung lute; she escaped saying it.
nuance: Kindness, not threat, nearly breaks her secret: the mother's tenderness is the danger. The bee that sucked the kanthal and now hums sweetly may be read as the man who enjoyed her and goes on content, but the poem gives only that one match, so it is a near miss for ullurai and stays scene. 'Modesty dearer than life' is the ranking the Tholkappiyam itself states.

thinai_evidence.note: falls, kanthal and the hill man

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: said to the friend so that another may hear; the colophon does not name who overhears

comparisons.tenor: the falls
the humming bee

tamil: முழு வலி முள் எயிறு அழுத்திய கதவின்
திரை தபு கடலின் இனிது கண் படுப்ப
reading: The friend tells the heroine, unable to bear the parting, that he will come and the many sorrows of her troubled heart will leave: he crossed the hill whose single shining waterfall is like the lone tusk of a war elephant whose fury is spent after its must was washed off, in the war camp of Poraiyan of the victorious spear and unconquerable army, lord of Thondi of the seaside grove whose gate has Moovan's thorn-sharp teeth pressed into it, where the sleepless warriors who make hearts tremble sleep sweetly like a sea whose waves have stilled.
nuance: The whole picture is of rest after violence (an elephant calmed when its must is washed, warriors who never sleep sleeping like a stilled sea), so the friend wraps her promise of return in a war that is over. Moovan's teeth set in Thondi's gate are a war trophy remembered in a love poem.

thinai_evidence.note: comfort to a woman whose man has crossed the hills

comparisons.tenor: the sleeping warriors

comparisons.vehicle: கடாஅம் கழீஇய கதன் அடங்கு யானைத் தடாஅ நிலை ஒரு கோட்டன்ன
comparisons.tenor: the single waterfall

tamil: இறவுப் புறத்து அன்ன பிணர் படு தடவு முதல்
பெருங் களிற்று மருப்பின் அன்ன அரும்பு முதிர்பு
விழவுக் களம் கமழும் உரவு நீர்ச் சேர்ப்ப
இன மணி நெடுந் தேர் பாகன் இயக்க
reading: To the man who has met her and is leaving, the friend says: lord of the shore of strong waters, where the thazhai with leaves thorny like a shark's horn, its rough bent trunk like a prawn's back and its buds ripening like a great tusker's tusks, stands out like a fine deer apart from the herd and fills the festival ground with scent, if you are going, your charioteer driving the tall chariot of clustered bells, then go, knowing well that she will not live through the few days until you come back.
nuance: The leave is granted only in form (செலீஇய சேறி ஆயின் ... சென்மே): 'go' brackets a sentence of death, which turns the farewell into a demand for marriage. The thazhai whose scent fills the festival ground is read by some as a love that can no longer stay hidden; the poem anchors no such pairing, so it is scene. Line 4's comparison is unsure.

colophon.thurai: புணர்ந்து நீங்கிய தலைவனைத் தோழி வரைவு கடாயது

comparisons.tenor: the thazhai's trunk
the thazhai's thorny leaves
the thazhai's buds
the thazhai standing apart

reading: To the husband back from another woman who says he knows no one, the heroine says: sir, I saw the young girl; having passed the night asleep on the lord's chest, her hair fragrant with honey-dripping kadamba blossom, her gait swaying, her cloth fluttering, her tight bangles jingling as she swung her arms, she went off down the street turning her flower-like kohl eyes to look about, long may the girl live, wearing bright jewels over her many fine spots, her drooping earring crushed in the chest-to-chest embrace, her garland withered on shoulders where an old longing has settled, she who clung like a creeper.
nuance: She never accuses; she describes, and the description is the evidence (the crushed earring, the withered garland, a night on 'the lord's chest'), closed by a blessing (வாழிய மடந்தை) that is pure irony. The colophon's second reading gives the speech to the friend, but the address ஐய, 'sir', fits the husband better.

colophon.thurai: பரத்தையிற்பிரிந்து வந்த தலைமகன் யாரையும் அறியேன் என்றாற்குத் தலைவி சொல்லியது வாயிலாகப் புக்க தோழிதலைவிக்குச் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: a wife answering a husband's denial of another woman

occasion.words: பரத்தையிற்பிரிந்து வந்த தலைமகன் யாரையும் அறியேன் என்றாற்குத் தலைவி சொல்லியது

comparisons.tenor: her kohl eyes

title: natrinai 21-40
theme: Natrinai 21 to 40: short poems across the five lands, the friend's voice above all; she presses the man to marry, pleads his case to the girl, mocks the god called to the veri and the husband who denies his women, and reports the girl's tears; men going for wealth and returning, a mother whose daughter has gone with her lover, a courtesan jeering at the husband's midnight visit to his son, with Korkai, Maranthai, Koodal and Kaandavaayil as measures of beauty and home.
source_issues: Natrinai colophons give speaker, addressee and occasion in prose; thurai_akam follows them, and where they name no addressee (29, 34, 40) the code is pira with a note.
23: the colophon thinai is குறிஞ்சி, but the poem's only native things are of the Korkai shore (pearls, neythal) and its situation is the girl's grief; I infer neythal.
28: the colophon thinai is பாலை; the poem has only hill things (falls, vengai, bamboo) and no road, so I infer kurinji, keeping pirithal as the uri.
32: the colophon has the friend speak to the girl, but the poem addresses வாழி தோழி; the friend may be so addressed, so I keep the colophon's speaker.
40: the colophon's தலைமகட்குச் பாங்காயினார் has ச் before ப, apparently a misprint for தலைமகட்குப்.
22 line 10, 37 line 4, 40 line 6: the lost -ஒடு vowel sign restored (text flag); 32 line 4, 36 line 9, 39 line 10: tamilvu.org readings replace ours (text flag); 31 line 5 repeats as 311 line 7.

tamil: விரைப் பரி வருந்திய வீங்கு செலல் இளையர்
அரைச் செறி கச்சை யாப்பு அழித்து அசைஇ
தீண்டா வை முள் தீண்டி நாம் செலற்கு
அரிக் குரல் மிடற்ற அம் நுண் பல் பொறிக்
பெயல் நீர் போகிய வியல் நெடும் புறவில்
reading: Returning with his work done, the man tells his charioteer to let the weary attendants loosen their tight girdles and come on slowly at their own pace, and to use the goad he has never had to use and drive on, and bids him look at the forest cock, its throat speckled like milk sprinkled on melted ghee, which on the wide scrubland the rains have left scratches up the wet sand for its morning food and stands looking to its hen.
nuance: The man is easy on his tired men while hurrying himself, and he gives the poem's last words, 'noble bearing' (பெருந்தகு நிலை), to the bird, not to himself: his longing for his wife is shown only through what he points the charioteer to.

thinai_evidence.note: the forest cock on the rain-washed scrubland and the hero's homecoming fix mullai

thurai_akam.note: the addressee is the charioteer (வலவ, line 5)

comparisons.tenor: the speckles on the cock's throat

iraicchi.act: the cock scratches up the wet sand for the day's food and, having caught it, stands looking to its hen

tamil: முந்து விளை பெருங் குரல் கொண்ட மந்தி
திரை அணற் கொடுங் கவுள் நிறைய முக்கி
கயம் கண் அற்ற பைது அறு காலை
reading: The friend tells the girl that the man has come, the lord of the land where a female monkey, taking the first-ripened heavy heads of the millet a hill girl guards, climbs the rock with her untaught mate and, crushing them in her palms and stuffing her cheeks, looks like rain-soaked ascetics eating from their hands; his coming is like rain pouring at midnight on paddy shrivelled in its sheath in a dry season when the ponds have lost their water.
nuance: The rain is timed to the last moment: it falls on paddy already shrivelled, at midnight when no one looks for it. The monkey who steals the guarded millet's first heads with her mate is a near miss for ullurai (only one pair, the guarded crop to the guarded girl, maps cleanly), so it is scene and simile here.

thinai_evidence.note: the hill girl's millet and the monkeys of the rock fix kurinji

comparisons.tenor: the female monkey crouched with millet in her cheeks and her back wet with rain
the man's coming to marry her

tamil: இடிப்பு மெய்யது ஒன்று உடைத்தே கடிக் கொள
reading: Pressing the man to marry, the friend says the girl's shoulders escaped blame because her bangles hid their thinness, and her loosened hair has the excuse of play with her companions, but her eyes, which besides weeping each time they see the old beauty her mother watches over wasting away, have faded like the small-leaved neythal flower in the clear water of Korkai's pearl-bearing harbour, cannot hide love.
nuance: The friend sorts the signs into those an excuse can cover (bangles, hair) and the one that cannot (the eyes); line 3 (இடிப்பு மெய்யது ஒன்று உடைத்தே) is hard, and the hair's excuse is my reading of it.

colophon.thurai: தலைவி துயர் ஆற்றாமை உணர்ந்த தோழி வரைவு கடாயது

thinai_evidence.note: the poem's only native things are of the Korkai shore, and its situation is the girl's grief that cannot be hidden

comparisons.tenor: her eyes, which have lost their brightness

tamil: பார் பக வீழ்ந்த வேருடை விழுக் கோட்டு
ஆட்டு ஒழி பந்தின் கோட்டு மூக்கு இறுபு
வெள்ளில் வல்சி வேற்று நாட்டு ஆர் இடைச்
reading: The woman tells her friend, who said 'good' when the man said they would go to the hard tract of a strange land, where wood-apple trees, their trunks rough as if monitor lizards clung to them, drop fruit like balls left after play, their stalks snapped, onto green creepers spread like a blanket, and wood-apple is the only food, that she did well: men whose minds are set on action leave for the wealth to be made, and that is their nature.
nuance: The colophon says she speaks with joy, and the maxim is given as approval; set beside the many parting poems in which the woman refuses, the praise may also be read as bitter, and the poem does not settle which.

colophon.thurai: பொருட்பிரிவுக்கு உடன்பட்ட தோழியைத் தலைவி உவந்து கூறியது

thinai_evidence.note: the man's going for wealth across a hard tract is pirithal

comparisons.tenor: the rough-barked trunk of the wood-apple
the fallen wood-apple fruit
the green creepers spread on the ground

tamil: செவ் வரி இதழ சேண் நாறு பிடவின்
நறுந் தாது ஆடிய தும்பி பசுங் கேழ்ப்
பொன் உரை கல்லின் நல் நிறம் பெறூஉம்
கிளை மலி சிறு தினைக் கிளி கடிந்து அசைஇ
அல்லல் அன்று அது காதல் அம் தோழி
தாது உண் வேட்கையின் போது தெரிந்து ஊதா
reading: Pleading the man's case, the friend tells the girl that the lord of the rich hill, where a bee dusted with the fragrant pollen of the pidavu, whose red-veined petals look like lac drawn on the back of a conch bangle, takes on the colour of a touchstone rubbed with gold, chased the parrots from the millet with them yesterday and, finding no chance to speak, went away; his going is not sorrow but love, and having seen his unwearied gaze, like a bee that, craving pollen, does not pick among the buds, she now thinks of her own graceless act of pressing back her slipping bangle.
nuance: The friend speaks as if the man's silent plea and her own refusal (the bangle pressed back) were hers, which lets her press his case without naming the girl's feelings; whether the 'graceless act' is the friend's or the girl's is not certain from the Tamil.

thinai_evidence.note: chasing parrots from the hill millet is the kurinji courtship scene

comparisons.tenor: the red-veined petals of the pidavu
the bee dusted with pollen
the man's unwearied gaze

tamil: விண்டுப் புரையும் புணர் நிலை நெடுங் கூட்டுப்
சுடர் முழுது எறிப்பத் திரங்கிச் செழுங் காய்
கெடு துணை ஆகிய தவறோ வை எயிற்று
reading: To keep the man from going, the friend asks: shall I grieve? her bangles have slipped; would it be a wrong if she, of the sharp white teeth, the gold-like spots, the full dark hair and broad shoulders, left her mother's house, with its tall granary of paddy, white-based and spotted, like a hill, to be your companion, even one who perishes, on the dry tract where under the full sun the jackfruit shrivels on the bent old tree?
nuance: The friend stops the journey by offering the girl as a fellow traveller, which the man must refuse; the rich granary of the mother's house is set against the shrivelled fruit of the road. Line 7 (கெடு துணை ஆகிய தவறோ) can also mean 'is it her fault that she has become a lost companion', and I cannot fix which.

colophon.thurai: தலைவி பிரிவு உணர்ந்து வேறுபட்டமை சொல்லி தோழி செலவு அழுங்குவித்தது

thinai_evidence.note: the man's going across the sun-burnt tract is pirithal

comparisons.tenor: the tall granary of the mother's house
the spots on her skin

tamil: ஒழி திரை வரித்த வெண் மணல் அடைகரைக்
கரந்து நாம் செய்தது ஒன்று இல்லை உண்டு எனின்
இற ஆர் இனக் குருகு ஒலிப்ப சுறவம்
கழி சேர் மருங்கின் கணைக் கால் நீடி
கண் போல் பூத்தமை கண்டு நுண் பல
reading: With the man listening nearby, the friend tells the girl that yesterday they only played in the grove by the backwater, on the white sand the waves had lined, chasing off the bees that sprinkle fine pollen, and did nothing in secret, or if they did, no one else knew; so what did mother mean when she said, 'do not go and pluck the small-leaved neythal that, on long stems by the backwaters where the herons cry in flocks and sharks come, has bloomed like eyes'?
nuance: The mother's ban on picking flowers is the girl's confinement told sideways, so that the man overhearing learns the meetings are over; the reversed simile (flowers like eyes) puts watching eyes on every stem.

thinai_evidence.note: the backwater grove, its herons, sharks and neythal fix the shore

comparisons.tenor: the neythal flowers

tamil: தன் கைக் கொண்டு என் நல் நுதல் நீவியும்
மணி என இழிதரும் அருவி பொன் என
ஆடு கழை நிவந்த பைங் கண் மூங்கில்
reading: The speaker says that the lord of the high-ridged hill, where falls drop like gems, the vengai spreads like gold over the slopes and swaying green bamboo rises to tear the running clouds, took her hand and pressed it to his eyes, stroked her brow with his own hand and spoke sweetly like a mother, yet he is cruel as thieves.
nuance: The two similes are set against each other in successive lines: like a mother, like thieves; the man's tender acts are the evidence for his cruelty, since they are what make his absence hurt.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவின்கண் ஆற்றாளாகிய தலைவிக்குத் தோழி சொல்லியது - குறை நயப்பும் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the poem has only hill things; separation is implied only by 'cruel'

thurai_akam.note: on this reading the friend tells how the man courted her, to press his case

comparisons.tenor: his sweet words
the man, cruel after his tenderness
the falling water
the spread vengai blossom

tamil: அழல் அவிர் நீள் இடை நிழலிடம் பெறாஅது
ஈன்று கான் மடிந்த பிணவுப் பசி கூர்ந்தென
புலி பார்த்து உறையும் புல் அதர்ச் சிறு நெறி
வனைந்து ஏந்து இள முலை நோவகொல் என
பேர் அமர் மழைக் கண் ஈரிய கலுழ
reading: The mother whose daughter has gone with her lover asks how the girl can manage the narrow grassy track where, in the lingering summer, the kanthal has withered, the long blazing stretch gives no shade, and a tiger, its mate starving after giving birth, waits in the dim evening to kill travellers, when at home, if her mother merely loosened her embrace for fear of hurting her young breasts, she would weep from her large rain-dark eyes and sigh hotly, that gentle girl of dark hair and great innocence.
nuance: The tiger hunting for its starving mate is a male providing for its mate, but striking its lines leaves the mother's question with no road to ask about, so it fails the deletion test and stays scene; the poem's weight is the contrast between a loosened hug and the tiger's track.

thinai_evidence.note: summer heat, shadelessness and the tiger on the track fix paalai

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no addressee; the mother speaks to those about her

tamil: கவல் ஏமுற்ற வெய்து வீழ் அரிப் பனி
reading: To the husband who says he knows no other woman, the friend says she has seen it, and what can she do: on the fine street where his bard's little lute hums like bees, the decked women who had laid claim to his chest stood watching for him to pass, and like the many who, when the ship capsizes in a gale, cling together to one plank with hot tears falling, they pull him this way and that in endless distress.
nuance: The shipwreck makes the man a plank, one object many lives cling to, so the friend's mockery deflates both his denial and his importance; the bard's lute, which announces his coming, is what gives him away.

colophon.thurai: பரத்தையிற் பிரிந்து வந்த தலைவன் யாரையும் அறியேன் என்றார்க்குத் தோழி சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the friend confronts the husband over the other women: oodal

comparisons.tenor: the hum of the bard's lute

comparisons.vehicle: கடல்மரம் கவிழ்ந்தெனக் கலங்கி உடன் வீழ்பு பலர் கொள் பலகை போல
comparisons.tenor: the women fighting over the man

tamil: மா இரும் பரப்பு அகம் துணிய நோக்கி
பாய் இரும் பனிக் கழி துழைஇ பைங் கால்
பெரும் புலம்பு உற்ற நெஞ்சமொடு பல நினைந்து
வேறு பல் நாட்டில் கால் தர வந்த
பல உறு பண்ணியம் இழிதரு நிலவு மணல்
நெடுஞ் சினை புன்னை கடுஞ் சூல் வெண் குருகு
reading: With the man standing nearby, the girl answers her friend's reassurance: the shore of small-flowered njaazhal, where a little white sea crow, having struck a red prawn after scanning the wide dark water, searches the cold backwater and calls to the mate it loves, would be sweet to her too, were she not grieving, thinking many things with a lonely heart, until she is married to the lord of the strong-watered shore, where goods brought by the wind from many lands are unloaded on the moonlit sand and a heavy-bellied white heron on the long-branched punnai fears the roaming tide.
nuance: The pregnant heron that fears the tide is close to the girl's own fear, but only that one pair maps, so it is scene. Line 5 recurs as Natrinai 311 line 7.

colophon.thurai: தலைவன் சிறைப்புறத்தானாக தலைவி வன்புறை எதிர் அழிந்தது

thinai_evidence.note: backwater, punnai, heron and the lord of the shore fix neythal

iraicchi.act: the male sea crow, having caught a red prawn, searches the backwater and calls the mate it loves to share it
iraicchi.sense: even the shore bird provides for and calls its mate, while the man has not yet married the girl

tamil: அம் மலை கிழவோன் நம் நயந்து என்றும்
வருந்தினன் என்பது ஓர் வாய்ச் சொல் தேறாய்
reading: The friend tells the girl that the lord of the hill, whose great slope is dark like Mayon and whose falls are bright white like Valiyon, desires them and has long suffered, yet she will not trust that true word: let her see him herself, weigh it with her people, learn his mind and judge, since once accepted it is hard to undo; the great take a friend only after inquiry, and do not inquire after they have befriended.
nuance: The closing maxim belongs to friendship (நட்பு), and the friend uses it in both directions at once: inquire, because once he is accepted there is no going back; the dark god and the white god give the hill its colours before any argument begins.

thinai_evidence.note: the great hill and its falls fix kurinji

comparisons.tenor: the dark slope of the great hill
the bright white waterfall

tamil: படு சுடர் அடைந்த பகு வாய் நெடு வரை
நிறை பெயல் அறியாக் குன்றத்து ஊண் அல்லில்
துவர் செய் ஆடை செந் தொடை மறவர்
நல் அக வன முலைக் கரை சேர்பு
மல்கு புனல் பரந்த மலர் ஏர் கண்ணே
reading: The friend tells the man that the girl, sobbing, looked into her face and said 'if he means to cross the fearful path where, when the setting sun reaches the cleft hills and evening spreads over the hamlet on the gravel, by the dreary common where loneliness feeds, in hills that have never known full rain, where muddy water is drawn from stony pits, bowmen in dyed cloth with arrows on the string lie in wait for travellers, could we, soft as we are, stop him?', and her flower-like eyes brimmed and overflowed onto her breasts.
nuance: The friend reports the girl's words rather than pleading herself, so the girl's question (could we stop him?) reaches him as a fact already decided: she has not asked him to stay, only wept.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவு உணர்த்தப்பட்ட தலைமகளது குறிப்பு அறிந்த தோழி தலைமகற்குச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the man's intended crossing of the bandit path is pirithal

comparisons.tenor: her eyes

tamil: குருதி ஒண் பூ உரு கெழக் கட்டி
மார்பு தர வந்த படர் மலி அரு நோய்
reading: Speaking as if to the god, the friend tells Murugan that the heavy lovesickness was given by the chest of the lord of the land where a nymph, wearing a garland of the unplucked blue lilies of the god's rock spring and blood-bright kanthal, dances to the sweet music of the falls on the great slope; knowing it is not his seizure, he still came, wearing a kadampu garland, to the veri house at the velan's call: god he may be, but he is surely a fool.
nuance: The friend's speech to the god is meant for the household, which has called the velan; by telling Murugan he knows the sickness is not his, she tells them where it came from (the hill lord's chest) without naming the man to them.

thinai_evidence.note: the hill spring, kanthal, the hill nymph and the velan's veri rite fix kurinji

tamil: பொங்கு திரை பொருத வார் மணல் அடை கரைப்
புன் கால் நாவல் பொதிப் புற இருங் கனி
கிளை செத்து மொய்த்த தும்பி பழம் செத்துப்
பல் கால் அலவன் கொண்ட கோட்கு அசாந்து
துறை கெழு மரந்தை அன்ன இவள் நலம்
reading: The day after the wedding, when the groom thanks her for keeping the girl well, the friend says that the girl's beauty, like that of Maranthai with its harbour, where on the long wave-beaten sandbank a bee takes the dark fruit of the naval for its kin and swarms on it, a crab takes the bee for fruit and seizes it, and the bee's buzz, like an untuned string, draws the prey-seeking heron, which lets them go, was always so, as he can see; but though he has not left her side, has her beauty slackened a little, or is it love, like the elation of toddy-drinkers, that has paled her eyes?
nuance: The chain of mistakes on the shore (bee taking fruit for kin, crab taking bee for fruit, heron letting all go) is a traditional site for hidden meaning, but no two of its parts map firmly onto the wedding situation, so it stays scene; the friend turns the groom's thanks back on him by giving the pallor to love rather than to her care.

colophon.thurai: மணமகனைப் பிற்றை ஞான்று புக்க தோழி நன்கு ஆற்றுவித்தாய் என்ற தலைமகற்குச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the wave-beaten sandbank, its crab and heron fix the shore

comparisons.tenor: the bee's buzzing

her love

tamil: குறுங் கை இரும் புலிக் கோள் வல் ஏற்றை
பூ நுதல் இரும் பிடி புலம்ப தாக்கி
தாழ் நீர் நனந் தலை பெருங் களிறு அடூஉம்
புரை இல் தீ மொழி பயிற்றிய உரை எடுத்து
தான் என் இழந்தது இவ் அழுங்கல் ஊரே
reading: With the man listening at the night tryst, the friend says that, trusting the word of the hill lord, in whose land a short-legged tiger, strong to kill, strikes down a great tusker in a deep pool so that his flower-browed mate is left to grieve, they have lost their beauty, while the noisy town, joining the gossiping women's whispers at midnight and taking up their wicked talk, has made an endless scandal of it: what has the town itself lost?
nuance: The tiger could instead be the man, whose word has cost them their beauty; either way the scene of the killing and the lone mate is not joined to the speech by any marker.

thinai_evidence.note: the tiger, the elephants and the hill lord fix kurinji

pairs.situation: the slandering town, which strikes at night
the lovers' bond struck down
the girl left lonely and grieving

ullurai.speaker_fit: the friend uses beasts of the hill in a kurinji poem (porul 7.27)

tamil: பிணங்கு அரில் வாடிய பழ விறல் நனந் தலை
உணங்கு ஊண் ஆயத்து ஓர் ஆன் தெள் மணி
நீர் சூழ் மா மலர் அன்ன கண் அழ
அணங்குடை அருந் தலை உடலி வலன் ஏர்பு
reading: The friend tells the man, who is leaving with the marriage put off, that it would be good if he took the sharp-toothed girl with him across the old wide wilds, where the tangled thickets have withered and a single cow's clear bell tinkles softly in a herd grazing on dry fodder; but if he leaves without love, so that her eyes like great water-girt blue lilies weep and she is distraught like a doe deserted by its stag, her grief will be more than the friend can bear when the rain-making evening comes, with the roaring thunder that strikes the dread heads of serpents as it wanders the sky.
nuance: The friend's threat is the rainy evening of mullai, the season of waiting, carried into a poem of the dry road: the danger she names is not the wilds but the evening at home.

thinai_evidence.note: the man's leaving across the dry wilds before marriage is pirithal

comparisons.tenor: her eyes
the girl, distraught when he leaves

tamil: இரும் பனந் தீம் பிழி உண்போர் மகிழும்
ஆர் கலி யாணர்த்து ஆயினும் தேர் கெழு
ஒலி கா ஓலை முள் மிடை வேலி
வெள் மணல் படப்பை எம் அழுங்கல் ஊரே
reading: The girl answers her friend's reassurance: though their noisy town, Kaandavaayil, with its gardens ringed by the backwater, its fences of thorny palm-leaf over which the palmyra climbs and its white sands, is full of bustle and plenty, the catch never failing, the nets rich, the rains never failing, the fishermen bartering and drinkers merry on sweet palm toddy, it turns desolate if the lord of the shore with his chariot leaves her.
nuance: The prosperity is listed only to be cancelled: the whole loud town weighs less than one man's going, and the closing 'our noisy town' (அழுங்கல் ஊர்) is the same noise heard as loneliness.

thinai_evidence.note: fishermen, nets, palmyra and backwater fix the shore

tamil: சொல்லின் சொல் எதிர் கொள்ளாய் யாழ நின்
கொடுங் கேழ் இரும் புறம் நடுங்கக் குத்தி
தலை மருப்பு ஏய்ப்ப கடை மணி சிவந்த நின்
அரண் தலை மதிலர் ஆகவும் முரசு கொண்டு
ஓம்பு அரண் கடந்த அடு போர் செழியன்
reading: At their second meeting the man tells the girl that she does not answer his words and bows her lovely face in shame, yet when love overflows is it easy to hold back? her eyes, red at the corners like the tusk tips of an elephant reeking of flesh after a tiger has gored its dark back and toyed with it, are not angry, but her shoulders painted with sugarcane designs, like the great-named Koodal of Cheliyan who took the drums and crossed the guarded walls of foes, overpower him, bright goddess.
nuance: Both similes are of violence (the gored elephant's bloody tusk, the conqueror's city), turned on a shy girl who says nothing: the man reads his own defeat in her body, and calls her அணங்கு, a power that strikes.

thinai_evidence.note: the tiger and the elephant of the hill and a meeting of the lovers fix kurinji

comparisons.tenor: the red corners of her eyes
her painted shoulders

tamil: நெடு நா ஒள் மணி கடி மனை இரட்ட
குரை இலைப் போகிய விரவு மணற் பந்தர்
பெரும் பாண் காவல் பூண்டென ஒரு சார்
வெறி உற விரிந்த அறுவை மெல் அணைப்
சீர் கெழு மடந்தை ஈர் இமை பொருந்த
reading: The other woman says, within hearing of the wife's attendants, that at the guarded house where the long-tongued bell rings, the sand-strewn pandal is roofed with leaves, great bards keep watch and decked women stand on one side seeking omens, while the boy sleeps on a soft bed under spread cloth beside a nurse smelling of new birth and the noble mother, bathed in ghee with white mustard, soft-bodied, has shut both eyes, the lord of the wide-ford town too came at midnight like a thief, because a son was born bearing his grandfather's name.
nuance: The 'too' (ஊரனும்) sets the husband among the other night visitors to a guarded house; the courtesan describes the birth-house rites in close detail, so her mockery shows she knows the household from outside.

thinai_evidence.note: the other woman's jibe at the husband's furtive visit to his own house is oodal

thurai_akam.speaker: parathai
thurai_akam.note: she speaks to her own companions; the overhearers are the wife's attendants

comparisons.tenor: the husband coming to his own house at midnight

title: natrinai 41-60
theme: Natrinai 41-60 across all five lands: men leaving for wealth and the friend's arguments for and against it (41, 43, 46, 48, 52), homecomings seen by the returning man (42, 59), the girl kept at home and the veri rite misreading her sickness (47, 51, 53, 57, 60), the friend's tricks and rebuffs (45, 50, 55, 58), and the woman alone with her heart, her evening and a heron (54, 56).
source_issues: 43 line 1 is the same as natrinai 99 line 2 (flagged repeated_line); marked as written, as a shared formula for the shimmering heat.
42 line 2 (அறத்தொடு வருந்திய அல்கு தொழில் கொளீஇய) is obscure: whose labour and what dwelling are meant cannot be fixed; the verse is marked uncertain.
46 line 6: பாணர் அயிர்ப்புக் கொண்டன்ன is obscure (what of the bards the kondrai pods resemble); the comparison is recorded with basis uru and the verse is marked uncertain.
48: who is included in எம் (the friend with the heroine, or the heroine's words in the friend's mouth) is uncertain, as is the reading of lines 8-9 as the elopement; marked uncertain.
50 lines 5-7: who is jostled and what யாணது பசலை means are uncertain; marked uncertain.
51 line 7 (பின்னு விடு முச்சி அளிப்பு ஆனாதே) is uncertain: whose caress, the mother's or the velan's; marked uncertain.
51: the colophon names no speaker; the speaker is taken as the heroine from வேறுபட்டாள் and the poem's address to தோழி.
56 ends on the participle தலைமணந்த, with the inverted order of poetry (நோய் தலைமணந்த qualifying the heart of line 5); no line seems lost.
44, 49, 53, 54, 56, 59, 60: lines repaired by show (tamilvu.org reading, lost -ஒடு vowel sign, ஃ encoding) are marked as repaired.

tamil: பைங் கண் யானை பரூஉ தாள் உதைத்த
வெண் புறக் களரி விடு நீறு ஆடி
கிளர் இழை அரிவை நெய் துழந்து அட்ட
விளர் ஊன் அம் புகை எறிந்த நெற்றி
reading: The friend steadies the wife by the way of the world: men go far and suffer in the waste, easing their weariness only at a small gravel-choked well after an elephant's kick has raised the salt dust, because they want the life in which a young wife, her forehead pricked with sweat from the smoke of ghee-stirred meat, cooks for a guest of good name who arrives at night.
nuance: The friend's comfort is not that he will soon return but that his suffering has a purpose she can picture: the household's hospitality. The close-up of sweat on the wife's forehead puts the reward of his journey in her own kitchen, so the absence is reframed as work done for her house.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவு உணர்த்தப்பட்டு ஆற்றாளாய தலைமகளைத் தோழி உலகியல் கூறி வற்புறுத்தியது

thinai_evidence.note: the man goes far away and suffers on the waste for the household's sake

tamil: மறத்தற்கு அரிது ஆல் பாக பல் நாள்
பழ மழை பொழிந்த புது நீர் அவல
நா நவில் பல் கிளை கறங்க மாண் வினை
சில் போது கொண்டு பல் குரல் அழுத்திய
மட மா அரிவை மகிழ்ந்து அயர் நிலையே
reading: Returning from his task, the man tells his charioteer he cannot forget how, because the croaking of the frogs in the rain-filled hollows would drown the chariot's bells, the servants ran ahead to tell her, and she quickly washed her unwashed hair, pressed a few flowers into it and, without fuss, embraced him in her joy.
nuance: Sending the servants ahead is a courtesy to her: she is spared being found unkempt. The poem's whole picture is the few minutes between the warning and the embrace, a domestic haste the hero treasures more than the welcome itself.

thinai_evidence.note: the first rains filling the hollows as the man comes home from his task

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the addressee is the charioteer (பாகன்)

tamil: பைங் கண் யானை வேந்து புறத்து இறுத்தலின்
reading: The friend tells the man that crossing the waste, where in heat that shimmers like spread cloth a starving red dog kills a weary wild cow and its leftovers feed travellers, is a joy to him, but for her, hearing of his going, ruin has come, like the king of a single fort whose overlord, after saying 'fear not', abandoned him when an elephant-led army laid siege and his broken wall found no defender.
nuance: The simile turns the hero's earlier promise into the overlord's 'fear not' (அஞ்சல் என்ற இறை): she is the vassal fort he pledged to protect, and his departure is the abandonment. The only food on the road is a predator's leftovers, the measure of what he trades her for.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவு உணர்த்தப்பட்ட தோழி தலைவனைச் செலவு அழுங்குவித்தது

thinai_evidence.note: the man's announced journey across the hot waste

comparisons.tenor: the glare of the heat over the hill slope
the woman abandoned by the man who promised her protection

tamil: நீர் அலைச் சிவந்த பேர் அமர் மழைக் கண்
நீடு இலை விளை தினை கொடுங் கால் நிமிரக்
கொழுங் குரல் கோடல் கண்ணி செழும் பல
பல் கிளைக் குறவர் அல்கு அயர் முன்றில்
பல் மர உயர் சினை மின்மினி விளக்கத்து
reading: Kept from her after her confinement, the man at the meeting place asks his heart whether the daughter of the hill lord, who bathed in the falls with her companions until her large eyes reddened, gave him an unaimed glance and a smile and went home, can know what it longs for, in the land where kuravar wearing kodal garlands rest in their yards after the millet harvest and by the light of fireflies in the jackfruit groves watch the clouds pass.
nuance: குறியா நோக்கம், a look not aimed at him, is all he has to go on, and the question to his heart is whether that look meant anything. The closing scene of people at ease in their yards watching clouds by firefly light is the leisure he no longer has.

colophon.thurai: இச்செறிப்பின் பிற்றை ஞான்று தலைமகன் குறியிடத்து வந்து சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the hill people, the millet harvest and the waterfall

tamil: நீல் நிறப் பெருங் கடல் கலங்க உள்புக்கு
இனப் புள் ஒப்பும் எமக்கு நலன் எவனோ
பெரு நீர் விளையுள் எம் சிறு நல் வாழ்க்கை
reading: The friend turns the suitor away: she is the daughter of fishermen of the shore hamlet who go out into the blue sea to spear fish, and he the dear son of a rich man of the old market town of long flags and swift chariots; we who drive birds off the shark meat we dry smell of fish, so move on, for our small life from the sea is no match for yours, though our people too have their men of worth.
nuance: The rebuff is pride dressed as humility: she lists their fish smell and small life only to end on செம்மலும் உடைத்தே, 'we too have our nobles'. The test is whether the rich man's son will persist across the difference of station.

thinai_evidence.note: the fishing people and their dried shark

tamil: எய் கணை நிழலின் கழியும் இவ் உலகத்து
அயிர்ப்புக் கொண்டன்ன கொன்றை அம் தீம் கனி
பறை அறை கடிப்பின் அறை அறையாத் துயல்வர
வெவ் வளி வழங்கும் வேய் பயில் அழுவத்து
மன்னாப் பொருட் பிணிப் பிரிதும் யாம் எனவே
reading: The friend tells the man who has announced his going that pleasure and youth pass day by day like the shadow of a shot arrow, which he cannot claim not to see, yet he will not cherish them: he says he will leave her jewelled breast lonely, crossing the hard waste where the hot wind blows through the bamboo and the kondrai pods swing like drumsticks beating, held by the desire for wealth that does not last.
nuance: Her argument uses the moralist's premise, that youth and pleasure are fleeting, to reach the lover's conclusion: what passes must be enjoyed now, and it is the wealth (மன்னாப் பொருள்) that is the impermanent thing. The image of the bards (line 6) is obscure; the drumstick image beside it is clear.

thinai_evidence.note: the man announces that he will leave for wealth

comparisons.tenor: pleasure and youth passing day by day
the sweet kondrai pods
the kondrai pods swinging in the hot wind

tamil: பெருங் களிறு உழுவை அட்டென இரும் பிடி
கானக நாடற்கு இது என யான் அது
வெறி என உணர்ந்த உள்ளமொடு மறி அறுத்து
reading: With the man listening, the friend asks the girl what harm there would be in telling the lord of the forest land, where a cow elephant whose great tusker a tiger has killed cannot move for grief and suffers like one gravely wounded, holding her calf with ears like green neythal leaves, that the mother, misreading the sign of the molucca beans as possession, kills a kid for the Murugu rite that cannot help her gold-like pallor.
nuance: The bereaved elephant shows what the friend fears the girl will become if he does not come to marry her, and the rite shows why no one at home can cure her. Telling him 'this' (இது) is the whole message, and he is standing where he can hear it.

thinai_evidence.note: the tusker and tiger of the forest and the Murugu rite

comparisons.tenor: the calf's ears
the cow elephant's suffering
the girl's pallor

ullurai.tenor: the girl, left to waste if her lover is lost to her

pairs.situation: the loss of the lover, which is what she faces if he does not come to marry her
the girl, kept in the house and unable to go to him
her pallor, a wound the mother's rite cannot reach

ullurai.speaker_fit: the friend uses the elephants of the hero's own forest land in a kurinji poem (porul 7.27)

tamil: அன்றை அனைய ஆகி இன்று உம் எம்
புல் இதழ்க் கோங்கின் மெல் இதழ்க் குடைப் பூ
புறவு அணி கொண்ட பூ நாறு கடத்திடை
கிடின் என இடிக்கும் கோல் தொடி மறவர்
reading: The friend tells the man who has announced his parting that even today, as on that day, the forest swirls before their eyes: the soft umbrella blossoms of the kongu shining like the stars at dawn in the flower-scented waste, the bangled bowmen with whetted arrows who came fearlessly at them, whom he drove off in the fight, and the forest where he hid them when their own kin came close.
nuance: The memory is of the elopement, when he fought robbers and hid her from her pursuing kin. Recalling it now, the friend sets his old courage for her against his present wish to leave her; the reproach is never spoken.

thinai_evidence.note: the remembered journey through the forest with the girl he took from her kin

comparisons.tenor: the forest of that day, as vivid as if it were still before their eyes
the kongu blossoms

tamil: படு திரை கொழீஇய பால் நிற எக்கர்த்
முடி வலை முகந்த முடங்கு இறா பரவைப்
மன்றப் புன்னை மா சினை நறு வீ
தெண் கடற் சேர்ப்பன் வாழ் சிறு நல் ஊர்க்கே
reading: The friend tells the girl that the bangled women have gone in from the milk-white dune and the shore is empty, the day has ended with driving birds off the curled prawns spread to dry, and their own men, happy with the sharks they speared, have stopped fishing and gone to rest; so what if they went now, feeling safe, to the small good town of the lord of the clear sea, where the punnai flowers of the common ground mingle their scent with the screwpine of the yard?
nuance: Every clause of the first half closes something down (the women, the shore, the day, the men), and only then does the friend propose they go to him. The stillness of their own people is the permission for the night meeting.

colophon.thurai: தோழி தலைமகளை இரவுக்குறி நயப்பித்தது சிறைப்புறமாகத் தோழி ஆற்றாமை வியந்தூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the dune, the punnai and the screwpine of the shore

tamil: நெடு நிமிர் தெருவில் கை புகு கொடு மிடை
reading: The friend tells the bard how his master, decked in earrings, garland and a small green bangle, jostled her as if a stranger in the narrow press of the long street as she went to join the festival dance, warning her that someone might hear and remarking on pallor, how she answered 'you have no shame, fellow' and came away, and how she had failed to guard the girl because she trusted him, unseeing, as a man even his enemies admire, taking his smallness for greatness.
nuance: The bard comes as go-between, and the friend answers with an incident that shows the master's true size. The last line is her own confession: the fault was trusting without looking.

thinai_evidence.note: the man's revelry at the town festival, for which the friend turns his bard away

tamil: காம்புடை விடர் அகம் சிலம்ப பாம்பு உடன்று
ஓங்கு வரை மிளிர ஆட்டி வீங்கு செலல்
கடுங் குரல் ஏறொடு கனை துளி தலைஇப்
பெருந் தண் குளவி குழைத்த பா அடி
reading: The girl asks her friend what they can do: the rain will not stop, with loud thunder that makes the bamboo clefts ring and angers the snakes and shakes the high hills, and with the rain the velan has come like stretched lightning, and the caressing of her loosened hair goes on, all for the lord of the hill where a killer tusker, its feet soaked in crushed wild jasmine and its forehead caked with mud, has broken the innocent young jackfruit tree among vengai trees strewn with flowers.
nuance: Her fear has two objects: the storm on the path he must take by night, and the rite that will expose her. பேதை ஆசினி, 'the innocent jackfruit', uses a word for a young girl, which marks the broken tree as her own case.

colophon.thurai: ஆற்றது ஏதம் அஞ்சி வேறுபட்டாள் வெறியாடலுற்ற இடத்து சிறைப்புறமாகச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the hill clefts and the storm on the mountain

comparisons.tenor: the velan's sudden arrival

ullurai.tenor: the hill lord and the girl his secret love has wasted

pairs.situation: the hill lord has broken the innocent girl's health
her beauty fallen away, the change the velan is called to cure

ullurai.speaker_fit: the girl uses the tusker and trees of her own hill, things she knows (porul 7.26)

tamil: தூத் தகட்டு எதிர் மலர் வேய்ந்த கூந்தல்
மணம் கமழ் நாற்றம் மரீஇ யாம் இவள்
அன்பு இலை வாழி என் நெஞ்சே வெம் போர்
மழவர் பெரு மகன் மா வள் ஓரி
ஐது ஏகு அம்ம இயைந்து செய் பொருளே
reading: The man answers his heart: he will not leave the embrace of his wife, whose hair is crowned with athiral and fresh pathiri blossoms, but the heart, intent on effort, wants a life of living apart and is never content; it is loveless, for even if wealth came equal to the giving of Ori, the generous lord of the Mazhavar fierce in war, wealth made by toil would be a slight thing.
nuance: The hero measures the most he could gain by a patron's giving and finds it small against one embrace. வாழி, 'long may you live', said to the loveless heart, is an ironic blessing.

thinai_evidence.note: the heart's wish for a life of living apart for wealth

tamil: யான் அஃது அஞ்சினென் கரப்பவும் தான் அஃது
வான் உற நிவந்த பெரு மலைக் கவாஅன்
ஆர் கலி வானம் தலைஇ நடு நாள்
கனை பெயல் பொழிந்தென கானக் கல் யாற்று
முளி இலை கழித்தன முகிழ் இணரொடு வரும்
reading: With the man listening, the friend tells the girl she hid it out of fear but wonders whether the mother knew or simply took pity, for the mother said: the sweet new water of the forest's stony stream, which after midnight rain on the sky-high hill slope comes down with dead leaves and budding clusters, is medicine too; if she drinks it cool, looks on it and bathes in it gladly, her shivering will pass; go.
nuance: The mother prescribes water from the lover's own hill. The friend's question (does she know, or is she being kind?) is meant for the man: if the mother knows, the secret is over and he must marry; if she pities, time is short. பனி is both the chill of fever and the trembling of love.

thinai_evidence.note: midnight rain on the high hill

tamil: இரும் புலா அருந்தும் நின் கிளையொடு சிறிது இருந்து
கருங் கால் வெண் குருகு எனவ கேண்மதி
reading: The woman begs the white heron with black legs, which after feeding in the curving water longs to fly home to its kin, to stay a little with its fish-eating flock and listen: the small dull evening is deeply lonely; if it knows that, it has love too, so let it tell her plight as it is, not with a stranger's heart, to the lord of its shore fenced with kandal, where the young njazhal whose shoots the leaf-skirted girls pluck is caressed by clear waves.
nuance: She calls the shore 'your shore' (நும் துறை), giving the bird a claim on the man that she does not yet have. The heron going home at evening is the very thing she lacks, which is why she asks it to wait.

thinai_evidence.note: evening on the shore of kandal and waves

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the addressee is a heron

tamil: ஓங்கு மலை நாட ஒழிக நின் வாய்மை
காம்பு தலைமணந்த கல் அதர்ச் சிறு நெறி
உறு பகை பேணாது இரவின் வந்து இவள்
பொறி கிளர் ஆகம் புல்ல தோள் சேர்பு
reading: The friend tells the hill lord to keep his truthfulness: he came by night down the stony path among the bamboo, careless of danger, and embraced the girl, and when countless bees swarmed on her from his sandal, the mother looked hard and asked 'were you like this before?'; the girl, unable to answer, looked at the friend's face, and the friend, wondering how she would escape, pointed to a burning sandalwood firebrand and said 'that is what did it'.
nuance: ஒழிக நின் வாய்மை is sarcasm: his honest love has forced the women into a lie. The friend's quick wit saves them once, which is her warning that the night visits cannot go on.

colophon.thurai: வரைவிடை மெலிவு ஆற்றுவிக்கும் தோழி தலைவற்குச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the night visit by the stony hill path

occasion.words: வரைவிடை மெலிவு ஆற்றுவிக்கும் தோழி தலைவற்குச் சொல்லியது

tamil: குறு நிலைக் குரவின் சிறு நனை நறு வீ
வண்டு தரு நாற்றம் வளி கலந்து ஈய
கண் களி பெறூஉம் கவின் பெறு காலை
தொல் நலன் இழந்த என் பொன் நிறம் நோக்கி
reading: The woman asks her friend whether, in this lovely season when the wind carries the scent bees bring from the small kuravam buds, her heart, which went after the man who loosened her bangles, is suffering with him, unwearied by his task, in the hope of coming back together with him, or whether, since he is not kind, it came back, saw her golden colour lost its old beauty, and went away saying 'she is a stranger', joined to her sickness.
nuance: Her two guesses are both about the heart's loyalty, not the man's: either it stays faithful to him, or it disowns her now that her beauty is gone. The poem ends on the word தலைமணந்த, as if broken off.

colophon.thurai: வரைவிடை மெலிவு ஆற்றுவிக்கும் தோழிக்குத் தலைவி சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the kuravam of the early hot season while the man is away at his task

tamil: துஞ்சு பதம் பெற்ற துய்த் தலை மந்தி
வீங்கு சுரை ஞெமுங்க வாங்கி தீம் பால்
கல்லா வன் பறழ்க் கைந் நிறை பிழியும்
செங் கோல் கொடுங் குரல் சிறு தினை வியன் புனம்
மை ஈர் ஓதி மாண் நலம் தொலைவே
reading: The friend tells the lord of the great hill that it is bewildering how on his slopes, when the herd of big-horned wild cows rests with their calves by the hill vengai, a tufted female monkey that has caught them asleep creeps up with her noisy troop, cupping her hands, squeezes the swollen udder and wrings the sweet milk into the hands of her untaught young; but when the time to pluck the red-stalked millet comes near, the girl's oiled dark hair will lose its beauty.
nuance: பதம, the right moment, links the two halves: the monkey takes its moment while the herd sleeps (துஞ்சு பதம்), and the girl's moment is closing as the millet reaches its plucking time (கொய் பதம்). The friend's message is that the stolen meetings end with the harvest.

thinai_evidence.note: the monkey, the wild cows and the millet field of the hill

ullurai.tenor: the secret love taken from the kin's keeping while they are off guard

pairs.situation: the lovers' meetings, taken while the household sleeps
the hero takes by stealth what the kin keep

ullurai.speaker_fit: the friend uses the beasts of the hero's own hill in a kurinji poem (porul 7.27)

tamil: வெண் கோடு இயம்ப நுண் பனி அரும்ப
ஓடு தேர் நுண் நுகம் நுழைந்த மாவே
reading: As the man leaves after the daytime meeting, the friend curses his horse: may it be beaten with a stick like the sparrow painted on the face of the red-striped toy drum hung on the small shoulder of a rich old family's gold-decked son, the horse yoked to the running chariot of the lord of the cold shore, which took him away at the hour when, with the evening lamp lit at the first drum of Veliyan Thithan of Veerai, the white conch sounding and fine dew forming, we turned back drooping and sad.
nuance: The curse is comic in scale, a toy drum and a painted bird, which keeps the anger from touching the man himself. The evening is fixed by a chieftain's court ritual, the lamp and drum of Thithan.

colophon.thurai: பகற்குறி வந்து நீங்கும் தலைமகன் போக்கு நோக்கி தோழி மாவின்மேல்வைத்துச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: evening at the cold shore

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi

thurai_akam.note: spoken at the hero's horse as he leaves

tamil: பல் வேறு பண்டத் தொடை மறந்து இல்லத்து
இரு மடைக் கள்ளின் இன் களி செருக்கும்
reading: Returning from his task, the man tells his charioteer that her town, she who lives holding him in her heart with the loving resolve she gave him, is in the hard forest land where the hunter who killed a monitor lizard, dug out a striped frog, cut termites from a tall anthill and struck down a hare, comes home with his load and, forgetting his many wares, revels in sweet toddy; and now that the mullai's fine buds have opened in the woods and the rocks are covered, it is painful too.
nuance: The hunter's evening is the homecoming the hero is driving toward: work over, the catch home, everything else forgotten in ease. The last line turns: the season of return has come, and its beauty hurts while he is still on the road.

thinai_evidence.note: the mullai buds opening in the woodland

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the addressee is the charioteer (பாகன்)

iraicchi.act: the hunter comes home with his catch and, forgetting his trade, takes his ease in his own house
iraicchi.sense: the hero, his task done, is going home to the rest and the wife that wait for him

tamil: பெரு நெற் பல் கூட்டு எருமை உழவ
கருங் கண் வராஅல் பெருந் தடி மிளிர்வையொடு
நீர் உறு செறுவின் நாறு முடி அழுத்த நின்
reading: With the man listening, the friend tells the ploughman of the buffaloes, whose paddy stacks stand like a mountain, who goes out sleepless at cool dawn after gorging on a heap of rice with thick slices of black-eyed varal fish, that if he goes with his planters to press the seedlings into the flooded field, he should spare the sedge and the water lilies there, for they are what the dark-haired girl of our house threads into her bangles and wears.
nuance: The request to spare the field plants is a message about the girl: she is kept at home now and will not be in the fields, and the man who used to meet her there is told so through a ploughman.

colophon.thurai: சிறைப்புறமாக உழவர்க்குச் சொல்லுவாளாய்த் தோழி செறிப்பு அறிவுறீஇயது
