title: natrinai 61-80
theme: Natrinai 61 to 80: night-long longing hidden from the mother, girls shut in the house and gossip pressing on secret love; men turned away who call the girl their only medicine; friends who keep the man from leaving for wealth that does not last; an evening of mullai and a shore at sunset; a mother picturing her eloped daughter's eyes; and Malaiyan's raid made the measure of a lover's lost relief.
source_issues: 66, 70, 76, 77, 78: the colophon thurai ends with the poet's name (இனிசந்த நாகனார், வெள்ளி வீதியார், அம்மூவனார், கபிலர், கீரங்கீரனார}) and the poet field is empty; copied as printed.
61: the colophon makes the friend the speaker, but the poem's 'I' lies awake and is asked by her mother why she does not sleep; read as the friend voicing the heroine's night.
65: line 7 விற் சுழிப்பட்ட is obscure; the hunters' clamour and the thunder in line 8 may be compared or merely heard together.
75: lines 1 to 3 (பாம்பு உயிர் அணங்கியாங்கும்) are hard to construe; the reading takes them as a comparison for cruelty.
79: line 1 சிறை நாள் is obscure; the season of the eengai bloom is not fixed.
78: the colophon names no speaker; the friend is assumed.
80: line 9 is repeated in Natrinai 140 line 11 (text flag).

tamil: சிரல் வாய் உற்ற தளவின் பரல் அவல்
reading: The speaker tells her friend that last night, tormented by longing and breathing hot, she suffered like a doe struck by an arrow; her mother, as if she guessed the cause, asked 'Don't you sleep, my little one?', and she, keeping the words from coming out, said softly in her heart: can eyes sleep for those who long for the man of the forest land, where by the rain-washed rock the stony hollow holds jasmine buds like a kingfisher's beak?
nuance: The answer is never spoken: the reply to the mother is made inside the heart (சொல் வெளிப்படாமை), so the poem shows secrecy holding even at the moment the mother comes closest to knowing. The colophon makes the friend the speaker, voicing this as the heroine's night so that the man, who has come and stands near, hears what his delay costs.

colophon.thurai: தலைவன் வரவு உணர்ந்து தலைவிக்குச் சொல்லுவாளாய்த் தோழி சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the man is lord of the forest land of rock and rain, and the hour is the night

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon says she speaks as if to the heroine, knowing the man has come; the poem's 'I' is the heroine's night voiced by the friend

comparisons.tenor: the speaker suffering through the night
the pointed jasmine buds

tamil: வேர் பிணி வெதிரத்துக் கால் பொரு நரல் இசை
குன்று ஊர் மதியம் நோக்கி நின்று நினைந்து
திலகம் தைஇய தேம் கமழ் திரு நுதல்
உரறு குரல் வெவ் வளி எடுப்ப நிழல் தப
கல் பிறங்கு உயர் மலை உம்பரஃது எனவே
reading: Pressed again toward wealth, the man reminds his heart how on the earlier journey, in the long-summer bamboo waste where wind-rubbed bamboos groan like a tethered elephant's weary sigh, he stood looking at the moon climbing the hill and thought: we too have a moon of our own, her sweet-smelling, tilakam-marked forehead, beyond that stony mountain where hot roaring wind has stripped the shade and left the trees dry.
nuance: The refusal to go is never stated: the poem offers only a memory, and the memory is enough. The moon he saw on the road is demoted to a second moon; the first is at home, so the journey is pictured as going away from the light.

colophon.thurai: முன் ஒரு காலத்துப்பொருள்வயிற் பிரிந்து வந்த தலைவன் பின்னும் பொருள்வலிக்கப்பட்ட நெஞ்சிற்குச் செலவு அழுங்குவித்தது

thinai_evidence.note: long summer, shadeless dried trees: the parched road of separation

comparisons.tenor: the groan of the wind-rubbed bamboos
her bright forehead

tamil: மிகு மீன் உணக்கிய புது மணல் ஆங்கண்
விழவு நாறு விளங்கு இணர் அவிழ்ந்து உடன் கமழும்
அறன் இல் அன்னை அருங் கடிப் படுப்ப
புள் உற ஒசிந்த பூ மயங்கு அள்ளல்
கழிச் சுரம் நிவக்கும் இருஞ் சிறை இவுளி
மலி திரைச் சேர்ப்பனொடு அமைந்த நம் தொடர்பே
reading: With the man standing by, the friend says the clamorous shore town, where fishermen dry their catch on fresh sand and the punnai blooms with a festival fragrance over the stench of fish, has no justice; so the unjust mother has put the girl under strict guard, and their bond with the lord of the wave-washed shore, whose dark-winged horses rise over the flower-choked backwater mud and are washed by the sea, may waste into pallor and die.
nuance: The word அறன் is used twice in two lines, of the town and of the mother: gossip and guard are the same injustice seen from outside and inside the house. The bond, not the girl, is what turns pale (பசலை), a bold shift of the lovesick sign onto the relation itself.

thinai_evidence.note: fishermen, punnai and the lord of the shore

tamil: மரல் நார் உடுக்கை மலை உறை குறவர்
வறிதால் இகுளை என் யாக்கை இனி அவர்
reading: When her friend wants to send him word, the woman says: stop thinking of him, whatever he is; what is the friendship of one who left us like this? As the small-leaved sandal tree that the hill Kuravar, clad in maral fibre, cut without knowing dries in the drought and slowly withers to an empty trunk, so my mind and heart have gone to him and my body is empty; even if he comes he is no medicine for this sickness, so let him stay there, and let my kin not see the suffering of love that crushes me.
nuance: The sandal tree is cut 'without knowing' (அறியாது), so the image blames carelessness, not cruelty; that is why she can refuse him without hating him. Her last wish is not for him but that her kin should not see: secrecy outlives hope.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவிடைத் தலைவியது அருமை கண்டு தூதுவிடக் கருதிய தோழிக்குத் தலைவி சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the hill Kuravar and the sandal tree

comparisons.vehicle: சிறியிலைச் சாந்தம் வறனுற்று ஆர முருக்கி பையென மரம் வறிதாகச் சோர்ந்து உக்காங்கு
comparisons.tenor: her body emptied once her mind and heart went to him

tamil: கிடங்கில் அன்ன இட்டுக் கரைக் கான் யாற்றுக்
ஒளிறு வெள் அருவி ஒண் துறை மடுத்து
நற் கோடு நயந்த அன்பு இல் கானவர்
reading: The friend, delighted, says: may our neighbour woman eat ambrosia, for she said 'he will come', the man of the great mountain land where, at the bright ford of a white waterfall and a forest river banked like a moat with swirling moss, an elephant wounded in a fight with a tiger is beset by pitiless hunters who covet its tusk, and their fearsome clamour sounds through the thunder.
nuance: The neighbour's chance words are taken as an omen (the colophon's விரிச்சி): the friend blesses an unknowing speaker for a sentence not meant for them. The violent hill scene that follows is the land's ordinary life, offered as the man's address, not as a warning.

thinai_evidence.note: tiger, elephant, hill hunters and the lord of the great hill

comparisons.tenor: the steep banks of the forest river

tamil: உலறு தலை உகாஅய்ச் சிதர் சிதர்ந்து உண்ட
புலம்பு கொள் நெடுஞ் சினை ஏறி நினைந்து தன்
பொறி கிளர் எருத்தம் வெறி பட மறுகி
புன் புறா உயவும் வெந் துகள் இயவின்
காழ் பெயல் அல்குல் காசு முறை திரியினும்
reading: The mother, at home after her daughter has left with her lover, wonders whether on the hot dusty track, where a dull dove, having pecked the pepper-sharp small fruits of the dry-topped ukaay, climbs a lonely long branch and, ruffling its spotted neck, moans, her deceitful little girl's flower-like eyes, which used to weep away their beauty if her garland was disarranged, her small bangle loosened or her coin girdle shifted, are now red, dimmed and troubled, even though she is with the man she loves.
nuance: The mother does not doubt the man; she grants that the girl has joined him (புணர்ந்தனள் ஆயினும்). Her worry is built from memory of tiny vanities, so the measure of the road's hardship is a childhood in which a loosened bangle was a disaster. மாயக் குறுமகள், 'deceitful little girl', is tender, not reproach.

thinai_evidence.note: the ukaay, the moaning dove and the hot dusty track

the girl's eyes

tamil: சேய் விசும்பு இவர்ந்த செழுங் கதிர் மண்டிலம்
இறவு அருந்தி எழுந்த கருங் கால் வெண் குருகு
வெண் கோட்டு அருஞ் சிறைத் தாஅய் கரைய
கணைக் கால் மா மலர் கரப்ப மல்கு கழித்
எல் இமிழ் பனிக் கடல் மல்கு சுடர்க் கொளீஇ
உடை கடற் படப்பை எம் உறைவின் ஊர்க்கே
reading: As the man who came for the day meeting turns to go, the friend says the red sun has crossed the far sky and hidden behind the great hill, the ford is lonely, the black-legged white herons that fed on prawns have settled on the black-branched punnai, paired sharks prowl the backwater hiding the big flowers, and our men, lighting lamps on the cold dark sea, have gone fishing: so what harm if you stayed in our seaside town where the spray-flinging waves rise with the sound of drums?
nuance: The invitation to stay one night is the pressure to marry: a man who sleeps in her town must become its son-in-law. The detail that 'our men' are out on the sea makes the offer bolder than it sounds, and the prowling sharks quietly tell him the shore path is no place for a night journey.

colophon.thurai: பகற்குறி வந்து நீங்கும் தலைமகனைத் தோழி வரைவு கடாயது

thinai_evidence.note: sunset on the lonely shore ford

comparisons.tenor: the roar of the rising waves

iraicchi.sense: even the birds come home to roost at dusk, so the man too should stay and make this town his home, that is, marry

tamil: குறு நுரை சுமந்து நறு மலர் உந்தி
பொங்கி வரு புது நீர் நெஞ்சு உண ஆடுகம்
உரவு உரும் உரறும் அரை இருள் நடு நாள்
ஆடு மழை இறுத்தன்று அவர் கோடு உயர் குன்றே
reading: With the man outside, the friend tells the girl: if we found someone to bow and say skilfully that for young girls to sit shut in the house, not playing orai with their companions, is neither right nor good for the household, and that they should bathe to their heart's content in the swelling new flood that carries small foam and pushes fragrant flowers, would mother let us go? Meanwhile at midnight, in half-dark, the mighty thunder roars spitting light, lightning flashes like waving banners, and the drifting cloud has settled on his high-peaked hill.
nuance: The friend's speech is a request for an intercessor, and the man listening is the obvious one: the person who can 'bow and speak' to the mother is a suitor asking for her. The storm on his hill at midnight closes the night path as firmly as the mother closes the door.

thinai_evidence.note: midnight storm on the hill

comparisons.tenor: the flashing lightning

tamil: பல் கதிர் மண்டிலம் பகல் செய்து ஆற்றி
சேய் உயர் பெரு வரைச் சென்று அவண் மறைய
மா எருத்து இரலை மடப் பிணை தழுவ
முல்லை முகை வாய் திறப்ப பல் வயின்
மதர்வை நல் ஆன் மாசு இல் தெண் மணி
ஐது வந்து இசைக்கும் அருள் இல் மாலை
reading: The wife who cannot bear his absence on work says: the many-rayed sun has done its day and set behind the far high hill, birds go home to their young, in the scrub the dark-necked stag embraces his gentle doe, jasmine buds open their mouths, thondri lights up the bushes, and the clear bells of the proud cows blend with the flutes of the cowherds with crooked staves in this pitiless evening; if evening came like this in the land where he went for his work, he could not hold to his resolve.
nuance: She does not accuse him; she supposes that his land has no such evening, since if it had he would be home. The excuse is also a reproach, and it keeps her faith intact.

thinai_evidence.note: evening in the scrub, the jasmine, cowherds and cattle

thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no addressee; the friend is assumed

iraicchi.sense: even the stag is with his mate at nightfall, which the absent husband is not

tamil: துறை போகு அறுவைத் தூ மடி அன்ன
எம் ஊர் வந்து எம் உண்துறைத் துழைஇ
சினைக் கெளிற்று ஆர்கையை அவர் ஊர்ப் பெயர்தி
reading: The woman calls to the little white heron, whose bright feathers are like the pure folds of cloth washed at the ford: you come to our town, search our drinking ford, eat the roe-filled keliru fish and go back to his town; is it your love or your great forgetfulness that you never tell the man of that good field town, whose sweet water spreads here, of my grief and my loosening bangles?
nuance: The heron already travels the route a messenger would take and eats at her ford, so its silence is a kind of ingratitude; the line about water flowing from his town to hers says the towns are joined while the man is not.

thinai_evidence.note: field towns joined by fresh water, the keliru of the ford

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: she addresses the heron

comparisons.tenor: the heron's white feathers

tamil: வளை அணி முன்கை நின் இகுளைக்கு உணர்த்து எனப்
வகை அமர் நல் இல் அக இறை உறையும்
வீழ் துணைப் பயிரும் கையறு முரல் குரல்
reading: The friend tells the man bent on the sickness for wealth that does not last: if you beg her friend in many ways to tell this to the bangled girl, she may let you go, saying 'go'; but if she does, can you stand before her, stroke her eyes and forehead and leave, sir, while the red-legged male of the coloured dove living under the inner eaves of a rich house calls its beloved mate in a helpless moaning voice, and each time she hears it alone without you, the woman of thick hair will tremble?
nuance: The friend concedes the woman's consent in advance, then removes its value: the leave-taking itself, the hand on her eyes, is what he cannot survive. மன்னாப் பொருள் calls wealth impermanent at the poem's first word.

thinai_evidence.note: the threatened departure for wealth

iraicchi.act: the male dove that lives in the house calls for its mate
iraicchi.sense: a bird that stays at home calls its mate, while the man means to leave his; she will hear in it the call he will not make

tamil: நினக்கு யான் மறைத்தல் யாவது மிகப் பெரிது
யான் யாய் அஞ்சுவல் எனினும் தான் எற்
reading: With the man outside, the friend tells the girl: it is shameful that the great do not cherish what they should; in a flawless friendship like one life between us, hiding anything from you would be a great wrong; once, when I said I feared mother, the lord of the shore would never think of leaving; now, even though our shore companions may know, he keeps asking 'has gossip come?', so I fear in my heart, friend, that his friendship is drying up.
nuance: The man's new question about gossip is read as a sign of cooling: caution once came from the girl's side and now comes from his. The friend speaks it within the women's own friendship (உயிர் ஓரன்ன) so the listener feels judged by two.

thinai_evidence.note: the shore grove and its lord

comparisons.tenor: the friendship of the two women

tamil: மயிர் நிரைத்தன்ன வார் கோல் வாங்கு கதிர்ச்
பூக் கெழு படப்பைச் சாய்க்காட்டு அன்ன என்
reading: The woman says that they say he will leave us here, we who are afraid even with him, in the cruel evening when the strong-mouthed ghoul with ungainly fingers like the ripe clusters of the summer murukku splits the public square to eat the flower offerings of the rich old town; pitiable then are the pallor that ruins my forehead, once lovely as Saykkadu with its flowered gardens where the swan sleeps in red-rice fields whose long bent ears are like rows of red hair, and the gossip the neighbours spread.
nuance: The fear is set at home, not on his road: it is the town's evening, with its ghoul in the square, that she will face alone. Her past beauty is measured by a rich field town, so what the pallor destroys is a kind of wealth, the very thing he leaves to seek.

colophon.thurai: செலவுக் குறிப்பு அறிந்து வேறுபட்ட தலைவி சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: his coming departure, leaving her behind

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the addressee and the stage are not given; the neighbours' gossip may mean the parting before marriage

comparisons.tenor: the ghoul's fingers
the long bent ears of red rice
the beauty of her forehead

tamil: வடிக் கதிர் திரித்த வல் ஞாண்பெரு வலை
சிறு வீ ஞாழற் பெருங் கடற் சேர்ப்பனை
புது மணற் கானல் புன்னை நுண் தாது
வெண் புறம் மொசிய வார்க்கும் தெண் கடல்
reading: Refusing the bard who comes for the man, the woman says they call even the lord of the great shore of small-flowered nyazhal, where fishermen push the boat loaded with a great net of strong twisted cord into the thunder-voiced sea as elephant-keepers with goads drive an elephant hard to hold, a stranger now; yet the town knows me as the woman of him whose town has kandal hedges by the clear sea, where each gust of the east wind shakes the fine pollen of the punnai in the fresh-sand grove until it heaps on the white backs of the herons, and that is hard to undo.
nuance: She refuses entry while admitting she cannot undo the bond: the town's knowledge makes her his whether he behaves or not. The punnai's pollen settling on the herons' backs is the image of a mark that the wind keeps adding and nothing washes off.

thinai_evidence.note: fishermen, nyazhal, punnai and kandal of the shore

comparisons.tenor: the fishermen pushing the laden boat

ullurai.tenor: the woman whom the town now knows as the man's

pairs.situation: the town's talk, gust after gust
the name of his woman heaped on her until it cannot be brushed off

ullurai.speaker_fit: the heroine uses the punnai and herons of her own shore, things she knows (porul 7.26)

tamil: பூம் பொறிப் பொலிந்த அழல் உமிழ் அகன் பை
சேயரி பரந்த மா இதழ் மழைக் கண்
reading: Turned away, the man says to the girl, so that her friend hears: not thinking 'this is the fruit of unkindness', as one might torment the life of a snake with a fire-spitting broad hood of bright spots, this is not fitting here; long live, little one: speak without laughing, for my heart is breaking; tell me how my aching heart can live, struck by the glance that will not look of your large rain-cool eyes streaked with red, like the arrow wet with raw flesh that the hill hunter with curved bow shot to kill a tusked beast on the slope.
nuance: உறாஅ நோக்கம், the look that does not touch, is the weapon: indifference wounds like a hunter's arrow. Asking her to speak 'without laughing' shows he fears her mockery more than her refusal.

thinai_evidence.note: the hunter and the tusked beast on the hill slope

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: he speaks to the girl (குறுமகள்) so that the friend, who has kept him off, may hear

comparisons.tenor: her unkindness tormenting him
her red-streaked eyes' unlooking glance

tamil: நுண் துளி மாறிய உலவை அம் காட்டு
இம்மென் பேர் அலர் நும் ஊர்ப் புன்னை
வீ மலர் உதிர்ந்த தேன் நாறு புலவின்
கல் உறச் சிவந்த நின் மெல் அடி உயற்கே
reading: Eloping with her, the man tells the girl on the way: in this forest of dry trees under a white sky that has hidden the coming rain and stopped even fine drizzle, rest from weariness in the banyan's shade; unafraid where there is cause for fear, resting where it is right to rest, go on without strain, girl of bright jewels, so that your soft feet, used to the long sand of the shore grove of your town, where the great gossip hums and fallen punnai flowers smell of honey and fish, and now reddened against the stones, may recover.
nuance: Her old town is remembered for its gossip and its soft sand in one breath: what she has left is both what hurt her and what was gentle to her feet. He sets the pace by her feet, not by the road.

colophon.thurai: புணர்ந்து உடன்போகாநின்ற தலைவன் இடைச் சுரத்துத் தலைவிக்கு உரைத்தது அம்மூவனார்

thinai_evidence.note: a rainless forest of dried trees on the elopement road

occasion.words: உடன்போகாநின்ற தலைவன் இடைச் சுரத்துத் தலைவிக்கு உரைத்தது

tamil: பெருந் துடி கறங்கப் பிற புலம் புக்கு அவர்
வாள் அரம் பொருத கோள் நேர் எல் வளை
அகன் தொடி செறித்த முன்கை ஒள் நுதல்
reading: The man who keeps following her tells his heart: as Malaiyan rode his horse into enemy land with the Pulaiyan's great tudi drum sounding, broke their hard strongholds and then breathed out his weariness, so once, heart, the glad innocent look of her kuvalai-dark kohl eyes brought me relief: the bright-browed girl with spotted hips, whose forearm is filled with broad bangles that the skilled smith of the small town of Ooral filed with a saw, where in the yard full of jackfruit hanging on every branch, the housewife sleeps at night to the roar of the white waterfall.
nuance: மன்னே marks the relief as past: the poem is spoken now that it is gone. The king's sigh comes after the raid, not during it, so the comparison is to exhausted ease after victory, not to conquest; the woman of the yard who sleeps by the waterfall's noise is the calm he no longer has.

thinai_evidence.note: the jackfruit yard and the waterfall of a hill hamlet

comparisons.tenor: the relief her look once gave him
her dark eyes

tamil: கோட் சுறா வழங்கும் வாள் கேழ்இருங் கழி
மணி ஏர் நெய்தல் மா மலர் நிறைய
பொன் நேர் நுண் தாது புன்னை தூஉம்
வீழ் தாழ் தாழைப் பூக் கமழ் கானல்
படர் வந்து நலியும் சுடர் செல் மாலை
நோய் மலி பருவரல் நாம் இவண் உய்கம்
வள் வாய் ஆழி உள் வாய் தோயினும்
புள்ளு நிமிர்ந்தன்ன பொலம் படைக் கலி மா
reading: The friend tells the girl: in the shore grove fragrant with the hanging-rooted thazhai, where in the dark backwater gleaming like a sword and roamed by killing sharks the punnai sprinkles fine gold-like pollen to fill the great gem-blue neythal flowers, we shall now escape the grief that torments us at the evening hour when the sun goes; listen, friend: the bell of the chariot of the lord of the mighty sea, whose horses with golden trappings leap like rising birds so that the charioteer never has to touch them with the whip, even when the sharp wheel-rims sink into the clear backwater.
nuance: The chariot is heard, not seen: the bell's sound alone is news of marriage. The horses that need no whip carry the point that he now comes of his own eagerness, not pressed.

thinai_evidence.note: neythal, punnai, thazhai and sharks of the backwater

thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no speaker; the friend is the usual bearer of this news, and she calls the girl தோழி

the punnai pollen
the leaping chariot horses
the gleaming backwater

tamil: சிறை நாள் ஈங்கை உறை நனி திரள்வீ
கூரை நல் மனைக் குறுந் தொடி மகளிர்
மணல் ஆடு கழங்கின் அறை மிசைத் தாஅம்
reading: Sensing he will leave, the woman tells her friend: shall we tell him our love, saying 'is anything harder than this, that those who parted come back and join us and then, having joined, plan to part again, by the forked path hard to cross where clustered eengai flowers fall on the rock like the molucca seeds that bangled girls of good houses play with on sand?' If we don't tell him, it has come for life itself; so, friend, by what can we stop the lover's going?
nuance: The argument she rehearses is a small piece of logic about cycles: union after parting should make parting harder, not easier. The last line asks for a means, not a reason: she already knows words may not be enough.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவு உணர்ந்து வேறுபட்ட தலைமகள் தோழிக்குச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: his planned departure

comparisons.tenor: the eengai flowers fallen on the rock

tamil: இன் தீம் பாற்பயம் கொண்மார் கன்று விட்டு
இழை அணி ஆயமொடு தகு நாண் தடைஇ
மருந்து பிறிது இல்லை யான் உற்ற நோய்க்கே
reading: Kept away, the man tells his heart so the friend can hear: in the dawn when the town's small boys, wanting the sweet milk of the common's dark buffalo with flowering head, loose its calf and ride it off, she came eager, and with her jewelled companions, restrained by fitting shyness and saying 'this one brought leaf skirts and garlands', she bathes in the cool pond in the month of Thai; there is no medicine but that broad-shouldered girl for the sickness I have.
nuance: His gifts (தழையும் தாரும்) are named in her voice, so he knows she has noticed him; the friend's refusal is answered by her own acknowledgement. The Thai bath is a maidens' rite, which makes her not yet anyone's.

colophon.thurai: சேட்படுக்கப்பட்டு ஆற்றானாய தலைவன் தோழி கேட்ப தன் நெஞ்சிற்கு உரைத்தது

thinai_evidence.note: a lover's suit before marriage, his gifts and his sickness: the situation of kurinji

title: natrinai 81-100
theme: Natrinai 81 to 100: returns and promised seasons kept or mistaken (the soldier racing home to a wife who longs to host guests, the friend who praises one man's punctuality and mocks the flowers that bloom for another's absence), hill trysts at night with owl, boar and elephant as the night's dangers, shore poems of memory and pallor pressing for marriage, a woman who resents that only men may speak their love, and marutham scenes of a poor girl at a festival swing and a courtesan laughing at a husband afraid of his wife.
source_issues: 86 lines 1 to 3: the construction of மறவர் வேல் என விரிந்த கதுப்பின் தோல பாண்டில் ஒப்பின் பகன்றை is unclear (what spreads like spears, and what தோல பாண்டில் is); the flower similes are read loosely and the verse is marked uncertain.

89: the colophon gives the poem to the friend (தோழி தலைவிக்கு உரைத்தது) on hearing that the man is returning, but the poem addresses தோழி and complains of 'those who do not come' (வாரா வன்கணாளர்), which fits the woman as speaker; the colophon is copied as given.
90 lines 10 to 12: the construction of ஊசல் உறு தொழில் பூசல் கூட்டா and who is blamed for the girl's tears is unclear; marked uncertain.
93 lines 3 to 4 (கூலம் எல்லாம் புலம்புஉக) and 11 to 12 (முன் உயிர்க் குறியெதிர்ப்பை) are hard; the reading of her life as a pledge is tentative and the verse is marked uncertain.
98 line 2: செய்ய்ம்ம் மேவல் is garbled (a doubled ய் and ம்); the boar's epithet is read as 'wanting to wallow' without fixing the word, and the verse is marked uncertain.
84 line 1 is missing from sangamtamil.com's text and recurs as Natrinai 219 line 1; it is kept as our text gives it.

tamil: ஆதி போகிய அசைவு இல் நோன் தாள்
கொய்ம் மயிர் எருத்தில் பெய்ம் மணி ஆர்ப்ப
பூண்கதில் பாக நின் தேரே பூண் தாழ்
உறு பகை தணித்தனன் உரவு வாள் வேந்தே
reading: Back from the king's war, the man tells his charioteer to yoke the chariot whose swift horses, prized by kings, have bells ringing on their clipped-mane necks: the strong-sworded king has quelled the enemy, and they will see the sweet smile of the lovely young wife who has stayed weeping, tears dropping on her breasts, worn out by her longing to welcome guests.
nuance: Her grief is named as a thwarted wish to host guests (விருந்து அயர் விருப்பு), a duty a wife cannot keep alone, so his return restores the household's work as well as the marriage. The king's victory is held back to the last line, as the thing that releases him.

thinai_evidence.note: the wife waiting at home and the husband freed by the war's end is the mullai situation

tamil: என் உயவு அறிதியோ நல் நடைக் கொடிச்சி
முருகு புணர்ந்து இயன்ற வள்ளி போல நின்
சிறு கட் பன்றிப் பெருஞ் சின ஒருத்தல்
சேறு ஆடு இரும் புறம் நீறொடு சிவண
வெள் வசிப் படீஇயர் மொய்த்த வள்பு அழீஇ
reading: The man asks the hill girl of graceful gait, whose bamboo-lovely shoulders could end his sickness and weakness, whether she knows his anguish: he cannot bear to look at her form, which strikes the eyes like Valli joined with Murugan, she of the small village where hunters carry home the spoil their dogs took when they broke the leash and swarmed an angry boar, its dark mud-bathed back mingled with dust, at the forked path where snakes go.
nuance: Line 1 credits her shoulders with ending the very sickness she causes. The closing scene of dogs swarming a proud boar while the hunters take the spoil can be read as the man brought down by her, but no second correspondence is anchored in the poem, so the boar stays scene (a near miss for ullurai). Line 7 recurs as Natrinai 386 line 1.

thinai_evidence.note: the hill girl, the boar and the hunters are kurinji things

comparisons.tenor: the girl's form that dazzles his eyes
her shoulders

tamil: கடவுள் முது மரத்து உடன் உறை பழகிய
தேயா வளை வாய் தெண் கண் கூர் உகிர்
வாய்ப் பறை அசாஅம் வலி முந்து கூகை
மை ஊன் தெரிந்த நெய் வெண் புழுக்கல்
எஞ்சாக் கொள்கை எம் காதலர் வரல் நசைஇத்
reading: The friend promises the owl that has long lived in the old god-haunted tree at the drinking ghat by their town's gate, sharp of claw and curved of beak, a rich feast of white rice cooked in ghee with dark meat and roasted white rat, if only it will not keep sounding its harsh, fearful cry in the hour when they lie awake and restless, longing for the coming of their lover of unfailing resolve.
nuance: The plea to the owl is meant for the man waiting outside: it tells him they are awake and waiting, and that the meeting depends on the house not being roused. Rice, ghee and meat are the stuff of offerings at a god's tree, so the friend is bribing an omen.

colophon.thurai: இரவுக்குறி வந்த தலைவன் சிறைப்புறத்தானாக தோழி சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: lying awake for the lover's coming is the night tryst of kurinji

tamil: பெரு நீர் ஒப்பின் பேஎய் வெண் தேர்
மரன் இல் நீள் இடை மான் நசையுறூஉம்
உவர் எழு களரி ஓமை அம் காட்டு
வெயில் வீற்றிருந்த வெம்பு அலை அருஞ் சுரம்
reading: The woman tells her friend that only yesterday he was here, praising her eyes, her shoulders, her cool fragrant hair and her speckled waist, and today they say he will go by the hard road where the sun sits enthroned, through omai forest on salt waste cracked like unformed butter split by heat, where the white ghost-chariot of the mirage, like a great water, lures the deer across the long treeless stretch: he is one who cannot live a home life that fails to relieve those who come to beg.
nuance: The last lines give his reason without blame: a household that cannot relieve suppliants is no life for him, so the ideal of giving is what takes him from her. ஏகுவர் என்ப (they say he will go) shows she has the news from others, not from him, and the colophon's 'in separation' anticipates a parting not yet made.

thinai_evidence.note: his going over the waste is the paalai parting

comparisons.tenor: the white mirage

comparisons.vehicle: சுடுமண் தசும்பின் மத்தம் தின்ற பிறவா வெண்ணெய் உருப்பு இடந்தன்ன
comparisons.tenor: the cracked white salt waste

tamil: ஆய் மலர் மழைக் கண் தெண் பனி உறைப்பவும்
வேய் மருள் பணைத் தோள் விறல் இழை நெகிழவும்
குறு வரி இரும் புலி அஞ்சிக் குறு நடைக்
ஆர் இருள் கடுகிய அஞ்சு வரு சிறு நெறி
கானவன் எய்த முளவு மான் கொழுங் குறை
reading: The friend tells the woman that though her fine flower eyes drip tears, her bangles slip from her bamboo-like shoulders and the gossiping old town is loud, she wishes the lord of the high mountain would not come for love of her by the narrow, fearful path black with night, where an elephant, afraid of the small-striped tiger, stands guarding its short-stepping calf: his is the land where the hill girl with honey-scented hair shares out, with tubers, in their kaanthal hamlet, the fat cut of the porcupine her hunter shot.
nuance: வாரற்கதில்ல (may he not come) is a wish against the woman's own longing, made from fear for him. The closing picture of the hunter's kill shared out in the hamlet sets the safe daylight order of a married hill household against the night path.

colophon.thurai: தலைவன் வரவு உணர்ந்த தோழி தலைவிக்கு உரைத்தது

thinai_evidence.note: the mountain and the dark night fix kurinji

comparisons.tenor: her rounded shoulders
her rain-cool eyes

iraicchi.act: the elephant, afraid of the tiger, halts on the dark path and stands guard over its short-stepping calf
iraicchi.sense: as the elephant keeps its young from the path's danger, the women's love for the man makes them wish him kept from that path at night, so love here means holding back, not coming

reading: The friend blesses the men as righteous: through the harsh dew of the late cold season, when the pakandrai blooms like leather cups and the great closed buds of the koongam open curled like a skilled craftsman's stitched work, they came back ahead of the early summer, when the eengai's good shoots sway, before the time they had named.
nuance: அறவர் (they are righteous) is praise for a kept promise, not for piety: keeping the season they named is what makes the man good. The flowers of the late dew and the not-yet-ripe summer fix that he beat his own deadline.

colophon.thurai: குறித்த பருவத்தின்வினைமுடித்து வந்தமை கேட்ட தோழி தலைவிக்கு உரைத்தது

thinai_evidence.note: the late dew and the early summer are seasons Tholkappiyam gives to paalai

comparisons.tenor: a spreading part of the flowering plant
the pakandrai flowers

comparisons.vehicle: கை வல் வினைவன் தையுபு சொரிந்த சுரிதக உருவின
comparisons.tenor: the opening koongam buds

tamil: உள் ஊர் மா அத்த முள் எயிற்று வாவல்
வெல் போர்ச் சோழர் அழிசிஅம் பெருங் காட்டு
பனி அரும்பு உடைந்த பெருந் தாட் புன்னை
துறை மேய் இப்பி ஈர்ம் புறத்து உறைக்கும்
பெருந் தண் கானலும் நினைந்த அப் பகலே
reading: The woman tells her friend that the day she spent thinking of the joys of the fisherfolk of his small village, where the dew-broken buds of the great punnai drip on the wet backs of oysters grazing at the shore, and of his great cool grove, has passed like the dream that a sharp-toothed bat, hanging asleep on a high mango branch in the town, dreams of the sour taste of gooseberries in Azhisi's great forest in the land of the war-winning Cholas.
nuance: The bat on the town's mango dreams of fruit in a far forest it is not in, as she dwells on a shore she has not reached: the simile makes her day of longing as unreal and as hungry as the bat's dream. The colophon says she saw a dream; the poem gives the dream to the bat and calls her own state remembering (நினைந்த).

colophon.thurai: வரைவிடை வைத்துப்பிரிய ஆற்றாளாய தலைவி கனாக் கண்டு தோழிக்கு உரைத்தது

thinai_evidence.note: the shore grove and the fisherfolk fix neythal

comparisons.tenor: her day of longing for his shore

tamil: அழுமே தோழி அவர் பழம் முதிர் குன்றே
reading: The friend tells the woman not to be stricken as though by old deeds of their own, not to grieve, but to rise so they can go, speak to him and come back; she fears the woman will melt away like the sea-grown salt that has taken the rain, and, look, his hill heavy with ripe fruit, taking his cruelty to them to heart and too kind to bear it, will weep with waterfalls for tears.
nuance: The friend refuses fate (யாம் செய் தொல் வினை) as an explanation and proposes to act, and says it for the ears of the man outside: his own hill is shown weeping at his cruelty, so the land shames its lord. The salt of the shore, called the sea's nectar, is a neythal thing used in a hill poem.

thinai_evidence.note: his fruit-laden hill and its falls fix kurinji

comparisons.tenor: the woman wasting away
the hill's waterfalls

tamil: திரைப் பிதிர் கடுப்ப முகடு உகந்து ஏறி
நிரைத்து நிறை கொண்ட கமஞ் சூல் மா மழை
அழி துளி கழிப்பிய வழி பெயற் கடை நாள்
இரும் பனிப் பருவத்த மயிர்க் காய் உழுந்தின்
reading: As the great full-bellied clouds that rose in ranks like the spray of waves have spent their last torrents and the season of heavy dew comes, the ungracious north wind, which every night tosses wide the broad leaves of the hairy-podded black gram, sighing like a caparisoned elephant, will come again, friend, with the sorrowful evening and loneliness before it, joined with the hard-hearted ones who do not come.
nuance: The wind and the evening are made allies of the absent men (வன்கணாளரோடு இயைந்த), so the season does his cruelty for him. The colophon gives the poem to the friend, who has heard he is coming back with wealth, but the address தோழி and 'the ones who do not come' read more naturally as the woman's own complaint.

colophon.thurai: பொருள் முற்றி மறுத்தந்தான் எனக் கேட்ட தோழி தலைவிக்கு உரைத்தது

thinai_evidence.note: waiting through the evening for one who has not come is the mullai situation

comparisons.tenor: the clouds climbing the sky
the north wind's sighing gusts

tamil: புகாப் புகர் கொண்ட புன் பூங் கலிங்கமொடு
பெருங் கயிறு நாலும் இரும் பனம் பிணையல்
பயன் இன்று அம்ம இவ் வேந்துடை அவையே
reading: In the old town loud with its dancing festival, the young daughter of a poor woman, with few bangles and lovely sparse hair, dressed in a flowered cloth that the tireless washerwoman, who never rests her hands for her many clients, had washed by night, ran up with an unfading garland swinging, but would not ride the great palmyra-rope swing though her bright-eyed companions urged her, and went away weeping; this king's assembly, keeping company with graceless men who would not end the quarrel over the swing, is of no use.
nuance: The poem says only that a poor girl lost her turn at the festival swing and that the court did nothing; said within the panan's hearing, it seems to set the wife, pushed aside in her own town while those who should judge look on, beside the girl. As ullurai it fails condition 1: the vehicle is a person and a court, not a native thing, so the hidden comparison is left to this note. The night-washed cloth and the unfading garland may mark her finery as borrowed.

colophon.thurai: தோழி தலைமகளுக்கு உரைப்பாளாய் பாணனை நெருங்கி வாயில்மறுத்தது

thinai_evidence.note: the festival in the old town is the marutham world

tamil: புன்னை பூத்த இன் நிழல் உயர் கரைப்
பாடு இமிழ் பனிக் கடல் துழைஇ பெடையோடு
உடங்கு இரை தேரும் தடந் தாள் நாரை
ஐய சிறு கண் செங் கடைச் சிறு மீன்
தாய்ப் பயிர் பிள்ளை வாய்ப் படச் சொரியும்
கானல் அம் படப்பை ஆனா வண் மகிழ்ப்
பெரு நல் ஈகை நம் சிறு குடிப் பொலிய
புள் உயிர்க் கொட்பின் வள் உயிர் மணித் தார்க்
நெடு நீர்ச் சேர்ப்பன் பகல் இவண் வரவே
reading: The friend tells the woman she must have sensed it: so that their small village may shine with a great, unstinting joy of giving, the long-shored lord's tall chariot, yoked to swift horses whose bells cry out like whirling birds, comes here by day, to the shore garden where the large-legged heron, searching the roaring cold sea with its mate under the high bank of flower-shedding punnai, drops red-edged little fish into the mouths of its calling young in the nest atop the branch.
nuance: Coming by day (பகல் இவண் வரவே) means coming openly, to ask for her in marriage; the giving that will make the village shine is the wedding's bounty.

thinai_evidence.note: the shore lord and the shore garden fix neythal

comparisons.tenor: the ringing of the horses' bells

iraicchi.act: the heron searches the sea together with its mate and drops the fish it catches into the mouths of its young in the nest
iraicchi.sense: the man who now comes openly will keep a house as the heron does, seeking with his wife and feeding their own

tamil: பய நிரைக்கு எடுத்த மணி நீர்ப் பத்தர்
புன் தலை மடப் பிடி கன்றோடு ஆர
reading: The friend asks whether they will not think of us, the men who crossed the waste where a summer chameleon with its mate and a slow-gaited snake shrivel among the striped maral, and where, on the summit of a drought-held hill by the wide well of a hunters' hamlet, a killing tusker, warding off the bowmen, lets its young she-elephant and her calf drink from the gem-clear trough drawn for the cattle, and then goes its way.
nuance: The question expects yes: what the man saw on the road, a male winning water for its mate and calf and then leaving, is what he himself is doing, so the friend makes the road remind him.

thinai_evidence.note: summer, drought and the waste fix paalai

iraicchi.act: the tusker wards off the bowmen so its mate and calf can drink at the hamlet's trough, and then goes on
iraicchi.sense: the man who crossed that land, seeing a male provide for its own and move on as he did, will think of the wife he left

tamil: மல்லற்று அம்ம இம் மலை கெழு வெற்பு எனப்
மருங்கு மறைத்த திருந்து இழைப் பணைத் தோள்
பூண் தாழ் ஆகம் நாண் அட வருந்திய
reading: The friend tells the lord of the great rock land, where those who leave lament that this hill-crowned mountain, its honeycombs hanging, its great fruits clustered, its white falls coming down like garlands and all its grains spilling, is rich every day, to rise and come, long life to him: the soft young girl, slender-waisted, with jewels on bamboo shoulders that hide her sides, has the old pallor of one worn by shame, and her life, given like a pledge, is hard to win even for kings whose hairy-eyed drums thunder.
nuance: குறியெதிர்ப்பை is a loan repaid in kind: her life is given to him as such a loan, one even kings could not obtain, so his delay wastes what kings could not buy. The opening praise of a land so rich that leavers weep hints that he too should not leave her.

thinai_evidence.note: the rock land and the mountain fix kurinji

comparisons.tenor: the white waterfalls

tamil: நோய் அலைக் கலங்கிய மதன் அழி பொழுதில்
கை வல் கம்மியன் கவின் பெறக் கழாஅ
மண்ணாப் பசு முத்து ஏய்ப்ப குவி இணர்ப்
reading: The woman tells her friend that when love-sickness tosses one and desire breaks composure, speaking out one's longing suits a man, while she must hold it in finely as womanhood restrains her; what kind of man is the lord of the fish-smelling shore, where punnai buds cluster like fresh pearls a skilled craftsman has not yet washed to beauty, that he does not know those who long for him and are tormented by his chest?
nuance: Said for the man outside to hear: she states the rule that only a man may speak his love and turns it into a reproach, since he, who may speak, does not. The pearls still unwashed, lovely but not yet brought out, are the shore's own figure for a love kept unspoken.

thinai_evidence.note: the fish-smelling shore and the punnai fix neythal

comparisons.vehicle: கை வல் கம்மியன் கவின் பெறக் கழாஅ மண்ணாப் பசு முத்து
comparisons.tenor: the punnai's clustered buds

tamil: கழை பாடு இரங்க பல் இயம் கறங்க
ஆடு மகள் நடந்த கொடும் புரி நோன் கயிற்று
அதவத் தீம் கனி அன்ன செம் முகத்
துய்த் தலை மந்தி வன் பறழ் தூங்க
கழைக் கண் இரும் பொறை ஏறி விசைத்து எழுந்து
reading: The man tells his companion where his heart is: on the hill where, while the bamboo pole hums and many instruments sound, the strong cub of a fluffy-headed monkey, red-faced like a sweet fig, swings on the strong twisted rope a dancing girl walked, then climbs the great rock by the bamboo and leaps up while the hill children clap time, there is a small hamlet ringed with thickets; in that hamlet is the hill girl of fragrant hair; and in her hand is his heart, bound so that no one else can free it.
nuance: The poem narrows like a chain, each phrase's last word starting the next (சீறூர், சீறூரோளே; கொடிச்சி, கொடிச்சி), from hill to hamlet to girl to her hand. The monkey cub playing on the dancer's rope while children clap is the place's ease, offered to the companion as directions.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகன் பாங்கற்கு இவ்விடத்து இத்தன்மைத்து என உரைத்தது

thinai_evidence.note: the hill girl, the monkey and the hill people's children are kurinji things

comparisons.tenor: the monkey cub's red face

tamil: இதுவே நறு வீ ஞாழல் மா மலர்தாஅய்
புன்னை ததைந்த வெண் மணல் ஒரு சிறை
கொடுங் கழி நிவந்த நெடுங் கால் நெய்தல்
அம் பகை நெறித் தழை அணி பெறத் தைஇ
reading: The friend points out to the woman the grove on one side of the white sand, crowded with punnai and strewn with the gnaazhal's fragrant flowers, where she newly joined him; the shore where the swelling waves played with them and he kindly dried the dark five-braided hair that hung down her back; and the shore garden where she went alone wearing a leaf dress woven of the long-stalked neythal of the curving backwater: thinking of them again and again she melts, and slowly the pallor has spread over her.
nuance: இதுவே, உதுவே, அதுவே point to this place, that one and the one further off, so the friend walks the overhearing man back through his own meeting places; ending on the pallor, which she addresses directly, she tells him the memories have become a sickness only marriage will cure. Line 8 recurs as Natrinai 123 line 7.

thinai_evidence.note: the backwater, the shore and the shore garden fix neythal

tamil: அழுந்து படு விழுப் புண் வழும்பு வாய்புலரா
தேறு நீர் கெழீஇய யாறு நனி கொடிதே
reading: The woman says that crueler than the koel, which cries out lonely though it is not parted, as cruel as a spear thrust into an aching heart whose deep wound's pus has not dried, is the river of clear water, and crueler still is the lone young daughter of the grove's farmers who wanders with a bee-circled basket calling, 'Won't you take mixed flowers of pitthikai and fresh kurukkatthi with fluffy-tipped petals?'
nuance: Each thing is crueler for being more ordinary: a bird's cry, then the river, then a farm girl selling flowers that a wife with her husband away will not wear, so the climax is a human voice selling the season. The koel is cruel because it laments without having been parted (பிரிவில புலம்பி). The colophon's mullai rests on the waiting; the season the poem names is spring.

colophon.thurai: பருவம் கண்டு ஆற்றாளாய தலைவி தோழிக்கு உரைத்தது

thinai_evidence.note: the koel and the kurukkatthi mark spring, the season Tholkappiyam gives to paalai

comparisons.tenor: the koel's cry

tamil: ஓங்கு மலை வியன் புனம் படீஇயர் வீங்கு பொறி
கண்ணொடு வாரா என் நார் இல் நெஞ்சே
reading: The friend tells the lord of the land where a small-eyed boar with coarse neck bristles like porcupine quills, coming to wallow in the wide millet field of the high mountain, is about to pass the gap where a heavy trap is set when a lizard chirps beside it, and at once backs away, slowly, slowly, to rest in its rock-cave bed: crueler even than his coming by night, watching for a lapse of the sleepless guards of her father's well-guarded wide house, is her own feckless heart, which will not keep company with eyes that cannot close any night.
nuance: The boar heeds a lizard's chirp and turns back from the trap; the man ignores the guards and keeps coming. 'My heart' may be the friend speaking in the girl's person: her heart goes out to him at night while her eyes stay awake, so the danger is now inside the house as well.

colophon.thurai: இரவுக்குறி வந்து ஒழுகும்தலைவனைத் தோழி வரைவு கடாயது

thinai_evidence.note: the high mountain and the night visit fix kurinji

comparisons.tenor: the boar's coarse neck bristles

ullurai.tenor: the man who comes to the guarded house by night

pairs.situation: he slips into the father's guarded house at the guards' lapse
the signs of danger that should warn him

pairs.scene: மெல்லமெல்லப் பிறக்கே பெயர்ந்து தன் கல் அளைப் பள்ளி வதியும்
pairs.situation: he should turn back from night visits and rest in a home of his own by marrying her

ullurai.speaker_fit: the friend uses a boar of the hill's own millet field in a kurinji poem (porul 7.27)

tamil: மறந்து கடல் முகந்த கமஞ் சூல் மா மழை
கார் என்று அயர்ந்த உள்ளமொடு தேர்வு இல
reading: The friend answers the young woman who asked whether this is the season the men promised when they crossed the hot waste, its long way waterless, its heat shimmering like spread cloth: the great full-bellied cloud, mindless and forgetting itself, scooped up the sea and, unable to bear the load, let fall a heavy rain, and the pidavam, the konrai and the kodal, taking it for the rains with minds that cannot tell, have bloomed in numbers, because they are foolish.
nuance: The friend does not deny that it rains; she denies that the rain means anything, by making both the cloud (மதி இன்று, மறந்து) and the flowers (மடவ) mistaken. Laughing at the flowers' folly lets the woman laugh at her own fear. The flowers mistake a sign as she did, so they are the poem's subject, not iraicchi.

tamil: குண்டு நீர் ஆம்பல் தண் துறை ஊரன்
தேம் கமழ் ஐம்பால் பற்றி என் வயின்
வான் கோல் எல் வளை வெளவிய பூசல்
பல் ஆ நெடு நிரை வில்லின் ஒய்யும்
தேர் வண் மலையன் முந்தை பேர் இசைப்
புலம் புரி வயிரியர் நலம் புரி முழவின்
reading: The other woman says she laughs whenever she thinks of it: when the lord of the town of cool fords, where aambal stands in deep water like the plumage of the sharp-clawed heron of the rains, seized her honey-scented braids and snatched her bright bangles, and at the uproar she said, with an angry face but no anger, that she would go and tell his wife, the good man's trembling terror throbbed like the clay-smeared face of the drum the musicians play lovingly in the land of Malaiyan, giver of chariots, of great old fame, whose bow drives off the long cattle herds of enemy towns.
nuance: She mocks him as நன்னர் ஆளன் (the good man) and makes sure the wife's people overhear: the man who grabs her in the street shakes at the thought of his wife, so the other woman claims the upper hand. A great raider's festival drum is borrowed to measure a philanderer's fright.

title: natrinai 101-120
theme: Natrinai 101 to 120: the hill tryst under threat of night paths, traps and confinement; the shore's evenings and returns; the man on the road for wealth held back by memory; and in two marutham and household poems the wife's hidden strength, in poverty and in the sulk a guest dissolves.
source_issues: 108: the colophon heading gives no poet and no '(?)' (text flag).
119: lines 7 and 8 carry the -ஒடு vowel sign restored from sangamtamil.com (text flags).
109: the colophon thinai is பாலை; the poem has the cold north wind, evening and the cattle shed of a waiting wife, and I infer mullai (irutthal).

110: the colophon thinai is பாலை and its thurai names no speaker; the poem names no land, and I infer mullai from the wife's steadfast household conduct, with the speaker inferred as the foster mother.

115: lines 3 and 4 (இன் நீர்த் தடங் கடல் வாயில் உண்டு சில் நீர் என) are hard to construe; 116: the opening maxim (lines 1 to 3, வழுவப் பிண்டம்) is obscure; 114: lines 1 to 4 (முணக்கவும், பையாந்திசினே) are uncertain.
Natrinai colophons name the speaker and occasion but rarely the addressee; addressees marked as inferred are mine.

reading: The man, within the friend's hearing, says the shore hamlet where curled prawns are heaped to dry in the punnai's shade was a sweet place to live, until he saw the deer-like look of the fisherman's young daughter.
nuance: The whole poem is a before and after: the busy, pleasant work of the shore is described only to be lost, and the loss is dated to one sight of her eyes; spoken where the friend can hear, it is his plea for her help.

நின் குறை முடித்த பின்றை என் குறை

reading: The woman begs the red-beaked parrot, with joined hands, to eat its fill of the millet without fear and then, when it goes to its kin on his jackfruit slopes, to tell the lord of that hill that the young daughter of this hill's kuravar has been set to guard the millet.
nuance: She strikes a bargain with the very bird she is posted to drive away: it may eat the crop if it carries her message, and the message itself (she is at the field by day) is the invitation.

thinai_evidence.note: parrot, jackfruit slope, hill hunters and millet are of the hill

tamil: ஒன்று தெரிந்து உரைத்திசின் நெஞ்சே புன் கால்
களிறு நின்று இறந்த நீர் அல் ஈரத்து
பால் அவி தோல் முலை அகடு நிலம் சேர்த்திப்
பசி அட முடங்கிய பைங் கட் செந்நாய்
reading: Midway on the road for wealth, the man tells his heart to decide one thing: in this strange hot forest, where a hungry red she-dog with dried teats lies curled on ground wet with no water and her mate, gone on his unfailing hunt, grieves thinking of her, we suffer; whether we go on for our work or turn back, it is your choice.
nuance: The wild dogs are a couple split by hunger exactly as he and his wife are split by the hunt for wealth; the male who has gone to hunt yet grieves for his mate is the man himself, so the heart's choice is already answered by the scene.

thinai_evidence.note: a man on the road away from his wife, in the burning waste

iraicchi.act: the male wild dog, gone on a hunt, grieves remembering his mate who lies starving
iraicchi.sense: the man who has left on his own hunt for wealth is bound to grieve for his wife in the same way, so the heart should turn back

tamil: பைந் தாள் செந்தினைப் படு கிளி ஓப்பும்
ஆர் கலி வெற்பன் மார்பு நயந்து உறையும்
உருமு சிவந்து எறியும் பொழுதொடு பெரு நீர்
reading: The woman asks whether anyone but she, who lives loving the chest of the lord of the loud hill where hill boys beat drums at a tiger fighting a tusker and others scare parrots off the millet, ever thinks of the narrow, hard-to-see path he takes at midnight, when thunder strikes the snake-holed hill and the flood blocks the way.
nuance: The hill's children turn the tiger-elephant fight into a game for their drums, fearless; she is the one person on that hill who is afraid, and the fear is for him.

thinai_evidence.note: tiger, millet, the hill lord and the midnight tryst

thurai_akam.note: addressee inferred

tamil: முளி கொடி வலந்த முள் அரை இலவத்து
வெவ் வளி வழங்கும் வேய் பயில் மருங்கில்
நெடு நீர் அற்ற நிழல் இல் ஆங்கண்
அருஞ் சுரக் கவலைய என்னாய் நெடுஞ் சேண்
குட வரைச் சுனைய மா இதழ்க் குவளை
அம் சில் ஓதி அரும் படர் உறவே
reading: The man scolds his heart, which wants to turn back midway: it never weighed the forked tracks of this shadeless, waterless waste where hot wind shakes the thorny silk-cotton and an elephant suffers with its calf, and now it has come far only to pine for her soft hair, fragrant as the bee-visited kuvalai of the springs on Kuttuvan's western hill.
nuance: The rebuke is double-edged: the heart is blamed for not foreseeing the road, but its real fault is that it already turns home to her, and the one rich image in the waste is her hair.

colophon.thurai: இடைச் சுரத்து மீளலுற்ற நெஞ்சினைத் தலைமகன் கழறியது

thinai_evidence.note: the waterless, shadeless track

tamil: எறி திரை கொழீஇய எக்கர் வெறி கொள
அசைஇ உள் ஒழிந்த வசை தீர் குறுமகட்கு
உயவினென் சென்று யான் உள் நோய் உரைப்ப
அறிவு அஞர் உறுவி ஆய் மட நிலையே
reading: Turning back as the season brings a past moment to mind, the man asks his charioteer whether he knows how, on the wave-heaped dune where the striped crab ran and she, unable to keep up, stayed behind, he went and told her his inner pain, and she, unable to answer, pulled down the gnaazhal's hanging cluster and crushed its sprouts till they fell from her hand, lost in her shy distress.
nuance: Her answer to his first confession is a gesture, not a word: her hand tearing at the flowering branch says what her mouth cannot, and it is this silence, not any speech, that calls him home.

colophon.thurai: பருவ வரவின்கண் பண்டு நிகழ்ந்ததோர் குறிப்பு உணர்ந்த தலைவன் அதனைக் கண்டு தாங்ககில்லானாய் மீள்கின்றான் தேர்ப்பாகற்குச்சொல்லியது

tamil: பிடி பிளந்திட்ட நார் இல் வெண் கோட்டுக்
கொடிறு போல் காய வால் இணர்ப் பாலை
செல் வளி தூக்கலின் இலை தீர் நெற்றம்
புல் இலை ஓமைய புலி வழங்கு அத்தம்
reading: The wasting woman tells her friend that she laughs whenever she thinks of it: her heart, which went with her lover along the tiger-haunted track of omai trees where dry paalai pods rattle in the wind like a waterfall, has the good share, while she, left here wearing endless gossip, has the share of pain.
nuance: She divides herself in two and envies the half that left; the laughter is at her own lot, and the pod simile (like the pincer-shaped stalk a she-elephant splits) turns on rare words.

thinai_evidence.note: the paalai tree, omai and the tiger's track

the rattle of the pods in the wind
her heart that went and herself who stayed

tamil: மலை அயற் கலித்த மை ஆர் ஏனல்
முகை ஏர் இலங்கு எயிற்று இன் நகை மடந்தை
reading: The friend tells the lord of the land where hill folk, with arrows, drums and slings, shout from the village edge at a fierce elephant parted from its mate as it nears the millet: even parting from a familiar enemy hurts; how could he let go the bond while this girl with bud-like teeth and flame-bright brow turns pale; she grieves for it.
nuance: The proverb at the turn (பழகிய பகையும் பிரிவு இன்னாதே) shames him: parting from a known foe is hard, and he parts lightly from a lover.

colophon.thurai: வரையாது நெடுங் காலம்வந்து ஒழுகலாற்றாளாய தோழி தலைமகளது ஆற்றாமை கூறி வரைவு கடாயது

her fine brow

his stealthy approach to the girl by night
the clamour and watch of the village that make secret visits dangerous

tamil: உலமர கழியும் இப் பகல் மடி பொழுதே
reading: The woman answers her friend, who keeps asking whether this is her state now that the lover of old friendship, who promised they would be one, has gone: listen; her sorrow cannot be told; as the evening passes with the north wind humming in the dark, she stands alone and turning, like a cow tied by the head in a dripping shed.
nuance: The simile is exact about helplessness: the tied cow in the cold shed cannot move to shelter or to its calf, as she can neither go to him nor stop waiting.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவிடை ஆற்றாளாய தலைமகளது நிலைகண்ட தோழிக்குத் தலைமகள் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: a wife waiting through the cold evening, with the cattle shed and north wind

comparisons.tenor: her lone, restless state

tamil: விரி கதிர்ப் பொற்கலத்து ஒரு கை ஏந்தி
புடைப்பின் சுற்றும் பூந் தலைச் சிறு கோல்
உண் என்று ஓக்குபு பிழைப்ப தெண் நீர்
அரி நரைக் கூந்தற் செம் முது செவிலியர்
reading: Wondering at a daughter's household, the speaker recalls the little girl who ran, gold anklets ringing, under the pandal to refuse the honeyed milk her old nurses chased her with, and asks where she learned this sense and conduct: now that her husband's family has fallen poor, she does not think of the rich rice her father sends, and eats only at alternate meals, small and strong-willed.
nuance: The poem rests on the gap between the two pictures, the spoilt child who would not eat and the wife who will not eat more than her husband's house can give; the closing simile of the fine ripples in flowing water is obscure.

thinai_evidence.note: a wife's steadfast keeping of her husband's house; no land is named

tamil: துய்த் தலை இறவொடு தொகை மீன் பெறீஇயர்
வரி வலைப் பரதவர் கரு வினைச் சிறாஅர்

nuance: The fleet's noisy homecoming is the sound that announces the chariot; the fishermen's sea is drawn as a paalai waste (திரைச் சுரம்) and their fishing as a deer hunt.

tamil: அரும்பு அற மலர்ந்த கருங் கால் வேங்கைச்
சுரும்பு இமிர் அடுக்கம் புலம்பக் களிறு அட்டு
பெருங் கல் நாடன் வரவு அறிந்து விரும்பி
மாக் கடல் முகந்து மணி நிறத்து அருவித்
தாழ் நீர் நனந் தலை அழுந்து படப் பாஅய்
சிலை வல் ஏற்றொடு செறிந்த இம் மழைக்கே
reading: The friend asks what feast she can give this rain-cloud that, knowing the coming of the lord of the great-rock land where vengai has bloomed and a fearless lion kills an elephant, has gladly scooped the dark sea, poured down the sapphire falls and flashes like the mountain blinking, packed with strong thunder.
nuance: She turns the rain, which the waiting woman dreads as a sign of broken time, into a guest who has come ahead of him, and the joke of feasting a cloud is her way of making the heroine smile.

thinai_evidence.note: vengai, lion and the land of great rocks

comparisons.tenor: the lightning

tamil: உழை அணந்து உண்ட இறை வாங்கு உயர்சினைப்
புல் அரை இரத்திப் பொதிப் புறப் பசுங் காய்
கல் சேர் சிறு நெறி மல்கத் தாஅம்
அருஞ் செயல் பொருட் பிணி முன்னி யாமே
பின் இருங் கூந்தலின் மறையினள் பெரிது அழிந்து

reading: Unable to go on in the wilds, the man says that though he has crossed the great forest where green iratthi pods, nibbled by deer, lie strewn on the stony path, her look has come with him: when he said he would go after hard-won wealth, she hid her neythal eyes in her long hair, broken, and sobbed like the ambal pipe the musicians blow on the hushed field after Udhiyan's loud battle.
nuance: The sob is likened not to a lament but to the pipe played on a battlefield after the fighting, so her one moment of grief carries the hush of a field of the dead.

tamil: வெண் கோடு கொண்டு வியல் அறை வைப்பவும்
துளி பெயல் பொறித்த புள்ளித் தொல் கரை
பொரு திரை நிவப்பின் வரும் யாறு அஞ்சுவல்
ஈர்ங் குரல் உருமின் ஆர் கலி நல் ஏறு
பாம்பு கவின் அழிக்கும் ஓங்கு வரை பொத்தி
reading: With the man nearby, the friend tells the woman that, awake all night, she heard the hamlet's noise as white tusks were laid on the rock and raw meat cut, and was troubled: he surely came last night, the hill lord, and she fears the river that rises in waves against its rain-pitted banks, and the thunder that struck the tusker coming down the high hill, leaving the young she-elephant grieving.
nuance: The hamlet's feast on a killed elephant and the thunder that kills another frame the night path as a place where tuskers die; she says it to the heroine but means him to hear.

colophon.thurai: ஆறு பார்த்து உற்ற அச்சத்தால் தோழி தலைவிக்கு உரைப்பாளாய் சிறைப்புறமாகச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the hill lord, elephants and the small hill hamlet

tamil: அன்னையும் சிறிது தணிந்து உயிரினள் இன் நீர்த்
தடங் கடல் வாயில் உண்டு சில் நீர் என
மயில் அடி இலைய மாக் குரல் நொச்சி
மனை நடு மௌவலொடு ஊழ் முகை அவிழ
reading: The friend tells the woman that the rains have come this morning, the peacock-foot leaved nocchi and the jasmine in the yard opening their buds, so that her tired playmates may sleep and even mother breathes easier; though her lover is in a far country he has very great love, and would not stay away even for endless fame: has she not heard what the sky's keeping of time shows?
nuance: The proof is the sky itself: the rains have kept their season, and the friend asks her to read his promise by it; the last words set love above the one thing puram men are praised for seeking, fame.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவிடை ஆற்றாளாய தலைமகளைத் தோழி பருவம் காட்டி வற்புறுத்தியது

thinai_evidence.note: the rains' coming and the jasmine

comparisons.tenor: the nocchi leaves

tamil: இரு வெதிர் ஈன்ற வேல் தலைக் கொழு முளை
சூல் முதிர் மடப் பிடி நாள் மேயல் ஆரும்
மாச் சினை துறந்த கோள் முதிர் பெரும் பழம்
விடர் அளை வீழ்ந்து உக்காஅங்கு தொடர்பு அறச்
ஏ கல் அடுக்கத்து இருள் முகை இருந்த
reading: Refusing her friend's comfort, the woman says the great say one should understand even those who wrong us; the friendship of the hill lord, where a pregnant young she-elephant grazes on bamboo shoots, has broken off and gone far, like a ripe jackfruit that leaves its branch and bursts in a rock cleft, yet the women of the kurinji town, not knowing that, still keep up their gossip about her.
nuance: The bitterness is that the gossip outlives the love it was about: the bond has burst like the fallen fruit, but the town's talk goes on; the opening maxim is hard to construe.

colophon.thurai: வரைவு நீட்டிப்ப ஆற்றாளாய தலைவி தோழிக்கு வன்புறை எதிரழிந்து சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: elephant, jackfruit and the kurinji town

comparisons.vehicle: பலவின் மாச் சினை துறந்த கோள் முதிர் பெரும் பழம்
comparisons.tenor: the broken friendship

tamil: இருங் கழி ஓதம் இல் இறந்து மலிர
வள் இதழ் நெய்தல் கூம்ப புள் உடன்
செல் சுடர் மழுங்கச் சிவந்து வாங்கு மண்டிலம்
கல் சேர்பு நண்ணிப் படர் அடைபு நடுங்க
reading: Refusing comfort, the woman tells her friend that in the sorrowful evening, when the sea roars, the tide overflows the houses, the neythal closes, birds go together to their nests and the reddened sun sinks to the hill, he does not think of her, and she will not live many days; people call her sickness something else, and it is not right that the blame should fall elsewhere either.
nuance: The closing lines turn from grief to a sharper point: if her love-sickness is taken for something else, the man escapes the blame, and she will not let him.

colophon.thurai: வரைவு நீட ஆற்றாளாய தலைவி வன்புறை எதிரழிந்து சொல்லியது சிறைப்புறமும்ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the shore at sunset

iraicchi.act: the birds go together to their nests in the grove at evening
iraicchi.sense: even the birds come home together at dusk, while he does not come or think of her

tamil: தளிர் கவின் எய்திய தண் நறும் பொதும்பில்
சேவலொடு கெழீஇய செங் கண் இருங் குயில்
புகன்று எதிர் ஆலும் பூ மலி காலையும்
வால் இதழ் அலரி வண்டு பட ஏந்தி
reading: The woman says that even in the flowering season, when the red-eyed koel with its mate calls back eagerly from the mango boughs on the bank, she thinks he who left has surely forgotten them; and beyond that, her heart aches at the stranger woman who goes street by street crying new pathiri flowers, fluffy-tipped like a painter's brush dipped in lac.
nuance: The flower-seller is a stranger to her grief and that is the wound: the season is being sold cheerfully in every street, and she must hear it.

thinai_evidence.note: the woman left behind in the spring by a man gone away

thurai_akam.note: addressee inferred

iraicchi.act: the koel, together with its mate, calls back eagerly in the flowering season

tamil: சிறு பொறி மாட்டிய பெருங் கல் அடாஅர்
ஒண் கேழ் வயப் புலி படூஉம் நாடன்
இன் முசுப் பெருங் கலை நன் மேயல் ஆரும்
பல் மலர்க் கான் யாற்று உம்பர் கருங் கலை
reading: With the man listening, the friend says that the lord of the land where a hill farmer's stone trap, set for the millet-eating boar, catches a bright strong tiger, though he came to have his fill, will come to the shade of the great hill beyond the flowered forest river, where langurs and stags leap with wild goats, wearing kulavi and kuuthalam, and will not get a single embrace; let his sulking be greater than his mountain.
nuance: She tells him that the girl is now shut in the house: he will come to the usual place in his hill garland and find no one.

thinai_evidence.note: millet, boar, tiger and hill flowers

ullurai.tenor: the lover and the girl's family who have shut her in
