pairs.situation: the family's confinement of the girl, set against intruders
the strong lover himself is caught and foiled by it

ullurai.speaker_fit: the friend uses the hill farmer's trap and tiger in a kurinji poem (porul 7.27)

tamil: தட மருப்பு எருமை மட நடைக் குழவி
தூண் தொறும் யாத்த காண்தகு நல் இல்
கொடுங் குழை பெய்த செழுஞ் செய் பேதை
சிறு தாழ் செறித்த மெல் விரல் சேப்ப
புகை உண்டு அமர்த்த கண்ணள் தகை பெறப்
பிறை நுதல் பொறித்த சிறு நுண் பல் வியர்
அம் துகில் தலையில் துடையினள் நப் புலந்து
reading: Having come in with a guest as his way in, the man says that in the fine house where buffalo calves are tied to every pillar, his young wife, her soft fingers reddening as she cuts wet slices of vaalai fish, eyes smarting with smoke, wiping the sweat from her crescent brow with her garment's edge and sulking at him, is in the kitchen; let guests come to them, for she will not be angry then, and he will see her face smile with small sharp teeth showing.
nuance: The guest is his weapon in the quarrel: hospitality forbids her a sour face, so the man who caused the sulk can count on her smile.

thinai_evidence.note: the wife's sulking, with buffalo and vaalai fish of the fields

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: spoken to no one named

comparisons.tenor: her brow

title: natrinai 121-140
theme: Natrinai 121 to 140: secret loves of the hills kept on the clock of millet-guarding and pressed toward marriage, shore laments of gossip and lost play, heroes who argue their hearts out of journeys for wealth, and returns home through rain, with the friend speaking for, against and as the woman.
source_issues: 128: line 12 of the text (குறை நேர்ந்த தோழி தலைவி குறை நயப்பக் கூறியது) is a colophon thurai, not verse; it is the first alternative of the colophon, whose printed thurai ends ...நின்றதூஉம் ஆம். The poem is lines 1 to 11.

134: line 6 differs strongly from sangamtamil.com (ஏவினன் மன்னே நுந்தை, யாயும்); ours kept, and the sense of who spoke (mother or father) depends on it. The colophon thurai keeps the old encoding அ·து for அஃது.
124: colophon thinai நெய்தல்; the poem is a friend stopping a departure, with mullai things (ஈங்கை, அதிரல், நவ்வி) and the rainy season; I infer paalai, mixed.
129: colophon thinai குறிஞ்சி; the poem answers an announced departure, which I infer as paalai, with the night thunder and snake of the hills.

132: colophon thinai நெய்தல்; the poem is a guarded house at night in rain with no shore things, which I infer as kurinji. The closing lament is in the first person though the colophon makes the friend the speaker.
133: colophon thinai குறிஞ்சி; the poem names no land and turns on enduring the wait, which I infer as mullai.
130: lines 1 to 4 (the chariot drum and செந் நீர்ப் பொது வினை) are hard to construe.
136: line 7 (நீப்ப நீங்காது வரின் வரை அமைந்து) is hard to construe; the reading of the father as subject is mine.

tamil: இடு முறை நிரப்பிய ஈர் இலை வரகின்
கவைக் கதிர் கறித்த காமர் மடப் பிணை
பரியல் வாழ்க நின் கண்ணி காண் வர
விரி உளைப் பொலிந்த வீங்கு செலல் கலி மா
வண் பரி தயங்க எழீஇ தண் பெயற்
கான் யாற்று இகுமணற் கரை பிறக்கு ஒழிய
மெல் இறைப் பணைத் தோள் துயில் அமர்வோயே
reading: The charioteer tells the hero, his work done and the king's leave given, not to fret: the town of the woman he loves lies in forest land where a young doe that nibbled the forked ears of millet rests beside her stag, and the plumed horses will cross the rain-cooled stream so that he may sleep tonight on the soft shoulders of the wife who is making ready the evening feast for guests.
nuance: The king's release is given in one clause and the rest of the poem is road and home: duty ends abruptly, and the charioteer measures the distance left by things the hero can see, the doe at rest, the stream bank falling behind, so that the wife's evening feast for guests becomes the poem's goal.

colophon.thurai: வினை முற்றி மறுத்தரும் தலைமகற்குத் தேர்ப்பாகன் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: millet fields, forest pasture and the deer pair of the mullai land, with a return home

thurai_akam.speaker: pira
thurai_akam.note: the speaker is the charioteer (தேர்ப்பாகன்), not among the person codes

comparisons.tenor: the wife's shoulders, rounded like bamboo

iraicchi.act: the doe, having fed on the millet ears, rests together with her stag
iraicchi.sense: the pair at rest after feeding promises the hero the same rest beside his wife tonight

tamil: நரை உரும் உரறும் நாம நள் இருள்
நின்று மதி வல் உள்ளமொடு மறைந்தவை ஆடி
reading: With the hero listening outside, the friend tells the girl that the red millet their brothers ploughed on the slope will soon be guarded, the jasmine by the hamlet has budded, the mother has turned a frowning face on her secret doings and asks whether the hill man really comes through the thunder-filled midnight, so the girl must herself decide how the flower garland can be made to fit, that is, how the man can be brought to marry.
nuance: Every detail is a clock for the man outside: the millet to be guarded, the jasmine in bud and the mother's question all say the meetings are nearly over, and the closing riddle of the garland leaves him to supply the word marriage.

colophon.thurai: சிறைப்புறமாகத்தோழி தலைவிக்கு உரைப்பாளாய்த் தலைவன் கேட்பச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: hill millet, the hamlet in the rocks and a night tryst nearing discovery

occasion.words: சிறைப்புறமாகத்தோழி தலைவிக்கு உரைப்பாளாய்த் தலைவன் கேட்பச் சொல்லியது

comparisons.tenor: the marriage that will bind the lovers openly

tamil: இரை ஆர் குருகின் நிரை பறைத் தொழுதி
வாங்கு மடற் குடம்பை தூங்கு இருள் துவன்றும்
கள் கமழ் அலர தண் நறுங் காவி
அம் பகை நெறித் தழை அணிபெறத் தைஇ
வரி புனை சிற்றில் பரி சிறந்து ஓடி
புலவுத் திரை உதைத்த கொடுந் தாட் கண்டல்
சேர்ப்பு ஏர் ஈர் அளை அலவன் பார்க்கும்
reading: With the hero outside, the friend asks the girl to speak: where flocks of fed herons crowd at dusk into nests among the curved fronds of the tall palmyra on the white sand, even their old games of the morning, weaving leaf skirts of fragrant cool lilies with the grove companions, running to the little striped play house, watching the crab at its wet hole under the kandal, have stopped, and the memory has become a great affliction.
nuance: The list of games is the real message to the listener: the girl who was a child of the grove in the morning is now unable to play, so the man who caused it must act; the only creatures with a settled home at nightfall are the herons.

thinai_evidence.note: backwater, palmyra, mangrove and crab of the shore

iraicchi.act: the herons, having fed, come back together at dusk to crowd into their nests
iraicchi.sense: even the birds of the backwater return to a shared home at night, while the man still leaves the girl without one

tamil: முகை வீ அதிரல் மோட்டு மணல் எக்கர்
reading: Told that the hero means to leave, the friend begs him not to go: she cannot bear a life of grief like the anril bird alone without its mate, and the season has come when the eengai buds, the athiral flowers on the sand dune, the deer's hooves sink in it, and bubbles slide over the cool pooled water like a vessel of molten silver.
nuance: The friend says யானும் ஆற்றேன், I myself cannot bear it, speaking in the first person for the woman; the season is offered as proof that a departure now would break the rule that men return before the rains.

thinai_evidence.note: the friend tries to stop a departure; the seasonal things are of mullai and the shore

comparisons.tenor: the lonely life of the woman left behind
the bubbles sliding on the pooled rainwater

tamil: இரை தேர் எண்கின் பகு வாய் ஏற்றை
ஊது உலைக் குருகின் உள் உயிர்த்து அகழும்
நடு நாள் வருதல் அஞ்சுதும் யாம் என
வரைந்து வரல் இரக்குவம் ஆயின் நம் மலை
நல் நாள் வதுவை கூடி நீடு இன்று
துஞ்சு களிறு எடுப்பும் தம் பெருங் கல் நாட்டே
reading: The friend comforts the girl as the marriage is delayed: if we tell him we fear his coming at midnight, when the hungry male bear tears at the striped anthill, roaring so the snake trembles and breathing like a smith's bellows as it digs, and beg him to come to marry, then after a wedding on a good day on our hill he will not delay but take us to his own great hill country, where men in vengai garlands driving oxen on a floor as wide as open land wake the sleeping elephant as they stack the millet.
nuance: The bear at the anthill is the danger of his night road, and a reader may hear in it the man's own hungry coming (seeking at midnight, frightening those within); only one pair holds clearly, so it is left as scene, a near miss for ullurai. The poem's comfort lies in the contrast of nights: the fearful midnight here, the noisy harvest that wakes an elephant in his country.

colophon.thurai: வரைவு நீட்டிப்ப ஆற்றாளாய தலைவியைத் தோழி வற்புறுத்தியது

thinai_evidence.note: bear, vengai and hill millet, with a night tryst and a wedding to come

comparisons.tenor: the bear breathing hard as it digs
the wide threshing floor

tamil: பைங் காய் நல் இடம் ஒரீஇய செங்காய்க்
கருங் களி ஈந்தின் வெண் புறக் களரி
இடு நீறு ஆடிய கடு நடை ஒருத்தல்
ஆள் பெறல் நசைஇ நாள் சுரம் விலங்கி
பனைக் கான்று ஆறும் பாழ் நாட்டு அத்தம்
இறந்து செய் பொருளும் இன்பம் தரும் எனின்
reading: The hero rebukes the heart that is set on wealth: across the ruined land where a dust-bathed bull elephant, hungry to find a man, blocks the path and, seeing no travellers, cools its rage on a palmyra, wealth won by crossing may give pleasure, but no wealth surpasses youth, and once youth has passed wealth cannot bring love, so go alone, heart, with your sickness for wealth that does not last, and may your business prosper.
nuance: The argument turns on a reversal of the usual order: wealth is called நில்லாப் பொருள், the thing that does not stay, and youth the true வளமை; the last line's blessing on the heart's business is ironic, since the man himself stays.

colophon.thurai: பொருள் வலித்த நெஞ்சினைத் தலைவன் நெருங்கிச் செலவு அழுங்கியது

thinai_evidence.note: the waste road and the elephant's rage, with a journey for wealth refused

tamil: இருங் கழி துழைஇய ஈர்ம் புற நாரை
கொழு மீன் ஆர்கைச் செழு நகர் நிறைந்த
reading: The friend turns away the bard: in this hamlet where the wet-backed stork that searched the backwater shivers in the flung spray, what if your man comes? The simple girl, whose brothers are the rough unlettered men who fill the rich fish-eating town, still takes up the doll she played with in the sand long ago and ponders it, and says 'let us go' only to the grove, not to the lord of the soft shore.
nuance: The refusal is made by calling the girl a child: the doll and the sand games say she is not yet a woman to be courted, and her fierce brothers say the courtship is dangerous. Refusing the bard's entry is usually marutham's oodal; here it is set wholly in shore things.

thinai_evidence.note: backwater, stork and seaside grove

tamil: பாம்பு ஊர் மதியின் நுதல் ஒளி கரப்பவும்
குறை நேர்ந்த தோழி தலைவி குறை நயப்பக் கூறியது
reading: The friend says the girl's body has paled like a lamp burning by day and her forehead's light is hidden like the moon the snake swallows, yet she has not told her who is like half of her own life, so let her stop weeping; and the girl answers that while she guarded the millet a man with a garland, an anklet and a chain came and coolly clasped her small back, and since then, with a heart full of that, this is the sickness she has.
nuance: Two similes of light put out by day and by eclipse make the friend's case before the girl speaks; the confession is all objects (garland, anklet, chain) and one touch, the clasp of the small back, which is the whole of the event.

thinai_evidence.note: the meeting in the millet field during its guarding

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the poem itself sets the friend's question (lines 1 to 6) before the girl's confession; the colophon's other alternative has slipped into the text as line 12

comparisons.tenor: the girl's paled body
her forehead whose light is hidden
the friend, as close as a half of the girl's life

tamil: தம் வினை முற்றி வரூஉம் வரை நம் மனை
கேழ் கிளர் உத்தி அரவுத் தலை பனிப்ப
reading: Hear a great joke, friend: the lover whose life changed if a single day passed without us says he will go, leaving us here with our thick hair, and says that we will live on in our house until he finishes his work and returns, and that while we hear alone, at midnight, the roar of thunder from the pouring clouds that makes the bright-hooded snake tremble.
nuance: The joke is the clash of his two sayings: the man who could not survive one day apart now proposes that we survive his whole absence; the closing midnight thunder is what 'we will live' will actually mean.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவு உணர்த்தப்பட்ட தோழி தலைமகளை முகம் புக்கது

thinai_evidence.note: the departure is announced; the night storm and snake belong to the hills

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the poem's 'we' (நம், நாமே) speaks for both women

tamil: வடு இன்று நிறைந்த மான் தேர்த்தெண் கண்
செந் நீர்ப் பொது வினைச் செம்மல் மூதூர்த்
எவன் செய்தனள் இப் பேர் அஞர் உறுவி என்று
எவ்வ நோய் பிறிது உயவுத் துணை இன்றே
reading: Wasting in separation and unmoved by comfort, the woman says that for men of the old town of the chief, where the drum sounds at the centre and the morning's common work begins, nothing is sweeter than the life of their own work; however much they love, they do not think of us, and not once did he look at her yielding heart, loosened shoulders and faded lines and ask what this suffering one will do, so her pain, past the bounds of the sea-girt world, has no companion.
nuance: The complaint is general before it is personal: men find their own work sweetest; then it narrows to the one sentence he never said. The opening lines of chariot, drum and public work are hard to construe and the sense of 'red-water common work' is not secure.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவிடை மெலிந்த தலைவி வன்புறை எதிரழிந்து சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: lament in separation, with no comfort accepted

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the addressee is the friend who offered comfort; not named in the poem

tamil: திரை முதிர் அரைய தடந் தாள் தாழைச்
சுறவு மருப்பு அன்ன முட் தோடு ஒசிய
இறவு ஆர் இனக் குருகு இறைகொள இருக்கும்
நறவு மகிழ் இருக்கை நல் தேர்ப் பெரியன்
reading: When the newly married hero praises the friend for keeping the girl from wasting, she answers: lord of the high sand shore, could we, whose sad hearts cannot even recall the games we played and the groves we rested in, have sulked at all? It was yours to forget, so that my shoulders, fair as Poraiyaru, fragrant with toddy, the town of Periyan of the fine chariot where the herons settle on the screwpine's shark-tooth leaves, grew loose.
nuance: She refuses the praise by refusing the credit: there was no sulking because there was not even strength to remember, and the wasting she prevented was his doing. She says என் நல் தோள், my shoulders, speaking as the girl.

colophon.thurai: மணமனையில் பிற்றை ஞான்று புக்க தோழியைத் தலைவன் வேறுபடாமை ஆற்றுவித்தாய் பெரியை காண் என்றாற்குத் தோழி சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: screwpine, prawns and herons of the shore

comparisons.tenor: the thorned leaves of the screwpine
the girl's shoulders, spoken of as the friend's own

tamil: திருந்து வாய்ச் சுறவம் நீர் கான்று ஒய்யெனப்
பெருந் தெரு உதிர்தரு பெயலுறு தண் வளி
போர் அமை கதவப் புரை தொறும் தூவ
கூர் எயிற்று எகினம் நடுங்கும் நல் நகர்ப்
யாமம் கொள்பவர் நெடு நா ஒண் மணி
reading: The great town sleeps and no one is awake to help; the rain-laden cold wind, spilling from the shark-mouthed spouts onto the broad street, sprays through every chink of the strong doors so that the sharp-toothed dog trembles; the high flowered bed in the fine mansion has guards beside it, and above all the watchmen crying 'guard the gate' strike the long-tongued bell in double beats; is today, wretched as I am, the day I die?
nuance: The whole town is asleep but the house is not: wind, dog, guards and the watchmen's bell are a ring of wakefulness around one bed, so the sleeping town gives no help. The shark-mouthed spouts are carved work, not a creature of the shore, so the poem has no shore things.

thinai_evidence.note: a night meeting barred by the household's guard

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the closing lament (அளியேன்) is in the first person; the friend speaks it as the girl or the colophon's speaker is open to doubt

tamil: சில் பொறி அணிந்த பல் காழ் அல்குல்
இரும்பு செய் கொல்லன் வெவ் உலைத் தெளித்த
நோய் மலி நெஞ்சிற்கு ஏமம் ஆம் சிறிதே
reading: The woman tells her comforting friend that her bangles keep slipping, her eyes have lost their sword-cut shape, pallor has spread over her forehead, and cruel-mouthed women spread talk about the dark girl with spotted skin and gem-bright hair; the loving friend's dear word that he will not cause us suffering is, to her sick heart, a small comfort, like the few drops a smith sprinkles from a dipped frond onto his hot furnace.
nuance: The simile measures the comfort exactly: a smith's sprinkle does not cool the furnace, it only checks it for a moment, and the closing சிறிதே, a little, is the poem's last word.

colophon.thurai: வரைவிடை வைத்துப்பிரிவு ஆற்றாளாய தலைவி வற்புறுத்தும் தோழிக்குச்சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: enduring the wait for marriage on the friend's word; no land is named

comparisons.tenor: the former shape of her eyes
her dark hair

comparisons.vehicle: கொல்லன் வெவ் உலைத் தெளித்த தோய் மடற் சில் நீர் போல
comparisons.tenor: the friend's comforting word to the sick heart

tamil: வரு குறி செய்த வரையகச் சிறு தினைச்
அவ் வாய்த் தட்டையொடு அவணை ஆக என
அம் மா மேனி நிரை தொடிக் குறுமகள்
செல்லாயோ நின் முள் எயிறு உண்கு என
reading: The friend tells the girl, who feared she would be shut indoors, that this must be what is meant by sweet things coming upon sweet: the mother herself told her, 'mountain girl, go with your rattle to drive the red-beaked parrots from the millet on the hill where the lover set the sign of meeting', and the father, long may he live, said softly, 'won't you go, little one of bangles, let me kiss your sharp teeth', while she answered as if unwilling.
nuance: The comedy is that the parents send the girl to the very field where the lover waits, and the friend can only pretend reluctance; the 'sweet upon sweet' proverb is both the joy of the errand and the relief that the confinement feared has not come.

colophon.thurai: இற்செறிப்பார் என ஆற்றாளாய தலைவியை அ·து இலர் என்பது பட தோழி சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: millet guarding with rattles on the hill, the meeting place

tamil: மா அரை புதைத்த மணல் மலி முன்றில்
தண் குடி வாழ்நர் அம் குடிச் சீறூர்
முழங்கு திரைப் புது மணல் அழுந்தக் கொட்கும்
reading: With the hero outside, the friend says their little seaside village, of sand-filled yards where palmyras with hanging leaves rise and the people of cool homes entertain arriving guests with gifts unstinted, was sweet indeed before the men of the chariot, whose white-plumed horses, worn from many dewy tracts, wheel and sink in the new sand of the roaring waves, began laughing with us.
nuance: The praise of a village that welcomes every guest is a pointed reproach: the man came as a guest and laughed with them but has not entered as a bridegroom, and since his visits the sweet village has become a place of talk.

colophon.thurai: வரைவு நீட்டிப்ப அலர்ஆம் எனக் கவன்ற தோழி சிறைப்புறமாகச்சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: palmyra village on the sand by the roaring sea

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no addressee; the girl is assumed

tamil: திருந்து கோல் எல் வளை வேண்டி யான் அழவும்
reading: With the hero outside, the girl tells her friend that when she wept for well-made bright bangles, her father, long may he live, as though he knew of the brief separation between them and the hill lord, did as a righteous physician does who, refusing the gravely sick what they crave, chooses a medicine and gives it: he fitted on her golden bangles that cannot slip off, a help that hides the blame her shoulders would tell.
nuance: She speaks for the man outside: the bangles that slip would announce her wasting, and the father's gold bangle, which cannot slip, hides it; the cure he chose treats the sign, not the sickness, which only the man can cure. The phrase நீப்ப நீங்காது வரின் வரை அமைந்து is hard to construe.

thinai_evidence.note: the hill lord's secret love and a short parting

comparisons.tenor: the father who gives tight gold bangles instead of what she wept for

tamil: தட மென் பணைத் தோள் மட நல்லோள்வயின்
அருவி ஆன்ற நீர் இல் நீள் இடை
கயந் தலை மடப் பிடி உயங்கு பசி களைஇயர்
பெருங் களிறு தொலைத்த முடத் தாள் ஓமை
reading: The hero tells his heart that if it plans to leave the young woman of cool fragrant hanging hair and broad soft shoulders, it has achieved a rare thing indeed, being strong enough to go far through the hill-set forest of the long waterless stretch where the falls of the red rocks have ceased, where the crooked-trunked omai that a great tusker broke to ease the wasting hunger of his young cow-elephant becomes resting shade for those crossing the hard track.
nuance: The praise of the heart is ironic: the 'rare thing' it has achieved is hardness, and the road it would travel shows a beast that breaks a tree to feed its mate.

thinai_evidence.note: the waterless road and a planned departure

comparisons.tenor: the woman's shoulders

iraicchi.act: the tusker breaks the omai tree to relieve the hunger of his young mate in the drought
iraicchi.sense: even the elephant in the waterless land feeds and stays by its mate, so the man who leaves his wife is harder than the beast

tamil: பண் அழி பழம் பார் வெண் குருகு ஈனும்
இழை அணி அல்குல் விழவு ஆடு மகளிர்
reading: With the hero outside, the friend tells the girl troubled by talk: the lord of the cool ford, where the white heron lays its eggs on the broken old cart floor left by bands of salt merchants who carry heaps of salt like hills up to the mountains to sell and abandon what fails them, once wove with us a garland of thick-stemmed neythal flowers; it was known only to our eyes then, but does the noisy old town, where festive women in fine girdles sway to the sweet beat of the waves, not know it today?
nuance: The heron nesting in the cart the wandering merchants abandoned could be read as the girl left by a passing man, but no second pair holds, so it stays scene. The contrast is between kinds of knowing: once only eyes knew, now the whole festive town does.

colophon.thurai: அலர் ஆயிற்று என ஆற்றாளாய தலைமகட்குத் தலைவன் சிறைப்புறமாகத் தோழி சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: salt, salt-merchants, neythal flowers and the shore ford

comparisons.tenor: the heaps of salt

tamil: படுமலை நின்ற நல் யாழ் வடி நரம்பு
புணர்ந்து இனிது நுகர்ந்த சாரல் நல் ஊர்
reading: Back from his work and lying in the bedchamber, the hero blesses the great roaring cloud: may it spread over every peak of the hills set in many places as the world's linchpin and worshipped by many, for with drops like the plucked fine string of a lute tuned to the padumalai mode, humming like the clay-smeared face of the drum, it scattered mixed flowers and poured night rain on the slope town where he lay embraced with the dark woman of thick curled hair and enjoyed her sweetly.
nuance: A blessing is a thanksgiving: the cloud is praised as a helper (உதவியோயே) for a private night, and the poem's music images (lute string, drum) make the rain an accompaniment to the reunion.

colophon.thurai: தலைவன் வினைமுற்றி வந்து பள்ளி இடத்தானாக பெய்த மழையை வாழ்த்தியது

thinai_evidence.note: the rain at night after a return

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the addressee is the rain cloud

comparisons.tenor: the hills that hold the world steady
the streaks and sound of the falling rain
the humming of the rain

tamil: கொண்டல் மா மழை குடக்கு ஏர்பு குழைத்த
சிறு கோல் இணர பெருந் தண் சாந்தம்
வகை சேர் ஐம்பால் தகை பெற வாரி
நெடுந் தேர் வழங்கும் நிலவு மணல் முற்றத்து
மருந்து பிறிது இல்லை யான் உற்ற நோய்க்கே
reading: Refused, the hero tells his heart not to weary of following: the merciless girl who combs into five parts the sandal paste of the cool tree fed by the eastern rain clouds, sheds its dust when it dries on her cropped hair, and goes with her ball across the moonlit sand yard where her father's tall chariot runs, to her big-eyed companions' delight; whether she is kind or not, there is no other medicine to end the hard grief of the sickness he has.
nuance: The girl he cannot win is shown entirely at play, combing, scattering dust, chasing a ball, and the word பரிவிலாட்டி, the woman without pity, is fitted to a child who does not yet know she has been asked.

colophon.thurai: குறை மறுக்கப்பட்ட தலைவன் தன் நெஞ்சினை நெருங்கியது

thinai_evidence.note: a suitor refused in the courting stage

comparisons.tenor: the girl's favour, the only cure

title: natrinai 141-160
theme: Natrinai 141-160: the night path and its dangers, feared by the woman (144, 154, 158) and refused or redirected by the friend (151, 156); the house that learns, through a mother's scent of hair (143), a girl's guilty denial (147), the town's gossip and the cane (145, 149); the madal rider's public ride (146, 152); men held back or summoned home by a woman's hair and season (141, 142, 157); separation borne (148, 153); first wonder and its answer (155, 160); a courtesan's mockery (150); and the friend's demands for marriage (159).
source_issues: 142 line 3 is a repaired line (lost vowel sign ொ restored, flagged by show); marked as repaired.
150 line 5: '·' is the old encoding of ஃ (flagged); marked as அஃது. Lines 2-6 (the Vazhuthi simile and who says 'we care nothing for it') are hard to construe; the verse is marked uncertain.
153 line 1 recurs word for word as Natrinai 346 line 1 (flagged); marked as written.
160: the record names no poet, and line 1 is not in sangamtamil.com (flagged); marked as our text has it.

143, 154 and 158: the colophon thurai names no speaker; the speaker in thurai_akam is inferred from the poem. 144's thurai reads ஆற்றது ஏதத்திற்குக்கவன்று, apparently for ஆற்றினது ஏதத்திற்குக் கவன்று; copied as written.
146 lines 6-11: the construction (who gathers, who is 'skilled in saying we are good', what the heart does) is uncertain; marked uncertain. 154 line 7 தூவிலாட்டி is a rare form; marked uncertain.
Thinai differs from the colophon in 146 and 152 (madal, perunthinai by porul), 149 (elopement, paalai by uri) and 155 (lovers' meeting, kurinji by uri); the colophon is copied unchanged.

tamil: இருஞ் சேறு ஆடிய கொடுங் கவுள் கய வாய்
பொரி அரை ஞெமிர்ந்த புழற் காய்க் கொன்றை
குன்று உறை தவசியர் போல பல உடன்
அருஞ் சுரம் எளியமன் நினக்கே பருந்து பட
பாண்டிலொடு பொருத பல் பிணர்த் தடக் கை
ஏந்து கோட்டு யானை இசை வெங் கிள்ளி
வம்பு அணி உயர் கொடி அம்பர் சூழ்ந்த
அரிசில் அம் தண் அறல் அன்ன இவள்
reading: The man tells his heart, bent on going for wealth, that the hard dry tract where long-podded konrai trees, rubbed by rain-season elephants muddy from wallowing, stand together in the heat like unbathed hill ascetics with long matted locks, would be easy for it; but he will not leave her spreading, thick hair, like the cool dark ripples of the Arisil that runs round Ambar of the tall flags, town of Killi, famous for his tusked elephants that fought chariots while kites wheeled above.
nuance: மன் in line 7 makes the ease counterfactual: the road would be easy, if he could go. The ascetic simile turns the konrai, a rain-season tree of the mullai, into figures of renunciation standing in the waste, which is exactly what he declines to become.

colophon.thurai: பொருள் கடைக்கூட்டிய நெஞ்சிற்குத் தலைவன் சொல்லிச் செலவு அழுங்கியது

thinai_evidence.note: a man weighing a journey through the waste for wealth, and refusing it

comparisons.tenor: the konrai trees, their long dry pods like matted hair, standing together unwashed in the heat
her spreading dark hair

tamil: வான் இகுபு சொரிந்த வயங்கு பெயற்கடை நாள்
பாணி கொண்ட பல் கால் மெல் உறி
ஞெலி கோல் கலப் பை அதளொடு சுருக்கி
பறிப் புறத்து இட்ட பால் நொடை இடையன்
நுண் பல் துவலை ஒரு திறம் நனைப்ப
தண்டு கால் வைத்த ஒடுங்கு நிலை மடி விளி
reading: Returning with his task done, the man tells his charioteer that her town lies in the woodland of unfailing plenty, where at the end of the rains a milk-trading herdsman, his rope-sling, fire-drill and pot bundled with a hide on his back, stands on one leg propped on his staff in the drizzle, whistling through folded lips to settle his small-headed flock; there lives the gentle young woman whose chastity befits the mullai, who rejoices when a guest comes even at night.
nuance: The herdsman holding still in the rain to keep his flock together is the picture of patient keeping that the last three lines give to the wife; and the praise he chooses is her welcome to guests at night, a householder's virtue, not her beauty.

thinai_evidence.note: the herdsman, his flock and the woodland, with the wife's waiting chastity

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the charioteer (தேர்ப்பாகன்)

comparisons.tenor: her chastity, which waits as the mullai land waits for the rains

tamil: தரு மணல் ஞெமிரிய திரு நகர் முற்றத்து
இன்னா இன் உரை கேட்ட சில் நாள்
reading: The mother, faint, says that every time she sees the swept sand of the fine courtyard, the girl's playmates and the nochchi, her eyes run with tears; yet the girl who called even her parrot kin is without fault: in the few days when she heard the cruel sweet talk of the gossiping women gathered in the old town, she lived on as if she did not know, and said only, 'your hair smells fragrant'.
nuance: The last line is a confession: the scent of her daughter's hair was the sign of a lover, and the mother, already hearing the gossip, let it pass with a remark. She clears the girl (வழு இலள்) and keeps the fault for herself.

thinai_evidence.note: the mother weeps in the house the girl has left

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no speaker; by the poem the mother, speaking to no one present and at the end to the absent girl

tamil: பெருங் களிறு உழுவை தாக்கலின் இரும் பிடி
போது ஏர் உண் கண் கலுழவும் ஏதில்
பிணவுப் புலி வழங்கும் அணங்கு அருங் கவலை
அவிர் அறல் ஒழுகும் விரை செலல் கான் யாற்றுக்
reading: With the man listening nearby, the woman tells her friend that as the dark she-elephant, when a tiger attacks her great bull, shrinks from the uproar as from the roar of massed rain-clouds, so her own flower-like eyes stream and her foolish heart frets, now that she knows he comes by night, flowers pressed on his shoulders, alone across the hard forked paths where the gaping tigress prowls and the deep pools of the fast forest stream are hard to cross.
nuance: Lines 1 to 2 can also be read as the beginning of the scene she fears rather than a matched picture; either way the she-elephant's fear for her mate stands next to the woman's fear for hers.

thinai_evidence.note: elephant, tiger and hill stream of the night path

comparisons.tenor: the uproar of the tiger's attack, heard as thunder
her kohl eyes

iraicchi.act: the she-elephant, when the tiger attacks her bull, is terrified for him
iraicchi.sense: the woman's fear for the man crossing tiger country by night is the fear even a beast feels for its mate, so it is love, not weakness, and he should end it

tamil: இருங் கழி பொருத ஈர வெண் மணல்
மாக் கொடி அடும்பின் மா இதழ் அலரி
தான் யாங்கு என்னும் அறன் இல் அன்னை
யான் எழில் அறிதலும் உரியள் நீயும் நம்
அம்ம வாழி தோழி அவர் தேர் மணிக் குரலே
reading: With the man listening, the friend tells the woman that their unjust mother, even before their bond with the handsome shore lord, where on the wet white sand by the dark backwater women add the large purple blossoms of the adumbu creeper to their garlands, had grown at all close, spoke as if she had already lain with him and asked where she had been; she has a right to read the change in their looks, and now even in the dead of night the bells of his chariot come softly to their punnai-lined street.
nuance: The midnight chariot bells are told to the man who drives the chariot: the house now hears what the mother only suspected, and the only way out of the suspicion is marriage.

colophon.thurai: இரவுக்குறி வந்து தலைமகன் சிறைப்புறத்தானாக தோழி வரைவுகடாயது

thinai_evidence.note: backwater, adumbu creeper and punnai of the shore

tamil: நல் ஏமுறுவல் என பல் ஊர் திரிதரு
கடன் அறி மன்னர் குடை நிழற் போலப்
பெருந் தண்ணென்ற மர நிழல் சிறிது இழிந்து
reading: Speaking so the friend will hear, the man who keeps following addresses a rider of the tall palmyra-stem horse, crowned with flowers no one would sell and roaming town after town as one well smitten: if he will take his word, let him come down a little into a tree's shade as cool as the umbrella of a king who knows his duty and rest before he goes on while the sun moves, for kind people will gather round him; such is the deluded heart that the dark girl, lovely as if painted by a master, has struck.
nuance: வில்லாப் பூ, the flower no one sells, is the erukku of the madal garland, named by what it is not. The colophon calls the poem kurinji; by its matter, the madal, it is the perunthinai of the Tholkappiyam.

thinai_evidence.note: the palmyra-stem horse and its flowers, the lover's public ride of the madal

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the addressee is a madal rider, the speaker's own case shown as another's (முன்னிலைப் புறமொழி)

comparisons.tenor: the cool tree shade offered to the madal rider
the dark girl's beauty, as if painted
the palmyra stem he rides

tamil: தேம் படு சாரற் சிறு தினைப் பெருங் குரல்
செவ் வாய்ப் பைங் கிளி கவர நீ மற்று
எவ் வாய்ச் சென்றனை அவண் எனக் கூறி
வெதிர் புனை தட்டையேன் மலர் பூக் கொய்து
சுனை பாய்ந்து ஆடிற்றும் இலன் என நினைவிலை
reading: With the man listening, the friend tells the girl of the bright forehead that they are done for: when their mother scolded her, asking where she had gone while the red-beaked green parrots carried off the heavy millet heads on the honeyed slope, she stood before her and said she neither knew nor had ever seen the lord of the great waterfall hills, nor plucked flowers with her bamboo clapper, nor dived and bathed in the pool; she did not think, and the lie told the truth; hearing it the mother bowed her head, and the girl's going to the field is over, poor thing.
nuance: The girl's denial lists, unasked, exactly what the lovers did, so the mother learns everything from it; told in the man's hearing, the comic scene is a warning that the field trysts are ended and only marriage remains.

thinai_evidence.note: millet, parrots and the waterfall hills

tamil: நீ அவண் வருதல் ஆற்றாய் எனத் தாம்
நெடுங் கயம் புரிந்த நீர் இல் நீள் இடை
செங் கால் மராஅத்து அம் புடைப் பொருந்தி
வாங்கு சிலை மறவர் வீங்கு நிலை அஞ்சாது
கல் அளைச் செறிந்த வள் உகிர்ப் பிணவின்
இன் புனிற்று இடும்பை தீர சினம் சிறந்து
செங் கண் இரும் புலிக் கோள் வல் ஏற்றை
உயர் மருப்பு ஒருத்தல் புகர் முகம் பாயும்
reading: The friend reassures the woman: he who, looking at her colour and speaking softly, said she could not bear to come there, set out today on his work; they say he is crossing the hard tract along the long waterless stretch where the deep ponds have dried, where in the shade of the red-stemmed kadamba, fearless of the bowmen with their bent bows, a red-eyed tiger, fierce at the kill, springs on the spotted face of a high-tusked bull elephant to end the pangs of his sharp-clawed mate, newly delivered in her rock cave; 'I will not grieve, friend; may his journey prosper.'
nuance: The last line can be heard in the woman's own voice, answering the comfort; the colophon gives the whole poem to the friend, who would then be modelling the answer she wants the woman to give.

thinai_evidence.note: he has left for his work across the waste

iraicchi.act: the male tiger hunts the elephant to relieve the hunger of his mate who has just given birth
iraicchi.sense: the man crossing that land is doing the same for the woman he left, so his going is care for her and she may bear it

tamil: புது மலர் தீண்டிய பூ நாறு குரூஉச் சுவல்
கடு மான் பரிய கதழ் பரி கடைஇ
நடு நாள் வரூஉம் இயல் தேர்க் கொண்கனொடு
அலர் சுமந்து ஒழிக இவ் அழுங்கல் ஊரே
reading: The friend tells the woman that the street women, some and many, glance sidelong and touch forefinger to nose-tip spreading the gossip, and their mother beats her with a little cane; worn out, she has made ready to go with the shore lord whose chariot comes at midnight driven by swift horses whose coloured manes smell of the fresh flowers of the seaside grove they brushed; let this clamouring town carry its gossip and be done.
nuance: The friend says 'I have made ready to go' (யானே) for the woman, speaking as one with her. The finger on the nose-tip is the town's gesture of scandal, the cane the house's answer, and the elopement is the answer to both. The colophon files it under neythal by its shore things; its situation is the elopement of paalai.

colophon.thurai: தோழி தலைவியை உடன்போக்கு வலித்தது சிறைப்புறமாகச் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the decision to leave home with the man

tamil: நகை நன்கு உடையன் பாண நும் பெருமகன்
மிளை வலி சிதையக் களிறு பல பரப்பி
அரண் பல கடந்த முரண் கொள் தானை
வழுதி வாழிய பல எனத் தொழுது ஈண்டு
மன் எயில் உடையோர் போல அஃது யாம்
என்னதும் பரியலோ இலம் எனத் தண் நடைக்
கலி மா கடைஇ வந்து எம் சேரித்
கதம் பெரிது உடையள் யாய் அழுங்கலோ இலளே
reading: The courtesan tells the bard that his lord is a fine joke: like the holders of strong forts who bow and cry 'long live Vazhuthi', whose warring army scattered elephants to break the guard-forest and took many forts, he bowed here, then said he cares nothing at all for it; he drove his prancing horse into her street, showed his garland and chaplet and took her whole heart; will he let it go now? Her mother, cane in hand, is furious and will not relent.
nuance: The Pandya's conquests are borrowed as a measure of submission: the lord is mocked as a vassal who paid homage and then denied it.

colophon.thurai: தலைநின்று ஒழுகப்படா நின்ற பரத்தை தலைவனை நெருங்கிப் பாணற்கு உரைத்தது

thinai_evidence.note: the courtesan's quarrel over the lord, through his bard

comparisons.tenor: the lord who first bowed to her and then disowned her

tamil: நல் நுதல் பசப்பினும் பெருந் தோள் நெகிழினும்
கொல் முரண் இரும் புலி அரும் புழைத் தாக்கிச்
செம் மறுக் கொண்ட வெண் கோட்டு யானை
முறி ஆர் பெருங் கிளை அறிதல் அஞ்சி
செம் முக மந்தி செய்குறி கருங் கால்
பொன் இணர் வேங்கைப் பூஞ் சினைச் செலீஇயர்
குண்டு நீர் நெடுஞ் சுனை நோக்கிக் கவிழ்ந்து தன்
reading: With the man listening, the friend says that even if the girl's fair forehead pales and her broad shoulders grow thin, may the hill lord not come by night, from the slope where a white-tusked elephant, its tusk reddened after goring a fierce tiger at a narrow pass, washes it in the waterfall on the rock, and where a red-faced she-monkey who mated in secret on the pepper-vine slope, afraid that the male's great leaf-eating troop will find out, bends over the deep pool and smooths her tousled hair before climbing the flowering branch of the gold-clustered vengai.
nuance: The elephant washing the tiger's blood from its tusk is the danger of the night path, told as scene; the monkey is the lovers' secret.

thinai_evidence.note: monkey, vengai and pepper slopes of the hill country

ullurai.tenor: the girl and the hill lord meeting secretly by night

pairs.situation: the lovers' secret union
the fear that her kin and the town will learn of it
the girl must hide the traces of the meeting before she is seen

ullurai.speaker_fit: the friend uses a monkey of the kurinji slopes in a kurinji poem (porul 7.27)

tamil: இலங்கு கதிர் மழுங்கி எல் விசும்பு படர
பெடை புணர் அன்றில் உயங்கு குரல் அளைஇ
reading: The man set on the palmyra-stem horse says, so the friend will hear, that love gave him the madal and the blossoms of the close-strung erukku gave him gossip; the sun, fond in its work, gave him loneliness as its bright rays dimmed and it crossed the evening sky; and on top of all that, as the north wind gently scatters spray, night too gave him helplessness, mixed with the weary call of the andril joined with its mate in the nest; what will become of him, pitiable as he is.
nuance: அலர் is both the blossom of the erukku and the town's gossip: the flower he wears is the talk he earns. Each line gives one hour its own gift of pain. The andril joined with its mate only calls; it does nothing a lover does, so it is scene, not iraicchi.

colophon.thurai: மடல் வலித்த தலைவன்முன்னிலைப் புறமொழியாக தோழி கேட்பச்சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the madal and its erukku garland, the lover's public ride

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: he addresses no one present; he speaks of himself so the friend will hear

tamil: குண கடல் முகந்து குடக்கு ஏர்பு இருளி
செம்பு சொரி பானையின் மின்னி எவ் வாயும்
தன் தொழில் வாய்த்த இன் குரல் எழிலி
உண்டல் அளித்து என் உடம்பே விறல் போர்
வெஞ் சின வேந்தன் பகை அலைக் கலங்கி
reading: The woman, wasting in separation, says that as the sweet-voiced cloud that scooped up the eastern sea, rose westward darkening, flashed like a smith's pot pouring copper so that the earth shone, and its work done everywhere went off to the south and was spent, so her heart has gone to him and stayed there; her body, left here, lives on by eating, like the lone man who stayed to guard the ruins of a great town whose people fled when the furious king of mighty wars struck it.
nuance: The poet is named Thanimakanaar, the lone man, from line 10. The body is not dead but a caretaker of an emptied place: it eats so that something remains to guard.

thinai_evidence.note: the woman left behind while her heart goes after the absent man

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no addressee; she speaks of herself

comparisons.tenor: the cloud's lightning
her heart that has gone to him and not come back
her body, left behind and kept alive only by eating

tamil: மஞ்சு தவழ் இறும்பில் களிறு வலம் படுத்த
வெஞ் சின உழுவைப் பேழ் வாய் ஏற்றை
பேர் அஞர் பொருத புகர் படு நெஞ்சம்
நீர் அடு நெருப்பின் தணிய இன்று அவர்
நிலம் பரந்து ஒழுகும் என் நிறை இல் நெஞ்சே
reading: With the man listening, the woman asks her friend whether she can sleep, not hearing it: the forest has fallen silent, the sky spreads a pitch dark as if to split the hills, the many-voiced cloud thunders on without pause, and in the cloud-wrapped thicket a fierce gaping-mouthed tiger that has felled an elephant roars fearfully; her heart, scarred by great distress, would cool like fire quenched with water if he did not come tonight, for each time she thinks of the hard path through the hills that bar the slope, her unrestrained heart runs out over the ground.
nuance: She would rather he did not come than come through such a night, which tells the listening man that the night meetings must end in marriage. தூவிலாட்டி in line 7 is a rare form of address.

thinai_evidence.note: tiger, elephant and the hill slopes of the night path

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no speaker; by the poem it is the woman (என் நிறை இல் நெஞ்சே)

comparisons.tenor: the pitch darkness spread over the sky
her scarred heart that would cool if he stayed away

tamil: விரி பூங் கானல் ஒரு சிறை நின்றோய்
பெருங் கடல் பரப்பின் அமர்ந்து உறை அணங்கோ
சொல் இனி மடந்தை என்றனென் அதன் எதிர்
reading: The man tells how, meeting her a second time, he said to her: you do not play the orai game with your bright-jewelled companions, you do not wear a garland of broad-petalled neythal, you stand apart in the flowering seaside grove; who are you? we bow to you and ask: with a beauty no one tires of seeing, are you a goddess who lives in the wide sea of clear waves, or have you settled on the bank of the dark backwater? speak now, girl; and in answer her sharp-toothed smile opened, and tears spread over her many-petalled kohl eyes.
nuance: She answers his question only with a smile and tears, which no goddess would give: the reply settles that she is a woman. The colophon files it under neythal by its shore; the situation, a meeting of lovers, is the punarthal of kurinji.

colophon.thurai: இரண்டாம் கூட்டத்துத்தலைவியை எதிர்ப்பட்டுத் தலைவன் சொல்லியது உணர்ப்பு வயின் வாரா ஊடற்கண் தலைவன் சொற்றதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the man's approach at a meeting of the lovers before marriage

occasion.words: உணர்ப்பு வயின் வாரா ஊடற்கண் தலைவன் சொற்றதூஉம் ஆம்

comparisons.tenor: the girl, too beautiful to be human

tamil: நீயே அடி அறிந்து ஒதுங்கா ஆர் இருள் வந்து எம்
யாமே நின்னும் நின் மலையும் பாடி பல் நாள்
ஆடு மழை இறுத்தது எம் கோடு உயர் குன்றே
reading: The friend tells the lord of the great rocky hills that his coming through darkness where feet cannot find the way, slipping past the guard of their wide house, shows his great love; but they, singing of him and his hill, will guard the small millet for many days and will go there, so let him come by day and end their many cares; for the people of their hamlet on the great hill of tall reeds, though they have drunk their toddy, are formidable, and the swaying rain has settled on their high-peaked hill, roaring in the rock clefts.
nuance: She refuses the night only by offering the day: the millet field the girls guard is the place she names for the meeting.

thinai_evidence.note: the millet field and the hill hamlet

tamil: இருங் கண் ஞாலத்து ஈண்டு தொழில் உதவிப்
பெரும் பெயல் பொழிந்த வழி நாள் அமையத்து
பல் பொறி அரவின் செல் புறம் கடுப்ப
யாற்று அறல் நுணங்கிய நாட் பத வேனில்
இணர் துதை மாஅத்த புணர் குயில் விளித்தொறும்
குறும் பொறை அயல நெடுந் தாள் வேங்கை
reading: Away for wealth, the man tells his heart, which has sensed the season, that now, after the great rains that served the world's labour, in early summer when the river sand is rippled fine like the back of a spotted moving snake, each time the paired koel calls from the cluster-laden mango, the dark girl with fine scattered freckles, like the pollen shed by the tall vengai beside the low rocks of the forest, will think of them and weep greatly as she hears it.
nuance: The paired koel only calls: its sound carries the season's pain but it does nothing a lover does, so it is scene, not iraicchi. He measures her grief by his own heart, which has already felt the season.

colophon.thurai: பொருள்வயிற் பிரிந்த தலைவன் பருவம் உணர்ந்த நெஞ்சிற்கு உரைத்தது

thinai_evidence.note: the man away from her imagines her weeping at the season

comparisons.tenor: the river sand rippled by the shrinking stream
her fine freckles

tamil: விடர் முகைச் செறிந்த வெஞ் சின இரும் புலி
குருதி பருகிய கொழுங் கவுட் கய வாய்
reading: With the man listening, the woman tells her friend that she has not seen it, for it lies hidden, the path the lord of the high hills comes by: there the stony track must surely break the feet, the thick darkness must surely put out the eyes, and a fierce tiger from a cleft in the rocks, having struck a spotted-faced elephant till it cries out, wipes its fat-cheeked, blood-drinking mouth against the trunk of a vengai.
nuance: Her fear is all imagination: she has never seen the path (யானோ காணேன்), and the tiger wiping its mouth on the vengai is what her mind sets on it.

colophon.thurai: ஆறு பார்த்து உற்ற அச்சத்தால் சிறைப்புறமாகச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: tiger, elephant and vengai of the hill path

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi

occasion.words: ஆறு பார்த்து உற்ற அச்சத்தால் சிறைப்புறமாகச் சொல்லியது

thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no speaker; by the poem it is the woman

tamil: உரவுத் திரை கொழீஇய பூ மலி பெருந் துறை
கொழு மீன் ஆர்கைச் செழு நகர்ச் செலீஇய
reading: The friend tells the man that on the great flower-strewn shore heaped up by the strong waves of the dark wide sea, gleaming like cut sapphire, on the steep sand dune piled like moonlight, they pass the day counting the lines of herons like clustered conches; then if they say 'rise, let us go to the rich house with its punnai yard swept and patterned by the wind, where fat fish are eaten', she will not agree, and they cannot tell her 'stay'; so let the chariot he loves lodge tonight in the little fishing hamlet that sleeps to the sound of breaking waves, so that it wakes in uproar.
nuance: The request that his chariot stay the night is a demand for publicity: a hamlet woken by it will know, and what the town knows must end in marriage.

colophon.thurai: தலைவியின் ஆற்றாமையும் உலகியலும் கூறி வரைவு கடாயது

thinai_evidence.note: herons, punnai and fish of the shore

comparisons.tenor: the dark wide sea
the white sand dune
the line of herons

tamil: எதிர்த்த தித்தி ஏர் இள வன முலை
ஐம் பால் வகுத்த கூந்தல் செம் பொறி
திரு நுதல் பொலிந்த தேம் பாய் ஓதி
அரி மதர் மழைக் கண் காணா ஊங்கே
reading: The man answers his friend's rebuke: good sense, friendship, shame, decency, usefulness, character and conduct that knows what is fitting, he once knew them better than his friend does, before he saw the wide, cool, intoxicating eyes of this girl, like a garland of facing kuvalai blossoms bloomed in an old pond, with her young breasts flecked with freckles, the fine pale spots as if sprinkled, her hair dressed in five parts and her fragrant locks over a fair forehead marked with a red dot.
nuance: He does not deny the virtues his friend preaches; he claims to know them better, so the rebuke teaches him nothing. The list of virtues runs two lines; the list of her features runs seven.

thinai_evidence.note: a man struck by a girl at first sight, before any union

comparisons.tenor: her eyes
the fine pale spots on her breasts

title: natrinai 161-180
theme: Natrinai 161 to 180: men going home and men about to leave, the friend's refusals of bards, dancers and night visits, and the jealousies of the married house.
source_issues: 161: line 9 repaired from a TSCII leftover (தெள்ளிதின்).

tamil: வீ ததர் வேங்கைய வியல் நெடும் புறவின்
நெடுந் தெரு அன்ன நேர் கொள் நெடு வழி
தோள் வலி யாப்ப ஈண்டு நம் வரவினைப்
reading: Going home with the king's hard work finished, the man tells his charioteer of the long straight road through the forest, where blue lilies open like eyes in every hill pool and the vengai sheds its flowers, and wonders whether the omen birds have already told of his coming to her, the honey-voiced woman who soothes their son with a pretence by pointing out strangers to him.
nuance: The hooves cut kaanthal petals that look like bangles (வளை என), and the next words wish her shoulders firm again (தோள் வலி யாப்ப): the road home is already undoing the slack bangles of her waiting. Pointing out strangers to the boy is read here as her passing them off as his father; the phrase is compressed.

colophon.thurai: வினை முற்றிப் பெயரும்தலைவன் தேர்ப்பாகன் கேட்ப சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: a man returning over forest land to a wife who waits is mullai's waiting

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the addressee is the charioteer (தேர்ப்பாகன்)

the long straight forest road
the kaanthal's broad petals

tamil: மனை உறை புறவின் செங் காற் பேடைக்
பெரும் பெயர்த் தந்தை நீடு புகழ் நெடு நகர்
reading: To the girl who weeps that she cannot bear to be alone at the painful evening when even the red-legged dove of the house joins its mate, and says she will come with him, the man answers that she, so delicate beside her mother in her famous father's great house, could hardly be strong enough for the waste where in summer the long hanging roots of the fig swing like a rope cradle in the west wind and stroke a sleeping she-elephant.
nuance: The refusal is tender: the one gentle thing he finds in the waste, a hanging root rocking a sleeping elephant like a cradle, recalls the nursed childhood he names in line 8. The doves of lines 1 and 2 come close to iraicchi (a pair joined at dusk), but the girl draws the sense herself (தனியே இருத்தல் ஆற்றேன்), so they stay scene.

colophon.thurai: உடன் போதுவல் என்ற தலைவிக்குத் தலைவன் சொற்றது

thinai_evidence.note: the girl asks to go with him across the waste

comparisons.tenor: the fig's long hanging roots swinging in the wind

tamil: கறங்கு இசை இன மணி கைபுணர்ந்து ஒலிப்ப
நிலவுத் தவழ் மணற் கோடு ஏறிச் செலவர
இன்று என் நெஞ்சம் போல தொன்று நனி
நீல் நிறப் புன்னைத் தமி ஒண் கைதை
வானம் மூழ்கிய வயங்கு ஒளி நெடுஞ் சுடர்க்
கதிர் காய்ந்து எழுந்து அகம் கனலி ஞாயிற்று
reading: Glad that the marriage is settled, she says: may they breathe again at last, the pitiable blue-dark punnai and the lone bright kaithai of the shore grove, which suffered long, as her own heart did, while day and night, in the sand-laden wind, the shore lord's horses, bells ringing, climbed the moonlit dunes, horses that appear with the beauty of the sun rising at dawn.
nuance: The pity goes to the trees: the punnai and kaithai trampled by his night visits carry the cost of the secret love, and the marriage frees them as it frees her heart (என் நெஞ்சம் போல). Whether அளிய (the pitiable ones) is the trees or the horses is not fixed.

thinai_evidence.note: the shore grove of punnai and kaithai

thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no speaker; the first person (என் நெஞ்சம்) points to the girl

tamil: செங் கதிர்ச் செல்வன் தெறுதலின் மண் பக
வெங் கடற்று அடை முதல் படு முடை தழீஇ
உறு பசிக் குறு நரி குறுகல் செல்லாது
reading: The friend reminds the girl that when he left in the season the rain had deserted and the sun cracked the earth, she told her he had done well though he went, yet the girl would not be convinced, unable to think he could come back unharmed through the waste where bowmen with red-shafted arrows take travellers' lives and even the starving jackal turns back from the rotting dead; now he has come back with his wealth.
nuance: The jackal that will not go near the dead (குறுகல் செல்லாது) measures the road: too dreadful even for the scavenger, so the girl's disbelief was fair, and the friend's news answers fear rather than reproach.

colophon.thurai: பொருள் முடித்து வந்தான் என்பது வாயில்கள்வாய்க் கேட்ட தோழி தலைவிக்கு உரைத்தது

thinai_evidence.note: sun-cracked earth and a waste of robbers

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the news came through the messengers (வாயில்கள்)

tamil: அமர்க் கண் ஆமான் அரு நிறம் முள்காது
அணங்கொடு நின்றது மலை வான் கொள்க எனக்
கடவுள் ஓங்கு வரை பேண்மார் வேட்டு எழுந்து
நப் புணர்வு இல்லா நயன் இலோர் நட்பு
reading: The friend tells the girl that the hill man, from a land where a hunter whose arrow missed a fierce-eyed wild cow decides the mountain held a god and goes up with his kin to worship the peak, keeps telling her how hard it is to meet, yet never says the word that would end it, while marriage messages from other suitors keep multiplying.
nuance: The hunter puts his failed shot down to the hill's divinity and goes to worship rather than shoot again; set beside a lover who only complains of difficulty, it may hint at a man who blames obstacles instead of acting, but only one point maps, so it stays scene. Lines 7 and 8 are hard to construe.

colophon.thurai: நொதுமலர் வரையும் பருவத்து தோழி தலைவிக்கு அறத்தொடு நிலை பயப்பச் சொல்லியது வரைவு மலிந்ததூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the hill hunter and the hill man

reading: To his wife, changed by signs that he means to leave, the man says her body and fragrant dark hair are like gold and sapphire, her eyes and shoulders like flowers and bamboo; whenever he sees them his heart fills and he is like those settled in virtue; their son with gold bracelets has learnt to play, and he has no work in another land, so why should he part from her, when his love is greater than the sea?
nuance: He answers her fear with an inventory of the home: her beauty, his settled virtue, the son's first games, no work abroad. Saying that delight at home makes him like those established in aram (அறம் நிலைபெற்றோர் அனையேன்) treats the household as the seat of virtue, and the very fullness of the denial is the kind of excess a wife reads as a sign.

colophon.thurai: செலவுக் குறிப்பினால் வேறுபட்ட கிழத்திக்குத் தலைவன் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: a feared parting, which he denies

comparisons.tenor: her body and her dark hair
her eyes and her shoulders
himself, content at home
his love

tamil: கருங் கோட்டுப் புன்னைக் குடக்கு வாங்கு பெருஞ் சினை
பண் அமை நெடுந் தேர்ப் பாணியின் ஒலிக்கும்
பயன் தெரி பனுவற் பை தீர் பாண
நின் வாய்ப் பணி மொழி களையா பல் மாண்
மணம் கமழ் கானல் மாண் நலம் இழந்த
பிறை ஏர் திரு நுதல் பாஅய பசப்பே
reading: The friend tells the bard who came with the shore lord's message, a knower of profitable songs and free of care, that his humble words will not remove the pallor spread over the crescent-bright forehead of the bangled girl, who lost her beauty in the fragrant grove where punnai and fresh ngaazhal flowers fall; on that shore the white heron, a guest on the punnai's westward-bending branch, cries with the sound of the tuned chariots bards received at Aay's generous feast-day assembly.
nuance: Each compliment to the bard is barbed: he knows songs that bring gain, he is free of grief, and his master's shore rings with the chariots bards win from Aay. This bard's errand earns nothing here; the only thing spread on his master's shore is the pallor (பாஅய பசப்பே) the master left.

colophon.thurai: தோழி பாணற்கு வாயில் மறுத்தது தூதொடு வந்த பாணற்குச் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the shore grove of punnai and ngaazhal

comparisons.tenor: the white heron's cry
her forehead

tamil: சுரும்பு உண விரிந்த கருங் கால் வேங்கைப்
பெருஞ் சினைத் தொடுத்த கொழுங் கண் இறாஅல்
புள்ளுற்றுக் கசிந்த தீம் தேன் கல் அளைக்
புன் தலை மந்தி வன் பறழ் நக்கும்
நன் மலை நாட பண்பு எனப் படுமோ
நின் நயந்து உறைவி இன் உயிர் உள்ளாய்
அணங்குடை அரவின் ஆர் இருள் நடு நாள்
மை படு சிறு நெறி எஃகு துணை ஆக
reading: The friend asks the lord of the good hill, where honey that birds have pierced from a comb on the vengai branch drips into a rock hollow and the young of the dull-headed female monkey lick what the hill children left, whether it can be called good conduct to come at midnight, in the thick dark of the dread snake, down the narrow black path with only his spear for company, his chest fragrant with sandal, to their small village on the slope, not thinking of the dear life of the girl who lives loving him.
nuance: The scene descends in shares: bees open the flowers, birds pierce the comb, the hill children drink, the monkey's young lick the leftovers. A reader may sense a love enjoyed by stealth and in pieces, but nothing in the poem anchors a second correspondence, so it stays scene. The reproach is for her life (இன் உயிர்), not his: his danger is her danger.

thinai_evidence.note: the midnight tryst on the hill slope

tamil: பரற் தலை போகிய சிரற் தலைக் கள்ளி
reading: On his way back with the task done, the man tells his heart: if we have finished what we set out to do, will you chirp, lizard of the long wall, to end the worry of the fair-browed one who waits saying he will come, in our great house in the small village, where at evening the strong-handed herdsman, turning back the leading sheep, plucks the jasmine that has climbed over the kalli on the gravel and weaves it with white palm strips into a garland whose scent fills the street?
nuance: He does not wait for her omen: he speaks to the lizard as if he could make it chirp, so the sign she listens for at home becomes a message he would send. The herdsman's jasmine garland scenting the street at dusk is the mullai evening at its gentlest, the hour she is likeliest to grieve.

thinai_evidence.note: jasmine, a herdsman and sheep at dusk

tamil: மடக் கண் தகரக் கூந்தல் பணைத் தோள்
வார்ந்த வால் எயிற்று சேர்ந்து செறி குறங்கின்
பலர் உடன் கழித்த ஒள் வாள் மலையனது
reading: Turning away the dancer sent for the husband, the friend describes a girl with innocent eyes, tagaram-scented hair, bamboo-smooth arms, white teeth and close thighs, wearing a leaf skirt, who has come alone and stands making the festival ground shine; rise, rise, she cries, to guard our husband, and yet, as the many Aryans thronging famous Mullur fled before the single spear of Malaiyan of the bright sword, what use are our numbers if this one woman's strength prevails?
nuance: The wives speak as an army and the rival as a lone champion, and the borrowed battle runs against them: in the story the many fled and the one won. The friend turns the household's numbers into a joke at its own expense, and the joke is her refusal: the dancer's errand is pointless when the husband is already won. The colophon gives the speech to the friend, though எம் கொழுநன் sounds like the wives' own voice.

thinai_evidence.note: wives guarding a husband against a festival dancer

comparisons.tenor: the many wives helpless before one rival
her arms

tamil: நிலம் செல செல்லாக் கயந் தலைக் குழவி
பன் மலை அருஞ் சுரம் இறப்பின் நம் விட்டு
வினைப் பூண் தெண் மணி வீழ்ந்தன நிகர்ப்பக்
reading: Told that the man will leave, the friend says to the girl: he comes from a land where the elephant, straining for water on the scorched summer slope, leaves behind its soft-headed calf that cannot keep pace, and the calf, to the pity of the village women, walks into the town with the cows' calves; if he crosses the many-hilled hard waste and leaves us, how will her eyes bear it, eyes used to lying on his chest with eager heart at midnight, the hour the ghosts walk?
nuance: The calf left behind by a herd gone for water is a near miss for iraicchi: one carrier, and its plight is hers, but it does nothing a person of the situation does; it is the one abandoned, and the poem never draws the parallel. A land where even a strayed calf is taken in sharpens the question of who will take her in. Lines 7 to 9 (ஞாங்க ... நிகர்ப்ப) are obscure.

thinai_evidence.note: the man is to cross the waste and leave her

comparisons.tenor: the hush of midnight

tamil: நெய் பெய் தீம் பால் பெய்து இனிது வளர்ப்ப
வலம்புரி வான் கோடு நரலும் இலங்கு நீர்த்
reading: The friend tells the shore lord who has come for a daytime meeting that as girls at play they pressed a seed into the white sand and forgot it; when it sprouted they raised it with sweet milk and ghee, and their mother said this punnai is your elder sister, nobler than you; so they are ashamed to laugh with him beneath it, and if he means to grant them grace there are other shades, on his shore where the white right-spiralled conch sounds like the pale music of guest bards.
nuance: The mother's word makes the tree kin, and kin may not witness a secret meeting: the friend's shame is a polite fiction that turns the tryst away and points him to the one proper shade, marriage, which நீ நல்கின் says without saying it.

colophon.thurai: பகற்குறி வந்த தலைமகனைத் தோழி வரைவு கடாயது குறிபெயர்த்தீடும் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the punnai on the white sand and the conch of the shore

comparisons.tenor: the sound of the right-spiralled conch

tamil: அம் மலை கிழவோன் செய்தனன் இது எனின்
படு வண்டு ஆர்க்கும் பைந் தார் மார்பின்
reading: With the man listening outside, the friend asks the girl: the mother who loves them took for the god's seizure what followed his gifts of spring flowers, garlands and red kaanthal chaplets of the hill, and has it shown in waking and in dreams; if she is told that the lord of that gem-bright mountain caused this sickness, which comes no other way, would that wrong tall Vel of the bee-loud green garland? Tell me, bangled one, I ask.
nuance: The question is a move, not a scruple: asking whether naming the man would offend Murugan lets the overhearing lover know that disclosure (அறத்தொடு நிலை) is near and that the veri rite is being held for the wrong cause.

colophon.thurai: தோழி தலைவிக்கு உரைப்பாளாய் சிறைப்புறமாகச் சொல்லியது வெறி அச்சுறீஇத் தோழி அறத்தொடு நிலை பயப்பித்ததூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: hill-spring flowers, red kaanthal and Murugan

occasion.words: வெறி அச்சுறீஇத் தோழி அறத்தொடு நிலை பயப்பித்ததூஉம்

comparisons.tenor: the gleaming mountain

tamil: ஆள் இல் அத்தத் தாள் அம் போந்தைக்
கோளுடை நெடுஞ் சினை ஆண் குரல் விளிப்பின்
புலி எதிர் வழங்கும் வளி வழங்கு ஆர் இடைச்
பிரியாது ஒரு வழி உறையினும் பெரிது அழிந்து
reading: To the friend who says that though her lover is back from the windy waste, where the lone palmyra bears fruit like ripe date clusters and the tiger walks when the male call sounds from its branch, and has embraced her sweetly and stays by her without parting, she is still wasted, the girl answers that it may look so to those who do not know: he has given his rich chest to a woman who takes without loving, and what is an embrace worth where there is no love?
nuance: The friend measures the return by presence (பிரியாது ஒரு வழி உறையினும); the girl measures it by love and finds it gone. The paalai waste of the opening is only the road he came back by; the grief is a marutham grief, another woman at his chest. வீழாக் கொள்கை வீழ்ந்த கொண்டி is compressed and its sense is not certain.

colophon.thurai: வினை முற்றி வந்து எய்திய காலத்து ஆற்றாளாய தலைவியைத் தோழி வற்புறீஇ நின்றாட்கு அவள் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: a returned husband who has another woman

comparisons.tenor: the palmyra's fruit clusters

tamil: நெடுங் கடல் அலைத்த கொடுந் திமிற் பரதவர்
கொழு மீன் கொள்ளை அழி மணல் குவைஇ
சிறு தீ விளக்கில் துஞ்சும் நறு மலர்ப்
அடு பால் அன்ன என் பசலை மெய்யே
reading: With the man listening, the friend says that the mother does not even know the lord of the shore, where fishermen who tossed on the long sea in curved boats heap their fat catch on the sand and sleep by small lamps of shells filled with fish oil under the fragrant punnai; yet at midnight, trusting the petty talk of the hamlet women, she looks as if to burn at my body, pale as boiled milk.
nuance: The mother has never seen the man and judges by gossip alone, so her burning look falls on the only evidence she can see, the pallor. The fishermen's small shell lamps, fires that let them sleep, stand against a mother's look that lets the girl have no rest.

tamil: எம் நயந்து உறைவி ஆயின் யாம் நயந்து
நல்கினம் விட்டது என் நலத்தோன் அவ் வயின்
போது பொதி உடைந்த ஒண் செங் காந்தள்
வாழை அம் சிலம்பின் வம்பு படக் குவைஇ
யாழ் ஓர்த்தன்ன இன் குரல் இன வண்டு
reading: The other woman, speaking to a dancer so that those close to the wife's friend may hear, asks whether the wife can really claim to love the man when she does not know how to keep him with grace, since she herself loved him and freely let him go; and she points to their home, a hill-fenced village on the plantain slope where red kaanthal bursts from the bud like the stripes on elephants' faces and bees hum like a lute to the drum of the falling stream.
nuance: The boast carries a jab: the rival says she let him go out of generosity, so his being at home is her gift, not the wife's hold. The soft hill-slope ending, bees and waterfall in one music, makes the wife's home sound idyllic only to say it could not keep him. Lines 1 to 4 are compressed and the sense is not fixed.

tamil: பரந்து படு கூர் எரி கானம் நைப்ப
ஒதுக்கு அரும் வெஞ் சுரம் இறந்தனர் மற்றவர்
reading: Reading his signs, the girl tells her friend that he has already crossed in mind the hot, hard waste where spreading fire wears down the forest and the trees burn; she has seen it in his ways: his spear is wiped bright along the blade, his shield crowned with peacock feathers and hung with bells, and he is far more tender than before; now, friend, the day seems to have come when the pupils of her painted eyes, aching again and again, will swim in a rising flood.
nuance: She reads two signs together, the war gear made ready and the excess of tenderness (பண்டினும் நனி பல அளிப்ப); either alone would mean little. Her tears become a flood the little figure in her eye must swim, grief turned into a drowning.

tamil: தோடு அமை தூவித் தடந் தாள் நாரை
கழி பெயர் மருங்கில் சிறு மீன் உண்ணாது
கைதை அம் படு சினைப் புலம்பொடு வதியும்
reading: With the man standing by, the friend says that the chariot of the lord of the cool shore, where the poor female heron, whose beauty her big-legged mate with crest feathers like finely kneaded soft pith has enjoyed, will not eat the small fish at the backwater's edge but sits in loneliness on the drooping kaithai branch, could once be seen with the eyes; now, ashamed, I get no sleep even in the dead of night, I take every bird cry for his bells and listen, and my heart that trusted him has perished.
nuance: The heron hen carries the whole situation unspoken: enjoyed and left (நலன் உணப்பட்ட), she will not eat, and she sits alone, as the girl, now kept at home (செறிப்பு), wastes and cannot sleep. The friend speaks the last lines in the girl's first person.

tamil: இல் எழு வயலை ஈற்று ஆ தின்றென
அவ் வயிறு அலைத்த என் செய் வினைக் குறுமகள்
முருந்து ஏர் வெண் பல் முகிழ் நகை திறந்தே
reading: The foster mother recalls that when the calving cow ate the vayalai creeper growing by the house, her girl threw her ball to the ground, cast away her doll and beat her own belly, and with a bewildered look like a doe's would not drink the honey and sweet milk she and the mother pressed on her but swelled with sobs; she was like that only yesterday, and today they say she has crossed the hard waste trusting the false word of a dark-bearded youth, opening her budding smile of white teeth like peacock-quill tips.
nuance: The poem ends on a smile: the child who sobbed over a creeper and refused milk from two mothers goes off smiling, and the bewilderment at home (மனை மருட்சி) is at that change. The speaker's யானும் தாயும் makes her the foster mother.

tamil: பலர்ப் பெறல் நசைஇ நம் இல் வாரலனே
இரு பெரு வேந்தர் பொரு களத்து ஒழித்த
reading: The friend, who had let the husband in, seeing the wife's jealousy says: the man of the town where the field heron rubs against the ant-swarmed nest on the bitter gourd and the ants spill like white rice mixed with red paddy, wanting many women, does not come to our house, and she, trusting her dark beauty, will not let him go; like the ruin of the punnai felled on the battlefield of two great kings, Anni great and the other greater, this quarrel of the two of them will end with me.
nuance: The friend casts herself as the punnai, the tree destroyed because two powers fought over it, and the go-between who let the husband in fears she will pay for the couple's quarrel. The heron breaking the ants' nest is a near miss for ullurai (a man breaking a household), but only one pair maps. Who trusts the dark beauty in line 5 is not certain.

title: natrinai 181-200
theme: Natrinai 181 to 200: shore and hill love in short scenes, a sparrow's evening and a moon called to witness, mothers left behind by eloping daughters, friends who press for marriage through confinement and harvest, and Kolli's god-made figure used to measure a girl's beauty as both danger and protection.
source_issues: 181, 183, 184: line repaired for the lost vowel sign of -ஒடு, as show flags.
190: line 3 has ஃ restored from the old encoding, as show flags.
197: line 4 is a repaired TSCII leftover (தேயர் is read as printed), as show flags.
198: the colophon makes the speaker the foster mother (செவிலி), but line 12 says ஈன்றேன் யானே, 'I bore her'; the speaker is coded sevili as the colophon has it.
186: the colophon says the heroine speaks to a friend who has wasted (மெலிந்த தோழிக்கு); it is copied as it stands.
182: line 7 repeats natrinai 235 line 7, as show flags.

tamil: உள் இறைக் குரீஇக் கார் அணற் சேவல்
பிற புலத் துணையோடு உறை புலத்து அல்கி
தார் அணி புரவி தண் பயிர் துமிப்ப
reading: The friend watches the evening: a sparrow cock that had lodged with companions in other fields comes back drenched, and the hen, guarding her small chicks bright as iingai flowers, first bars him from the nest, then, seeing his wet back, gives him a place beside her and calls him in with a softened heart; because that helpless, bewildering evening had come, the chariot came, its garlanded horses cutting the cool crops, and the beauty of this girl's brow is saved.
nuance: Line 2 lets the cock's night away be read as a stay with another mate, which would make the hen's relenting a lesson in forgiveness; the friend does not press it, and the poem only needs the evening return. The horses 'cutting the cool crops' shows the chariot taking the shortest way, through the fields.

colophon.thurai: வினை முற்றிப் புகுந்தது கண்ட தோழி மகிழ்ந்து உரைத்தது

reading: With the man listening outside, the friend tells the girl the moon has set and darkness has come, and the mother of great wealth who guards her, doll-like, in the wide house that looks like a painting, sleeps; let us go softly, see him, and embrace his good chest close as one takes up a fine jewel that was lost, for he has come alone like a great tusker left by the keepers above and below, out in the cold.
nuance: The proposal is addressed to the girl but aimed at the listener: the riskiness of the night, the sleeping guardian and his lonely state as a keeperless elephant all tell him that secret visits cannot go on, which is how the friend presses for marriage.

tamil: நெடு நெறி ஒழுகை நிலவு மணல் நீந்தி
அவண் உறை முனிந்த ஒக்கலொடு புலம் பெயர்ந்து
இன மீன் ஆர்ந்த வெண் குருகு மிதித்த
reading: The friend tells the shore lord, who is leaving with the marriage put off, that even the salt merchants' going is painful, who bring white paddy from their own country, cry the price of salt from another, drive long lines of carts across moonlit sand and move with their kin; he is foolish, for evenings with the cruel wind now hold the loneliness of his absence, and he does not consider that she will not live, like a neythal in shallow water trampled by a white heron that has fed on shoals of fish.
nuance: The salt merchants are strangers who leave with their whole household and still sadden the shore; he leaves without taking anyone, which is the friend's point about marriage. The heron has fed full and the flower is trampled in passing: the harm is careless, not cruel.

colophon.thurai: வரைவிடை வைத்துப் பிரியும் தலைவற்குத் தோழி சொல்லியது

tamil: பெரு மலை அருஞ் சுரம் நெருநல் சென்றனள்
இனியே தாங்கு நின் அவலம் என்றிர் அது மற்று
மணி வாழ் பாவை நடை கற்றன்ன என்
reading: The mother says she had one daughter, and she too went yesterday with a sharp-speared youth across the hard waste of the great hills; you tell me to bear my grief, wise ones, but how can that be, when my heart burns at the very thought, seeing the bright nochchi and the raised terrace where my lovely girl played, she who was like the figure in the eye's pupil learning to walk.
nuance: 'One daughter' is the whole argument against consolation: there is no other child to turn to. The pupil image is doubled, the dearest thing in the eye and a tiny figure only just learning to walk, so the girl is remembered as a toddler at the moment she has gone off as a bride.

tamil: பரிசில் பெற்ற விரி உளை நல் மான்
கவி குளம்பு பொருத கல் மிசைச் சிறு நெறி
உரை சால் உயர் வரைக் கொல்லிக் குடவயின்
அகல் இலைக் காந்தள் அலங்கு குலைப் பாய்ந்து
reading: The man says that if you will not even look on the helpless pain of passion grown past bearing, then she, like the finely wrought figure a god painted on the western face of the famous high Kolli of Porayan, where the bards' gift horses with worn hooves climb the small rock path and suppliants go up without tiring, where honeycombs hang among kaanthal clusters, has plotted my death; shall I grieve?
nuance: நல்காய், 'you do not grant', suits the second alternative better, the friend who keeps him off. The girl is a figure painted by a god: a made, divine beauty, so the plot to kill is hers and not hers; and the long praise of Porayan's open-handed hill sets her refusal against a lord who turns no suppliant away.

colophon.thurai: பாங்கற்குத் தலைவன் சொல்லியது சேட்படுக்கும் தோழிக்குத் தலைவன் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

tamil: கல் ஊற்று ஈண்டல கயன் அற வாங்கி
இரும் பிணர்த் தடக் கை நீட்டி நீர் நொண்டு
பெருங் கை யானை பிடி எதிர் ஓடும்
வேனில் ஓதி நிறம் பெயர் முது போத்து
பிறர்க்கு என முயலும் பேர் அருள் நெஞ்சமொடு
reading: The woman tells her wasting friend that the road their beloved took runs through a scorched, drought-struck forest where the great elephant, the rock springs not filling, stretches its rough trunk, scoops up water and runs to his mate, and the old lizard, its colour changed by summer, climbs the tall yaa bent like the end of a bard's lute; he went with a great-hearted wish to strive for others, held by the lovely bond of wealth.
nuance: The roles are reversed: the wife defends the absent husband to the friend, and justifies the journey by its purpose, wealth sought to be given to others, not by its gain.

tamil: கல் சேர் மண்டிலம் சிவந்து நிலம் தணிய
இன மணி ஒலிப்ப பொழுது படப் பூட்டி
மெய்ம் மலி காமத்து யாம் தொழுது ஒழிய
இன் நகை மேவி நாம் ஆடிய பொழிலே
reading: The girl, to herself, watches the evening close in, the neythal folding, shadows running east, the sun reddening at the hill and the many-flowered shore grove going quiet, as his chariot is yoked with ringing bells and its back vanishes while she stands worshipping in full desire; she asks what will become, with the town, of the grove where they played and laughed with the shore lord of the bee-humming garland and bright curved ornaments.
nuance: The worry is about the place, not the man: 'with the town' (ஊரொடு) fears that the grove of their meetings will become the town's talk. Every sign of the hour is also a sign of closing, the flower, the shadows, the grove, and then the chariot's back.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகன் பகற்குறி வந்து மீள்வானது செலவு நோக்கி தலைமகள் தன்னுள்ளே சொல்லுவாளாய்ச் சொல்லியது

tamil: கொடு மடல் ஈன்ற கூர் வாய்க் குவி முகை

வள் இதழ் தோயும் வான் தோய் வெற்ப
reading: The friend tells the lord of the sky-touching hill, where on a wet slope the banana's curved sheath has put out a sharp closed bud that touches the broad kaanthal petal as women's soft fingers touch their bright bangles, that had the girl known well then that even good fortune comes with harm, her bamboo-like shoulders would not now be wasting.
nuance: The banana bud touching the kaanthal is a near miss for ullurai (the man's approach to the girl), but it gives one pair only, so it stays scene. The maxim of line 6, good bringing harm with it, turns their happy daytime meetings into the cause of her wasting, which is why the friend refuses them.

tamil: தம் அலது இல்லா நம் நயந்து அருளி
எவ் வினை செய்வர்கொல் தாமே வெவ் வினைக்
கொலை வல் வேட்டுவன் வலை பரிந்து போகிய
reading: The friend says that though he, who has no one but us and loves us, has not yet come, will he really go off in the ships of the Ganges before the hard-to-anger god of the Chenniyar, where the heron's sweet voice sounds like a plucked string of the small lute; what can they be doing, who crossed the lovely forest of withered branches where the wood-dove cock that broke free of the cruel hunter's net now fears even the spider's thread on the bough?
nuance: The dove that escaped the net and now shies at a cobweb is not iraicchi under the rule (it fears, it does not do what a lover does or should do); it gives the road its mood of fright after danger. Lines 2 to 5 are best taken as a reassuring question: he will not go as far as the Ganges.

thinai_evidence.note: a forest of dead branches

comparisons.tenor: the heron's sweet call

tamil: ஆர் அரண் கடந்த மாரி வண் மகிழ்த்
தேம் கமழ் விரி தார் இயல் தேர் அழிசி
காமர் பணைத் தோள் நலம் வீறு எய்திய
சில் மொழித் துவர் வாய் நகைக்கு மகிழ்ந்தோயே
reading: The man tells his heart to suffer now, the heart that delighted in the few words and coral-mouthed smile of the young girl with eyes cool and frightened as a netted deer's, whose lovely shoulders took a beauty like Arkkadu of Azhisi, father of Chendan of the spotted spear, giver lavish as rain in his joy, lord of the fine chariot and fragrant garland, where neythal blooms among the paddy in fields of toddy.
nuance: The heart is blamed for its pleasure: 'suffer now' because it once rejoiced. The fields of Arkkadu are marutham, so a kurinji love is measured by a lowland town; the colophon's three alternatives fit because the poem names no occasion.

ஒண் பொறிச் சுணங்கின் ஐது படத் தாஅம்
அணிக் கவின் உண்மையோ அரிதே மணிக் கழி
