reading: With the man listening, the friend says that in their lovely hamlet fenced with kandal, where the honeyed bright clusters of the small-flowered njaazhal fall lightly on the spotted breasts of the sand dolls the girls shape on the long sand, the town has raised talk, saying a chariot came at night, and among them all mother looked at me; if I do not pick the blue mundakam tomorrow there will be nothing to adorn her, and harder still will be his chariot coming to the fragrant shore grove and going away empty.
nuance: The confinement is announced without naming it: if the girls cannot go out for flowers tomorrow, the man's chariot will find the grove empty. The flowers dropping on the sand doll's breasts recall the girls' play that is about to end.

colophon.thurai: தோழி தலைமகன் சிறைப்புறமாக செறிப்பு அறிவுறுப்பான் வேண்டிச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: njaazhal, kandal and mundakam of the shore

tamil: குருதி வேட்கை உரு கெழு வய மான்
வலி மிகு முன்பின் மழ களிறு பார்க்கும்
மாரி எண்கின் மலைச் சுர நீள் இடை
நீ நயந்து வருதல் எவன் எனப் பல புலந்து
பயம் கெழு பலவின் கொல்லிக் குட வரைப்
விரி கதிர் இள வெயில் தோன்றி அன்ன நின்
reading: The man tells the girl, who wept and complained at length asking why he comes in love by the long mountain path where the blood-thirsty tiger watches the young elephant and rain-dark bears graze daily like the Puzhiyar's flocks in the dense grove, that when he comes thinking of her fine beauty, like the new figure the spirits set on the western hill of Kolli rich in jackfruit, shining like young sunlight of spreading rays, the mountain path itself becomes his safety.
nuance: Her fear lists the dangers, his answer does not deny them: the thought of her is a charm (ஏமம்) that makes the road safe. The comparison to a figure set up by spirits gives her beauty the protective power of a shrine.

thinai_evidence.note: bears, jackfruit and the hill path

comparisons.tenor: the bears grazing in herds
the girl's beauty

tamil: துய்த் தலைப் புது மலர்த் துளி தலைக் கலாவ
நிறை நீர்ப் புனிற்றுப் புலம் துழைஇ ஆனாய்
இரும் புறம் தழூஉம் பெருந் தண் வாடை
பணைத் தோள் எல் வளை ஞெகிழ்த்த எம் காதலர்
reading: The woman asks the great cold north wind, which roams the new-wet flooded fields, mixes drops into the soft-tipped new flowers of the iingai with round buds the colour of molten lac, and endlessly hugs her dark back, whether she has done it any harm: her lover, who loosened the bright bangles of her shoulders, has left for hard-won wealth, so let it not torment one who sits alone in a corner in great sorrow.
nuance: The wind 'embraces her back' (இரும் புறம் தழூஉம்): the only embrace she has is the cold one, and she reproaches it as if it were a person doing a wrong.

thinai_evidence.note: separation for wealth; the cold season is the season of her waiting

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: she speaks to the north wind

comparisons.tenor: the iingai buds

tamil: வலன் உயர் மருப்பின் நிலம் ஈர்த் தடக் கை
மந்தியும் அறியா மரம் பயில் ஒரு சிறை
பெருங் குரல் கொள்ளாச் சிறு பசுங் கிளிக்கே
reading: The friend, with the hill lord listening, asks what return they can make, not only to the lordly elephant with high tusks and trailing trunk that moves with his mate beside their soft-mouthed calf, but to the small green parrot that can no longer take the great ears of millet the sickle has seized, since thanks to them they played with the hill lord in a hidden corner of dense trees that even the monkey does not know, leaving the lone guard platform on the rock deserted.
nuance: The thanks are ironic and the news is plain: the millet is reaped, so the girls' guarding and their meetings in the field are over. Why the elephant is thanked is not said; it may be the danger that kept others off the field.

thinai_evidence.note: millet, parrot and guard platform

iraicchi.act: the tusker goes about together with his mate beside their calf
iraicchi.sense: the hill lord should keep the girl as the tusker keeps his mate and young, in a household, now that the field meetings have ended

tamil: நெல் அரி தொழுவர் கூர் வாள் உற்றென
reading: The friend tells the lord of the gentle shore, where an otter cub gorges on fat fish of the dark backwater and sleeps in the thillai thicket, that it is cruel not to show grace: she has seen that the eyes of the girl he loves weep wet, like the many-petalled unclosing neythal of Thondi, shore of clamouring birds, tossing in water when the reapers' sharp sickles strike it.

colophon.thurai: களவின்கண் நெடுங்காலம் வந்தொழுக ஆற்றாளாயின தோழி வரைவு கடாயது

thinai_evidence.note: backwater, otter and thillai of the shore

comparisons.tenor: the girl's weeping eyes

ullurai.tenor: the lover who enjoys the girl and rests at ease

pairs.situation: he takes his pleasure of the girl in secret love
he then rests content and does not hasten to marry her

ullurai.speaker_fit: the friend uses a creature of the backwater in a neythal poem without leaving its land (porul 7.27)

tamil: நற் கவின் இழந்த என் தோள் போல் சாஅய்
reading: The woman, alone with the full moon, tells it that since it has nobility and rectitude, a moon of many crystal rays and fresh white light as if scooped from milk, which no ladder reaches, and since no world can hide from it, it should show where they live who hide from her; or else, shrinking little by little like her shoulders that lost their beauty, it will waste, as a witness that knows and lies must.
nuance: She argues like a litigant: the moon sees everything, so it is a witness, and a witness who knows and keeps silent is a liar; its monthly waning is then the punishment she wishes on it, the same wasting her own shoulders suffer.

colophon.thurai: நெட்டிடை கழிந்து பொருள்வயிற் பிரிந்த காலத்து ஆற்றாளாகிய தலைமகள் திங்கள் மேலிட்டுத் தன்னுள்ளே சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: a night lament with no land; irangal decides

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: she speaks to the moon

comparisons.tenor: the moon's many rays
the moon's white light
the waning moon

tamil: தெளிந்தனம் மன்ற தேயர் என் உயிர் என
வண்டு படு புது மலர் உண்துறைத் தரீஇய
பெரு மட மகளிர் முன்கைச் சிறு கோல்
பொலந் தொடி போல மின்னி கணங் கொள்
செல் மழை தவழும் அவர் நல் மலை நாட்டே
reading: The friend tells the girl, whose bangles slip, whose brow is overrun with pallor like peerkku flowers and whose eyes hold cool tears, not to sink saying her life will surely wane: in his good hill country the moving clouds now crawl, flashing like the gold bangles on the small forearms of young women who bring bee-visited new flowers to the bathing ghat, thundering like a troop of sweet-voiced drums, massed like the many shields of kings scaling forts.
nuance: The colophon is paalai, but the poem's comfort is the rainy season on his hills, the time a man returns; the three similes move from women's bangles to drums to shields, as if the clouds were an army coming home.

colophon.thurai: வரைவு நீட ஆற்றாளாகிய தலைமகளைத் தோழி ஆற்றுவித்தது

thinai_evidence.note: the coming rains, lightning and thunder are mullai's season of waiting

occasion.words: வரைவு நீட ஆற்றாளாகிய தலைமகளைத் தோழி ஆற்றுவித்தது

comparisons.tenor: the pallor on her brow
the lightning in the clouds
the thunder
the massed moving clouds

tamil: தன் ஊர் இடவயின் தொழுவேன் நுண் பல்
வார்ந்து இலங்கு வால் எயிற்று பொலிந்த தாஅர்
மை அணல் எருத்தின் முன்பின் தடக் கை
வல் வில் அம்பின் எய்யா வண் மகிழ்த்
reading: The woman who followed the girl into the waste tells those she meets on the forest path of tall yaa and omai that her daughter passed this way yesterday, and her eyes are sunk in tears; she describes the girl, with spotted waist, fine bright teeth, few bangles and thick hair, learns that this is the town of the youth's father, a strong bowman whose arrows do not miss and who gives freely in his joy, and blesses them: I am the one who bore her; may your name prosper.
nuance: The search ends in a blessing rather than a demand: finding herself at the house of the youth's father, the woman gives the girl up and wishes the family well.

colophon.thurai: பின் சென்ற செவிலி இடைச் சுரத்துக் கண்டார்க்குச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: following the eloped daughter across the waste

tamil: ஓங்கு மணல் உடுத்த நெடு மாப் பெண்ணை
வீங்கு மடல் குடம்பைப் பைதல் வெண் குருகு
அள்ளல் அன்ன என் உள்ளமொடு உள் உடைந்து
கடுஞ் சுறா எறிந்த கொடுந் திமிற் பரதவர்
வளி பொரக் கற்றை தாஅய் நளி சுடர்
reading: The girl tells her friend that each time the grieving white heron in its nest in the swollen frond of the tall palmyra on the high dune cries in the dense midnight, she melts, her heart breaking inside like a mire; she lives on only until she meets the body-touching embrace of the shore lord, where the lamps of fishers in curved boats that hunt fierce sharks, strung out on their bent lines and scattered by the wind, twinkle slowly like stars in the blue sky.
nuance: She answers the friend's comfort by refusing it: she 'lives' (உளெனே) only provisionally. The heron only cries, so it carries mood, not iraicchi; the twinkling lamps of the fishers are the lights of his shore seen from hers.

thinai_evidence.note: palmyra, shark and fishers of the shore

comparisons.tenor: the girl's heart
the fishers' lamps

tamil: சாறு என நுவலும் முது வாய்க் குயவ
பொய் பொதி கொடுஞ் சொல் ஓம்புமின் எனவே
reading: The friend, while the bard who came as go-between listens, calls the old-tongued potter who, wearing a nochchi garland of bright clusters like a chaplet of grain ears, cries the festival through the long wide street that lies like a river, and asks him to cry this too in the pond town of sweet fields thick with water-lily: the troubles this bard of the hand-plucked lute has caused are many, so let the women with fine teeth and broad hips guard themselves from his lie-wrapped crooked words.
nuance: The insult is public by design: the town crier is asked to proclaim the bard a liar, so the refusal reaches the husband through the whole street rather than through his messenger.

colophon.thurai: தோழி தலைமகளது குறிப்பு அறிந்து வாயிலாகப் புக்க பாணன் கேட்ப குயவனைக் கூவி இங்ஙனம் சொல்லாயோ என்று குயவற்குச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: refusing the husband's go-between in the field town

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi

occasion.words: குயவனைக் கூவி இங்ஙனம் சொல்லாயோ என்று குயவற்குச் சொல்லியது

thurai_akam.note: she addresses the potter who cries the festival

comparisons.tenor: the potter's nochchi garland
the long wide street

title: natrinai 201-220
theme: Natrinai 201 to 220: hill courtships pressed toward marriage by millet harvests, a mother's look and a madal the children play at; shore girls who lament nightfall or refuse to blame the man they chose; paalai partings for wealth weighed against a wife's beauty and mocked by the promised rain; and marutham rebukes that define true wealth as fear of a dependant's distress.
source_issues: 205: line 1 repeats Natrinai 399 line 1 (text flag); a formula opening, not an error.
214: the colophon thinai is பாலை; the poem is a wife waiting as the promised rains arrive (irutthal), so I infer mullai.
217: the colophon thinai is குறிஞ்சி; the things are of the hills but the uri is the wife's sulk and refusal of entry, so I infer marutham, mixed.
220: the colophon thinai is குறிஞ்சி; the poem has no hill things and turns on the madal costume, so I infer perunthinai. The colophon joins two alternatives with a full stop (ஆம்.தான்).

tamil: மலை உறை குறவன் காதல் மட மகள்
செவ் வேர்ப் பலவின் பயம் கெழு கொல்லித்
தெய்வம் காக்கும் தீது தீர் நெடுங் கோட்டு
கால் பொருது இடிப்பினும் கதழ் உறை கடுகினும்
உரும் உடன்று எறியினும் ஊறு பல தோன்றினும்
பெரு நிலம் கிளரினும் திரு நல உருவின்
reading: The man answers the companion who told him the hill hunter's young daughter is too closely guarded, too young and too unwilling to be thought of: like the image on Kolli's western hill that the god guards, which no wind, lashing rain, thunder or heaving earth can move, she will not leave his heart.
nuance: The companion's four objections (hard to win, guarded, deaf to words, young) are met by five assaults on the image (wind, rain, thunder, many harms, the earth rising), so the reply outnumbers the rebuke; and the guarded girl is answered by a guarded image, the god's keeping set against her father's.

thinai_evidence.note: a hill girl held fast in the lover's heart during secret love

comparisons.vehicle: திரு நல உருவின் மாயா இயற்கைப் பாவையின்
comparisons.tenor: the girl, fixed in his heart

tamil: புலி பொரச் சிவந்த புலால் அம் செங் கோட்டு
ஒலி பல் முத்தம் ஆர்ப்ப வலி சிறந்து
மடப் பிடி தழீஇய தடக் கை வேழம்
தேன் செய் பெருங் கிளை இரிய வேங்கைப்
reading: Eloping with the girl, the man bids her look at the great hill's rifts, where a tusker whose tusk reddened fighting a tiger breaks a thick tree and feeds his cow and calf golden mouthfuls of vengai, and at the forest decked with kongam flowers like the long rows of lamps lit in the holy month of the six stars.
nuance: The festival of the Karthigai month is the girl's home festival, so the hero dresses the strange forest in the lights she has just left; நுந்தை in line 8 (your father) is hard to place, and may tie the lamps to her father's town.

thinai_evidence.note: the lover leading the girl through the forest in elopement

comparisons.tenor: the vengai flowers fed to the cow

comparisons.vehicle: அறம் செய் திங்கள் செல் சுடர் நெடுங் கொடி
comparisons.tenor: the kongam in flower across the forest

iraicchi.act: the tusker embraces his young cow and calf and feeds them golden mouthfuls of vengai
iraicchi.sense: the man leading her away from her kin will feed and shelter her on the road as the tusker does his mate

tamil: தடந் தாட் தாழை முள்ளுடை நெடுந் தோட்டு
அக மடல் பொதுளிய முகை முதிர் வான் பூங்
எறி திரை உதைத்தலின் பொங்கித் தாது சோர்பு
மணம் கமழ் கானல் இயைந்த நம் கேண்மை
ஒரு நாள் பிரியினும் உய்வு அரிது என்னாது
கதழ் பரி நெடுந் தேர் வரவு ஆண்டு அழுங்கச்
reading: With the man listening, the friend says that in the fragrant shore grove, where screwpine flowers like drawn-out conch burst their pollen under the waves and wipe the fish smell from the hamlet's street, their bond was formed, and he, not thinking a day apart unbearable, has let his swift chariot stop coming, a fault of his own, while this noisy town has fallen into distress.
nuance: The screwpine's scent that overcomes the street's fish smell is a near miss for ullurai (the love whose fragrance escapes into the town as talk): only one pair is clear, so it stays scene; the closing 'this clamorous town' turns the gossip itself into the sufferer.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகன் சிறைப்புறத்தானாக தோழி சொல்லி வரைவு கடாயது

thinai_evidence.note: screwpine, shore grove and fishing hamlet, with the friend pressing for marriage

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the addressee is not named; the poem speaks of 'our bond' to the girl

comparisons.tenor: the white screwpine flower

tamil: தளிர் சேர் தண் தழை தைஇ நுந்தை
குளிர் வாய் வியன் புனத்து எல் பட வருகோ
குறுஞ் சுனைக் குவளை அடைச்சி நாம் புணரிய
இன் சொல் மேவலைப்பட்ட என் நெஞ்சு உணக்
கூறு இனி மடந்தை நின் கூர் எயிறு உண்கு என
யான் தன் மொழிதலின் மொழி எதிர் வந்து
தான் செய் குறி நிலை இனிய கூறி
ஏறு பிரி மடப் பிணை கடுப்ப வேறுபட்டு
reading: The man who has followed the girl tells his heart, with the friend listening, how he asked whether he should come at dusk to her father's millet field wearing a leaf skirt or bathe with her on the slope of their meeting, begging a word to slake his heart; she answered by naming sweetly the place of tryst, and went off changed, like a young doe parted from its stag, to the bamboo-high village, and his heart, sent after her, will not let her go.
nuance: He offers to come in a leaf skirt (தழை), the girl's own dress, so the lover proposes to pass unseen as one of the millet guards; and the heart he 'sent' with her is the subject of the last line, as if the heart, not he, had refused to return.

colophon.thurai: பின்னின்ற தலைமகன் ஆற்றானாய் தோழி கேட்பத் தன் நெஞ்சிற்குச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the millet field, the hill slope and the hill girl naming a tryst

comparisons.tenor: the girl turning away from him

tamil: ஆளி நன் மான் வேட்டு எழு கோள் உகிர்ப்
பூம் பொறி உழுவை தொலைச்சிய வைந் நுதி
ஏந்து வெண் கோட்டு வயக் களிறு இழுக்கும்
கொடு முள் ஈங்கை நெடு மா அம் தளிர்
ஆய் நிறம் புரையும் இவள் மாமைக் கவினே
reading: The man tells his heart, which counts as nothing the forest by the waterfall slopes where the aali drags off the white-tusked bull elephant that killed a striped tiger, that if he leaves for wealth with her here, her dark beauty, like the fine colour of tender mango and thorny eengai shoots in the garden after heavy rain, will be gone from this very day.
nuance: The forest's chain of killing (tiger by elephant, elephant by aali) measures danger to the traveller; the beauty at home is measured by tender rain-washed shoots, so the poem sets the strongest beast against the most perishable leaf, and the leaf wins: he stays.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகன் தன் நெஞ்சிற்குச் சொல்லி செலவு அழுங்கியது தோழி செலவு அழுங்கச் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: a parting for wealth across a hard forest, weighed and put off

comparisons.tenor: her eyes
her dark beauty

tamil: துய்த் தலைப் புனிற்றுக் குரல் பால் வார்பு இறைஞ்சி
செவ் வாய்ப் பாசினம் கவரும் என்று அவ் வாய்த்
நல் நாள் வேங்கையும் மலர்கமா இனி என
reading: The friend, with the man listening, says that father came saying the milky millet ears are bending and red-beaked parrots gather on the rocks, so beat the clapper and string the sling; and mother, saying 'now may the vengai of the good day flower', looked at her face: does she mean to let them go out or to shut them in, and has she learned of their bond with the man of the stony land?
nuance: The vengai's flowering marks the season of weddings, so the mother's wish is ambiguous on purpose: a wedding with a stranger or a suspicion of the lover; the friend's 'I do not know' is the pressure on the listening man.

thinai_evidence.note: millet guarding, parrots and the vengai, in secret love near discovery

tamil: முடி முதிர் பரதவர் மட மொழிக் குறுமகள்
reading: Telling the foster mother the truth when strangers seek the girl, the friend says a tall chariot keeps coming noisily to the fishers' hamlet of thatched huts among the backwaters, crossing dunes like hills, and asks whether its rider will turn back; yet in a night gathering of young and old, the girl of the old shark-scarred fishermen has been given to the murderous young men who go to sea with net and line.
nuance: The chariot is the lover's and marks a man not of the fishers; the friend sets it against the kin's choice of sea-going youths, so the revelation is made by contrast, without naming him; who the 'fierce youths' are (the strangers' party or the girl's own kin) is not certain.

colophon.thurai: நொதுமலர் வரைவுழி தோழி செவிலிக்கு அறத்தொடு நின்றது

thinai_evidence.note: backwaters, fishermen and their nets

comparisons.tenor: the heaped sand dunes

tamil: விறல் சால் விளங்கு இழை நெகிழ விம்மி
அறல் போல் தெள் மணி இடை முலை நனைப்ப
விளிவு இல கலுழும் கண்ணொடு பெரிது அழிந்து
எவன் இனைபு வாடுதி சுடர் நுதற் குறுமகள்
தருவது போலும் இப் பெரு மழைக் குரலே
reading: The friend asks the weeping girl why she wilts, her bangles loosening and tears clear as stream water wetting her breasts: their lover will not go, and if he goes he cannot bear the pain; he deserves trust, loves deeply and grieves more than they, and will come back even with his wealth unwon; besides, this great rain's voice sounds as if it were seeking out those parted from sweet partners to bring them home.
nuance: The friend reasons in steps (he won't go; if he goes he'll suffer; if he suffers he'll return), then gives the clinching proof to the rain, which she makes a fetcher of the parted.

colophon.thurai: செலவுற்றாரது குறிப்பு அறிந்து ஆற்றாளாய தலைமகள் உரைப்ப தோழி சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: a feared parting for wealth

comparisons.tenor: her clear tears
the rain's voice

tamil: தளி பதம் பெற்ற கான் உழு குறவர்
சில வித்து அகல இட்டென பல விளைந்து
மழலை அம் குறுமகள் மிழலைஅம் தீம் குரல்
reading: Refused, the man tells his heart that the girl in the millet field, where hill farmers sowed a few seeds widely on a cleared slope after rain and reaped plenty, has a sweet lisping voice that even the parrots know; when it reaches him his sorrow ends, and if it stays away it will take his life and everything with it.
nuance: The few seeds that yield a heavy crop sit beside the friend's small favour he begs for (the colophon says the friend hears and grants the suit); one pair only, so a near miss for ullurai, left as scene. The parrots 'know' her voice because they hear her scare them all day.

colophon.thurai: குறை மறுக்கப்பட்டுப் பின்னின்ற தலைமகன் ஆற்றானாய் நெஞ்சிற்குச் சொல்லுவானாய்ச் சொல்லியது தோழி கேட்டுக் குறை முடிப்பது பயன்

thinai_evidence.note: hill farmers' millet and parrots, with a lover's suit refused

tamil: அரிகால் மாறிய அம் கண் அகல் வயல்
செல்வம் அன்று தன் செய் வினைப் பயனே
reading: The friend tells the lord of the rich town, where the seed basket carried to a re-ploughed wet field comes home full of fish, that grand talk and harsh riding are not wealth but the fruit of one's deeds; what the worthy call wealth is the gentle-eyed wealth of a nature that fears the distress of those who depend on one.
nuance: The friend grants him entry while lecturing him, and the lecture is a definition of wealth aimed at a rich man who has hurt his dependant wife. The basket that went out with seed and returns with fish (more than was sent) is a near miss for ullurai: one pair only.

colophon.thurai: தோழி தலைமகனை நெருங்கிச் சொல்லுவாளாய் வாயில் நேர்ந்தது

thinai_evidence.note: ploughed wet fields and a rich town's lord at fault

tamil: யார்க்கு நொந்து உரைக்கோ யானே ஊர் கடல்
கொடுங் கழி மருங்கின் இரை வேட்டு எழுந்த
கருங் கால் குருகின் கோள் உய்ந்து போகிய
எறி திரை தொகுத்த எக்கர் நெடுங் கோட்டுத்
துறு கடற் தலைய தோடு பொதி தாழை
reading: Alone and overheard, the friend asks to whom she can tell her pain: the lord of the shore, where a bent-backed male prawn that escaped a black-legged heron hunting in the salt pans takes fright at the white screwpine bud on the dune, has abandoned the girl, so they say.
nuance: The prawn fears a harmless flower that looks like the heron, as the girl, who has come safely through the lover's absences, now dreads a report (எனவே, so they say) as if it were the desertion itself.

colophon.thurai: வரைவு நீட ஒருதலை ஆற்றாளாம் என்ற தோழி சிறைப்புறமாகத் தன்னுள்ளே சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: salt pans, backwater, heron, prawn and screwpine

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: she speaks to herself (தன்னுள்ளே)

ullurai.tenor: the girl, afraid of the rumour that the man has left her

pairs.situation: she has come through the dangers of the secret love so far
she now dreads a mere report as though it were the desertion

ullurai.speaker_fit: the friend uses a prawn and a screwpine of the shore in a neythal poem (porul 7.27)

tamil: நெடுங் கால் கணந்துள்அம் புலம்பு கொள் தெள் விளி
கடுங் குரற் பம்பைக் கத நாய் வடுகர்
நெடும் பெருங் குன்றம் நீந்தி நம் வயின்
செம் பொன் கழல்தொடி நோக்கி மா மகன்
reading: The friend tells the girl that across the wasteland, where the clear lonely cry of the long-legged kanandhul, afraid of a decoy hunter's net, is caught by passing bards on their strings, and across the tall hills of the Vadugar with their harsh drums and fierce dogs, he has come back to them, who grew anxious each time they heard their little son's sweet voice asking to be held as he looked at the red gold bracelet on his hand.
nuance: The bards tune their strings to a frightened bird's cry, so even the road's terror becomes music; the household's anxiety is told through the child, whose request to be held stands for the absent father.

colophon.thurai: பொருள் முடித்துத் தலைமகனோடு வந்த வாயில்கள்வாய் வரவு கேட்ட தோழி தலை மகட்குச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the wasteland road of the man's journey for wealth

tamil: வேர்க் கொண்டு தூங்கும் கொழுஞ் சுளைப் பெரும் பழம்
வேய் பயில் இறும்பின் ஆம் அறல் பருகும்
பெருங் கல் வேலிச் சிறுகுடி யாது என
செங் கேழ் ஆடிய செழுங் குரற் சிறு தினைக்
reading: Seeking the friend's help, the man asks the long-armed girls which is the small village fenced by great rocks near the roaring falls, where a young red cow eats the ripe jackfruit hanging by the roots of the common's tree where calves are tied and drinks clear water in the bamboo thicket; if they will not say even that, is the guarding of this red-eared millet, swaying after the cloud's rain, theirs too?
nuance: The question is a pretext: asking the way and who owns the field is how the lover opens talk, and the second question presses them to admit they are the guards he can meet there.

thinai_evidence.note: waterfall, jackfruit and millet field, with the lover approaching the girls

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: he addresses the girls in the plural (நீள் தோளீரே)

tamil: அசையுநர் இருந்தோர்க்கு அரும் புணர்வு ஈன்ம் என
அரும்பு அவிழ் அலரிச் சுரும்பு உண் பல் போது
அணிய வருதும் நின் மணி இருங் கதுப்பு என
மை சூழ் வெற்பின் மலை பல இறந்து
செய் பொருட்கு அகன்ற செயிர் தீர் காதலர்
இலங்கு வளை நெகிழ்த்த கலங்கு அஞர் எள்ளி
ஆர்ப்பது போலும் இக் கார்ப் பெயற் குரலே
reading: The woman asks her friend whether her lover, who left for wealth saying fame, pleasure and giving do not come to those who sit idle, and who swore he would return to deck her hair with alari flowers, will not hear this rain cloud's voice, flashing as if to mock the grief that loosened her bangles and roaring as if to shout at it.
nuance: His reason is a maxim in three terms, quoted back to her, and the season he promised arrives without him: the thunder mocks not his absence but her trust in the maxim and the oath.

colophon.thurai: உலகியலால் பிரிவு உணர்த்தப்பட்ட தலைமகன் குறித்த பருவம் கண்டு தலைமகள் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: a wife waiting as the promised rains come, which is irutthal, not the parting itself

comparisons.tenor: the lightning
the thunder of the rain

tamil: குண கடல் இவர்ந்து குரூஉக் கதிர் பரப்பி
இலங்கு வளை மகளிர் வியல் நகர் அயர
மீன் நிணம் தொகுத்த ஊன் நெய் ஒண் சுடர்
நீல் நிறப் பரப்பில் தயங்கு திரை உதைப்ப
கொடு முடி அவ் வலை பரியப் போகிய
reading: As the sun that climbed from the eastern sea sinks behind the western hill and the lonely evening comes, with bangled women lighting fish-fat lamps in the wide houses of the noisy hamlet by the shore, the friend asks the man what harm there is in staying with them tonight, since their kin, out after a shark that tore through their net, have not come back from a failed hunt.
nuance: The invitation is also a refusal: staying the night openly in the hamlet is what only a husband could do, so the friend's 'stay' presses for marriage, as the colophon's second reading says.

colophon.thurai: பகற் குறி வந்து மீள்வானை அவள் ஆற்றும் தன்மையள் அல்லள் நீயிர் இங்குத் தங்கற் பாலீர் எமரும் இன்னது ஒரு தவற்றினர் எனத் தோழி தலைமகற்குச் சொல்லியது இரவுக் குறி மறுத்து வரைவு கடாயதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: sunset in a shore hamlet, the evening sorrow of neythal

occasion.words: இரவுக் குறி மறுத்து வரைவு கடாயதூஉம் ஆம்

reading: The other woman, speaking to the bard so the wife's people hear, says that even if her lovers do not come to end her sulking and do not help in her sorrow as the hand helps a hurt eye, the town where they live is not hateful, since one lives where one sees those who look kindly; but others than one's own beloved, even if they are like those who heard of Thirumaavunni, who cut off a breast at the field near the fire-red vengai the god guards, are unbearable.
nuance: Thirumaavunni, who tore off a breast when a stranger's trouble wrung her, is a story the poet's audience knew and we only partly know; lines 6 to 11 are hard, and the sense that 'those who heard her story' stand for pitying outsiders is a guess.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகட்குப் பாங்காயினார் கேட்பத் தலைமகன் தலைநின்று ஒழுகப் படாநின்ற பரத்தை பாணற்கு ஆயினும் விறலிக்குஆயினும் சொல்லுவாளாய் நெருங்கிச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the other woman's sulk and the fields of the town

thurai_akam.speaker: parathai
thurai_akam.note: or to the virali; the overhearers are the wife's companions (தலைமகட்குப் பாங்காயினார்)

comparisons.tenor: the help a lover should give
the vengai in flower
the others, who are not her beloved

tamil: காண் தொறும் பொலியும் கதழ் வாய் வேழம்
இருங் கேழ் வயப் புலி வெரீஇ அயலது
reading: The wife tells her friend that though the man of the hill country, where a fierce elephant, more splendid each time it is seen like the wealth of those who live in fame, takes fright at a tiger and vents its rage on a black-stemmed vengai until its anger cools, is very sweet to her, she will brood and sulk, for making him feel her sulk is the strong way to drive off her long loneliness.
nuance: The elephant that fears the tiger and spends its anger on a tree is a near miss for ullurai (the man who takes out on the wife what he dares not face elsewhere): the second pair is not anchored, so it stays scene. Line 9 can also mean that making him understand is hard, which reverses her confidence.

thinai_evidence.note: the wife's sulk is marutham's uri, though the things are of the hills (porul 1.15)

comparisons.tenor: the elephant, finer at every sight

tamil: எல்லியும் பூ வீ கொடியின் புலம்பு அடைந்தன்றே
reading: Answering the friend's reassurance, the girl says the sun has set with dimmed rays, the night grows lonely like a creeper whose flowers have dropped, bats fly to their haunts, the cock calls each time his mate laughs, the season named by the man who swore love on the path has passed, the owl in the forked neem hoots through the night; worn by unending pain, must she still hear alone the andril's cry from the thick palmyra?
nuance: Every creature at nightfall either goes home or calls its mate, and the last, the andril, is the bird of inseparable pairs, so the catalogue ends on what she lacks; lines 3 and 4 (the laughing cock) are obscure.

thinai_evidence.note: sunset lament with the andril on the palmyra

comparisons.tenor: the lonely night

tamil: அலவனொடு பெயரும் புலவுத் திரை நளி கடல்
கங்குல் மாட்டிய கனை கதிர் ஒண் சுடர்
reading: The girl tells her friend that though her eyes, shoulders and cool fragrant hair lose their old beauty and pallor spreads, and though her life should pass into death, she will not be angry at all, because the lord of the wide shore, where fishermen light flames at night that look like the light of a sun not yet risen, and she joined of their own accord.
nuance: தானே யானே: he himself and I myself, with no go-between; the union was their own choice, so there is no one to blame, not even him.

colophon.thurai: வரைவிடை வைத்துப் பிரிய ஆற்றாளாய தலைமகள் தோழிக்குச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: crabs, fishermen and the lord of the shore

comparisons.tenor: the fishermen's night flames

tamil: சிறு மணி தொடர்ந்து பெருங் கச்சு நிறீஇ
reading: The little boys who tie small bells to a band, wear erukku-bud garlands, make a horse that does not eat and roam the street with him are truly wise; but the deluded people of this festive town of ever-sounding drums, who call themselves the town, would join him too if they knew fellow-feeling, telling him not to be a stranger to the sweet-voiced girl with eyes like kayal fish.
nuance: The boys' game is the madal itself, played as a toy, so the lover's last resort has become a street spectacle children copy; calling the children 'great worthies' (சான்றோர்) mocks the town's elders by contrast.

colophon.thurai: குறை நேர்ந்த தோழி தலைமகளை முகம் புக்கது பின்னின்ற தலைமகன் தோழி கேட்பத் தலைமகளை ஓம்படுத்ததூஉம் ஆம்.தான் ஆற்றானாய்ச் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the madal costume and the palm horse, which the Tholkappiyam sets under perunthinai

occasion.words: குறை நேர்ந்த தோழி தலைமகளை முகம் புக்கது

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: he speaks to no one named

comparisons.tenor: the girl's eyes

title: natrinai 221-240
theme: Natrinai 221-240: homecoming and departure set against the seasons (the son who calls his father, the clouds like a patron's elephants, the cloud that is not noble), the friend's pressure for marriage through gossip, seclusion and the night tryst, and the woman's maxims against wealth-seeking.
source_issues: 234: no text in the core file (the poem is lost); not marked.
225: the colophon files a kurinji poem under an alternative in which the courtesan speaks, a situation of marutham; the alternative is recorded as given.
228 line 6: கானவன் சிறு புறம் கடுக்கும் is obscure; the tusker is read as startled by the hunter's arrow, and the verse is marked uncertain.
233 lines 1 to 5: the sense of மாணா வன் பறழ் ... ஒளிக்கும் and of இனி என கொள்ளலைமன்னே is uncertain; marked uncertain.
238 lines 6 to 10: the construction (அவர் நிலை அறியுமோ ஈங்கு என வருதல்; பாம்பு பை மழுங்கல் அன்றியும்) is uncertain; marked uncertain.
239 lines 9 to 12: who weeps or clamours (கலுழ்ந்த இவ் ஊர்) and the sense of அமைந்து தொழில் கேட்டன்றோ இலமே are uncertain; marked uncertain.
226 lines 4 and 5: நாம் தம் உண்மையின் உளமே and தாம் கசிந்து are read as 'our life rests on his' and 'moved'; uncertain.
229 line 9: குழைவான் கண்ணிடத்து ஈண்டி is obscure; read as clouds gathering low.
237: the poem's rising rain clouds point to mullai against the colophon's paalai.
231 lines 5 to 9: the syntax of பண்டும் ... நீங்காமாறே is uncertain; marked uncertain.
240: the colophon gives two speakers; the reading follows the hero alternative, which the poem's first line and embrace description fit better.

tamil: ஒண் பூந் தோன்றியொடு தண் புதல் அணிய
நீர் அணிப் பெரு வழி நீள் இடைப் போழ
செல்க பாக நின் செய்வினை நெடுந் தேர்
மின் ஒளிர் அவிர் இழை நல் நகர் விளங்க
reading: His task done, the man tells his charioteer to drive the long chariot through the red-soil scrub, where karuvilai blue as a gem and bright thondri deck the bushes and konrai clusters hang like gold chains from every bough, so that he may hear the sweet words of his little son, newly walking on untried feet, who leaves his bed and cries 'come, father', in the shining house of his wife who loves to receive guests.
nuance: The reward he drives toward is not first the wife but the household she keeps, hospitable and now with a child who has just learned to call him; the flowering season tells him he is already late.

colophon.thurai: வினை முற்றி மறுத்தராநின்ற தலைமகன் பாகற்குச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the konrai and thondri of the rainy forest edge on the road home

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the addressee is the charioteer (பாகன்)

comparisons.tenor: the dark blue karuvilai flowers
the konrai clusters hanging from the boughs
the red-soil forest edge spread with flowers

tamil: கருங் கால் வேங்கைச் செவ் வீவாங்கு சினை
கை புனை சிறு நெறி வாங்கி பையென
விசும்பு ஆடு ஆய் மயில் கடுப்ப யான் இன்று
துஞ்சு பிடி மருங்கின் மஞ்சு பட காணாது
reading: The friend, knowing the man stands near, asks the girl whether she should push her today on the swing hung from the bent red-flowered vengai branch, its twisted rope scarring the bark, so that she, holding her girdle of green beads, may rise like a peacock playing in the sky and see his far tall hill, where on the slope of plantain, wazhai and bamboo the great tusker, unable to see his mate asleep beside him when the mist comes down, trumpets.
nuance: 'Today' is the edge: the girl is about to be kept indoors, so this is the last swing and the last sight of his hill, and the man listening is told so without being addressed.

colophon.thurai: தோழி தலைமகன் வரவு உணர்ந்து சிறைப்புறமாகச் செறிப்பு அறிவுறீஇ வரைவு கடாயது

thinai_evidence.note: vengai, hill slope and tusker of the mountain

comparisons.tenor: the girl rising on the swing

iraicchi.act: the tusker trumpets because the mist hides his mate, who sleeps right beside him
iraicchi.sense: once the girl is shut in the house she will be near yet out of his sight, and the man will cry out like the tusker unless he marries her

tamil: இவள்தன் காமம் பெருமையின் காலை என்னாள் நின்
reading: The friend tells the man of the shore that because the girl's desire is great she forgets it is daytime, and because his love is great he comes even by day to the flower-filled grove; that is sweet, but gossip will have her strictly guarded, so let him come at night instead, except that this gossiping town has women whose eyes never sleep even at the ford of the wide sea where shark shoals teem.
nuance: The offer of a night tryst is withdrawn in the same breath: neither day nor night is safe, so the only road left is marriage, which is what the friend wants him to hear.

colophon.thurai: பகற்குறி வந்து மீள்வானைத் தோழி இரவுக்குறி நேர்வாள் போன்று அதுவும் மறுத்து வரைவு கடாயது

thinai_evidence.note: the shore grove, the ford and the sharks of the sea

occasion.words: இரவுக்குறி நேர்வாள் போன்று அதுவும் மறுத்து வரைவு கடாயது

tamil: செங் கண் இருங் குயில் எதிர் குரல் பயிற்றும்
இனி எவன் மொழிகோ யானே கயன் அறக்
கண் அழிந்து உலறிய பல் மர நெடு நெறி
reading: Told by her friend that he is leaving, the woman says: they are loving, and great besides; yet the kuravu has budded ahead of the late dew, the red-eyed koel calls from the clusters as if saying 'you who are joined, stay joined', and sweet spring has come to us; what can I say now to those who assured me 'we will not part' and have set their minds on the hot hard waste of dried pools and withered trees where bowmen swarm at the forks?
nuance: Her praise of him (loving, great) is what makes argument impossible: she cannot accuse, only set his promise against a season that is itself pleading for union.

colophon.thurai: தோழியால் பிரிவு உணர்த்தப்பட்ட தலைமகள் பெயர்த்தும் சொல் கடாவப்பட்டு அறிவிலாதேம் என்னை சொல்லியும் பிரியார் ஆகாரோ என்று சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the man is setting out across the waste

tamil: முருகு உறழ் முன்பொடு கடுஞ் சினம் செருக்கிப்
வாழை ஈன்ற வை ஏந்து கொழு முகை
பூவொடு துயல் வரும் மால் வரை நாடனை
தொய்யில் வன முலை வரி வனப்பு இழப்பப்
reading: The woman asks her friend whether anyone has had to beg the lord of the great mountain, where the plantain's swollen bud, like the white tusk of an elephant that fought in fury with Murugan's strength, sways with its flower like the loose hair of soft women, for the chest without kindness that will not help those who love it, so as to cure the pain that has risen and ruined the drawn lines of her breasts.
nuance: The question is bitter: a help that has to be begged for is no help, so she refuses the friend's comfort by asking whether any lover should need to plead.

colophon.thurai: வன்புறை எதிர் அழிந்தது பரத்தை தலைமகட்குப் பாங்காயின வாயில் கேட்பச் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the mountain lord, the hill plantain and the tusker

thurai_akam.speaker: parathai

occasion.words: பரத்தை தலைமகட்குப் பாங்காயின வாயில் கேட்பச் சொல்லியதூஉம்

thurai_akam.note: the courtesan speaks to her own company so that the heroine's go-betweens overhear

comparisons.tenor: the fighting elephant's strength
the plantain's swollen bud
the bud swaying with its flower

tamil: உரம் சாச் செய்யார் உயர்தவம் வளம் கெடப்
தாம் செய்பொருள் அளவு அறியார் தாம் கசிந்து
reading: Answering comfort, the woman says that people do not take a medicine that kills the tree, the great do not do a penance that kills their strength, and kings do not take gold that ruins the land's wealth; yet since our life hangs on his, our lover, not knowing the measure of the wealth he goes to make, has gone over the long scorched way and left us, and the whole world knows it is always so.
nuance: Each maxim is about taking from a source without destroying it; she makes herself the source he is draining, so the proverbs of the wise become the charge against him.

thinai_evidence.note: the summer heat on the long way he took

comparisons.tenor: the lover who seeks wealth at the cost of the wife who lives by him

tamil: பின் ஈர் ஓதி என் தோழிக்கு அன்னோ
reading: The friend tells the man that worse than losing precious life is to have the wise say one lacks virtue, and yet, alas, his grace to her friend of long thick hair, who met him at the tryst in the punnai grove, has become talk as loud as the streets of the Cholas' Arkkadu, with its belled elephants and banners, where birds cry without stop by the toddy vats and chariots ply.
nuance: 'Your grace' is the sting: what he gave as kindness has turned into the town's noise, and only marriage turns it back into virtue.

colophon.thurai: வரையாது நெடுங்காலம் வந்து ஒழுக தோழி தலைமகனை வரைவு முடுகச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the punnai grove of the shore as the trysting place

comparisons.vehicle: ஆர்க்காட்டு ஆங்கண் கள்ளுடைத் தடவில் புள் ஒலித்து ஓவாத் தேர் வழங்கு தெருவின்
comparisons.tenor: the gossip about her

tamil: அதிர் குரல் எழிலி முதிர் கடன் தீர
கண் தூர்பு விரிந்த கனை இருள் நடு நாள்
பண்பு இல் ஆர் இடை வரூஉம் நம் திறத்து
சிறு புறம் கடுக்கும் பெருங் கை வேழம்
வெறி கொள் சாபத்து எறி கணை வெரீஇ
reading: The friend, speaking to the girl so that the man nearby hears, asks what it can mean that on a midnight of thick darkness, when lightning splits the thundering clouds and they pour out their full load, the lord of the mountain of leaping falls, where the great tusker, startled by the arrow shot from the hunter's fierce bow, slides into a crevice and its cry echoes, comes by the cruel hard path: is it that he has no pity for us?
nuance: Her fear is for him, not of him: his coming through the night's dangers is called pitiless because it puts the girl through terror, which is the friend's way of urging marriage. The elephant falling into the cleft may be read as the danger awaiting the man, but no second correspondence is stated, so it is left as scene.

colophon.thurai: தோழி சிறைப்புறமாகத் தலைமகட்குச் சொல்லுவாளாய் தலைமகன் கேட்பச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the mountain and midnight

occasion.words: சிறைப்புறமாகத் தலைமகட்குச் சொல்லுவாளாய் தலைமகன் கேட்பச் சொல்லியது

tamil: அதனால் சென்மின் சென்று வினை முடிமின் சென்றாங்கு
இழை அணி ஆகம் வடுக் கொள முயங்கி
reading: Told by the man that he is leaving, the friend says: since you keep saying 'we go, we go', I fear to sulk and say 'go', and if I say 'do not go' I fear the petty words of many that wound; so go, go and finish the work, but once there do not linger, for she trembles alone at midnight even when you are near after an embrace that marks her jewelled breast; and have you seen that the north wind has already come and stands here, after the young rains that played coolly where the clouds gathered?
nuance: Her consent is made of two fears, and its last line undoes it: the cold wind that has already come is the season in which no man should be away, so the permission ends as a plea to stay, which is why the colophon gives the alternative reading that she held him back.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகனால் பிரிவு உணர்த்தப்பட்ட தோழி தலைமகளை ஆற்றுவித்துச் செல்ல உடன்பட்டது செலவு அழுங்குவித்ததூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the man's departure for his work

tamil: கயக் கணக் கொக்கின் அன்ன கூம்பு முகை
கணைக் கால் ஆம்பல் அமிழ்து நாறு தண் போது
குணக்குத் தோன்று வெள்ளியின் இருள் கெட விரியும்
முனிவு இல் பரத்தையை எற் துறந்து அருளாய்
reading: Refusing the man entry, the friend says in the wife's voice: lord of the town with ponds full of carp, where the cool water-lily, its green leaves like a young she-elephant's ears and its closed buds like a flock of herons, opens smelling of nectar as the morning star rises in the east and the dark goes, you left me for a tireless courtesan and showed no grace; how sweet it is to see you, like a full flood spreading coolly over a field gripped by fresh drought, ending the loneliness that tormented me.
nuance: The flood simile can be heard straight or as irony: so rarely does he come that his sight is like rain on a parched field, which is itself the reproach that keeps the door shut.

thinai_evidence.note: the courtesan and the lord of the pond town

comparisons.tenor: the water-lily's green leaves
the water-lily's closed buds

comparisons.vehicle: புதுவறம்கூர்ந்த செறுவில் தண்ணென மலி புனல் பரத்தந்தாஅங்கு
comparisons.tenor: the sight of the man ending her loneliness

tamil: மை அற விளங்கிய மணி நிற விசும்பில்
பெருங் கடற் பரப்பின் இரும் புறம் தோய
பெரும் போது அவிழ்ந்த கருந் தாட் புன்னைக்
reading: The friend, with the man within hearing, tells the girl that the shore where many small white crows play, dipping their dark backs in the wide sea like the seven stars worshipped by custom in the spotless sapphire sky, is now desolate, though before it was such that the love given by the lord of the grove of black-trunked punnai, whose big blossoms open like sparrows' eggs broken in the inner town, never left us.
nuance: The playful crows in company make the shore's emptiness sharper; the friend recalls the old love only to say that the place where it lived is now lonely, so the man must marry to restore it.

thinai_evidence.note: crows of the sea, punnai of the shore and the shore lord

comparisons.tenor: the small white crows on the dark sea
the opened punnai blossoms

tamil: சிறு கண் யானைப் பெருங் கை ஈர் இனம்
செங் காற் பலவின் தீம் பழம் மிசையும்
reading: The friend tells the man who comes by day: lord of the great mountain, where a herd of small-eyed, great-trunked elephants muddies the cool pool of wild jasmine, tires of the grove's plantains and eats the sweet fruit of the red-stemmed jackfruit beside the bamboo-fenced village while the village cries out, we beg you to grant her love; long may you live, our lord, if you stay the night and go from our stony hamlet, whose courtyard is strewn with fallen vengai blossom.
nuance: The elephants that leave the grove for the village's own trees and set it crying are what his daytime visits look like from the house: the request to come by night and lodge in the hamlet is a step toward being received there openly.

colophon.thurai: பகல் வருவானை இரவு வா எனத் தோழி சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: elephants, vengai and the mountain lord

ullurai.tenor: the man who comes by day close to the girl's house

pairs.situation: he is no longer content with meetings in the grove by day
his coming near the village sets the household and the town in alarm

ullurai.speaker_fit: the friend uses the elephant herd of the kurinji hill in a kurinji poem (porul 7.27)

tamil: மட மா மந்தி மாணா வன் பறழ்
கோடு உயர் அடுக்கத்து ஆடு மழை ஒளிக்கும்
reading: The friend, so that the man nearby hears, tells the girl who suffers from the long unmarried visits: if you have given your grace to the lord of the great rocky land, where on the high slope the sturdy young of the female monkey, whose untaught male trembles, hides in the drifting cloud, why will you not take my word? I say one plain thing: be sure that he is a worthy man who keeps the tenderness of a kind heart and does not stray from the path the wise have walked.
nuance: Praise is pressure: by calling him one who walks the path of the wise in his hearing, the friend makes delay a breach of that path. The trembling monkey and the hidden young may hint at the anxious family, but only one correspondence is clear, so no ullurai is tagged.

colophon.thurai: வரையாது நெடுங்காலம் வந்து ஒழுக இவள் ஆற்றாள் என்பது உணர்ந்து சிறைப் புறமாகத் தலைமகட்குத் தோழி சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the monkeys of the high slope

tamil: உரவுத் திரை பொருத பிணர் படு தடவு முதல்
அரவு வாள் வாய முள் இலைத் தாழை
பல் பூங் கானல் பகற்குறி வந்து நம்
தண் தார் அகலம் வண்டு இமிர்பு ஊத
reading: The friend tells the girl that though the lord of the long waters came to the day tryst in the shore grove where the saw-edged, thorny-leaved thaazhai on the wave-beaten rough trunk and the gold-pollened punnai give off their scent together, and left so that her beauty wasted, they should now climb the heaped dune that rises like a hill and watch the road by which he will come, bees humming over the cool garland on his chest, driving his proud horses with ringing bells.
nuance: The grievance and the joy are in one sentence: the wasting he caused is admitted, then set aside for the sight of him arriving with the full show of a bridegroom.

colophon.thurai: வரைவு நீட ஆற்றாளாங் காலத்துத் தோழி வரைவு மலிந்தது

thinai_evidence.note: thaazhai, punnai and the dunes of the shore

comparisons.tenor: the punnai pollen
the heaped sand dune
the serrated thaazhai leaf

tamil: உரை இனி வாழி தோழி புரை இல்
நுண் நேர் எல் வளை நெகிழ்த்தோன் குன்றத்து
reading: The woman tells her friend, with the man standing by: my sickness is past bearing and my body burns as if spitting fire; so go and tell my mother of the hellish heart that if I am let out into the courtyard to breathe a little I will recover much, for a little while ago the wind that played on the tall peak of the hill of him who loosened my fine bright bangles, and plunged into its wide rock pools, touched my pale body and cooled it.
nuance: Only she and the overhearing man know why the courtyard would heal her: the wind comes from his hill, so her cure is to be nearer him, which is a plea to him to come.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகன் சிறைப்புறமாக வற்புறுக்கும் தோழிக்குத் தலைமகள் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: his hill, its peak and rock pools

tamil: இன் உயிர் அன்ன பிரிவு அருங் காதலர்
reading: The friend asks the girl, her shoulders pale and shrunken and her eyes full of tears as never before, whether she has no sulk at all against the lover dear as life who has left and stays away; look there, she says, the rain clouds of many shapes beyond telling are rising high and wonderful so that the world rejoices, like the elephants Andiran gathered when he undertook to keep the suppliants who come to him.
nuance: The friend turns from grief to a sign: the clouds rise like a patron's gift laid up for those who ask, so the season itself promises that what is owed will come, and the girl's sulk can wait for him.

thinai_evidence.note: the rains rising while she waits for the man who stays away

comparisons.tenor: the lover
the dark rain clouds of many shapes

tamil: வறம் கொல வீந்த கானத்து குறும் பூங்
அவர் நிலை அறியுமோ ஈங்கு என வருதல்
இனிய அல்ல நின் இடி நவில் குரலே
reading: Seeing the season, the woman reproaches the great cloud: in the forest the drought had killed, the pidavam has opened as bees part it, like rows of women wearing short flower garlands, and you, cloud that brings the season along the dim paths of evening, come here as if asking whether I know where he is; that is not how the noble behave; and besides dulling the hoods of snakes in the water spread by the roaring thunder, even to a heart that has not softened your thundering voice is not sweet.
nuance: She judges the cloud by the conduct of the noble, who would not torment a woman alone; the season that should mean his return arrives as an insult because he has not.

thinai_evidence.note: the pidavam, evening and the season's rain

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: she addresses the rain cloud

comparisons.vehicle: குறும் பூங் கோதை மகளிர் குழூஉ நிரை
comparisons.tenor: the opened pidavam blossoms
the cloud (denied: it does not behave like the noble)

tamil: இனிது பெறு பெரு மீன் எளிதினின் மாறி
புல் இதழ் பொதிந்த பூத் தப மிதிக்கும்
மல்லல் இருங் கழி மலி நீர்ச் சேர்ப்பற்கு
வார் கோல் எல் வளை உடைய வாங்கி
reading: The friend, with the man within hearing, says: as the setting sun hides behind the western hill in the dimming evening, the glad fishermen easily trade the great fish they caught and, on the way to their lovely hamlet with its fish-smelling sandy yard where crabs play, trample the neythal flowers whose dull petals unwrap like a bundle of fine gems; we have not even agreed to hear of the shore lord's suit, and yet this town has stirred up talk as if he had pulled my friend's bright bangles till they broke, saying 'embrace'; what would it make of it if we did something more?
nuance: The fishermen treading down the flowers on their careless way home have been read as the man's carelessness of her, but the pairs are not secure; the poem's point is that gossip already runs ahead of any deed, so he must act to make it true by marrying.

thinai_evidence.note: fishermen, neythal flowers and crabs of the shore at sunset

comparisons.tenor: the opening neythal flowers

tamil: வை ஏர் வால் எயிற்று ஒள் நுதற் குறுமகள்
கை கவர் முயக்கம் மெய் உறத் திருகி
reading: Pushed by his heart toward wealth, the man says: how strange is the one who made this world! though the embrace of the young girl with fine sharp white teeth and bright brow, her arms clasping, body pressed and twisting, her swelling breast heaving, is such that sleep can come between us, still the forest, where at the well dug with picks in a pebbled hollow sheltered from the burning sun the elephant herd seizes the trough the herders dug for the cattle, stands before me like a firm mountain.
nuance: He knows even the closest embrace has gaps, and that is the excuse the heart uses; but the road, where even the herders' water is taken by elephants, is the obstacle he cannot argue away. The colophon also gives the lines to the heroine wasting in separation.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவிடை மெலிந்த தலைமகள் சொல்லியது நெஞ்சினால் பொருள் வலிக்கப்பட்டு ஆற்றானாய தலைமகன் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the sun-scorched forest where water is dug from wells

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: no addressee is named; likely her friend

comparisons.tenor: the forest road he must cross

title: natrinai 241-260
theme: Natrinai 241 to 260: the seasons and the night in the voices of the friend and the wife; the friend reads omens and denies the rains, presses the hill lord to marry because the millet is ripening and the girl is shut in, and plays the shore lord's suit, while the wife grieves wealth set above virtue, shies from her husband at their son's side, and men give up or hurry back from journeys with the stag and his doe as their emblem.
source_issues: Natrinai colophons give speaker, addressee and occasion in prose; where they name no speaker or addressee (243, 249, 251, 255) the code is my inference or pira, with a note.
246: the colophon thinai is பாலை; the poem is the waiting at home in the rains (konrai, pidavu, thunder), so I infer mullai.
251: the colophon names no speaker; 'my body' (line 7) could make the girl the speaker rather than the friend; the sense of நயவா (line 4) is unsure.
254: the sense of lines 10 and 11 (the salt pans' staves) and of who the promised companion is cannot be fixed.
253: the colophon's அறிவிறீஇ is apparently a misprint for அறிவுறீஇ (as in 251, 258, 259).

Text flags: 242 line 8, 246 line 8, 252 line 3 lost -ஒடு vowel signs restored; 243 line 1 and 245 line 6 TSCII repairs; 247 line 4 ஃ restored; 252 line 9 repeats as 301 line 3; 259 line 5 repeats as 334 line 2.

tamil: நீர் அழி மருங்கின் ஈர் அயிர் தோன்ற
வேந்து வீசு கவரியின் பூம் புதல் அணிய
reading: The woman asks her friend whether they do not think of her, the men who left her for the restless sickness of wealth, now that the water has drawn back to show wet fine sand printed with the feet of curve-winged birds, the northern wind stirs the reed's white flowers till they deck the bush like the whisk a king waves, and the sun, in a sky cleared of rain, opens and shuts like a blinking eye and is gone, so that in the dewy midnight her kohl-lined eyes run with tears.
nuance: Everything she names is a sign of the cold season settling in: the receded water, the north wind, the reed in flower, a sun that only blinks between clouds. The question is not whether he remembers her in general but whether this season, which she reads hour by hour from dusk to midnight, reaches him where he is.

thinai_evidence.note: the man has gone for wealth and she grieves the parting; the things around her are of the river bank

comparisons.tenor: the reed's white flowers spread over the bush
the sun showing and hiding between clouds

tamil: இலை இல பிடவம் ஈர் மலர் அரும்ப
புதல் இவர் தளவம் பூங் கொடி அவிழ
பொன் எனக் கொன்றை மலர மணி எனப்
பல் மலர் காயாங் குறுஞ் சினை கஞல
கழிப் பெயர் களரில் போகிய மட மான்
விழிக் கட் பேதையொடு இனன் இரிந்து ஓட
reading: Returning with his work done, the man sees the rains begin (the leafless pidavam budding, the thalavam vine opening on the bush, konrai flowering like gold and kaayaa crowding its twigs with gem-blue blossom) and tells his charioteer to drive fast this morning, pointing to the stag on the salt flat who, when the herd fled with his young doe, stands with a longing heart, not leaving, searching for her.
nuance: The poet's name, Vizhikkat Pethai Perungannanar, is taken from line 8, the wide-eyed doe. The stag is the one creature in the poem that does not move: everything else opens, blooms or flees, and he stands searching, which is the man's state put outside him.

colophon.thurai: வினை முற்றி மறுத்தராநின்ற தலைமகன் கார் கண்டு பாகற்குச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the flowers of the first rains and the returning man fix mullai

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the addressee is the charioteer (பாக, line 6)

comparisons.tenor: the konrai's yellow blossom
the kaayaa's blue blossom

iraicchi.act: when the herd scatters, the stag does not run with it but stands searching for his young doe
iraicchi.sense: the man too will not rest until he has found his wife again, so the chariot must hurry

tamil: தேம் படு சிலம்பில் தெள் அறல் தழீஇய
அலங்கு சினை பொதுளிய நறு வடி மாஅத்துப்
பொதும்புதோறு அல்கும் பூங் கண் இருங் குயில்
reading: The woman says that the dark koel, staying in every grove of the fragrant mango on the bank of the clear stream below the honeyed slope, sits body to body with its mate and calls lovingly, as if rebuking those who leave helplessly, 'wise ones, do not go away and leave a life that does not stay, like dice turned over'; and if parting for wealth even in such a painful season is the nature of men, then wealth, surely, is dearer than virtue.
nuance: The last line turns the moral order upside down on purpose: by men's conduct wealth is rated above virtue. The koel's call is given words by the speaker herself, so the rebuke she cannot speak to him she puts in a bird's mouth.

thinai_evidence.note: a parting for wealth; the hill stream and mango grove are not its own land

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no addressee; the poem speaks of men in general

comparisons.tenor: a life that does not stay
the koels' calling

tamil: துயர் மருங்கு அறியா அன்னைக்கு இந் நோய்
மணி கெழு நெடு வரை அணி பெற நிவந்த
மதன் இல் மா மெய்ப் பசலையும் கண்டே
reading: The girl tells her friend she is cruel: she could tell the lord of the high hill, where on the cool rain-soaked slope the koothalam flower of the cold season smells and the asunam listens to the sweet humming of bees, or she could tell the mother, who does not know where the grief comes from, that this is how the sickness will abate; she does neither, though she has seen the pallor on the girl's body, like the tender shoots of the asoka on the tall gem-bright hill.
nuance: She sets out the friend's two possible acts as a choice (ஒன்றோ ... ஒன்றோ) and blames her for taking neither, which is the moment of அறத்தொடுநிலை from the girl's side. The asunam, an animal that hangs on music, listening to bees, is scene; read as a hint that the girl too is held by sweet sound it is a single match of mood, not iraicchi.

colophon.thurai: அறத்தொடுநிலை வலித்த தோழியைத் தலைவி முகம் புக்கது

thinai_evidence.note: the hill slope, its creature and its trees, and a secret love not yet told

comparisons.tenor: her pale body

tamil: மணி மருள் ஐம்பால் வண்டு படத் தைஇ
அரிது புணர் இன் உயிர் வவ்விய நீ என
பூண் மலி நெடுந் தேர்ப் புரவி தாங்கி
reading: The friend, who has agreed to help him, tells the girl it makes her laugh: when they had woven a garland of mundakam flowers into her gem-dark hair and played with their companions in the clear sea, the shore lord reined in the horses of his tall chariot and, asking 'who are you, slender-waisted, sweet-spoken, who have seized my life?', told them how he had been struck, never knowing that he was striking them, and stood with joined hands gazing at her bright brow.
nuance: The joke is the reversal: the man reports himself as the victim of an அணங்கு, while the girls are the ones afflicted, so each side thinks itself the one struck. The friend makes the girl laugh in order to open her to the man's suit.

colophon.thurai: குறை நேர்ந்த தோழி தலைமகளை முகம் புக்கது

thinai_evidence.note: the sea, the shore grove and its water-thorn flowers

comparisons.tenor: her dark hair

tamil: மனை மா நொச்சி மீமிசை மாச் சினை
வினை மாண் இருங் குயில் பயிற்றலும் பயிற்றும்
உரம் புரி உள்ளமொடு சுரம் பல நீந்தி
பொன் வீக் கொன்றையொடு பிடவுத் தளை அவிழ
reading: The friend tells the wasting woman that he will come and does not lie, though he crossed many wastes with a firm heart for wealth to be made: the lizard on the long wall chirps sweetly on the lucky side, the dark koel on the top branch of the house's nochchi calls again and again, and in the scrub the golden konrai is out with the pidavu buds opening and the sky rumbling with sweet sound; is this not the season he named when he said 'we will come'?
nuance: The reassurance moves from the house outward: two household omens first (the lizard, the koel on the nochchi by the door), then the land, then the sky, and it closes as a question, so the friend's certainty is offered for the woman to confirm. The colophon's thinai is paalai, by the man's road; what the poem shows is the waiting at home in the rains.

thinai_evidence.note: the poem is the waiting for a promised return in the rains; the waste is only where he went

tamil: தொன்று படு துப்பொடு முரண் மிகச் சினைஇக்
அழி துளி பொழிந்த இன் குரல் எழிலி
கோடு உயர் நெடு வரை ஆடும் நாட நீ
நின் வழிப்படூஉம் என் தோழி நல் நுதல்
மருந்து பிறிது இன்மை நன்கு அறிந்தனை சென்மே
reading: The friend tells the hill lord, in whose land the sweet-voiced cloud, having poured heavy drops that wash the red tusks of an elephant killed in a fierce old enmity, turns to carded cotton and plays over the tall peaks at dawn, that even if he does not grant grace, even if he does unkind things, her fair-browed friend will follow his way; and that he knows well there is no medicine but him for the pallor that has come to her like a guest.
nuance: The pallor is a விருந்து, a guest who has settled in the house; a guest is fed and kept, so the figure says the girl's sickness is now at home with her. The killed elephant whose tusks the rain washes is scene; a reading of it as the danger he runs, or as a wrong the rain cleans away, has only one point of contact.

thinai_evidence.note: the hill, its elephant and its morning cloud, and a lover pressed to marry

comparisons.tenor: the cloud after rain
the pallor that has settled on her

tamil: சிறு வீ முல்லைத் தேம் கமழ் பசு வீ
பொறி வரி நல் மான் புகர் முகம் கடுப்ப
தண் புதல் அணிபெற மலர வண் பெயல்
பொய் இடி அதிர் குரல் வாய் செத்து ஆலும்
reading: Addressing the cloud, the friend says that he said the season would be when the small honey-scented mullai flowers bloom to adorn the cool bush like the spotted face of the striped deer and the rich rain comes; now, lacking love, the cloud practises unkindness with the roaring voice of false thunder to see the suffering heart tremble; but will she be fooled like the flock of young peacocks that take it for true and dance? Long live, cloud!
nuance: She grants that the signs look right and refuses them: the thunder is பொய், and she sets herself apart from the peafowl who believe it. To deny the season is to keep the man's promise unbroken, since if this is not the season he is not late.

colophon.thurai: பருவம் கண்டு ஆற்றாளாகிய தலைமகளைத் தோழி மழை மேல் வைத்துப் பருவம் மறுத்தது

thinai_evidence.note: the mullai in flower and the season of rain awaited

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: spoken to the cloud (மழையே, line 9) for the woman to hear

comparisons.vehicle: பொறி வரி நல் மான் புகர் முகம் கடுப்ப
comparisons.tenor: the mullai flowers spread over the bush
herself, if she believed the thunder

tamil: புலிப் பொறிக் கொண்ட பூ நாறு குரூஉச் சுவல்
வரி வண்டு ஊதலின் புலி செத்து வெரீஇ
reading: The shore lord's chariot came clattering into the rich street and went, setting gossip rising in the old whispering town: there, under the punnai with its trunk like iron, leaves like sapphire, clusters like silver and pollen like gold falling between, the striped bees hummed on the horse's flower-scented neck, spotted like a tiger with the pollen, and the horse, taking itself for set upon by a tiger, leapt like a ball and would not stand however it was reined.
nuance: The chain of causes is comic and exact: pollen spots the horse, bees come to the pollen, the horse takes the spots and the humming for a tiger, bolts, and the noise in the street announces what the lovers kept secret. The poem ends on the chariot going, so the gossip outlasts the visit.

thinai_evidence.note: the punnai of the shore and the shore lord

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names neither speaker nor addressee; the girl wasting before the marriage is the likeliest speaker

comparisons.tenor: the punnai's dark trunk
its green leaves
its white flower clusters
its pollen
the pollen-spotted neck of the horse
the horse's leaping

tamil: பூ நாறு செவ் வாய் சிதைத்த சாந்தமொடு
பிறை வனப்பு உற்ற மாசு அறு திரு நுதல்
நாறு இருங் கதுப்பின் எம் காதலி வேறு உணர்ந்து
reading: The man, come home with his son, tells the bard to come and laugh with him: when his sweet-lisping son, anklets ringing, was practising walking his little chariot in the street, his flower-scented red mouth smeared with sandal paste, the man, his heart urging him, came close wanting to hug him, and his beloved, with her crescent-lovely brow and fragrant dark hair, taking it otherwise, shied away like a startled doe and stood apart, saying 'who are you?'
nuance: The joke is against himself: the wife greets her own husband with the question a stranger gets. He used the son as his way back into the house, and she reads even his embrace of the child as coming from elsewhere; the 'laugh' covers his failure.

colophon.thurai: புதல்வனொடு புக்க தலைமகன் ஆற்றானாய்ப் பாணற்கு உரைத்தது

thinai_evidence.note: the wife's estranged sulking at the husband returning by way of the son

comparisons.tenor: the wife moving away
her brow

tamil: நெடு நீர் அருவிய கடும் பாட்டு ஆங்கண்
பிணி முதல் அரைய பெருங் கல் வாழைக்
கொழு முதல் ஆய் கனி மந்தி கவரும்
நல் மலை நாடனை நயவா யாம் அவன்
நனி பேர் அன்பின் நின் குரல் ஓப்பி
தளிர் ஏர் மேனித் தொல் கவின் அழிய
பலி பெறு கடவுட் பேணி கலி சிறந்து
நுடங்கு நிலைப் பறவை உடங்கு பீள் கவரும்
reading: With the man listening outside, the speaker turns to the millet: in the land of the good hill where the falls roar and a female monkey snatches the fine fruit from the thick stem of the great wild plantain, we, loving its lord, have guarded you with great love and driven the birds off your ears, you have seen it; now that the old beauty of my shoot-like body is fading and the household, worshipping the god of offerings, makes a festival, do not bend your ears for the swaying birds to snatch, but rise and ripen late, long live, millet!
nuance: The plea to the millet is the news the man is meant to hear: when the crop is in, the girl's days in the field end and she is shut in the house. Whether the festival for the god is a harvest rite or the mother's remedy for the girl's changed looks, the text does not settle.

thinai_evidence.note: falls, monkey and millet of the hill, and a secret love at risk

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: spoken to the millet (தினையே, line 11); the colophon names no speaker, and the 'my body' of line 7 may make it the girl

comparisons.tenor: her body

iraicchi.act: the female monkey takes the ripe fruit from the plant while it is there to be taken
iraicchi.sense: the man should take the girl now, while she is still in the field, before the harvest shuts her away

tamil: திறம் புரி கொள்கையொடு இறந்து செயின அல்லது
அரும் பொருட் கூட்டம் இருந்தோர்க்கு இல் என
வினை இடை விலங்கல போலும் புனை சுவர்ப்
ஐது ஏய்ந்து அகன்ற அல்குல் மை கூர்ந்து
மலர் பிணைத்தன்ன மா இதழ் மழைக் கண்
முயல் வேட்டு எழுந்த முடுகு விசைக் கத நாய்
reading: The friend tells the anxious woman that his heart, once unresolved, resolved on the far country's track where the dead oomai stands bent and cicadas shrill, holding that rare wealth does not gather for those who stay unless they go with a firm will and act; but the work so planned seems to be blocked by her qualities: her blameless look like a doll on a painted wall, her wide hips, her dark rain-eyes like flowers strung in pairs, her small feet like the good tongue of the fierce dog leaping to hunt a hare, and her full hair and fine jewels.
nuance: The man's maxim is given its full weight before it is checked, and what checks it is not counter-argument but a list of her features: the friend comforts her by telling her what her own beauty does to his resolve. The dog's tongue simile, red and soft and narrow, is the oddest and most exact of the set.

colophon.thurai: பொருள்வயிற் பிரியும் எனக் கவன்ற தலைமகட்குத் தோழி சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the dry waste of withered trees and cicadas, and a planned going for wealth

comparisons.tenor: her look
her eyes

comparisons.vehicle: முடுகு விசைக் கத நாய் நல் நாப் புரையும்
comparisons.tenor: her small feet

tamil: பல் குடைக் கள்ளின் வண் மகிழ்ப் பாரி
reading: The friend tells the man that when birds return to their roosts or he sees couples together he sighs hot breaths like a stalled elephant, wasting with pain, and does not hear her, only thinks; the bright-jewelled girl, whom one trembles even to think of, has come to great beauty and is now hard to reach, guarded like the jackfruit-laden hill of Paari, generous with many pots of toddy, where thunder of great sound and rain have closed round.
nuance: Paari's hill is the measure of both beauty and inaccessibility: rich and besieged, it could not be taken by force. The friend's point is that the time for stealing visits is over.

thinai_evidence.note: the girl now guarded and a lover pressed to marry, with a hill for the image

comparisons.tenor: the man's hot sighing
the girl, grown beautiful and closely guarded

tamil: குன்று ஓங்கு வெண் மணற் கொடி அடும்பு கொய்தும்
கணம் நாறு பெருந் தொடை புரளும் மார்பின்
நேர் கண் சிறு தடி நீரின் மாற்றி
reading: The friend tells the lord of the wide roaring sea, who built sand houses with them, kicked the incoming waves, plucked the adumbu creeper on the high white dune and spoke sweet words without sulking, but got no answer and is going away slowly, wearied, that if he stays in their small hamlet by the shore, whose farming (changing the water with small straight staves) needs no rain, and eats today the rice bartered for the salt the umanar brought, he will not sleep alone with no companion, his chest where the large blue-lily garland rolls.
nuance: The colophon says the friend says what she has made up (படைத்து மொழிந்தது): the invitation is a test or a feint, and the reader cannot tell whether the companion she promises is the girl. The salt pan, farming that needs no sky, is a picture of the shore people's self-sufficiency set against the man's need.

thinai_evidence.note: the dune creeper, the salt traders and the shore hamlet

tamil: வயக் களிறு பொருத வாள் வரி உழுவை
மென் தோள் நெகிழ்ந்து நாம் வருந்தினும் இன்று அவர்
உருமுச் சிவந்து எறியும் ஓங்கு வரை ஆறே
reading: The girl says the ghouls stir and the town has gone to sleep, the hill folk of the guarded house stay awake singing the awesome kurinji, and the sword-striped tiger that fought a strong tusker roars on the slope of rock caves; alas, though our soft shoulders loosen and we suffer, it would be good if he did not come tonight, by the path on the high hill where lightning flashes on the ridges, rain and wind mingle past midnight, the snake wanders searching for its gem and the thunder, red, strikes.
nuance: She wishes away the meeting she longs for, setting her own wasting (மென் தோள் நெகிழ்ந்து) against his danger and choosing his safety; the path itself is the poem's subject, as the colophon's ஆறு பார்த்து says.

thinai_evidence.note: midnight on the hill, the hill folk's song, the tiger and the night tryst

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no speaker; the girl speaks of 'our' shoulders and 'him'

tamil: நீயே பாடல் சான்ற பழி தபு சீறடி
காடே நிழல் கவின் இழந்த அழல் கவர் மரத்த
இந் நிலை தவிர்ந்தனம் செலவே வைந் நுதிக்
மடப் பிணை தழீஇய மா எருத்து இரலை
காழ் கொள் வேலத்து ஆழ் சினை பயந்த
reading: The man tells his wife, who grieved thinking he had left for wealth: you have small blameless feet worth singing, great beauty and warring eyes, while the forest's trees, seized by fire, have lost the beauty of their shade, and loneliness sits enthroned there; so we have given up going; and even the cool forest of the rains, when the kalaa blooms with the pidavu and the dark-necked stag, holding his young doe, rests in the striped shade of the thorny vela tree, we have given that up too.
nuance: He renounces both seasons of the road, the burnt summer forest and the pleasant forest of the rains, and the doubled refrain (தவிர்ந்தனம் செலவே) is the promise. The stag who holds his doe in the shade is what he chooses to be.

colophon.thurai: பொருள்வயிற் பிரிந்தான் என்று ஆற்றாளாகிய தலைமகளைத் தலைமகன் ஆற்றியது

thinai_evidence.note: a journey given up; the scorched forest is paalai's and the rain forest mullai's

iraicchi.act: the stag holds his young doe close and rests with her in the shade
iraicchi.sense: the man will stay and keep his wife as the stag keeps his doe, even in the season that invites travel

tamil: விளிவு இல் அரவமொடு தளி சிறந்து உரைஇ
மழை எழுந்து இறுத்த நளிர் தூங்கு சிலம்பின்
கழை அமல்பு நீடிய வான் உயர் நெடுங் கோட்டு
இலங்கு வெள் அருவி வியன் மலைக் கவாஅன்
அரும்பு வாய் அவிழ்ந்த கருங் கால் வேங்கைப்
பொன் மருள் நறு வீ கல்மிசைத் தாஅம்
இயங்குநர் மடிந்த அயம் திகழ் சிறு நெறிக்
reading: The friend tells the lord of the good hill, where cloud has risen with endless roar and pouring drops and settled on the cold dripping slope, bamboo grows thick to the sky on the tall peak, white falls shine on the side of the wide hill and the dark-trunked vengai's gold-like fragrant flowers spread on the rock, that he loves but is not gracious: knowing that fierce beasts roam the narrow path by the pools where no traveller goes, he comes at midnight, and she grieves for it.
nuance: 'You love, yet you are not gracious' splits the man's two duties: desire brings him at midnight, but grace would spare her the fear, which only marriage can do. The scene is all beauty; the danger is stated in two lines without description.

colophon.thurai: தோழி தலைமகனது ஏதம் சொல்லி வரைவு கடாயது

thinai_evidence.note: the hill slope, the vengai and the midnight visit

comparisons.tenor: the vengai's flowers

tamil: திருவுடை வியல் நகர் வரு விருந்து அயர்மார்
கொக்கு உகிர் நிமிரல் மாந்தி எல் பட
reading: The friend tells the shore lord that she is going, she who frequented the day trysts in the flowered shore grove: the mother has shut the girl in, seeing her close-fitting bright bangles slipping, the girl who is like the port of Marungur, where the gold-bangled women of the rich wide houses spill at the back door the rice, like heron's claws, cooked for arriving guests, and the fresh-eyed crow, having eaten it while the sun burns the rocks, at dusk snatches the fresh prawns heaped in the shade of the market and roosts on the mast of a rocking ship.
nuance: The comparison runs on the port's fullness, a whole day of plenty from the guest's rice to the roost on the mast, and the girl is like that abundance; the crow that eats freely all day is set against the girl now shut in. Read as the man feeding at will, the crow has one point of contact, not two, so it stays scene.

thinai_evidence.note: the shore grove, the prawns, the ships and the port

comparisons.tenor: the cooked rice grains
the girl

tamil: பெருங் கல் நாடனொடு இரும் புனத்து அல்கி
செவ் வாய்ப் பைங் கிளி ஓப்பி அவ் வாய்ப்
பெரிது அமர்ந்து இயைந்த கேண்மை சிறு நனி
reading: The friend asks the girl what they will do: the friendship they made in great delight with the lord of the great-rock land, on the honey-scented slope where the gold-flowered vengai stands tall (staying in the wide millet field, chasing the red-beaked green parrots, bathing in the falls of the great hill's side, smoothing on the slope's sandal where bees settle), she now sees becoming very hard to keep, for the millet heads have taken their dry ripeness, like the spreading waves of the sea drawing back.
nuance: The list of shared pleasures is all of the field season, so the ripened millet ends the whole catalogue at once; the sea simile in a hill poem measures the field's change from green waves to dry stalks.

colophon.thurai: தோழி தலைமகளைச் செறிப்பு அறிவுறீஇ வரைவு கடாயது

thinai_evidence.note: vengai, parrots, millet and the hill lord's friendship

comparisons.tenor: the ripened millet field

tamil: குன்று சேர் வெண் மணல் துஞ்சும் ஊர
மலி புனல் வாயில் இருப்பை அன்ன என்
ஒலி பல் கூந்தல் நலம் பெறப் புனைந்த
reading: The wife tells the lord of the town, where the dark-legged buffalo, having grazed on the red lilies and tired of the cold lotus of the field, walks like warriors with staves and sleeps on the hill-high white sand nearby, that he embraces her as if he desired her; but he who withered the bud-opened garland once adorned to beautify her thick hair, beautiful as Iruppai at the flood-fed gate of the red-speared warrior who wore down his foes, was her enemy, and she cannot forget it and be at peace.
nuance: 'My enemy' (பகைவன்மன்) is said with the regretful மன்: he was, once, the man who spoiled her garland in love; now he is the man who spoils it by neglect, and the old embrace makes the new one a counterfeit.

thinai_evidence.note: the wife's sulking at a straying husband, in the field country of the buffalo

comparisons.tenor: the buffalo's gait
the beauty of her hair
the husband who goes from woman to woman

ullurai.tenor: the husband and the women he goes to

pairs.situation: he has had his fill of one woman
he tires of another

pairs.scene: அயலது குன்று சேர் வெண் மணல் துஞ்சும்
pairs.situation: he sleeps away from home, not in his wife's house

ullurai.speaker_fit: the wife uses the buffalo of her own field town, a thing she knows (porul 7.26)

title: natrinai 261-280
theme: Natrinai 261 to 280: the friend at the hill and the shore turning night trysts, veri rites and slander into pressure for marriage; male birds that feed their pregnant mates on the neythal shore; a hero torn between his wife and the shame of poverty; two mothers whose daughters have eloped; a heroine who curses a bee for not carrying word; and a wife who has no time to sulk because her house, like the Velir's Kunrur, is always full of guests.
source_issues: Natrinai colophons give speaker, addressee and occasion in prose; where they name no speaker or addressee (262, 266, 267, 268, 271, 272, 276, 277, 279) thurai_akam supplies one from the poem, with a note.
262: the colophon names no speaker; the poem is the hero speaking to his heart (பிரிவல் நெஞ்சு என்னும்), so the speaker is coded thalaivan, addressee nenju.

268: the colophon says the poem is spoken to the heroine, but the poem's own vocative is தோழி (line 7) and the speaker proposes to question the velan herself; on the poem's evidence the heroine may be the speaker. Kept as the colophon has it.
270: the colophon thinai is நெய்தல்; the screwpine is a shore thing, but the situation is the friend's sarcasm to a husband who wanders (oodal), so I infer marutham.
271: the colophon gives no poet (text flag).
277: the colophon's பொருள்வயிற் பிரியஆற்றளாகிய looks like a misprint for பிரிய ஆற்றாளாகிய.

262 line 2, 275 line 3, 279 line 5: the lost -ஒடு vowel sign restored (text flag); 267 line 9: TSCII repair read as தெள் with tamilvu.org; 273 line 1: ஃ restored; 276 line 1: நாயொடு restored by rule and not confirmed by sangamtamil.com.
