265 is syntactically incomplete as we have it (a run of comparisons ending in நம் வயினானே with no main verb), and the sense of சிறு கோற் சென்னி ஆரேற்றன்ன is not clear to me; 270 lines 1 to 5 and 279 lines 5 to 7 are also hard to construe.

tamil: வெஞ் சுடர் கரந்த கமஞ் சூல் வானம்
நெடும் பல் குன்றத்துக் குறும் பல மறுகி
தா இல் பெரும் பெயல் தலைஇய யாமத்து
வெளிறு இல் காழ் மரம் பிணித்து நனி மிளிர்க்கும்
சாந்தம் போகிய தேம் கமழ் விடர் முகை
reading: The friend, knowing the man stands within hearing, tells the girl he has no pity: he comes at midnight in the heavy rain, when lightning splits the dark sky and thunder roars over the many tall hills, by the narrow path of the great rock where a raging python that has caught an elephant coils round a hard-cored tree and wrenches it, past caves fragrant with sandal and tall eruvai flowers.
nuance: 'He has no grace' is said of a man who risks his life to come: the complaint is the friend's way of telling him, overhearing, that the night tryst must end and the only safe road is marriage. The python crushing the elephant gives the hearer the path's danger in one picture.

colophon.thurai: சிறைப்புறமாகத் தோழி இரவுக்குறி விலக்கி வரைவு கடாயது தலைமகள் இயற்பட மொழிந்ததூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: hill paths at midnight in the rains fix kurinji

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: on this reading 'he has no grace' is the girl's fond complaint in his favour

tamil: தண் புனக் கருவிளைக் கண் போல் மா மலர்
நடுங்கு பிணி நலிய நல் எழில் சாஅய்
துனி கூர் மனத்தள் முனி படர் உழக்கும்
பணைத் தோள் அரும்பிய சுணங்கின் கணைக் கால்
reading: The hero tells his heart that she is already wasting: in the midnight of the sleeping town, when the north wind sways the great karuvilai flowers like the feathers of a dancing peacock, a trembling sickness thins her beauty; yet even if the heart, set on effort, says it will leave this girl with flower-scented hair and honeyed speech, the shame of having nothing is hard to bear.
nuance: The poem ends on the other side of the scale: the last line, about the shame of poverty, is the argument for going, and the colophon reads the whole as his checking his departure. He imagines her suffering in a future night as if it were already present.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகள் ஆற்றாக் குறிப்பு அறிந்து பிரிவிடை விலக்கியது

thinai_evidence.note: the parting for effort, not the scene, decides paalai

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no speaker; the poem's பிரிவல் நெஞ்சு makes it the hero to his heart

comparisons.tenor: the karuvilai flowers, shaped like eyes
the flowers swaying in the north wind

tamil: பிறை வனப்பு இழந்த நுதலும் யாழ நின்
ஊர் அலர் தூற்றும் கௌவையும் நாண் விட்டு
முட முதிர் நாரை கடல் மீன் ஒய்யும்
reading: Overheard by the man, the friend tells the girl that though they never speak of it to him, out of shame, the forehead that has lost its crescent beauty, the bangles that slip from her wrist and the gossip of the town, her kohled tears, hidden again and again, have overflowed and told it all at the sight of the gentle lonely shore where an old lame stork, hunting, carries sea fish to his hen who, heavy with young, stays back in the field.
nuance: The tears 'speak' though the women do not: the friend makes the girl's body the messenger, so that the man hears a demand without being addressed.

thinai_evidence.note: the stork fishing the sea by the shore grove fixes neythal

iraicchi.act: the old lame stork goes hunting and brings sea fish to his pregnant hen, who cannot reach the shore
iraicchi.sense: even a crippled old bird provides for the mate who carries his young; the man, whole and young, has not even married the girl he has made to suffer

tamil: பாம்பு அளைச் செறிய முழங்கி வலன் ஏர்பு
வான் தளி பொழிந்த காண்பு இன் காலை
அணி கிளர் கலாவம் ஐது விரித்து இயலும்
மணி புரை எருத்தின் மஞ்ஞை போல நின்
வீ பெய் கூந்தல் வீசு வளி உளர
ஈகாண் தோன்றும் எம் சிறு நல் ஊரே
reading: Leading the girl away with him, the man urges her on: the rain has poured with thunder that drives snakes into their holes, the morning is lovely, and she walks with the wind stirring her flower-strewn hair like a peacock with a sapphire neck spreading its bright tail; the day is ending, so go on, girl, for listen, the clear bells on the cows the cowherds have tied in the bamboo thicket are ringing, and there is our small good town.
nuance: The road of elopement, which paalai poems fill with heat and danger, is here a rain-washed mullai evening, and the end of it is not a wilderness but 'our town' with its cow-bells: the man reassures her by showing her the home she is coming to.

colophon.thurai: உடன் போகாநின்ற தலைமகன் தலைமகளை வற்புறீஇயது உடன்போய் மறுத்தரா நின்றான் ஊர்காட்டி வற்புறீஇயதும் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the elopement journey is paalai's parting, whatever the landscape

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: bringing her back after the elopement, he shows her the town

comparisons.tenor: the girl walking with her hair stirred by the wind
the peacock's neck

tamil: இறுகு புனம் மேய்ந்த அறு கோட்டு முற்றல்
reading: The man who has followed the girl tells his heart that her thick soft hair, precious as Paaram that Minjili, chief of the bowmen whose whistling arrows bring down the spotted stag, guards, as the town of the Chola with the small sceptre, and like the plumage of the joyous peacocks on Kolli, the hill of Ori whose giving is like the rain, is now ours.
nuance: Each comparison is a guarded or famous possession of a chief, so the girl's hair is praised as a prize won from the strongholds of the hill; the poem has no main verb as we have it, and the sense of the Chenni line is not certain.

thinai_evidence.note: the hill stag, the peacock of Kolli and the cleared hill field fix kurinji

comparisons.tenor: the girl's hair, a guarded prize
the girl's hair
her thick soft hair

tamil: குறுங் காற் குரவின் குவி இணர் வான் பூ
reading: The friend tells the man that they are folk of a small village on the wide land where, by the cowherds' little field, the short-stemmed kuravam blooms its clustered white flowers for the goatherd to wear, and that is enough for them; but besides love, if he leaves them she will say one thing: if a man flees once she has been made to live apart from her own people, is that not a great thing to say of the great?
nuance: The village's contentment with wild kuravam flowers is the friend's claim that they ask for no wealth, so the only reason to leave is his own; the last line praises 'the great' in a way that shames him.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகனைச் செலவுடன்பட்டது கடிநகர் வரைப்பில் கண்டு மகிழ்ந்த தலைமகற்குத் தோழி நும்மாலே ஆயிற்று என்று சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: cowherds, the goatherd and the kuravam of the forest fields fix mullai

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no speaker; the poem's ஐய and எம் give the friend

tamil: இலங்கு எயிற்று ஏஎர் இன் நகை மகளிர்
உணங்கு தினை துழவும் கை போல் ஞாழல்
மணம் கமழ் நறு வீ வரிக்கும் துறைவன்
தனியே வருதல் நனி புலம்பு உடைத்து என
சிறு நா ஒண் மணித் தெள் இசை கடுப்ப
இன மீன் ஆர்கை ஈண்டு புள் ஒலிக்குரல்
reading: The friend, speaking where the man can hear, says that she would not have come to the sweet grove where the lord of the shore, whose crowds of crabs with eyes like nochchi buds scratch at fragrant njaazhal flowers as women with shining teeth stir drying millet with their hands, first met the girl, since coming there alone is so lonely; yet she came, and before she could say that the cries of the birds swarming over the shoals of fish, like the clear sound of small-tongued bells, were no man, he appeared there, strong as a lion.
nuance: The friend pretends the grove is haunted only by memory and birds, then lets the man's sudden arrival end the poem: the meeting place is still in use, and with the guard tightened, that is the reason to marry.

colophon.thurai: தோழி காப்புக் கைமிக்குக் காமம் பெருகிய காலத்துச் சிறைப்புறமாகச் சொல்லியது வரைவு கடாயதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: crabs of the dunes, njaazhal and the shore grove fix neythal

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi

occasion.words: காப்புக் கைமிக்குக் காமம் பெருகிய காலத்துச் சிறைப்புறமாகச் சொல்லியது

thurai_akam.note: no addressee is named; the girl is the likely hearer

comparisons.tenor: the crabs' eyes
the crabs scratching the flowers
the cries of the birds
the man as he appears

tamil: சூருடை நனந் தலைச் சுனை நீர் மல்க
மால் பெயல் தலைஇய மன் நெடுங் குன்றத்து
கருங் காற் குறிஞ்சி மதன் இல் வான் பூ
reading: Of the man of the land where, in the tall hills, heavy rain fills the springs of the haunted wide places and the honey of the black-stemmed kurinji's pure white flowers oozes in hives built at the rock's edge as if painted, the speaker asks why the love he made has become unlove: let us ask, friend, by guarding the sand-strewn courtyard and bringing the velan with his molucca beans.
nuance: The veri rite is meant to name the god who has seized the girl; turning it to the question 'why has his love failed?' mocks the rite and points, past the velan, to the man as the real cause.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகட்குச் சொல்லியது தலைமகன் வந்தொழுகவும் வேறுபாடு கண்டாள் அவன் வருவானாகவும் நீ வேறுபட்டாய் வெறி எடுத்துக் கொள்ளும் வகையான் என்றதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the kurinji flower, hill honey and the velan's rite fix kurinji

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the friend tells her the mother will hold a veri because she has changed though the man keeps coming

comparisons.tenor: the honeycombs built on the rock

tamil: குரும்பை மணிப் பூண் பெருஞ் செங் கிண்கிணிப்
பால் ஆர் துவர் வாய்ப் பைம் பூட் புதல்வன்
அவ் எயிறு ஒழுகிய அவ் வாய் மாண் நகைச்
செயிர் தீர் கொள்கை நம் உயிர் வெங் காதலி
reading: Refusing the man entry, the friend reminds him of his son with bead-jewels and a big red anklet, his milky coral mouth, who climbs down his chest on the evening bed, and of the wife dear as their own life, with lovely teeth and a fine smile and blameless ways, whose eyes rove over his face, who binds him every day like the valli creeper; men who cross the many small hills do not think of that, and who knows what they intend?
nuance: The friend never says 'do not go': she sets the bed, the child and the wife's gaze before him and ends on a question about 'those who cross the hills', talking of him in the third person as if he were already gone.

colophon.thurai: தோழி வாயில் மறுத்தது செலவு அழுங்குவித்ததூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the crossing of the hills for gain is paalai's parting

comparisons.tenor: the wife who binds him

tamil: இருள் புரை கூந்தல் பொங்கு துகள் ஆடி
உருள் பொறி போல எம் முனை வருதல்
விரி உளைப் பொலிந்த பரியுடை நன் மான்
reading: Letting the husband in, the friend tells him with irony that he has been far kinder to her than to the girl of broad shoulders who knows only how to adorn herself and not how to bind him, while the other woman with dark hair fragrant of the screwpine comes rolling to their side like a toy wheel; his cruelty is worse than the cruelty Nannan, the spear-lifting king of fine maned horses who routed kings, did to a woman's hair, and she will never forget his valour.
nuance: The praise of his valour and the comparison with Nannan's notorious cruelty turn the friend's consent into a rebuke: she lets him in by naming what he has done.

colophon.thurai: தோழி வாயில் நேர்கின்றாள் தலைமகனை நெருங்கிச் சொல்லி வாயில் எதிர்கொண்டது உடனிலைக் கிளவி வகையால்

thinai_evidence.note: the friend's sarcasm to a straying husband is marutham's sulking

occasion.words: தோழி வாயில் நேர்கின்றாள் தலைமகனை நெருங்கிச் சொல்லி வாயில் எதிர்கொண்டது

comparisons.tenor: the other woman's hair
the other woman's coming to their side
the husband's cruelty

tamil: இரும் புனிற்று எருமைப் பெருஞ் செவிக் குழவி
பைந் தாது எருவின் வைகு துயில் மடியும்
செழுந் தண் மனையோடு எம் இவண் ஒழிய
செல் பெருங் காளை பொய்ம் மருண்டு சேய் நாட்டுச்
சுவைக் காய் நெல்லிப் போக்கு அரும் பொங்கர்
வீழ் கடைத் திரள் காய் ஒருங்குடன் தின்று
வீ சுனைச் சிறு நீர் குடியினள் கழிந்த
தா இன்று கழிக எற் கொள்ளாக் கூற்றே
reading: A mother, bewildered in her house, says her daughter with kohled lily eyes has left the rich cool house, where the big-eared calf of the dark buffalo sleeps on fresh dung, to go with a bold youth, deceived by his lies, to a far land, eating with him the fallen gooseberries of the impassable grove and drinking the little water of flower-strewn springs; while her playmates, girls of her age who cut palm-leaf toys, go home in the evening moonlight, she asks that the great dark urn cover her and curses Death for passing her by.
nuance: The calf asleep by its mother at home stands against the daughter who has gone, and the playmates returning at evening measure her absence; the mother's grief turns into a wish to be buried.

thinai_evidence.note: the daughter's journey to a far land through hard groves is paalai

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: no addressee; the mother speaks aloud in the house

comparisons.tenor: the daughter's eyes
the playmates of her age

tamil: பொம்மல் அடும்பின் வெண் மணல் ஒரு சிறை
இருஞ் சேற்று அயிரை தேரிய தெண் கழிப்
பெருங் கையற்ற என் சிறுமை பலர் வாய்
reading: The girl, worn by his long visits without marriage, says that the lord of the shore, where the red-beaked sea crow searches the flowered pool of the clear backwater for ayirai fish of the dark mud to feed his lovely hen resting heavy with young on a strip of white sand among the adumbu that ascetic women have stripped, has not been kind; her hope has come to nothing, her helplessness is in many mouths in the old town of gossip, and that has become a sickness greater than the sickness.
nuance: 'Greater than the sickness' ranks the pains: love-sickness she can bear, the town's talk she cannot, which is the reason the friend wants the man to hear.

colophon.thurai: வரையாது நெடுங்காலம் வந்தொழுக ஆற்றாளாய தலைமகள் சொல்லியது தோழி தலைமகளுக்குச் சொல்லுவாளாய் தலைமகன் கேட்பச் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the sea crow fishing the backwater fixes neythal

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi

occasion.words: வரையாது நெடுங்காலம் வந்தொழுக ஆற்றாளாய தலைமகள் சொல்லியது

thurai_akam.note: no addressee is named; the friend is the likely hearer

iraicchi.act: the male sea crow searches the backwater pool for fish to feed his hen resting heavy with young
iraicchi.sense: a crow provides for the mate it has made pregnant, while the man of the same shore leaves the girl he has taken neither married nor cared for

tamil: நீர் கொள் நெடுஞ் சுனை அமைந்து வார்ந்து உறைந்து என்
கண் போல் நீலம் தண் கமழ் சிறக்கும்
நெஞ்சு நடுக்குறூஉம் அவன் பண்பு தரு படரே
reading: The friend, knowing the man has come, tells the girl, so that he may hear, that the mother, not knowing about them and troubled by the fearful suffering spreading through her body, will hear the velan call it the god's seizure; and her heart trembles whenever she thinks of the man of the hill country, where a lordly elephant drinks at a deep spring and the cool blue lily like her eyes grows fragrant.
nuance: Announcing the veri within his hearing is the friend's lever: if the rite is held the secret will come out, and only marriage forestalls it.

colophon.thurai: தோழி தலைமகனது வரவு உணர்ந்து தலைமகட்கு உரைப்பாளாய் நின் வேறுபாடு தாய்க்குப் புலனாக அவள் வேலனைக் கூவி வெறி அயரும் என்பது படச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the hill man, the velan and the mountain spring fix kurinji

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon's தலைமகனது வரவு உணர்ந்து implies he overhears

comparisons.tenor: the blue lily of his hill

tamil: நெடு வான் மின்னி குறுந் துளி தலைஇ
உழை படு மான் பிணை தீண்டலின் இழை மகள்
பொன் செய் காசின் ஒண் பழம் தாஅம்
reading: The friend tells the girl that the man who once asked her to come with him through the hills where rain has poured from the lightning of the tall sky, where a doe brushing past scatters the bright kumizh fruits like gold coins on the many short paths, has now changed and crossed the wasteland of great rocks where the tiger roams in the groves: does he still have such words to say?
nuance: The rains that should bring him home only remind her of the invitation he made in the same season; the friend's question sets his old words against his present absence.

thinai_evidence.note: the man gone across the wasteland makes it paalai

comparisons.tenor: the scattered kumizh fruits

tamil: தெறு கதிர் இன் துயில் பசு வாய் திறக்கும்
reading: Overheard by the man, the girl answers her friend's comfort: to the lord of the great-water shore, where a simple neythal flower, cut with its stalk by red-paddy reapers with sharp sickles who did not see it, lies among the sheaves and, not knowing its own ruin, slowly opens its fresh mouth to the burning sun as if waking from sweet sleep, she would not remember or grieve; even if that graceless man praised her she could bear it, she says, but in vain.
nuance: The -மன் of வல்லேன்மன் makes the boast hollow: she knows she cannot hold out, and the flower opening its face to the sun that will kill it is her own case.

colophon.thurai: சிறைப்புறமாகத் தலைமகனது வரவுணர்ந்து வற்புறுப்ப வன்புறை எதிர்மொழிந்தது

thinai_evidence.note: the neythal flower and the great-water shore fix neythal

ullurai.tenor: the girl, ruined by the man and still turning to him

pairs.situation: she was taken unawares by one who did not care what he cut
she does not yet own the harm done to her

pairs.scene: தெறு கதிர் இன் துயில் பசு வாய் திறக்கும்
pairs.situation: she still opens to the man who scorches her

ullurai.speaker_fit: the heroine uses the neythal flower of her own shore and the paddy harvest she sees (porul 7.26)

tamil: காடு தேர்ந்து அசைஇய வய மான் வேட்டு
reading: The friend tells the man who leaves after a daytime meeting that if he takes them for daughters of hunters who hunt the strong beast that rests after searching the forest with fierce dogs, they are only daughters of the hill folk, girls of the hill; their village is among the rocks, where the forest peacock nests on the high-legged platform the watchman built; so he should not go, but stay and go later, drinking the toddy matured in the curved bamboo of the great hill and watching the kuravai dance in the courtyard under the vengai.
nuance: Under 'the ways of the world' the colophon names, the friend offers the hill's hospitality, toddy and dance, to a man who comes only by day and leaves: an invitation to be received openly in the village, which is to say, to marry.

colophon.thurai: பகற்குறி வந்து பெயரும் தலைமகனை உலகியல் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: hill women, the vengai, the peacock and bamboo toddy fix kurinji

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi

occasion.words: பகற்குறி வந்து பெயரும் தலைமகனை உலகியல் சொல்லியது

thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no speaker; the poem's we-forms give the friend

tamil: மனை உறக் காக்கும் மாண் பெருங் கிடக்கை
நெஞ்சு நெகிழ் செய்ததன் பயனோ அன்பு இலர்
என் நிலை உரையாய் சென்று அவண் வரவே
reading: The girl, whose lover went far for wealth without marrying her, tells the bee it is cruel and wishes her sickness on it: besides its black body, is its mind black too? It sucks the pollen-rich peeram flowers on the fine-thorned hedge of the well-guarded house but will not touch her pallor, the same yellow, because it has no scent; she has cared for it, and it brings her nothing; let it go to the loveless men who crossed the hard hot hills, tell them her state, and come back.
nuance: The yellow peeram and the yellow pallor are set side by side: the bee can tell them apart only by smell, and so cannot be made to carry the one that matters.

colophon.thurai: பட்ட பின்றை வரையாது கிழவோன் நெட்டிடைக் கழிந்து பொருள்வயிற் பிரியஆற்றளாகிய தலைமகள் தும்பிக்குச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the man gone across hot wastelands for gain makes it paalai

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the addressee is a bee (தும்பி)

comparisons.tenor: her pallor, the same yellow, which the bee will not touch

tamil: அடு மரல் மொக்குளின் அரும்பு வாய் அவிழ
பொன்னின் அன்ன தாது படு பல் மலர்
நெய் கனி பசுங் காய் தூங்கும் துறைவனை
கழிச் சேறு ஆடிய கணைக் கால் அத்திரி
reading: The friend tells the girl that she now knows the lord of the shore, where the broad-trunked punnai's buds open like bubbles, its gold-like pollen-laden flowers are what garland-makers left over, and green ghee-rich fruit hangs from every branch, is to be her husband: the red prawns have shrunk away even under the hooves of the thick-legged mules that splashed in the backwater mud, and the garlands are all white sand in the north wind.
nuance: The proof is in the mud: tracks of many mules on the shore mean a large party has come, the kind that comes to ask for a bride.

thinai_evidence.note: punnai, backwater mud and prawns fix neythal

comparisons.tenor: the punnai buds opening
the punnai's pollen

tamil: தேம் பால் செற்ற தீம் பழம் நசைஇ
நெய் தோய் திரியின் தண் சிதர் உறைப்ப
நாட் சுரம் உழந்த வாள் கேழ் ஏற்றையொடு
பசிப் பிடி உதைத்த ஓமைச் செவ் வரை
reading: The mother whose daughter has gone off with her lover asks whether the feet of her jewelled girl, whose anklets were taken off and who has gone to another's house, are weary struggling on the path through a wasteland that glitters in the sun's heat, where bats, tired of neem fruit and craving the sweet milky iluppai, drip cold drops from every branch like ghee from a wick, and a hungry she-elephant has kicked the red bark of the omai tree.
nuance: The removal of the anklets (சிலம்பு கழீஇய) was the rite before marriage; the mother names it as the one wealth of a girl who has gone to marry elsewhere, so the poem grieves both the road and the wedding she did not see.

thinai_evidence.note: the sun-scorched wasteland path fixes paalai

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: no addressee; the mother speaks to herself

comparisons.tenor: the drops dripping from the bats
the kicked bark of the omai

tamil: தொன்று முதிர் வேளிர் குன்றூர் அன்ன என்
reading: The wife tells the friend who asks her not to sulk at the man of the cool-ford town, where the sweet fruit the stork missed falls with a plop into the deep pool among water-lily buds shaped like a stork's hunched stance, for his endless philandering, that she will not sulk: her good house, like Kunrur of the ancient Velir where field guards break curly snails on the green-mossed back of the field turtle, is so busy feasting guests that she has no leisure for it.
nuance: The refusal is a sulk in itself: 'I have no time to sulk' says that she has the house, the guests and the standing, and he has nothing she needs. The fruit missed by the stork that drops among stork-shaped buds hints at favours falling to the women who look like the wife, but it does not give two clear pairs.

colophon.thurai: வாயில் வேண்டிச் சென்ற தோழிக்குத் தலைமகள் மறுத்து மொழிந்தது தலைமகனை ஏற்றுக்கொண்டு வழிபட்டாளைப் புகழ்ந்து புக்க தோழிக்குத் தலைமகள் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the wife's sulk at a philandering husband is marutham

occasion.words: வாயில் வேண்டிச் சென்ற தோழிக்குத் தலைமகள் மறுத்து மொழிந்தது
தலைமகனை ஏற்றுக்கொண்டு வழிபட்டாளைப் புகழ்ந்து புக்க தோழிக்குத் தலைமகள் சொல்லியதூஉம்

comparisons.vehicle: கொக்கின் கூம்பு நிலை அன்ன முகைய ஆம்பல்
comparisons.tenor: the water-lily buds
her good house, full of guests

title: natrinai 281-300
theme: Natrinai 281 to 300: the friend's voice again leads, pressing for marriage with the hidden lover listening, fearing the veri rite and the mother's watch, and refusing the night visit; men are torn between work and the woman, a mother curses the mother of the youth who took her daughter, a courtesan mocks the husband as a bee, and puram fame (Malaiyan's cattle raids at Mullur, Thazhumban's Unur, Chezhiyan's Koodal, the Cholas' Kazhar) is turned into the measure of akam loss.
source_issues: Natrinai colophons give speaker and occasion in prose; thurai_akam follows them, and where they name no addressee (287, 293) the code is pira with a note.
286: the poet's name ends பாலங் கொற்றனார, with the final consonant ர் apparently lost.
297 and 298: the colophon thurai has a word split by a space (சொல்லி யது, நெருங் கிச்); copied as is.
300: the colophon thurai runs on into what looks like an editor's note (மாற்றோர் நொதுமலாளர் வரைவின் மேலிட்டு மருதத்துக் களவு), copied as is.
281 line 8, 297 lines 10-11 and 298 lines 10-12: the syntax is hard and the readings given are marked uncertain.
Inferred thinai agrees with the colophon for all twenty poems.

tamil: மாசு இல் மரத்த பலி உண் காக்கை
வளி பொரு நெடுஞ் சினை தளியொடு தூங்கி
நல் வகை மிகு பலிக் கொடையோடு உகுக்கும்
மழை அமைந்து உற்ற மால் இருள் நடு நாள்
reading: The woman tells her friend that their lover has no love: on this rain-soaked midnight the crows that live on offerings hang dripping on the wind-beaten branch, thinking of the great meat-and-rice offerings the Cholas take at Kazhar, while he, who knows that even with him beside us we lie sleepless and wretched in the cold, has left us to it.
nuance: The crows endure the wet night on the memory of a feast; the woman endures it on the memory of the man. Line 8 (தாம் நம் உழையராகவும்) can also be read of the crows (though they are near us) rather than of the lover, which changes who is beside her.

colophon.thurai: வன்பொறை எதிர் அழிந்த தலைமகள் தோழிக்குச் சொல்லியது ஆற்றாள் எனக் கவன்ற தோழி தலைமகட்கு உரைத்ததூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the lover's absence and the charge that he is without love decide separation

occasion.words: வன்பொறை எதிர் அழிந்த தலைமகள் தோழிக்குச் சொல்லியது
ஆற்றாள் எனக் கவன்ற தோழி தலைமகட்கு உரைத்ததூஉம் ஆம்

iraicchi.act: the crows hang on the dripping branch through the rainy night, sustained only by thinking of the feast to come
iraicchi.sense: she too lies awake through the cold night living on the thought of what she longs for, and he who knows it is not with her

tamil: தோடு அமை செறிப்பின் இலங்கு வளை ஞெகிழ
கோடு ஏந்து அல்குல் அவ் வரி வாட
நல் நுதல் சாய படர் மலி அரு நோய்
அகில் சுடு கானவன் உவல் சுடு கமழ் புகை
நாடு கெழு வெற்பனொடு அமைந்த நம் தொடர்பே
reading: With the man listening, the friend says the girl's bangles slip, the lines of her waist fade and her forehead pales with a sickness her lover gave, which the old diviner with his possession-beans will explain without knowing; it would be fine indeed if his words could ease their bond with the man of the hill where the smoke of agil and brush a hunter burns hides the slope like drifting cloud.
nuance: The closing image is apt to the friend's purpose: a fragrant smoke that hides the hillside as cloud does, as their love has been hidden, though its scent now spreads; it has one match, not the two that ullurai needs.

colophon.thurai: சிறைப்புறமாகத் தோழி செறிப்பு அறிவுறீஇ வரைவு கடாயது

thinai_evidence.note: the hunter burning agil on the hill slope and the diviner's rite fix kurinji

comparisons.tenor: the smoke of burnt agil and brush hiding the slope

tamil: ஒள் நுதல் மகளிர் ஓங்கு கழிக் குற்ற
கண் நேர் ஒப்பின கமழ் நறு நெய்தல்
அகல் வரிச் சிறு மனை அணியும் துறைவ
reading: The friend asks the lord of the shore, where bright-browed girls pick fragrant neythal flowers like eyes from the backwater to deck their little striped sand-houses, whether it is right that the girl's long-admired beauty should waste away so, for those who trusted his word, truer than the sun that rises over the sea and is worshipped by many.
nuance: The praise is the reproach: by setting his word above the sun that all trust, the friend makes any delay in marrying a breach of something public.

colophon.thurai: பகற்குறி வந்த தலைமகனைத் தோழி வரைவு கடாயது. கடிநகர் புக்க தோழி பிற்றை ஞான்று வேறுபடாது ஆற்றினாய் என்று சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: backwater, neythal flowers and the shore lord fix neythal

occasion.words: பகற்குறி வந்த தலைமகனைத் தோழி வரைவு கடாயது
கடிநகர் புக்க தோழி பிற்றை ஞான்று வேறுபடாது ஆற்றினாய் என்று சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

comparisons.tenor: the neythal flowers

comparisons.vehicle: பலர் தொழத் தோன்றி ஏமுற விளங்கிய சுடரினும்
comparisons.tenor: the man's word, truer than the sun

tamil: நிறம் பெறும் ஈர் இதழ்ப் பொலிந்த உண்கண்
ஒளிறு ஏந்து மருப்பின் களிறு மாறு பற்றிய
reading: Away on work not yet done, the man says his heart urges him to go to the woman of the dark hanging hair and flower-coloured kohl eyes and end its pain, while his reason, weighing the outcome, says that leaving a task unfinished brings ignorance and disgrace and bids him not hurry at all; caught between them, he asks whether his aching body will perish like an old frayed rope that two tuskers with gleaming tusks have seized at either end.
nuance: The heart and the reason are both given speech (என்னும், twice), so the poem is a debate in which the body is the only loser; the poet's name is taken from the rope.

thinai_evidence.note: the man held away by unfinished work longs to go back: separation

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: he reports the speech of his heart and of his reason to himself

comparisons.vehicle: போதின் நிறம் பெறும் ஈர் இதழ்ப் பொலிந்த உண்கண்
comparisons.tenor: her eyes

comparisons.vehicle: ஒளிறு ஏந்து மருப்பின் களிறு மாறு பற்றிய தேய்புரிப் பழங் கயிறு
comparisons.tenor: his body pulled between heart and reason

tamil: அரவு இரை தேரும் ஆர் இருள் நடு நாள்
வன் கைக் கானவன் வெஞ் சிலை வணக்கி
நடு காற் குரம்பைத் தன் குடிவயிற் பெயரும்
reading: With the man listening, the friend tells the girl that the friendship of the hill lord, where a hunter who has shot a porcupine with his bow goes home to his stilted hut delighted, his house dog romping beside the kill, is good for them indeed: not only does he come in the dead of night when the snake hunts its prey, but, never kept away by the neighbours' talk, he now comes by day to the cleared field as well.
nuance: The praise is ironic: coming by night and by day has made the talk loud, and the friend's real word is that the affair can no longer stay hidden. The hunter carrying his catch home is the act the man has not yet done.

colophon.thurai: தோழி சிறைப்புறமாகத் தலைமகட்குச் சொல்லுவாளாய் தலைமகன் கேட்ப அம்பலும் அலரும் ஆயிற்று என்று சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the hill hunter, the porcupine and the hill lord fix kurinji

iraicchi.act: the hunter brings his kill home to his own hut and household in open delight
iraicchi.sense: the man should likewise take what he has won home openly, instead of coming to her by night and by day

tamil: புனை இழை நெகிழ விம்மி நொந்து நொந்து
reading: The friend tells the grieving girl, who sobs again and again with her jewels slipping, 'he has surely gone over the bare hills where the kumizh flower, like a bright swinging earring in a slit lobe, streaks the rock floor; let my life go', to stop lamenting: if she thinks about it, he went to win the advancement of his friends and to come back so that her shoulders regain their beauty.

thinai_evidence.note: the wasteland kumizh on the bare rock hills and the lover's going fix paalai

comparisons.tenor: the kumizh flower

tamil: பைங் கண் யானை வேந்து புறத்து இறுத்த
பெருந் தகை மறவன் போல கொடுங் கழிப்
reading: The girl, unable to bear the tightened watch, says that since the day the lord of the cold shore of neythal-leaved backwaters came, driven by great love and unafraid of the dread crocodile, like a noble warrior who says 'we hold the good fort' while a king with green-eyed elephants besieges its sky-high wall, her heart has not left him, and whenever in the dead of night she hears a bird's cry she takes it for the clear chime of his chariot bell and forgets sleep while the whole town sleeps.
nuance: The siege simile is grammatically the man's (fearless before the crocodile), but the colophon's watch (காப்பு மிகுதி) lets it fall also on her: a heart besieged by her household that still says 'we hold it'.

thinai_evidence.note: backwater, neythal and the shore lord fix neythal

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no addressee

comparisons.vehicle: பைங் கண் யானை வேந்து புறத்து இறுத்த நல் எயிலுடையோர் உடையம் என்னும் பெருந் தகை மறவன்
comparisons.tenor: the shore lord who fears no crocodile

tamil: ஞாங்கர் இள வெயில் உணீஇய ஓங்கு சினைப்
நல் நுதல் பரந்த பசலை கண்டு அன்னை
செம் முது பெண்டிரொடு நெல் முன் நிறீஇ
ஏனற் செந் தினைப் பால் ஆர் கொழுங் குரற்
reading: With the man listening, the friend tells the girl that, seeing the pallor spread on her forehead since the lord of the hill went away, the hill where a plumed peacock dances with its hen on a high branch of the waterfall-loud, god-haunted peak to take the young sun, their mother has set paddy before the red old women to consult the diviner; and if she asks, will the diviner not say that the girl went to the hill to scare small parrots from the red millet and that great Vel has seized her?
nuance: The diviner's verdict names the true place (the millet field) and the wrong cause (the god), so the friend's fear is also a hint to the listener that the truth is half out.

colophon.thurai: தோழி சிறைப்புறமாகத் தலைமகட்கு உரைப்பாளாய் வெறி அறிவுறீஇ வரைவு கடாயது

thinai_evidence.note: peacock, millet and the hill lord fix kurinji

iraicchi.act: the peacock dances together with its hen on the high branch in the morning sun
iraicchi.sense: the creatures of his own hill keep company with their mates while he has gone away and left her to pale

tamil: கனை பெயல் பொழிந்து கடுங் குரல் பயிற்றி
reading: The woman tells her friend that her lover would not shift from a word he had spoken even if the earth shifted from its place, yet the sky has scooped up the sea, darkened thickly, poured heavy rain and sounded its harsh voice again and again, and has made the rainy season here beside her; meanwhile, like the great log the herdsmen of the scrub set burning at night, she is unpitied and wretched.
nuance: She does not doubt his word; the season he named has simply arrived without him, so the burning log, lit and left by others to burn down alone, carries the whole of her complaint.

thinai_evidence.note: the rains come and herdsmen of the scrub fix mullai

comparisons.vehicle: கொல்லைக் கோவலர் எல்லி மாட்டிய பெரு மர ஒடியல்
comparisons.tenor: the woman, unpitied and wasting

tamil: வயல் வெள் ஆம்பல் சூடு தரு புதுப் பூக்
தொடர்பு நீ வெஃகினை ஆயின் என் சொல்
நெடு நீர்ப் பொய்கை நடு நாள் எய்தி
reading: Aiming her words at the wife through the dancing woman, the courtesan says to her: if you want the friendship of the lord of the town where an old slow-footed bull grazes on the leftovers of the fresh white field lilies that a cow with a new calf has eaten, do not take my word for it, sharp-toothed one: you are a great beauty, but he, they say, is a bee that comes at midnight to the deep pond and sucks the cool fragrant new flowers; they do not call him a man.
nuance: The courtesan's mockery cuts three ways: at the dancing woman as the new favourite, at the wife as the cow whose leftovers he grazes, and at the man as a bee, not a man.

colophon.thurai: பரத்தை விறலிமேல் வைத்துத் தலைமகளை நெருங்கிச் சொல்லியது பரத்தையிற்பிரிய வாயிலாய்ப் புக்க பாணன் கேட்ப தோழி சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: field lilies, the buffalo-bull and the town lord fix marutham

thurai_akam.speaker: parathai

comparisons.tenor: the man

the new young women he takes up

ullurai.speaker_fit: the courtesan, not bound to the heroine's world, may use any thing, and the bull at the field is of her own marutham town (porul 7.29)

tamil: நீர் பெயர்ந்து மாறிய செறி சேற்று அள்ளல்
நெய்த் தலைக் கொழு மீன் அருந்த இனக் குருகு
தண் பெரும் பௌவ நீர்த் துறைவற்கு நீயும்
மா இரு முள்ளூர் மன்னன் மா ஊர்ந்து
பல் ஆன் கிழவரின் அழிந்த இவள் நலனே
reading: The friend, knowing the wife's mind, tells the bard who came as the man's go-between to tell the lord of the cool sea shore exactly what he has seen: where the water has drawn back from the thick mire, a flock of herons that came to eat fat oily-headed fish climbs the heaped white sand and shines like the bright array of kings' armies; and her beauty is ruined like the owners of the many cows the king of great dark Mullur drove off at nightfall, riding his horse.
nuance: The herons that feast where the water has left mirror a man who has taken his pleasure and gone; the closing simile takes the side of the herd-owners, not of the raiding king the puram poets praise.

colophon.thurai: வாயிலாகப் புக்க பாணற்குத் தோழி தலைமகளது குறிப்பு அறிந்து நெருங்கிச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: herons on the sea shore and the shore lord fix neythal

comparisons.tenor: the flock of herons on the white sand

comparisons.vehicle: மா ஊர்ந்து எல்லித் தரீஇய இன நிரைப் பல் ஆன் கிழவரின்
comparisons.tenor: her ruined beauty

ullurai.tenor: the man who took his pleasure of her and went

pairs.scene: நீர் பெயர்ந்து மாறிய செறி சேற்று அள்ளல்

tamil: நெடுந் தண் ஆரத்து அலங்கு சினை வலந்த
பசுங் கேழ் இலைய நறுங் கொடித் தமாலம்
களிறு பொரக் கரைந்த கயவாய்க் குண்டு கரை
ஒளிறு வான் பளிங்கொடு செம் பொன் மின்னும்
கருங் கற் கான்யாற்று அருஞ் சுழி வழங்கும்
reading: The friend tells the man that he does not think of the forest where honey-gatherers pull down and break the fragrant green-leaved tamaala creeper wound round the swaying branch of tall cool sandal, nor heed the crocodile that moves in the hard whirlpools of the black-rock forest stream whose deep bank, broken where elephants fought, glitters with crystal and red gold; if he comes by night in this thick dark dew, she will not live.
nuance: Traditionally the creeper torn from the sandal by honey-takers is the girl harmed by the man's pleasure; the poem gives no second correspondence, so it stays scene.

thinai_evidence.note: forest stream, night visit and dense dew fix kurinji

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no speaker; the friend refuses for the girl

tamil: பலிக் கள் ஆர் கைப் பார் முது குயவன்
reading: The mother, bewildered in her house, wishes that the mother who bore the cruel young man, who won her thick-haired daughter with his words and resolved to take her away, may, whenever she sees the bright-eyed band of girls in the wide common of the ancient town of old renown, where the festival has begun and the old potter in his nochchi garland, toddy of the offering in hand, cries out the offerings, tremble with as great an anguish as hers.
nuance: The curse falls not on the young man but on his mother, the one person whose loss would match her own; the festival crowd of girls is where the absent daughter would have been.

colophon.thurai: தாய் மனை மருண்டு சொல்லியது அவரிடத்தாரைக் கண்டு சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the daughter's going with her lover is the uri of paalai

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: no addressee: she speaks to herself

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: to people of the young man's side

tamil: தொன்று உறை துப்பொடு முரண் மிகச் சினைஇக்
செம் புடைக் கொழு முகை அவிழ்ந்த காந்தள்
reading: The friend, entering the wedding house and seeing the bride's beauty, says it is no illusion: just as the sky bore both fire and wind, so the open chest of the lord of the shining hill, whose slopes are fragrant with kaanthal whose red-sided buds have opened like the tusk of an elephant killed by an old enemy in the bamboo-thick rock clefts, has become both the sickness and the joy.
nuance: The cosmological simile (the sky as the source of both fire and wind) makes the cure and the sickness one origin, now that the marriage has turned the one into the other.

colophon.thurai: மணமனையுள் புக்க தோழி தலைமகளது கவின் கண்டு சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: kaanthal on the hill slope and the hill lord fix kurinji

occasion.words: மணமனையுள் புக்க தோழி தலைமகளது கவின் கண்டு சொல்லியது

comparisons.tenor: the man's chest, the source of her sickness and her joy
the opening red-sided kaanthal bud

tamil: புறன் அழிந்து ஒலிவரும் தாழ் இருங் கூந்தல்
வேறு பல் நாட்டுக் கால் தர வந்த
பல வினை நாவாய் தோன்றும் பெருந் துறை
கலி மடைக் கள்ளின் சாடி அன்ன எம்
reading: The friend, with the man able to hear, says that the girl's long dark hair, spoiled at the back like valli creeper crushed on a broken slope, has set her playmates grieving and her mother knowing, and the mother has laid a hard watch on her; so, at our father's great port where ships of many tasks come wind-driven from many lands, our young beauty, like the toddy jar at a noisy feast, will be left behind the house door while we go on and grow old.
nuance: The toddy jar is set out for a crowd and emptied by others; the friend's image warns that beauty kept indoors under guard is spent with no one to enjoy it.

colophon.thurai: தோழி செறிப்பு அறிவுறீஇ வரைவு கடாயது சிறைப்புறமும் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: ships at the great port fix the shore

comparisons.tenor: her dishevelled hair
their young beauty

tamil: வினை வல் யானைப் புகர் முகத்து அணிந்த
பொன் செய் ஓடைப் புனை நலம் கடுப்ப
புழற் காய்க் கொன்றைக் கோடு அணி கொடி இணர்
ஒழிதும் என்ப நாம் வருந்து படர் உழந்தே
reading: Told by her friend that he is leaving, the woman asks what will become of her: even in the rare season when the parted grieve, when the kondrai's tube-podded hanging clusters bloom grandly on the lone rock like the gold forehead-plate on the spotted face of a king's war elephant, they say her lover will hurry off with a heart set only on his work, and they say she will stay behind, suffering in grief.
nuance: The repeated என்ப (they say) twice keeps the news at second hand, so her question is also a refusal to take it as settled.

thinai_evidence.note: the lover's leaving decides separation, though the flowering is of the rains

comparisons.vehicle: மன்னர் வினை வல் யானைப் புகர் முகத்து அணிந்த பொன் செய் ஓடைப் புனை நலம்
comparisons.tenor: the kondrai clusters in bloom

tamil: பொன் செய் வள்ளத்துப் பால் கிழக்கு இருப்ப
பல் மாண் சேக்கைப் பகை கொள நினைஇ
சிதர் நனை முணைஇய சிதர் கால் வாரணம்
reading: With the man listening, the friend tells the girl that she leaves her milk in its gold bowl, does not stir her red feet, quarrels with her fine bed, wears a joyless look as if joyful, and never asks herself why: the sign showing in her is very plain, and the mother, seeing that the lord of the land where the spotted-legged jungle fowl, sated on fallen buds, sleeps in the ripe pepper vines, came softly and won her heart, will be troubled, and has already held her close without a doubt.
nuance: The friend's list of symptoms is aimed at the hidden listener as much as at the girl; the last lines are hard and can also be read as the mother's suspicion rather than her embrace.

colophon.thurai: தோழி சிறைப்புறமாகத் தலைமகட்கு உரைப்பாளாய் தலைமகன் கேட்பச் சொல்லி யது தோழி தலைமகளை அறத்தொடுநிலை வலிப்பித்ததூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the jungle fowl in the pepper vines of the hill lord's land fix kurinji

tamil: செங் கணை தொடுத்த செயிர் நோக்கு ஆடவர்
மடி வாய்த் தண்ணுமைத் தழங்கு குரல் கேட்ட
பெரும் பல் குன்றம் உள்ளியும் மற்று இவள்
கரும்புடைப் பணைத் தோள் நோக்கியும் ஒரு திறம்
பற்றாய் வாழி எம் நெஞ்சே நல் தார்ப்
reading: Having been urged by the friend to go for wealth and then come back to the woman, the man tells his heart that it holds to neither side: it thinks of the many great hills of the fearful forked wasteland, where fierce-eyed men with red arrows fitted watch for travellers and the male vulture, hearing the slack-mouthed drum, goes back to its flock, and it looks at her bamboo-smooth shoulders painted with sugarcane; can it both embrace the great mountains and keep its gaze on her hair, fragrant with dark flowers like the rare buds of Koodal of Chezhiyan of the golden chariot?
nuance: The man stays: the colophon calls it செலவு அழுங்கியது. The closing lines are hard; the reading of Koodal's flower as the measure of her hair is a guess.

colophon.thurai: தோழியால் பொருள் வலிப்பித்துத் தலைமகளை எய்தி ஆற்றாதாய நெஞ்சினை நெருங் கிச் சொல்லி தலைமகன் செலவு அழுங்கியது

thinai_evidence.note: the robber-held wasteland forks fix paalai

tamil: உரு கெழு யானை உடை கோடு அன்ன
ததர் பிணி அவிழ்ந்த தாழை வான் பூ
தயங்கு இருங் கோடை தூக்கலின் நுண் தாது
வில் எறி பஞ்சி போல மல்கு திரை
reading: With the man listening, the friend says that even if the lovely little village, where the strong west wind shakes the great white thazhai flower, loosened from its tight bonds like the broken tusk of a fearsome elephant, and spreads its fine pollen on the sand-play of the jewelled girls, should grieve, they had known that without him they would be nothing, before ever they laughed with the lord of the shore of the dense sea where full waves rise in spray, struck by wind, like cotton beaten by a bow.
nuance: The syntax of lines 5 to 9 is loose; the friend seems to say the girl went into the affair knowing its cost, which makes the man's delay the only thing left to answer for.

thinai_evidence.note: thazhai flowers and the shore lord fix neythal

comparisons.tenor: the thazhai flower opening
the spray of the waves

tamil: சுடர்த் தொடிக் கோமகள் சினந்தென அதன் எதிர்
சிறு வளை விலை எனப் பெருந் தேர் பண்ணி எம்
இரும் பாண் ஒக்கல் தலைவன் பெரும் புண்
பிச்சை சூழ் பெருங் களிறு போல எம்
reading: The friend tells the lord of the town of the cool ford, where the water lily, swaying under a strong wind, bows to the lotus as the tender attendants bow with joined hands to an angry princess, that a man has decked his great chariot as the price of the girl's little bangles, stood it at our front gate and gone; and you too come with your chariot and will not leave, touching our kitchen's palm-leaf screen like the great begging elephant at Unur of Thazhumban of the great scar, chief of the bards' kin whose soft-fibred strings shine as if dripping ghee.
nuance: The colophon's note says rival strangers have already offered marriage; the friend uses that chariot at the gate to shame the lover, who comes for scraps like a begging elephant instead of asking for her.

colophon.thurai: வாயில் மறுத்தது வரைவு கடாயதூஉம் ஆம் மாற்றோர் நொதுமலாளர் வரைவின் மேலிட்டு மருதத்துக் களவு

thinai_evidence.note: water lily, lotus and the town lord fix marutham

comparisons.vehicle: சுடர்த் தொடிக் கோமகள் சினந்தென அதன் எதிர் மடத் தகை ஆயம் கைதொழுதாஅங்கு
comparisons.tenor: the water lily bowing to the lotus
the lute strings
the lover hanging about the kitchen

title: natrinai 301-320
theme: Natrinai 301 to 320: the end of the millet field and the guarded midnight in kurinji and neythal; the false rain and the lying promise of the man gone for wealth; a man melted from his journey by her silence; and the courtesan's voice, mocking a go-between and a town of anxious wives, and grieving as an old boat laid aside.
source_issues: 310: line 12 (வாயிலாகப் புக்க விறலியைத் தோழி சொல்லியது) is a colophon line run into the verse; the colophon thurai ends 'சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்', the alternative to it. The verse has 11 lines.
316: the colophon thurai has வற்புறுத்தது, a misprint for வற்புறுத்தியது; copied as it stands.
305: line 7 carries a repaired TSCII form (தெள் விளி); 311: line 2 ஃ restored from the old encoding; 317: line 1 -ஒடு vowel sign restored (text flags).

313: line 3 (கண்ணழி கட்டழித்து) is obscure; 310: lines 5 to 8 are hard to construe; 315: lines 1, 4 and 5 are hard to construe; 312: line 4 (காழ் களைந்தருள) is uncertain; 301: line 9 (தேம் மறப்பு அறியா) is uncertain.
302: the colophon thinai is பாலை; the poem is the wife at home reading the season's flowers, and I infer mullai (irutthal), with the road's paalai things marked as mixed.
Natrinai colophons rarely name the addressee; addressees marked as inferred are mine.

tamil: நீள் மலைக் கலித்த பெருங் கோற் குறிஞ்சி
மலர் பிணைத்தன்ன மா இதழ் மழைக் கண்
reading: The friend, to herself, recalls how the mother praises the girl item by item, a body like the fresh kurinji bloom of the long hill, rain-dark eyes like paired flowers of the spring, a peacock's grace, a parrot's speech, a doll's beauty, and sees that the girl the mother never once forgets is the one now kept from her lover.
nuance: The catalogue of beauty is the mother's, not the lover's, and that is the point: the same loving attention that praises every limb is the watch that never lapses, so the friend hears in the praise the reason the man is kept away.

colophon.thurai: சேட்படுத்து பிரிவின்கண் அன்பின் இயற்கையில் தகுவகையதோர் ஆற்றாமையினான் என்று தோழி தன்னுள்ளே சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the kurinji bloom of the long hill and the mountain spring

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the friend speaks to herself; the praise she repeats is the mother's

comparisons.tenor: the girl's body
her large dark eyes
her grace of movement
her speech
her whole beauty

tamil: நீடு சுரி இணர சுடர் வீக் கொன்றைக்
வரு மழைக்கு எதிரிய மணி நிற இரும் புதல்
நரை நிறம் படுத்த நல் இணர்த் தெறுழ் வீ
களிறு உதைத்து ஆடிய கவிழ் கண் இடு நீறு
reading: The woman, seeing the season pass, says that though the forest has flowered with konrai clusters as lovely as jewelled women, surely the man who crossed the far waste, where elephant-kicked dust hides the old sad track among hard-cored velam trees, will notice the therul flowers strewn on the dark bushes that face the coming rain.
nuance: She does not doubt his love but his eyes: the rain's flowers are everywhere at home, and her hope is that somewhere on his road the same sign is falling where he must see it.

thinai_evidence.note: a wife waiting at home as the rains' flowers come, not the parting on the road

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the addressee is inferred

comparisons.tenor: the konrai in bloom

tamil: துணை புணர் அன்றில் உயவுக் குரல் கேட்டொறும்
வன் கைப் பரதவர் இட்ட செங் கோல்
கொடு முடி அவ் வலை பரியப் போக்கி
reading: The woman tells her friend that at deep midnight, when the bustling hamlet has fallen silent, every cry of the anril joined with its mate in the palmyra nest of the common ground keeps her sleepless and wasting, and she asks whether the lord of the shore, where the shark tears the fishermen's nets and roams the deep water, holds in his heart the thought that she suffers for him.
nuance: The paired anril is no comfort but a reproach, a creature that does not part from its mate crying beside her; the shark that tears the net and swims free may hint at a man who slips every bond, but no second correspondence is drawn, so it stays scene.

colophon.thurai: வேட்கை தாங்ககில்லாளாய்த் தோழிக்குத் தலைமகள் சொல்லியது சிறைப்புறத்தான் என்பது மலிந்ததூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: fishermen, the shark and the lord of the shore

tamil: வாரல் மென் தினைப் புலர்வுக் குரல் மாந்தி
வளி எறி வயிரின் கிளி விளி பயிற்றும்
நளி இருஞ் சிலம்பின் நல் மலை நாடன்
மணி மிடை பொன்னின் மாமை சாய என்
தண் கமழ் நறுந் தார் விறலோன் மார்பே
reading: Answering her friend's reassurance, the woman says that the hill lord's cool fragrant-garlanded chest is like the hands of those who kill the asunam, full of pleasure and of pain: when he joins her, her beauty joins her, and when he parts, pallor fades her gem-and-gold complexion and wrecks her looks.
nuance: The asunam is the creature that is lured by music and then killed, so the simile says that his chest gives joy and pain from the same hand, not by turns from different causes; the parrots calling like a wind-blown horn set the scene of the hill.

colophon.thurai: வரையாது நெடுங்காலம் வந்தொழுக ஆற்றாளாகிய தலைமகள் வன்புறை எதிர் மொழிந்தது

thinai_evidence.note: millet, parrots and the hill lord

comparisons.tenor: the parrots' repeated call
her complexion
his chest, which gives both joy and pain

tamil: மயில் அடி அன்ன மாக் குரல் நொச்சியும்
கடியுடை வியல் நகர் காண் வரத் தோன்ற
எரி சினம் தணிந்த இலை இல் அம் சினை
வரிப் புறப் புறவின் புலம்பு கொள் தெள் விளி
விலங்கு மலை ஆர் இடை நலியும்கொல் எனவே
reading: The mother tells the friend that the striped ball, the withered vayalai creeper, the nochchi with clusters like a peacock's foot and the garden her daughter used to see alone have become a burning pain to her; and she wonders whether the girl, hearing a striped dove's lonely call on a leafless branch in the shimmering heat, fears that the hill pass may harm the young man with the white spear.
nuance: The mother's grief turns at line 6 into the daughter's fear: she pictures the girl on the road not afraid for herself but for the man she went with.

colophon.thurai: நற்றாய் தோழிக்குச் சொல்லியது மனை மருட்சியும் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: a leafless branch, the heat and the hard pass

thurai_akam.speaker: nartaay
thurai_akam.note: the mother bewildered in the house, speaking to no one named

comparisons.tenor: the clusters of the nochchi

tamil: குளிர் படு கையள் கொடிச்சி செல்க என
சூற் பொறை இறுத்த கோல் தலை இருவி
விழவு ஒழி வியன் களம் கடுப்பத் தெறுவர
சிறு புனத்து அல்கிய பெரும் புற நிலையே
reading: Within hearing of the man, the friend says the millet the father sowed is being reaped, the hunters sending the cold-handed hill girl home with kind words, and the stubble stands like a festival ground after the feast; how will he come, day after day, to see the sad bare field where the sweet-voiced girl once stayed?
nuance: The friend says nothing of marriage; the empty field does the work, since its emptiness means she is now kept at home and he can meet her only by asking for her.

colophon.thurai: புனம் மடிவு உரைத்துச் செறிப்பு அறிவுறீஇயது சிறைப்புறமும் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the millet field, the hunters and the hill girl

comparisons.tenor: the reaped millet field

tamil: கவர் பரி நெடுந் தேர் மணியும் இசைக்கும்
கடல் ஆடு வியல் இடைப் பேர் அணிப் பொலிந்த
பூ விரி கானல் புணர் குறி வந்து நம்
அல்லல் அரும் படர் காண்கம் நாம் சிறிதே
reading: The friend tells the woman, anxious that the tryst is delayed, that the lord of the long sands is coming, his chariot bells ringing and his young men calling; let them hide behind the dark trunk of the drum-rooted punnai and, when he comes at midnight to the flowered grove, watch a little of the pain he suffers at not finding them.
nuance: The comfort is a game: by turning the waiting round, so that he is the one who searches and grieves, the friend gives the woman back the upper hand the delay had taken from her.

colophon.thurai: குறி நீட ஆற்றாளாகிய தலைமகளைத் தோழி வற்புறுத்தியது

thinai_evidence.note: the punnai of the shore grove and the lord of the sands

occasion.words: குறி நீட ஆற்றாளாகிய தலைமகளைத் தோழி வற்புறுத்தியது

comparisons.tenor: the punnai's swollen trunk

tamil: மலர் ஏர் உண்கண் பனி வர ஆயிழை
வெறி கமழ் துறு முடி தயங்க நல் வினைப்
பொறி அழி பாவையின் கலங்கி நெடிது நினைந்து
ஈர் மண் செய்கை நீர் படு பசுங் கலம்
reading: The man, urged by his heart to go for wealth, tells it that when she noticed the bustle of departure she came slowly, tears in her flower-like eyes, unable to ask or to stop him, troubled like a doll whose mechanism has broken, and pressed herself to his chest; and at that his wealth-filled heart melted into hers like a fresh pot of wet clay set out in the heavy rain, and he will not go.
nuance: She wins without a word: the poem stresses that she could neither question nor hold him, and the silence is what undoes his resolve; the unfired pot in the rain says his purpose dissolved, not that it was overruled.

colophon.thurai: நெஞ்சினால் பொருள் வலிக்கப்பட்ட தலைமகன் தலைமகளை எய்தி ஆற்றானாய் நெஞ்சினைச் சொல்லிச் செலவு அழுங்கியது

thinai_evidence.note: a parting for wealth, here given up

occasion.words: நெஞ்சினால் பொருள் வலிக்கப்பட்ட தலைமகன் தலைமகளை எய்தி ஆற்றானாய் நெஞ்சினைச் சொல்லிச் செலவு அழுங்கியது

comparisons.tenor: her eyes
her troubled, faltering movement

comparisons.vehicle: ஈர் மண் செய்கை நீர் படு பசுங் கலம் பெரு மழைப் பெயற்கு ஏற்றாங்கு
comparisons.tenor: his wealth-filled heart melting into hers

tamil: தளிர் வனப்பு இழந்த என் நிறனும் நோக்கி
யான் செய்தன்று இவள் துயர் என அன்பின்
கொழு மடல் அகல் இலைத் தளி தலைக் கலாவும்
reading: The woman consoles her friend, who sees her slack arms, faded lines and lost leaf-bright colour and grieves that she caused it: do not sink in grief; you may say that no one knows the hill lord's friendship has become our trouble, but I trust his friendship.
nuance: The roles are reversed from the usual: the friend has broken down and the heroine does the comforting, and her comfort is a single act of trust set against all the visible evidence of her own wasting.

colophon.thurai: வரைவு நீட ஆற்றாள் எனக் கவன்று தான் ஆற்றாளாகிய தோழியைத் தலைமகள் ஆற்றுவித்தது

nuance: Lines 5 to 8 are hard to construe (who has agreed to give a daughter, and who are the mothers with failing speech), so the exact charge is uncertain; the leaping fish that scatters the bathing women may glance at the man's disorder in the households, but only one correspondence can be drawn, so it stays scene.

reading: Consoling the woman who suffers from gossip, the friend praises their old town, rich with paddy when it rains and with white salt from the backwater pans when it is dry, and its ford sweet with the smoke of roasting fish and njazhal flowers; its grove has one fault only, that the bees drunk on punnai pollen hum so loudly that his chariot's sweet sound is hard to hear.
nuance: The friend never names the gossip; she moves the blame onto the grove, where the drunken bees' din drowns his chariot, and the hearer is left to match the bees with the talking town.

tamil: பனிப் புதல் ஈங்கை அம் குழை வருட
reading: The man, set on wealth, tells his heart that he grieves and it grieves too: in the misty cold when the rains have stopped, when the shivering white heron sits with folded wings and even the decoy hunter takes up his stakes in pity, she who shivers in the summer months even with him beside her, what will become of her in the north wind's great cold?
nuance: The reason to go is never stated, only the reason not to; the hunter who lays off in pity of a cold bird is the one figure in the scene who does what the man is being asked to do.

tamil: கருங் கால் வேங்கை நாள் உறு புதுப் பூ

reading: With the man listening, the friend asks the woman what will become of them, now that he who, longing to see her, dressed her thick hair with fresh vengai blossom like a goldsmith's work must find the koothalam grove on the kaanthal slope deserted; for the millet they guard with shouts, its leaves dried, has reached the time for reaping, and they will go back to town.
nuance: The vengai flowers he set in her hair are the memory of the kalavu, and the reaping is its end; the friend speaks as one who fears the separation, so that the listening man hears the date of it.

tamil: வாழ் நாள் வகை அளவு அறிஞரும் இல்லை

கருங் கண் வெம் முலை ஞெமுங்கப் புல்லிக்
reading: The wasting woman says that the old never get back their lost youth and no one knows the measure of a life, yet the men who held her close, saying 'let the night pass so', lied by the strength of their words and went, may they live, into the long hot track where a dull lonely dove climbs the swaying kalli, whose pods crack like snapping fingers, and calls to its fallen mate.
nuance: The opening maxim is her argument against his journey: youth does not return and life's length is unknown, so the time he spends earning is spent out of the only time love has; her blessing on the liars is bitter.

nuance: Calling the cloud foolish declares the rain false: it has come before its time, so his promise is not yet broken; the comfort works by blaming the season rather than the man.

nuance: The friend tells only what the elephants did and leaves him to match it: he is the tusker who turns off by another path, and the cow's cry echoing in the rocks is what his leaving will bring.

reading: The man, kept away by the close watch, says to himself that the tide has stopped roaring and the wind is still over the pollen-strewn grove, the male owl and its mate hoot fearfully from the crossroads of the sandy old town, and at midnight, when spirits walk in the thick dark and even the fish's eyes sleep, he lies awake longing to embrace the girl of doll-like beauty; what will become of him?
nuance: Everything in the night is stilled or asleep, even the fish that never closes its eyes, so his wakefulness is set against the whole world; the owl pair and the walking spirits make the hour that a meeting would need, and that the watch denies him.

reading: The courtesan, within hearing of those on her side, says the festival is over and the drum is hung up, and if you ask what she meant: for no more than a young girl in a leaf skirt walking down the street, the town broke into uproar like the land of his enemies when Kaari entered the great street where old Ori was killed, and the fair-bangled wives shut the watch tight and grew anxious, guarding their husbands.
nuance: She mocks the wives by measuring their panic against a town sacked in war: one girl walking past is enough to make the household behave like a captured city.

title: natrinai 321-340
theme: Natrinai 321 to 340: night meetings arranged by landmarks and dreaded for the tiger, bear and lightning on the hill path; velan rites mocked and mothers who begin to see; a wife's chest claimed as inheritance and a lover's hair weighed against wealth; the heron and the monkeys that keep their mates while men stay away; and Vaanan's Sirukudi made the measure of what an unfaithful husband has taken.
source_issues: 332: the colophon thurai runs two words together (வற்புறுப்பதலைவி for வற்புறுப்பத் தலைவி); copied as printed.
334: the colophon gives no poet.
324: the colophon thinai is குறிஞ்சி, but the poem is an elopement through elephant forest with pity for the mother left behind; inferred paalai.
336, 339: the colophon names no speaker; the friend is assumed.
340: the colophon's பரத்தையிற் மறுத்தந்த looks corrupt (perhaps for பரத்தையின் மறுத்து வந்த); copied as printed.
322: how lines 1 and 2 (ஆங்கனம் தணிகுவதுஆயின்) relate to the velan's rite is unclear.
323: lines 3 to 5 are hard to construe, and புலி வரிபு (line 7) is obscure.
328: line 4 பிறப்பு ஓரன்மை is hard to construe.

tamil: செந் நிலப் புறவின் புன் மயிர்ப் புருவை
பாடு இன் தெள் மணித் தோடு தலைப்பெயர
கல் சுடர் சேரும் கதிர் மாய் மாலை
reading: His task done, the man tells his charioteer that at this evening, when the short-fleeced sheep of the red grassland turn home to the clear sweet sound of their bells, brahmin women wear the wide-mouthed wild jasmine at the edge of the slope and the sun's rays sink into the rock, his finely-jewelled wife may be grieving quietly as she looks at the dull empty house; so drive fast, for as the low kurundhu-flowered hillocks go by, the trees of the old noisy town come into view.
nuance: The flock going home with its bells is the evening's picture of return, and it makes the house he imagines, empty and dull, the sharper: he reads his own lateness in the scene before he names her grief, and the urging of the chariot follows from it.

thinai_evidence.note: grassland, wild jasmine and kurundhu at evening, with a wife waiting at home

thurai_akam.speaker: pira
thurai_akam.note: the man, his task done, speaks to his charioteer (தேர்ப்பாகன்)

tamil: எறிந்து செறித்தன்ன பிணங்கு அரில் விடர் முகை
ஊன் தின் பிணவின் உயங்கு பசி களைஇயர்
ஆள் இயங்கு அரும் புழை ஒற்றி வாள் வரிக்
கடுங் கண் வயப் புலி ஒடுங்கும் நாடன்
தண் கமழ் வியல் மார்பு உரிதினின் பெறாது
நல் நுதல் பசந்த படர் மலி அரு நோய்
reading: The speaker asks her friend, so the man nearby may hear, whether it is true that if the sickness were eased that way nothing anywhere would be crueller: for the grievous longing that paled the girl's fine brow, because she cannot rightly have the cool fragrant chest of the man of the land where a fierce sword-striped tiger crouches at the narrow track men use to ease the hunger of its flesh-eating mate in a thicket-choked cleft, the velan has declared to be a spirit's work, singing to sweet instruments and scattering many flowers as an offering of praise.
nuance: The friend's scorn falls on the velan's diagnosis: the cause is a man's chest, and a rite to a spirit cannot reach it. The tiger that waits at the men's track to feed its mate keeps the danger of the night path in view; read as the man who should provide for his mate it is a near miss for iraicchi, since the act carries no single sense the closing lines confirm. How lines 1 and 2 bear on the rest is not certain.

tamil: ஆய நட்பின் மாண் நலம் ஒழிந்து நின்
வண்டு இமிர் இன் இசை கறங்க திண் தேர்த்
reading: Agreeing to a night meeting, the friend tells the man that the tall sweet-toddy palm stands in the very middle of the small shore hamlet of the father of the bangled girl who, unknown to her companions and to the friend, set aside their fine friendship and took kinship with him; there, where bees humming with honeybees over the heavy pollen the punnai sheds on the tiger-striped dune make sweet music, the bells of his strong chariot will hardly be heard: this is the way to come, and he must not forget it.
nuance: The friend gives a route by landmarks, and her real point is practical: the hum of the punnai grove will cover the chariot bells, so he can come unheard. Lines 3 to 5 (the companions and I not knowing, the friendship set aside) are hard to construe and the sense of புலி வரிபு is not certain.
