tamil: பொன் போல் மேனித் தன் மகள் நயந்தோள்
reading: Alas, pitiable is the mother: crushed by grief, what will become of her who loved her gold-bodied daughter, now that this girl of lovely sparse locks, who in her rich father's wide house of oil-sheened strong spears ran about as if chasing a ball at play, walks on her soft cotton-like feet through a forest full of full-tusked elephants?
nuance: The pity goes not to the girl, who still runs as at play, but to the mother at home, so the elopement is weighed by what it costs the house left behind. The colophon's thinai is குறிஞ்சி, but nothing of the poem's situation belongs to the hill tryst.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகன் பாங்கற்குச் சொல்லியது இடைச் சுரத்துக் கண்டோர் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the girl has gone with her lover through elephant forest and the speaker grieves for the mother left behind

thurai_akam.speaker: kandor
thurai_akam.note: onlookers on the wasteland road, speaking among themselves

comparisons.tenor: the daughter's body
the sheen of the father's strong-shafted spear
the girl running on
the softness of her feet

tamil: நீடு செயல் சிதலைத் தோடு புனைந்து எடுத்த
முர வாய் வள் உகிர் இடப்ப வாங்கும்
ஊக்கு அருங் கவலை நீந்தி மற்று இவள்
reading: The friend asks the man whether it is fitting for him to cross the hard forked paths where a bent-headed thick-haired male bear, eager for food, goes out at night and with rough mouth and strong claws tears open the snake-haunted termite mound that long-working termites built up in layers, even after seeing tears swell from her flower-like kohl eyes and spoil their fresh beauty; lord, give up your going.
nuance: The bear wrecks in a moment what the termites built over a long time, which is what the friend says his going will do to the girl's new beauty; she never draws the match herself.

thinai_evidence.note: the friend begs the man not to set out across the forked paths of the wasteland

comparisons.tenor: her kohl-lined eyes

ullurai.tenor: the man going after wealth and the fresh beauty his going will ruin

pairs.situation: he leaves driven by desire for gain

pairs.scene: நீடு செயல் சிதலைத் தோடு புனைந்து எடுத்த
pairs.situation: the slowly built mound is her fresh beauty, which his going will undo
the ruin is done at one stroke, as her tears spoil her eyes

ullurai.speaker_fit: the friend uses a bear met on the forked paths the man must cross, a thing of the poem's own road (porul 7.27)

tamil: கொழுஞ் சுளைப் பலவின் பயம் கெழு கவாஅன்
செழுங் கோள் வாங்கிய மாச் சினைக் கொக்கினம்
நுண் கொடிப் பீரத்து ஊழ் உறு பூ எனப்
அரி அமர் வனப்பின் எம் கானம் நண்ண
மலர் என மரீஇ வரூஉம் இவள் கண்ணே
reading: Pressing the man to marry, the friend tells the lord of the land where, on the fruitful jackfruit slope, a fluff-headed female monkey sneezes, unable to bear the smell of the fish the heron flock bring onto the dark fruit-laden branch, that she is ashamed to say it even to him: for many days pallor has spread over the girl like the ripe flower of the fine-stemmed peerkku, alas, while even the bees, knowing no better, take her eyes for flowers and come to them when she enters their lovely forest.
nuance: The pallor and the eyes the bees mistake for flowers are set side by side: her beauty is fading and still draws the bees, so the time to marry her is now. The herons' fish smell on the jackfruit slope, which the monkey cannot bear, may suggest gossip reaching the hill, but no second correspondence is anchored in the poem, so it stays scene (a near miss for ullurai).

thinai_evidence.note: a jackfruit slope with monkeys, and the forest where the girl roams

comparisons.vehicle: நுண் கொடிப் பீரத்து ஊழ் உறு பூ
comparisons.tenor: the pallor spreading over the girl
her eyes, which the bees take for flowers

tamil: கடன் நிலை குன்றலும் இலர் என்று உடன் அமர்ந்து
reading: Answering her friend's reassurance, the girl says that if trusting the sought-after noble ones is a fault, then wasting away with eyes that weep without rest, and even dying, is sweet, dear friend; and if it is not so, since the noble never fall short of what they owe, it is right that the soft chest of the lord of the cool shore, where punnai with opening buds stands over the grove, should become her settled inheritance, which the world gathered together will acknowledge.
nuance: She puts it as all or nothing: either her trust was a fault and death is sweet, or he is truly one of the noble and his chest is her lawful portion. The word தாயம், inheritance, gives the marriage she wants the standing of a property claim acknowledged in public.

colophon.thurai: வரையாது நெடுங்காலம் வந்தொழுக ஆற்றாளாய தலைமகள் வன்புறை எதிர் அழிந்தது

thinai_evidence.note: punnai over the shore grove of the lord of the cool shore

tamil: கிழங்கு கீழ் வீழ்ந்து தேன் மேல் தூங்கி
தினை கிளி கடியும் பெருங் கல் நாடன்
அது இனி வாழி தோழி ஒரு நாள்
சிறு பல் கருவித்து ஆகி வலன் ஏர்பு
எண் பிழி நெய்யொடு வெண் கிழி வேண்டாது
கலம் பெறு விறலி ஆடும் இவ் ஊரே
reading: Comforting the girl in the wait before marriage, the friend says they have come to know that the lord of the great hill land, where tubers go down and honey hangs above and a little sown yields much as people drive parrots from the millet, is not of a birth apart from theirs; so may the clouds one day gather and rise to the right and pour great rain and flood; and now, in this town on the high sandal-covered slope among cross-lying ranges, the virali who receives ornaments dances, asking for no sesame oil or white cloth.
nuance: The hill where little sown yields much reads as a promise for the union, and the dancing virali points to the wedding festival the friend says is near; but the sense of பிறப்பு ஓரன்மை (line 4) and why she wishes for the flood are hard to fix.

thinai_evidence.note: millet guarded from parrots on the great hill slope

tamil: கொன்று ஆற்றுத் துறந்த மாக்களின் அடு பிணன்
இடு முடை மருங்கில் தொடும் இடம் பெறாஅது
புனிற்று நிரை கதித்த பொறிய முது பாறு
இறகு புடைத்து இற்ற பறைப் புன் தூவி
ஆடு கொள் நெஞ்சமோடு அதர் பார்த்து அல்கும்
reading: The friend comforts the wasting wife: though he has crossed the wasteland where greedy men who care nothing for hell kill travellers and leave them, where an old spotted vulture, finding no room by the reeking corpses, flaps out the broken down of its wings, and hard-eyed men whose red arrows are fletched with it lie watching the track with their hearts set on plunder, he will not stay away forsaking her; look there, the dark clouds have drawn up the sea and flash, shaking the vast sky.
nuance: The friend sets the road's horrors and the season's sign side by side, so that the rain clouds, the time he named for his return, answer the fear the road raises.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவிடை மெலிந்த தலைமகளைத் தோழி பருவம் காட்டி வற்புறுத்தது

thinai_evidence.note: a wasteland road watched by robbers

tamil: தட மருப்பு எருமைப் பிணர்ச் சுவல் இரும் போத்து
மட நடை நாரைப் பல் இனம் இரிய
நெடு நீர்த் தண் கயம் துடுமெனப் பாய்ந்து
நாட் தொழில் வருத்தம் வீட சேண் சினை
இருள் புனை மருதின் இன் நிழல் வதியும்
யாணர் ஊர நின் மாண் இழை மகளிரை
எம் மனைத் தந்து நீ தழீஇயினும் அவர்தம்
reading: Refusing the man entry, the friend tells the lord of the rich town, where a wide-horned rough-necked dark male buffalo plunges with a splash into the deep cool pond, scattering the many flocks of soft-stepping herons, and rests from the day's labour in the sweet shade of the marutham tree whose far branches are clothed in darkness, that even if he brings his finely-jewelled women into their house and embraces them, truth in their mean hearts is rare, and rarer still that they should bear sons as the green-bangled wives do and stand on the household's side in good and grateful chastity.
nuance: The friend grants the worst, that he brings the other women home, and argues past it: what she denies them is the household's virtues, truth, children and karpu, so the refusal is a judgement on them more than a plea to him.

thinai_evidence.note: buffalo, pond and marutham tree of a rich town

ullurai.tenor: the man, his other women and the household he disturbs

pairs.scene: நெடு நீர்த் தண் கயம் துடுமெனப் பாய்ந்து
pairs.situation: he plunges into the company of other women
the household is scattered by his doings

pairs.scene: இருள் புனை மருதின் இன் நிழல் வதியும்
pairs.situation: after his pleasure he would rest at ease in the wife's house

ullurai.speaker_fit: the friend uses the buffalo of the marutham pond in a marutham poem (porul 7.27)

tamil: புலவு மீன் உணங்கல் படு புள் ஓப்பி
மட நோக்கு ஆயமொடு உடன் ஊர்பு ஏறி
எந்தை திமில் இது நுந்தை திமில் என
திண் திமில் எண்ணும் தண் கடற் சேர்ப்ப
இனிதேதெய்ய எம் முனிவு இல் நல் ஊர்
reading: Agreeing to a night meeting, the friend tells the lord of the cool sea, where salt-makers who never plough keep guarded heaps of brine-grown salt in the grove for the coming of the salt carters, and girls scaring birds from the drying fish climb up with their soft-eyed companions and count the strong boats of the kinsmen gone fishing, 'that is my father's boat, that is yours', that their faultless good town is sweet: if he comes now there is no wrong in it, for how would anyone come to know, when the town has streets where kin do not know kin?
nuance: The girls naming each boat by its owner show a town where everyone is known by family; the friend's last line turns it round, saying the town is so crowded that kin do not know kin, so a night visitor will pass unknown.

thinai_evidence.note: salt pans, salt carters and fishing boats of the sea shore

tamil: தொல் நிலை வழீஇய நின் தொடி எனப் பல் மாண்
ஈன் பிணவு ஒடுக்கிய இருங் கேழ் வயப் புலி
இரை நசைஇப் பரிக்கும் மலைமுதல் சிறு நெறி
reading: To her friend, who keeps telling her in many ways that her bangles have slipped from their old place, the girl says to stop and asks what this can be called: like people who gather water-lilies and still thirst for water, her shoulders waste though he embraces her day after day; and how can her shining bangles stay tight when she sees him come through thick darkness night after night, no longer heeding as on the first day, by the small path at the mountain foot where a dark strong tiger that has sheltered its newly delivered mate in a rock cleft prowls for prey?
nuance: The wasting is not from his absence but from fear for him: she has him every day and still pines, because every meeting means the tiger's path at night. பேணலன் may mean that he no longer heeds the danger or that he cares for her less than on the first day; the reading takes the first.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவிடை மெலிந்த தலைமகளைத் தோழி களவுக் காலத்து வற்புறுப்பதலைவி கூறியது வன்புறை எதிர்மறுத்ததூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: a tiger in the hill cleft on the night path he takes

comparisons.tenor: her longing that grows though he embraces her daily

tamil: மழை தொழில் உலந்து மா விசும்பு உகந்தென
கழை கவின் அழிந்த கல் அதர்ச் சிறு நெறிப்
பரல் அவல் ஊறல் சிறு நீர் மருங்கின்
பூ நுதல் யானையொடு புலி பொருது உண்ணும்
சுரன் இறந்து அரிய என்னார் உரன் அழிந்து
அரும் பொருட்கு அகன்ற காதலர் முயக்கு எதிர்ந்து
உயர் புகழ் நல் இல் ஒண் சுவர்ப் பொருந்தி
reading: The friend tells the grieving wife to let her sorrow go: her lover, who went far for rare wealth wanting the means to give, and who does not call hard the wasteland where, after the clouds have ended their work and the bamboo has lost its beauty along the stony path, a tiger fights the spot-browed elephant to drink at the little seep in a pebbled hollow, now seems, his resolve worn down and his heart full, ready to come back to her embrace and have her fine-jewelled bamboo shoulders; for the lizard of pleasing voice, clinging to the bright wall of their high famous house, chirps at deep midnight each time she thinks of him.
nuance: The comfort rests on a household omen, not on news: the lizard answering each of her thoughts is taken to show that the absent man is turning home. The motive the friend gives him is வண்மை, wealth sought so that he can give.

colophon.thurai: பொருள்வயிற் பிரிவின்கண் ஆற்றாளாகிய தலைமகளைத் தோழி வற்புறுத்தது

thinai_evidence.note: a wasteland the rains have left, crossed for wealth

comparisons.tenor: her shoulders

tamil: கரு விரல் மந்திச் செம் முகப் பெருங் கிளை
வெற்பு அணி நறு வீ கற்சுனை உறைப்ப
மாரி நின்ற ஆர் இருள் நடு நாள்
என்னோ தோழி நம் இன் உயிர் நிலையே
reading: The friend asks the girl what would become of their dear life if the lord of the hill land, where a big red-faced troop of black-fingered female monkeys bathe in the falls of the high range, swing on tall bamboo and frolic with their male while the fragrant vengai blossoms that adorn the hill drop into the rock pool, should come at midnight in the dense dark of lingering rain, bearing a single spear along the slope of falls by the light of the splitting lightning.
nuance: The colophon says the friend opens the matter of a night meeting; she does it by voicing her fear of it, so that the girl's consent and the man's danger are raised in one breath.

thinai_evidence.note: monkeys, vengai and falls of the hill, and the night meeting

iraicchi.act: the troop of female monkeys bathes in the falls, swings on the bamboo and frolics together with their male by day
iraicchi.sense: the lovers of this hill should have their joy together openly, as the monkeys do, not by a lone night journey through rain and lightning

tamil: திங்களும் திகழ் வான் ஏர்தரும் இமிழ் நீர்ப்
ஒலி சிறந்து ஓதமும் பெயரும் மலி புனற்
பல் பூங் கானல் முள் இலைத் தாழை
சோறு சொரி குடையின் கூம்பு முகை அவிழ
வளி பரந்து ஊட்டும் விளிவு இல் நாற்றமொடு
விரல் கவர்ந்து உழந்த கவர்வின் நல் யாழ்
reading: Overcome by longing, the girl says the moon rises in the shining sky, the surging waves of the roaring sea never stop their sound, the tide comes loud and goes, the wind spreads the unending fragrance of the thorn-leaved thaazhai in the flowered grove as its closed bud opens like an umbrella spilling rice, the anril on the dark palm calls in distress so that it pierces to the bone, and besides, a good lute plucked by grasping fingers keeps on so that the night cannot be survived: love is great, and there is no one to clear it away.
nuance: Every sound and scent of the shore night presses on her at once, and she names no man: the poem is the night itself closing in, ending in the bare statement that love is great.

colophon.thurai: காமம் மிக்க கழிபடர்கிளவி மிதூர்ந்து தலைமகள் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: sea, thaazhai, palmyra and anril of the shore at night

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: she speaks to no one named, to the night itself

comparisons.tenor: the opening thaazhai bud

tamil: கல் அதர் அரும் புழை அல்கி கானவன்
குடி முறை பகுக்கும் நெடு மலை நாட
உரவுச் சின வேழம் உறு புலி பார்க்கும்
ஈர் அளைப் புற்றம் கார் என முற்றி
reading: Fearing the path, the speaker tells the lord of the tall mountain, where a hunter lying in wait at the hard narrow stony pass brings down with his bow the white-tusked boar that raided the thick-stalked millet with its slack-teated sow, and his wife of dressed dark hair cuts it up and shares it among the households in turn: you do not fear the night when the fierce elephant watches for the tiger, but I do; do not come by the small path at the mountain foot where a pack of bears hunting food dig into the snake's wet-holed mound.
nuance: The opening is a raid ending in a fair share: the boar that took the millet is killed and divided by custom. A reader may see the secret lover and the town's sharing of talk in it, but the poem anchors no such match, so it is left as scene (a near miss for ullurai).

thinai_evidence.note: boar, millet, hunter and elephant of the hill

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no speaker; the friend is assumed

tamil: பராரைப் பாதிரிக் குறு மயிர் மா மலர்
அணி நிறம் கொண்ட மணி மருள் ஐம் பால்
reading: Seeing that the man means to leave for wealth, the friend asks whether the great ones forgot, when the world was made: those who have made wealth have the custom of living apart, not taking the rare great gift of gently burrowing into her long fragrant five-plaited hair, coloured like sapphire, where the scents of early-summer athiral, the soft-haired dark flowers of thick-based paathiri and fragrant morodam gather as from an opened casket.
nuance: The complaint aims past the man at the order of the world: she blames whoever fixed custom for a rule under which wealth is bought with the very pleasure it should serve.

colophon.thurai: தோழி தலைமகன் பொருள்வயிற் பிரிதலுற்றானது குறிப்பறிந்து விலக்கியது தோழி உலகியல் கூறிப் பிரிவு உணர்த்தியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the man means to leave for wealth in early summer

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the poem's vocative தலைவ fits the first alternative better

comparisons.tenor: the gathered fragrance of her hair
the dark colour of her plaited hair

tamil: அடும்பு கொடி துமிய ஆழி போழ்ந்து அவர்
நெடுந் தேர் இன் ஒலி இரவும் தோன்றா
வியல் இரும் பரப்பின் இரை எழுந்து அருந்துபு
ஆடு அரைப் பெண்ணைத் தோடு மடல் ஏறி
reading: Answering her friend, who says she must hold firm against the grief that torments her, the wife asks how she can, when the harsh-rayed sun has gone behind the hill, the sweet sound of his tall chariot whose wheel cuts the adumbu creepers is not heard even by night, and, as dusk blurs everything, the pitiable heron that rose to feed on the wide dark sea flies as if its life would leave it to reach its curved-beaked mate's nest on the frond of the swaying palm in the commons of the fish-smelling hamlet, never ceasing to call its partner.
nuance: The heron's homecoming is the reproach she cannot say outright: the bird keeps calling to its mate as it hurries back, and the chariot that should come at the same hour is silent.

colophon.thurai: ஒருவழித் தணந்த காலை ஆற்றாத தலைமகள் வன்புறை எதிர்மொழிந்தது

thinai_evidence.note: adumbu creeper, palmyra and heron of a fishing hamlet at sunset

iraicchi.act: having fed on the wide sea, the heron flies as if its life would leave it to reach its mate's nest on the palm frond, never ceasing to call its partner
iraicchi.sense: even the heron hurries home at nightfall to the mate it calls, while her man, gone only a short way, does not come

tamil: சீர் கெழு வியல் நகர் வருவனள் முயங்கி
நீர் அலைக் கலைஇய ஈர் இதழ்த் தொடையல்
ஒள் நுதல் பெதும்பை நல் நலம் பெறீஇ
பல் மலர் கஞலிய வெறி கமழ் வேலித்
reading: So that the man standing by may hear, the friend tells the girl that their mother seems to know the flood of distress the two of them swim, saying strange things with unsettled hearts and fearing 'will this not turn to gossip?' now that the unfailing lover has left them and shows no grace: the mother came into the fine great house, embraced her and said, 'tomorrow, so that this lightning-haired, bright-browed young girl in her wet petalled garland may get back her good looks, let her bathe in the clear gem-water spring in the fragrant hedged place crowded with flowers; what is this way of girls?'
nuance: The mother's plan of a bath to restore the girl's looks shows she has seen the change; whether she suspects love or illness is left open, and the friend reports it within the man's hearing so he knows time is short. Who embraces whom in line 6, and the tone of the mother's last question, are not certain.

thinai_evidence.note: secret love near to exposure, with the mother's suspicion, and a hill spring

thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no speaker; the poem's 'we two' points to the friend

tamil: படை மாண் பெருங் குள மடை நீர் விட்டென
கால் அணைந்து எதிரிய கணைக் கோட்டு வாளை
பகடு சேறு உதைத்த புள்ளி வெண் புறத்து
செஞ் சால் உழவர் கோல் புடை மதரி
கோள் நேர் எல் வளை நெகிழ்த்த நும்மே
reading: The wife tells the man, back from other women, that she will not embrace him nor even sulk: he loosened her bright well-fitting bangles, precious as Vaanan's Sirukudi, where, when Chezhiyan of the unschooled elephants and swift chariots lets out the sluice water of his great tank, the vaalai fish with arrow-like spines meets the inflow, runs into the mud fields and, bold, flips at the base of the ridges of the green-stalked fields, struck by the ploughmen's sticks on its spotted white back where the bullocks kicked up mud.
nuance: Refusing both embrace and sulking is the coldest answer akam allows, since sulking would still be a lovers' game. The whole fertile town is spent on the bangles he has loosened, so what he has taken from her is measured by a king's wealth.

title: natrinai 341-360
theme: Natrinai 341 to 360: a war-camp soldier and a road-weary traveller who picture the women they left, wives who refuse the husband back from courtesans, friends who use proverb, gossip and the mother's misreading to push the man to marry, a woman who prays to the oath-god for the lover who broke his word, and a sleepless woman who asks whether the whole rejoicing world is fighting her; with Kolli of Porayan, Iruppai of Viraan and Marungai of Valuthi as measures of beauty.
source_issues: 345: the colophon thurai reads தௌ¢விடை, a TSCII leftover for தெளிவிடை; copied as printed.
345 line 10, 358 line 4: the TSCII leftover ௌ for ெளி repaired (text flag); 343 line 7, 348 lines 3 and 6: the lost -ஒடு vowel sign restored (text flag); 359 line 4: · read as ஃ (text flag).
355: the colophon names no poet.
343: the colophon thinai is பாலை, but the poem has only mullai things (mullai, cows, the village, evening) and its situation is the woman's waiting; I infer mullai.

358: the colophon's first reading runs together the friend's fear (இவளை இழந்தேன் எனக் கவன்றாள்) and the reassurance (வற்புறுத்தது) without naming who reassures; I take the woman as speaker, as in the second reading. The colophon also prints ஆற்றா ளாயினாள் with a stray space.
354: the colophon begins தோழியால், which reads as a misprint for தோழி.
Natrinai colophons give speaker, addressee and occasion in prose; thurai_akam follows them, and where they name no addressee (341, 345, 348, 359) the code is inferred with a note.

tamil: வங்கா வரிப் பறைச் சிறு பாடு முணையின்
செம் பொறி அரக்கின் வட்டு நா வடிக்கும்
விளையாடு இன் நகை அழுங்கா பால் மடுத்து
வெம் பகை அரு முனைத் தண் பெயல் பொழிந்தென
நீர் இரங்கு அரை நாள் மயங்கி கூதிரொடு
reading: Alone in the war camp on a hostile frontier, where cool rain has poured, water drips through half the night and the north wind of a strange land buffets him in the cold season, the man pictures the girl at home well companioned: tired of the vangaa bird's small song she plays with a red-spotted lac piece, drinks her milk without losing her laughter, waves a harmless twig and trades little riddles with the hill man and her kin, while he is without companion, alone, in the camp.
nuance: The poem turns on the double துணை: she has companions in plenty (துணை நன்கு உடையள்), he has none (துணை இலேம்). Rather than imagine her pining, he envies her company, which makes his own loneliness the subject. Lines 1 to 4 describe her games in rare words (வட்டு நா வடிக்கும், அலையா உலவை), and their exact sense is not sure.

thinai_evidence.note: the cold season, the middle of the night and the hill home fix kurinji's time and land

tamil: மா என மதித்து மடல் ஊர்ந்து ஆங்கு
மதில் என மதித்து வெண் தேர் ஏறி
என் வாய் நின் மொழி மாட்டேன் நின் வயின்
வண்டு உண் நறு வீ நுண்ணிதின் வரித்த
reading: The friend, who agreed to carry the man's plea, says to herself that she took his words into her mouth as one takes a palmyra stem for a horse and rides the madal, or a mirage for a wall and climbs it: she told the girl that one who has love must always be gracious to those who come to her from another street, put it sweetly, and still the girl would not take it; now she even thinks of laying at the girl's red feet his head, striped with the bee-sipped flowers of the shore grove, and wonders what would come of that.
nuance: The madal, the man's last threat, is here the friend's own image for her errand: she has ridden a palm stem as if it were a horse. Taking the mirage (வெண் தேர்) for a wall is a second figure of the same self-deception. The last lines may mean she will bring him to fall at the girl's feet; the syntax of lines 7 to 10 is compressed.

colophon.thurai: குறை நேர்ந்த தோழி தலைமகளை முகம்புக்க தன் சொல் கேளாது விடலின் இறப்ப ஆற்றான் ஆயினான் என உணர்ந்து ஆற்றாளாய்த் தன்னுள்ளே சொல்லியது தலைமகனுக்குக் குறை நேர்ந்த தோழி தலைமகளை முகம் புக்கலளாய் ஆற்றாது தன்னுள்ளே சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

tamil: முல்லை தாய கல் அதர்ச் சிறு நெறி
தாது எரு மறுகின் ஆ புறம் தீண்டும்
உகு பலி அருந்திய தொகு விரற் காக்கை
reading: The woman asks her friend whether there is no such evening in the land where her lover went, leaving them to seek hard-won wealth: here, in the small village off the stony mullai-covered path, where cows rub their backs on the long-rooted banyan of the god in the dung-dusted street, the crow that ate the spilt offerings goes to crowd in with its kin in the sad dusk, and the grieving evening comes as if with an army.
nuance: The question is whether evening exists where he is: if it did, he could not stay. The colophon files it under paalai for the parting, but nothing in the poem is of the road; the village, cows, mullai and evening are all mullai.

thinai_evidence.note: the woman bearing the evening at home while he is away is mullai's waiting

tamil: மணி ஏர் தோட்ட மை ஆர் ஏனல்
இரும் பிடித் தடக் கையின் தடைஇய பெரும் புனம்
நம் நிலை இடை தெரிந்து உணரான் தன் மலை
சாரல் நீள் இடைச் சால வண்டு ஆர்ப்ப
பெருங் கல் விடரகம் சிலம்ப இரும் புலி
களிறு தொலைத்து உரறும் கடி இடி மழை செத்து
இன் கல் யாணர்த் தம் உறைவின் ஊர்க்கே
reading: With the man listening unseen, the friend tells the girl that if they are set to guard the great field of dark millet on the hill slope, its heads bent like a she-elephant's trunk, he will not learn how things stand with them; will he simply go home, bees humming along the long slope at his sandal-smeared chest, to his town of rich rocks, where people mistake the roar of a tiger that has killed an elephant in the echoing cave for thunder and gather up the red millet drying in the yard?
nuance: Meant for the man's ears: once the millet is ripe the field-watch, and with it their meetings, will end. The closing scene, where a tiger's roar is taken for thunder and the drying millet is hurried in, is a near miss for ullurai (an alarm misread and a harvest gathered in might answer to gossip and the girl kept indoors), but neither pair is anchored in the poem, so it is scene.

thinai_evidence.note: millet fields, the tiger and the elephant are kurinji things

comparisons.tenor: the heavy bent heads of the millet

tamil: கானற் கண்டல் கழன்று உகு பைங் காய்
நீல் நிற இருங் கழி உட்பட வீழ்ந்தென
reading: To the lord of the shore, where the green fruit of the kandal drops into the dark blue backwater and the water lily, swung by the strong wind, opens white like a small white gull yawning, the friend says: if even upright men like you, who have taken on nobility and whose friendship is always kind and great, delay and do not want her, so that her unassured heart withers helplessly, what is the use of living; let assurance perish.
nuance: The curse falls on தெளிவு itself, the assurance he gave: if even the noble do not keep it, let trust perish. The falling fruit that sets the lily swinging open is a near miss for ullurai, with only one pair (his act, her opening), so it is scene.

thinai_evidence.note: mangrove, backwater and the shore lord fix neythal

tamil: குண கடல் முகந்து குடக்கு ஏர்பு இருளி
தண் கார் தலைஇய நிலம் தணி காலை
அரசு பகை நுவலும் அரு முனை இயவின்
ஆள் இல் மன்றத்து அல்கு வளி ஆட்ட
பெருந் தண் கொல்லிச் சிறு பசுங் குளவிக்
மட மா அரிவை தட மென் தோளே
reading: The man, on the hard frontier road where kings speak of war, in a small village with its fence destroyed and its common empty and swept by lingering wind, in the season when cool rain clouds drawn from the eastern sea have darkened the west and cooled the land, tells his heart that it seemed to laugh today at the thought of the broad soft shoulders of his young wife, whose hair smells of the small green kulavi of the great cool Kolli of Porayan, who shines like the full moon.
nuance: The rains of line 2 are mullai's season and the kulavi of Kolli a kurinji flower, so the road poem is mixed. Lines 6 and 7 (தாள் வலி ஆகிய வன்கண் இருக்கை / இன்று நக்கனைமன் போலா) are hard: the heart may have laughed once, or seem to laugh now, at the memory.

colophon.thurai: பொருள்வயிற் பிரிந்த தலைமகன் ஆற்றானாய்த் தன் நெஞ்சிற்குச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the man away on a hard, war-torn road, his heart turning home, is paalai's parting

comparisons.tenor: the shining of Porayan

tamil: முழங்கு கடல் முகந்த கமஞ் சூல் மா மழை
ஓங்கு வரை மிளிர ஆட்டி பாம்பு எறிபு
நீர் அன நிலையன் பேர் அன்பினன் எனப்
reading: The woman tells her friend that the bards who praise in many ways the lord of the great hill, where in the rain the great cloud, heavy with the roaring sea, hides the directions, shakes the high peaks, strikes the snakes and pours, and the falls come down sounding like a drum struck on its left face by the drummer, calling him as steady as water and full of love, make grand speeches as pitiable as frogs in summer; will her beauty come back for the sight of such praise?
nuance: The praise she scorns is the bards' (பரிசிலர்), the professional voices of puram; she turns their நெடுமொழி, the word for a hero's vaunt, into the croaking of frogs in a season with no rain, so the court's praise is weighed against a man who will not marry.

colophon.thurai: வரையாது நெடுங்காலம் வந்தொழுக ஆற்றாளாய தலைமகளைத் தோழி வற்புறுக்க மறுத்தது

thinai_evidence.note: the falls of the great hill fix kurinji

comparisons.tenor: the sound of the falls

tamil: நிலவே நீல் நிற விசும்பில் பல் கதிர் பரப்பி
ஊரே ஒலி வரும் சும்மையொடு மலிபு தொகுபு ஈண்டி
கானே பூ மலர் கஞலிய பொழில் அகம்தோறும்
யானே புனை இழை ஞெகிழ்த்த புலம்பு கொள் அவலமொடு
உலகமொடு பொரும்கொல் என் அவலம் உறு நெஞ்சே
reading: The woman says the moon has spread its many rays across the blue sky like a sea full of milk, the town in its noisy crowds celebrates a festival in its busy streets, in every flower-thick grove the bees hum with the mates they love, and she alone, her jewels slipping, in lonely grief, has no sleep through the dense dark night; so is this world fighting her, or is her grieving heart fighting the world?
nuance: Three ‑ஏ clauses (நிலவே, ஊரே, கானே) set out the full world before the fourth, யானே, sets her apart; the closing question will not settle whether she or the world is at fault.

colophon.thurai: வேட்கை பெருகத் தாங்கலளாய் ஆற்றாமை மீதூர்கின்றாள் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: lonely grief and sleeplessness are neythal's lament; the poem names no land

tamil: கொடுங் கழி மருங்கின் அடும்பு மலர் கொய்தும்
ஒளிறு வேல் அழுவத்துக் களிறு படப் பொருத
reading: The man says to himself, the friend listening, that riding his swift chariot or going on foot, plucking adumbu flowers by the curving backwater, lifting the screw-pine and picking the neythal, his heart feeling as if they had already met, he is distressed day after day; and he asks what the fisher girl can think of him, who never tires of hanging back behind her like the ghoul that hovers by men gravely wounded in the camp's spear-bright battlefield, where crowned kings fell and elephants were killed.
nuance: He gathers her shore's flowers as if gathering her, then sees himself as she must: a battlefield ghoul waiting by the wounded. The simile brings a whole puram scene into a love poem.

tamil: தேர் வண் விராஅன் இருப்பை அன்ன என்
கவவுக் கை தாங்கும் மதுகைய குவவு முலை
reading: The wife tells the man that even if her old beauty, like Iruppai of Viraan of the generous chariots, where the reapers' drum in the white paddy scares the many birds of the field into flight and the hanging clusters of the bent marutham drop, should perish, let it; she will not let him near, for to embrace him, his sandal crushed by the round breasts of another and his garland withered, would be like clasping a vessel that gives no hold; do not come, and long life to the woman who held you.
nuance: She stakes her beauty, which is a prosperous town, on the refusal: let it wane rather than let him in. The crushed sandal and withered garland are the evidence she reads off his body. ஆசு இல் கலம் is obscure: a vessel without a grip, or without a flaw, which would reverse the sense.

thinai_evidence.note: paddy reapers, field birds and the marutham tree fix the watered land

tamil: இளமை தீர்ந்தனள் இவள் என வள மனை
வருந்தல் வாழி வேண்டு அன்னை கருந் தாள்
களிற்றுத் துப்பு அஞ்சாப் புலி அதள் இதணத்து
reading: The friend tells the mother that, saying the girl had outgrown childhood, she shut her in strict guard in the rich house, yet does not see that the girl has only grown paler; let her not toil for many days worshipping the gods with a troubled heart: if the girl guarded the wide field of small millet from the platform of tiger hide, fearless of the elephant's might, built of sandalwood in the fork of the black-trunked vengai, she would surely get her beauty back.
nuance: The cure she prescribes is the cause: the millet field is where the girl meets the man. Her words tell the mother as much as can be told without confessing the affair.

thinai_evidence.note: the vengai, the watch platform and the millet field fix kurinji

tamil: இலை மாண் பகழிச் சிலை மாண் இரீஇய
நிழலொடு கதிக்கும் நிணம் புரி முது நரி
தேர் திகழ் வறும் புலம் துழைஇ நீர் நயந்து
reading: Halfway through the waste, the man says to himself that on this fearful forked road, where loveless men with bows and leaf-bladed arrows have killed many travellers, the old fat-loving jackal, driving off the cock bird with fire-red ears, runs with its shadow, gorges on raw flesh, grows hot, searches the bare mirage-bright ground for water and finds no shelter even in the shade of the cairns; the road has been hard even for him, so how has she come, the fine young girl of bamboo shoulders, pitiable as she is?
nuance: The closing question may mean she has come to him in thought across a road too hard for him, which is the likeliest reading, or that she followed him; the poem does not settle it.

colophon.thurai: பொருள்வயிற் பிரிந்த தலைமகன் இடைச் சுரத்துக்கண் ஆற்றானாய்த் தன்னுள்ளே சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the hard waste and the bare ground fix paalai

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: he speaks to himself (தன்னுள்ளே)

comparisons.tenor: the red ears of the cock bird
her shoulders

tamil: நுணங்கு நுண் பனுவல் போல கணம் கொள
ஆடு மழை தவழும் கோடு உயர் நெடு வரை
முட முதிர் பலவின் குடம் மருள் பெரும் பழம்
கரு விரல் மந்திக்கு வரு விருந்து அயரும்
இரும் புலி தொலைத்த பெருங் கை யானை
reading: The friend tells the lord of the sky-touching hill, where clouds drift in flocks over the high peaks like the fine thread that husbandless women spin by hand, and the hill people's dear young daughter feasts the black-fingered female monkey on the pot-sized fruit of an old bent jackfruit tree as on an arriving guest, that he is not noble, even if their love ripens, because he comes at midnight on the fearful narrow path where the great elephant that killed a tiger roars like fierce thunder.
nuance: சான்றோய் அல்லை is a hard word for a lover: his nobility is measured by whether he spares her the fear of his night journey.

colophon.thurai: தோழி ஆற்றது அருமை அஞ்சி தான் ஆற்றாளாய்ச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: jackfruit, hill people and the monkey fix kurinji

comparisons.tenor: the drifting clouds
the great jackfruit
the elephant's roar

iraicchi.act: the hill girl feeds the jackfruit to the monkey, treating it as an arriving guest
iraicchi.sense: in this country a guest who comes openly is fed and made welcome, so the man should come as a guest by marriage, not by the fearful night path

tamil: ஆடு அரை ஒழித்த நீடு இரும் பெண்ணை
நல் அரை முழுமுதல் அவ் வயின் தொடுத்த
கடு வெயில் கொதித்த கல் விளை உப்பு
நெடு நெறி ஒழுகை நிரை செலப் பார்ப்போர்
reading: The friend asks the man how the girl is to bear it, and tells him that at the spray-wet shore of the grove, with its yard of long sand near the grove fenced with fallen fronds of the tall dark palmyra and a small boat tied to the trunk of the punnai dark as night, his friendship has become gossip as loud as the din of the salt men watching their carts of sun-boiled salt move in rows down the long road.
nuance: The long description is of the girl's own yard, now a place he cannot reach; the salt carts are the noise of trade, and his secret love has become as public as a market.

colophon.thurai: தோழியால் செறிப்பு அறிவுறீஇ வரைவு கடாயது மனைவயின் தோழியைத் தலைமகன் புகழ்ந்தாற்கு மறுத்துச் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: palmyra, punnai and the salt pans fix neythal

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: on this reading the man praises the friend at the house (மனைவயின்) and she turns the praise aside

comparisons.tenor: the dark punnai
the gossip about his friendship

tamil: முலை வாய் உறுக்கும் கை போல் காந்தட்
அம் மடல் பட்ட அருவித் தீம் நீர்
அம் சில் ஓதி என் தோழி தோட் துயில்
நின் கண் அல்லது பிறிது யாதும் இலளே
reading: The friend tells the lord of the land, where the kaandal cluster touches the plump banana leaf as a flower-eyed young mother who has borne a son presses her breast to his mouth, and the red-faced monkey drinks the sweet falls-water caught on the leaf, that the truly refined will drink even poison if friends of long standing offer it; even if he finds no joy at heart in sleeping on her friend's shoulders, let him be kind for her sake, for the girl has nothing but him.
nuance: She asks him to act by கண் ஓடி, kindly regard, with the proverb of the poison as her proof: a refined man takes even what he does not want from a friend. The kaandal that guides the falls-water to the monkey like a mother's hand is a near miss for ullurai (the hand that offers maps to the friend who offers the girl, but no second pair holds), so it is a simile and scene.

colophon.thurai: தோழி அருகு அடுத்தது தோழி தலைமகளது ஆற்றாமை கண்டு வரைவு கடாயதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: kaandal, the falls and the monkey fix kurinji

comparisons.vehicle: புதல்வன் ஈன்ற பூங் கண் மடந்தை முலை வாய் உறுக்கும் கை போல்
comparisons.tenor: the kaandal cluster pressing on the banana leaf

tamil: நிலம் தாழ் மருங்கின் தெண் கடல் மேய்ந்த
விலங்கு மென் தூவிச் செங் கால் அன்னம்
பொன் படு நெடுங் கோட்டு இமயத்து உச்சி
அசைவு இல் நோன் பறை போல செல வர
வருந்தினை வாழி என் உள்ளம் ஒரு நாள்
reading: Refused the girl in marriage, the man tells his heart that it has toiled going and coming like the tireless strong wings of the red-legged swan with soft crossing feathers, which grazes in the clear sea where the land lies low and carries the gathered food to its unfledged chicks on the peak of the tall gold-bearing Himalaya, haunt of the celestial women; one day, with his beloved beside him, joy will come to them too, like the morning star rising in the east.
nuance: The swan's flight spans the whole land, from the southern sea to the Himalaya, and it flies to feed young that cannot yet fly: the heart's errands are for a future household. The morning star is an omen of the good day.

colophon.thurai: வரைவு மறுக்கப்பட்டு ஆற்றானாகிய தலைமகன் தன் நெஞ்சிற்குச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the hope of union after a refused proposal is kurinji's; the swan of the sea comes in only as a simile

comparisons.tenor: the heart's going and coming
the day of union to come

tamil: நின் குறிப்பு எவனோ தோழி என் குறிப்பு
பெயல் உழந்து உலறிய மணிப் பொறிக் குடுமிப்
அம் கண் அறைய அகல் வாய்ப் பைஞ் சுனை
reading: The woman asks her friend what she means to do, and says that her own mind, though it does not stay with her, never fades but has scarred her heart: the day she played with the man of the slopes, wearing a garland of blue lilies like her kohl eyes, gathered from the wide green pool among the rocks of the grove on the far-seen hillside where the peacock with gem-spotted crest dances after drying from the rain, the garland loosened by the tossing water.
nuance: The peacock that dances once it has dried after the rain is close to her own case, but it only shows a mood and does nothing a person of the situation does, so it is scene. The poet is a woman, Kurumakal Kuriyeyini.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகன் வரைவு நீடிய இடத்து ஆற்றுவல் என்பது படச் சொல்லியது மனை மருண்டு வேறுபாடாயினாய் என்ற தோழிக்குத் தலைமகள் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: peacock, hill pool and the man of the slopes fix kurinji

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon's first reading names no speaker; the poem's தோழி and the memory make it the woman

comparisons.tenor: the blue lilies of her garland

tamil: பெருந் தோள் நெகிழ அவ் வரி வாட
சிறு மெல் ஆகம் பெரும் பசப்பு ஊர
கணம் கெழு கடவுட்கு உயர் பலி தூஉய்
சிறு வெண் காக்கை நாள் இரை பெறூஉம்
பசும் பூண் வழுதி மருங்கை அன்ன என்
reading: The woman tells her friend: since he, ashamed to see her so, her broad shoulders slack, her fine lines fading and pallor spreading over her small soft chest, swore assurances to the friend, let them go scatter high offerings to the god who dwells with its host and pray, long life to you, never harm him in any way, though he is the one hard enough to stay away there while her rare beauty, like Marungai of Valuthi of the green jewels, where the small white gull gets its daily food of the curled-headed big red shrimp, fades.
nuance: The god punishes broken oaths, so the woman, the one wronged, prays for the oath-breaker's safety. The prayer reassures the friend while it names his fault.

colophon.thurai: பட்டபின்றை வரையாது பொருள்வயிற் பிரிந்த காலத்து தோழி இவள் ஆற்றா ளாயினாள் இவளை இழந்தேன் எனக் கவன்றாள் வற்புறுத்தது அக்காலத்து ஆற்றாளாய் நின்ற தலைமகள் தோழிக்குச் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the shrimp and the white gull of the shore fix neythal

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the woman reassures the friend who feared she would not survive

comparisons.tenor: her rare beauty

tamil: அலங்கு குலைக் காந்தள் தீண்டி தாது உக
reading: The friend says the lord of the hill land, where a small-horned red cow grazing the slope brushes the swaying kaandal and is so covered in pollen that her calf does not know her, has given them a leaf skirt to wear; if they wear it they fear the mother, if they give it back they fear hurting the kinsman; meanwhile will those leaves wither, so hard to pluck from his hill's god-haunted slopes where even the fighting mountain goats do not leap?
nuance: The gift is precious because of where it grew: leaves from slopes even the goats will not climb. The friend's dilemma, between the mother and the man, is set out in two balanced clauses (உடுப்பின் ... கொடுப்பின்).

colophon.thurai: தோழி தழையேற்றுக் கொண்டு நின்று தலைமகன் குறிப்பின் ஓடியது

thinai_evidence.note: kaandal, the slope and the mountain goat fix kurinji

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no addressee; the poem's யாம் speaks for both women, so the girl is assumed

ullurai.tenor: the girl marked by the man's gift, and her mother

pairs.situation: the girl who wears the leaves from his hill is marked by them
the mother would find her daughter changed and grow alarmed

ullurai.speaker_fit: the friend uses a cow, its calf and the kaandal of the hill slope in a kurinji poem (porul 7.27)

tamil: இன்று தரு மகளிர் மென் தோள் பெறீஇயர்
reading: The friend tells the man to go and win the soft shoulders of the women brought today, having taken the fresh beauty of those he joined yesterday and left them like the doll in the festival ground after the festival, when the drums' faces have dried and the turns of dancing are done; may his courtesans flourish; she is glad at the great distress he has come to, which he wastes like the morsel that an elephant in a sulk, goaded with spikes by its keepers, smears over its body instead of eating; and the lazy sleep of the house will come again.
nuance: The festival doll is the courtesans' fate, not the wife's: he uses each woman for a day. Lines 6 to 11 are hard; whose shame (பல்லோர் பழித்தல் நாணி) and whose sleep is meant is not certain.

colophon.thurai: பரத்தையிற் பிரிந்த தலைமகனைத் தோழி தலைமகள் குறிப்பறிந்து வாயில் மறுத்தது தலைமகள் ஊடிச் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the man's going to courtesans and the refusal at the door are marutham's oodal

comparisons.tenor: the women he enjoyed yesterday and abandoned
the man's distress, got and wasted

title: natrinai 361-380
theme: Natrinai 361 to 380: returns read in mullai garlands, bells and herdsmen's flutes, with the wife eager to feast guests; the hill girl's millet field closing as mothers sense the secret and the friend warns or threatens publicity; a lover's madal and an eloper who will fight strangers but hide from her kin; shore laments at evening; and in marutham a husband's tender memory of his wife's lying-in set against the friend's use of the same motherhood to refuse his bard.
source_issues: 364 lines 4 and 12, 367 lines 4 and 8, 380 line 1: line repaired for the lost vowel sign of -ஒடு, as show flags.

363: the first colophon alternative describes a speech in which the friend reassures the departing hero that she will console the heroine, which the verse does not contain; the verse asks him to bring the smith's sand for a crushed anklet. Copied as it stands; the verse is marked uncertain.
367: the colophon (வரவு மலிந்தது) names no speaker; the friend is inferred from the verse.
siddhar:922: the shared index reading says the hero 'will not hide', but the Tamil ends உமராயின் மறைகுவனே, 'if they are your kin I will hide'; the link from natrinai 362 follows the Tamil.

tamil: சிறு வீ முல்லைப் பெரிது கமழ் அலரி
விசும்பு கடப்பன்ன பொலம் படைக் கலி மா
படு மழை பொழிந்த தண் நறும் புறவில்
நெடு நா ஒண் மணி பாடு சிறந்து இசைப்ப
மாலை மான்ற மணம் மலி வியல் நகர்த்
reading: The friend, answering the go-betweens, says the tall man's chariot has come home at evening to the fragrant house: he and his young men wear the small-flowered mullai, his gold-harnessed horses run as if crossing the sky, his long-tongued bells ring through the rain-cooled scrub, and the woman of fine jewels, her long ache put away, is now eager to feast guests.
nuance: The proof of the return is a garland, not a sight of the man: the friend tells the go-betweens that even his young men wear the mullai, so the waiting is over and their errand is not needed; the wife's wish to feast guests is the sign that the house is whole again.

thinai_evidence.note: the rain-cooled scrub at evening and the mullai garland of the returning man

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the addressees are the go-betweens (வாயில்கள்) whom she disputes with

comparisons.tenor: the speed of the horses

tamil: தலை நாட்கு எதிரிய தண் பத எழிலி
அணி மிகு கானத்து அகன் புறம் பரந்த
மணல் இடு மருங்கின் இரும் புறம் பொருந்தி
reading: The eloping man tells the girl who moved like a crafted doll and crossed the bounds of her father's house that she may play a while, watching and gathering the red velvet mites spread over the forest that the first cool rains have adorned, while he leans on the broad trunk of a vengai rubbed by a young elephant: if a fight comes he will not fear but drive it off, and if her own people come he will hide.
nuance: His courage has a precise limit: strangers he will fight, her kin he will hide from, because a blow against her people would end the marriage the flight is meant to make; the road is offered to her as a playground of red mites, not a waste.

thinai_evidence.note: the flight from her father's house decides it, though the forest is green with first rain

comparisons.tenor: the girl's walk

tamil: தெண் கடல் நாட்டுச் செல்வென் யான் என
உறு வினைக்கு அசாவா உலைவு இல் கம்மியன்
பொறி அறு பிணைக் கூட்டும் துறை மணல் கொண்டு
reading: The friend tells the lord of the full-watered shore that if he takes leave saying he will go to his clear-sea country of backwater fields hedged with kandal, he should come back bringing the sand of the ford with which the tireless smith fuses broken links, for yesterday at fine evening, with him, her green leaf-skirt was torn, her garland faded, a few bright bangles slipped, and the anklet of the girl who made the crabs dance was crushed.
nuance: The torn skirt, faded garland, loosened bangles and crushed anklet are the evidence of the day's meeting that the house will read; the friend's demand for the smith's fusing sand is a half-joking order to undo the damage before anyone sees it.

colophon.thurai: பகற்குறி வந்து நீங்கும் தலைமகனைத் தோழி தலைமகளை என்னை ஆற்றுவிக்குமென்று ஆகாதோ எம்பெருமான் கவலாது செல்வது யான் ஆற்றுவிக்குமிடத்துக் கவன்றால் நீ ஆற்றுவி எனச் சொல்லியது கையுறை நேர்ந்த தோழி தலைமகட்குக் கையுறை உரைத்ததூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: kandal hedge, backwater and crabs of the shore

tamil: மயங்கு இருள் நடு நாள் மங்குலோடு ஒன்றி
ஆர் கலி வானம் நீர் பொதிந்து இயங்க
இன்ன சில் நாள் கழியின் பல் நாள்
உரும் இசை அறியாச் சிறு செந் நாவின்
ஈர் மணி இன் குரல் ஊர் நணி இயம்ப
reading: The heroine tells her friend that the season he named is past, and at midnight the roaring sky moves heavy with water in the mist and the cold north wind brings misery; if a few more such days pass she will not live many more, when in turn the sweet bells with small red tongues that never knew thunder ring near the town, and the unlettered herdsmen who brought home the many cows play sweet kondrai flutes in every common, in the evening that hurries life away, if it comes together with the faultless rain.
nuance: The thunder and the midnight storm she can bear; it is the softest sounds, bells too small to know thunder and the flutes of unlearned herdsmen, that she says will take her life, because they mark the evening hour of homecoming in which he does not come.

thinai_evidence.note: the named season, the rain and the herdsmen's evening

tamil: அகல் வயற் படப்பை அவன் ஊர் வினவி
reading: The friend, with the hero standing unseen nearby, tells the heroine: let us slip mother's strict watch, pass the great door, go into the common and, in daylight before everyone, ask aloud the way to his town of wide fields, and tell the lord of the sky-touching hill, whose slopes roar with falls even when the clouds have not rained for many days, 'you are not a man of worth', and come back.
nuance: The hill gives water when the sky gives none, and the reproach lies in the gap: its lord does not give even what is due. The threat is to make the secret public in daylight, the one step a woman of the house is not supposed to take; a near miss for ullurai, since only one pair (the hill's unfailing falls, his failing presence) can be named.

colophon.thurai: தோழி தலைமகன் சிறைப்புறத்தானாக தலைமகட்கு உரைப்பாளாய் இயற்பழித்துஇன்னது செய்தும் என்பாளாய்ச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the hill lord of waterfalls

tamil: வீடுறு நுண் துகில் ஊடு வந்து இமைக்கும்
மணி ஏர் ஐம்பால் மாசு அறக் கழீஇ
இரும் பல் மெல் அணை ஒழிய கரும்பின்
வேல் போல் வெண் முகை விரியத் தீண்டி
முதுக் குறைக் குரீஇ முயன்று செய் குடம்பை
reading: The man tells his heart, set on leaving for wealth, that those who part from the girl with great shoulders, whose fine cloth lets her many-stranded girdle gleam through like a rising snake, whose gem-dark hair is washed clean and tied with short-stemmed cold-season mullai visited by bees, and leave her soft bed in the north wind that opens the spear-white buds of the sugarcane and shakes the nest the wise sparrow toiled to hang from the bamboo, are fools, and long live this world.
nuance: The argument is made by season rather than by road: the cold wind that would lash the traveller is the same wind that rocks a sparrow's hard-built nest, so the poem ends on the general maxim the colophon calls உலகியல், that leavers are fools.

colophon.thurai: உலகியல் கூறிப் பொருள்வயிற் பிரிய வலித்த நெஞ்சிற்குத் தலைமகன் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: leaving for wealth is weighed and refused

comparisons.tenor: her girdle of many strands
the sugarcane buds

iraicchi.act: the wise little sparrow labours to build its nest and keeps to it while the north wind shakes it on the bamboo
iraicchi.sense: even a small bird holds to the home it built when the cold wind blows, so a man who leaves his wife's bed in that wind is a fool

tamil: கொடுங் கண் காக்கைக் கூர் வாய்ப் பேடை
நடுங்கு சிறைப் பிள்ளை தழீஇ கிளை பயிர்ந்து
கருங் கண் கருனைச் செந்நெல் வெண் சோறு
மெல் இயல் அரிவை நின் பல் இருங் கதுப்பின்
தளை அவிழ் அலரித் தண் நறுங் கோதை
பரியாது வருவர் இப் பனி படு நாளே
reading: The friend tells the soft girl: in the far-famed little village of Aruman's old house, where the sharp-beaked hen of the crooked-eyed crow, gathering her trembling-winged chick and calling her kin, snatches the white rice of red paddy with dark fried meat along with the offering to the fierce god and sits in flocks at the house rich in food, the young men have come wearing a cool garland of open mullai bound with blue lily, like the one in your thick dark hair, and our man too, driving fine horses with spread manes, will come without fail this dewy day.
nuance: The crow hen gathering her chick and kin to the house's food is read traditionally as the omen of a coming guest; here it does not pass the act test cleanly (her feeding is not something the wife does or fails to do) and is left as scene, a near miss for iraicchi. The proof is again the retinue's garland.

thinai_evidence.note: the returning retinue's mullai garland

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no speaker; the voice that calls her அரிவை and says நமரும் is the friend's

comparisons.tenor: the young men's garland

tamil: பெரும் புனம் கவரும் சிறு கிளி ஓப்பி
கோடு ஏந்து அல்குல் தழை அணிந்து நும்மொடு
நெறி படு கூழைக் கார் முதிர்பு இருந்த
வறிது உகு நெஞ்சினள் பிறிது ஒன்று சுட்டி
reading: The friend tells the hero: what is sweeter than driving small parrots from the great field, swinging on the black-stemmed vengai and playing with you in leaf-skirts and coming home? But mother, seeing the wild fragrance in her coiled dark hair and the pallor spreading on her small forehead, her heart sinking for no clear reason, hinting at something else, sighed hot breaths; sir, we are afraid, we are to be pitied.
nuance: The mother never accuses; she reads two signs, the strange scent in the hair and the pallor, says something else, and sighs, and that silence is what tells the friend the girl will be kept indoors. The joy of the first four lines exists to be lost.

thinai_evidence.note: millet field, parrots and vengai swing

tamil: நிறை பறைக் குருகினம் விசும்பு உகந்து ஒழுக
அரும்பு வாய் அவிழும் பெரும் புன் மாலை
ஞெமை ஓங்கு உயர் வரை இமையத்து உச்சி
கங்கைஅம் பேர் யாற்றுக் கரை இறந்து இழிதரும்
சிறை அடு கடும் புனல் அன்ன என்
reading: The heroine tells her friend that as the sun's anger cools and it reaches the hill, flocks of herons with full wings rise and stream across the sky, the day slowly passes and the mullai buds open their mouths in the great dim evening; if this comes again today she does not know, does not know, how she will swim across her love, which breaks her restraint as the fierce flood of the Ganga, falling from the shining white falls of the sky on the Himalaya's peak where ñemai trees rise, overruns its banks and breaks the dams.
nuance: The simile is built as a pun: the flood breaks dams (சிறை அடு) and her love breaks restraint (நிறை அடு), so the far-off Ganga falling from the Himalaya measures a feeling at the evening shore. She does not ask how to stop the flood but how to swim it.

colophon.thurai: பட்ட பின்றை வரையாது பொருள்வயிற் பிரிந்து ஆற்றாளாகிய தலைமகள் வன்புறை எதிர் அழிந்தது

thinai_evidence.note: her lament at evening with the shore's herons; the mullai buds are of another land

comparisons.tenor: her love that breaks restraint

tamil: கடும்புடைக் கடுஞ் சூல் நம் குடிக்கு உதவி
புதல்வன் ஈன்றெனப் பெயர் பெயர்த்து அவ் வரித்
துஞ்சுதியோ மெல் அம் சில் ஓதி என
reading: The man, whose wife's sulking has gone on too long, says: come, bard, let us laugh; when she who had helped our clan with her heavy pregnancy among her kin lay in the bright house shining with mustard seed glistening with ghee, and, having borne a son, changed her name and became, with her lined waist, an 'old woman', I came near saying 'are you asleep, soft one of thin locks?', laid a blue lily on her lovely belly and stood thinking, and she saw me, slowly showed a smile shy as a bud, and covered her flower-like painted eyes with her hand.
nuance: The joke he invites the bard to share is his wife's new title, 'old woman', given her by the birth of a son, and her shyness at being found by him in the lying-in room; in a marutham poem of oodal the tenderest scene is told as his evidence that she is still the bashful girl he married.

colophon.thurai: ஊடல் நீட ஆற்றானாய் நின்றான் பாணர்க்குச் சொல்லியது முன் நிகழ்ந்ததனைப் பாணர்க்குச் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: a husband's memory used against a long sulk

comparisons.tenor: her shy smile
her eyes

tamil: மா மலை விடர் அகம் விளங்க மின்னி
வியல் இரு விசும்பு அகம் புதையப் பாஅய்
நிழல் திகழ் சுடர்த் தொடி ஞெகிழ ஏங்கி
reading: The man returning with his work done tells his charioteer: like kondrai on a hill of kaayaa, lightning flashes so that the clefts of the great mountain shine, and the cloud that had not rained, looking toward the land where his dark girl lives, has spread to cover the wide sky and begun to rain; she, her bright bangles slipping, sighs and has begun to burn; and against that the herdsmen have begun their flutes, in the night of roaring thunder.
nuance: Three verbs of beginning (தொடங்கினவே, தொடங்கினளே, தொடங்கினரே) run in parallel: the rain begins, she begins to burn, the herdsmen begin to play; he imagines her evening at the very hour it starts, which is why the chariot must hurry.

thinai_evidence.note: the rains begun over the kaayaa hills and the herdsmen's flutes

thurai_akam.note: the addressee is the charioteer (பாகன்)

comparisons.tenor: lightning on the dark cloud over the hill

tamil: வள் இதழ் நெய்தல் வருந்த மூக்கு இறுபு
கிளைக் குருகு இரியும் துறைவன் வளைக் கோட்டு
இருங் கழி துழவும் பனித் தலைப் பரதவர்
reading: The heroine, knowing she is to be kept indoors and speaking for the hero to overhear, tells her friend it is ruinous: on the backwater the honey-full overripe fruit of the grove's palm falls, crushing the broad-petalled neythal, its tip breaking, and sinks deep in the dark mire so the flock of herons flees, at the shore of the lord who, on the white sand like the curve of a conch, looked at her sweetly with a willing heart; and they say, fearing she would grieve as when the swaying white thing mother gave was broken, her people tell her not to grieve over what has come, in the good town hedged with kandal where cold-headed fishermen at home count the lights of the sturdy boats that search the dark backwater.
nuance: A near miss for ullurai: the ripe palm fruit that crushes the neythal and scares off the herons invites the reading of a love that has fallen on her and set the town talking, but only one pair can be named with confidence and the poem does not anchor it. Lines 8 to 10 are obscure.

colophon.thurai: மேல் இற்செறிப்பான் அறிந்து ஆற்றாளாகி நின்ற தலைமகள் ஆற்ற வேண்டி உலகியல் மேல் வைத்துச் சிறைப்புறமாகச் செறியார் எனச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: backwater, neythal flower and fishermen

comparisons.tenor: the white sand

tamil: மை படு மால் வரை பாடினள் கொடிச்சி
கார் அரும்பு அவிழ்ந்த கணி வாய் வேங்கைப்
reading: The friend asks whether it will be ours tomorrow too, the joy of the girl of the hills who sang of her father's dark cloud-capped mountain as she pounded white hill-paddy while the grey-headed monkey scattered the fallen jackfruit segments in the yard, bathing with the man of the land in the falls of the god-haunted slope, and climbing the built platform on the vengai whose rain-opened buds tell the season, to drive the green flock from the curved ears of the small millet.
nuance: The whole poem is one long relative clause hanging on the final question, so the day's meeting is listed in full as something that may not happen again; the warning of confinement is never stated, only implied by நாளையும் 'tomorrow too'.

thinai_evidence.note: hill girl, vengai platform and millet field

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no addressee; நமக்கே takes the heroine in, and the warning is meant for the hero

tamil: வீழ் மா மணிய புனை நெடுங் கூந்தல்
reading: The man returning with his work done asks the wayfarers with tall umbrellas, who quell their hunger with the fruit of the salt-land tamarind on the unfinished road of hard gravel, by the little village crowded with salt merchants, whether he still has what he had before, and then how it is with the sweet-spoken girl of fine jewels who, eager to feast guests, suffers as the water from her long hair dressed with dark gems wets her freckled breast.
nuance: Line 5 is compressed: he seems to ask whether the life he had before still waits for him, and only then to ask after her; the formula 'eager to feast guests' (also natrinai 361) shows she keeps the house ready while she weeps.

colophon.thurai: வினை முற்றி மீள்வான் இடைச் சுரத்துக் கண்டார்க்குச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the wife waiting at home for his return; the road itself is paalai

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the addressees are travellers met on the waste (இடைச் சுரத்துக் கண்டார்)

tamil: நீடு சினைப் புன்னை நறுந் தாது உதிர
கோடு புனை குருகின் தோடு தலைப் பெயரும்
பல் பூங் கானல் மல்கு நீர்ச் சேர்ப்ப
அன்பு இலை ஆதலின் தன் புலன் நயந்த
இரவுத் தலை மண்டிலம் பெயர்ந்தென உரவுத் திரை
உயர் மணல் படப்பை எம் உறைவின் ஊரே
reading: The friend tells the lord of the full-watered shore of many-flowered groves, where the long-branched punnai drops fragrant pollen and the flocks of crested herons move off, that since he lacks love it would be good if he came in a way that gladdened the girl of fine brow, who desired him with her senses, and me and her shame together, to our town of high sand gardens, where at the head of night, when the moon has moved, the strong waves come as if they were hurling themselves.
nuance: 'Come so that her shame too rejoices' means come openly, as a suitor: a coming that pleases shame is a wedding, not a tryst. The reading of lines 4 and 5 is uncertain in its syntax.

colophon.thurai: வரையாது நெடுங்காலம் வந்தொழுக தலைமகளது நிலை உணர்ந்த தோழி வரைவு கடாயது

thinai_evidence.note: punnai, herons and the shore grove

comparisons.tenor: the waves at night

tamil: இறைஞ்சிய குரல பைந் தாட் செந் தினை
reading: The friend, with the hero standing unseen, tells the curve-beaked green parrots who eat together with their kin, as freely as the hill lord gives, the red millet with green stalks whose heads droop like the bent trunk of a winnow-eared elephant: if you see the man with the good garland on his chest, a cool wet chaplet of kullai, kulavi, koothalam and blue lily woven with illam, a bow bound round, appearing by the asoka, tell him plainly so he knows that our mother without justice, afflicting like an affliction, will not stop guarding the empty field.
nuance: The parrots share their millet as the hill lord shares his wealth, which flatters the overhearing hero and hints at what he should do; the harvested field still guarded by the mother means the meeting place is closed.

colophon.thurai: தோழி கிளிமேல் வைத்துச் சிறைப்புறமாகச் செறிப்பு அறிவுறீஇயது

thinai_evidence.note: millet, parrots and the asoka of the hill

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the addressees are the parrots

the parrots eating with their kin
the mother

tamil: பசுங் கதிர் மதியத்து அகல் நிலாப் போல
reading: The man, turned away, says within the friend's hearing: shall we, riding the palm-stem horse and wearing a garland, praising the beauty of the bright-browed girl through lands and towns of wide spaces, intent on doing it and suffering hard, not die of it as of a sickness? Her lovely forehead fringed with curls, like the wide light of the green-rayed moon that the snake has bitten into in the vast dark sky, chides and wastes me and has become my disease.
nuance: Riding the madal would put him in perunthinai; here it is still a threat spoken for the friend's ears, so the poem stays in kalavu. The eclipse simile is exact: the dark curls bite into the bright forehead as the snake bites the moon.

colophon.thurai: சேட்படுக்கப்பட்டு ஆற்றானாகிய தலைமகன் தோழி கேட்ப தன்னுள்ளே சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the madal threat of a hill lover turned away; the poem gives no land of its own

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: he speaks within himself (தன்னுள்ளே) for the friend to hear

comparisons.tenor: her forehead fringed with curls

tamil: இரவு இறந்து எல்லை தோன்றலது அலர் வாய்
வரி ஆர் சிறு மனை சிதைஇ வந்து
reading: The friend, with the hero standing unseen, tells the heroine: the night watch is long, the backwater is long, and love grows and lets the eyes not close, as the clear sea's roaring waves, slow as a drum's beat, toss like men with an old wound; though these afflict us, nowhere does day come after the night, and the neighbours' wives sing of her pallor with gossiping mouths; this, friend, is the measure of the bond formed without inquiry with the lord of the cold shore loud with sound, trusting the humble words he spoke, touching us to comfort us, after he came and ruined our little striped sand-house.
nuance: Three long things open the poem, the watch, the backwater and love, and the ending names its cause in a word of the ethics books: a friendship made without inquiry (நாடாது). The ruined sand-house is the girls' play, so the courtship began as a boy's prank on their game.

colophon.thurai: தோழி சிறைப்புறமாகச் சொல்லியது தலைமகன் ஒருவழித் தணந்த பின்னை வன்புறை எதிர்மொழிந்ததூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: backwater, sea and the lord of the shore

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the second alternative makes it the heroine's reply to her friend's reassurance

comparisons.tenor: the beat of the waves
the tossing sea

tamil: புன் தலை மந்தி கல்லா வன் பறழ்
தேம் பெய் தீம் பால் வெளவலின் கொடிச்சி
ஆடு மழை தவழும் கோடு உயர் பொதியில்
reading: The friend tells the hero that when the strong untaught young of the grey-headed monkey, not leaving the yard by the hill, clung to the low branch of the vengai with flower clusters like leaping flame and snatched the honey-sweet milk from her hand, the hill girl wept till the painted beauty of her eyes was spoiled, and they became like the blue lilies that bloom wet in the rain-filled moat at the gate of Kudanthai of the Cholas rich in chariots, and her fingers, beating her lovely belly without stopping, reddened like the plump buds of kanthal flowering on the dark slopes of high-peaked Pothiyil where clouds drift.
nuance: A child's grief over stolen milk is drawn with two royal similes, a Chola moat and the Pothiyil hill, so the friend's report of the girl's simplicity is also a portrait of her beauty; told to the hero, it says she is too young to be left waiting.

colophon.thurai: தோழி தலைமகற்குத் தலைமகளை மடமை கூறியது காப்புக் கைம்மிக்க காலத்துத் தலைமகள் தோழிக்குச் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: monkey, vengai and the hill girl

comparisons.tenor: the vengai clusters
her wet eyes
her reddened fingers

tamil: திதலை மென் முலைத் தீம் பால் பிலிற்ற
பொன் புரை நரம்பின் இன் குரல் சீறியாழ்
கொண்டு செல் பாண நின் தண் துறை ஊரனை
பாடு மனைப் பாடல் கூடாது நீடு நிலைப்
விரகு இல மொழியல் யாம் வேட்டது இல் வழியே
reading: The friend refuses the bard: our clothes and shoulders are soiled with ghee and the smoke of seasoning, sweet milk oozes from our soft spotted breasts, and holding our son we smell of new birth; we are no match for the chariot-man who shows himself in the street of brightly jewelled women; so, bard, though you can raise your small lute of sweet voice with strings like gold, do not bow, take your lord of the cool ford and go; even the horses that stand long tire of the harness while he is kept from the singing houses; do not speak artless words where we have no wish.
nuance: The refusal is made with the body of new motherhood itself: the ghee, the smoke, the milk and the smell of birth are offered as the reason she cannot compete with the jewelled women, which is both humility and accusation. Lines 10 and 11 are compressed.

thinai_evidence.note: refusal of the go-between bard for a husband who visits courtesans
